# Build with Canvas

Repository package version: 4.3.1. This is source documentation, not proof
that npm has published this version.

Canvas (`@nannier/canvas`) is a React Native UI kit for native iOS and Android
apps and the web through React Native Web. Use one component API with platform
skins, semantic boolean props, layout primitives and theme providers. Native
materials use optional native integrations; check the installation guide for your
runtime rather than treating a browser skin preview as native verification.

## Check the version first

This page describes the source package's onboarding workflow. As of 2026-11-01,
the published `4.0.0` package does **not** include the CLI shown below. These
commands require a package containing the CLI. Check the installed package's
`package.json` for the `canvas` executable before using them; otherwise follow
the [installation guide](/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) and installed declarations.
Repository previews and generated source snapshots do not prove publication.

In an existing project, read the resolved version in your lockfile or run
`npm ls @nannier/canvas`. Use documentation and declarations matching that
installed version. The currently generated [documentation index](/ai/4.3.1/index.md)
identifies its package version, source snapshot status and source digest.

## Start a project with an available CLI

Choose one recipe and a new destination:

```sh
npx @nannier/canvas init --recipe settings --dir ./my-app
```

The other recipes are `dashboard` and `booking`. Canvas copies a starter and
recipe files, refuses to overwrite existing files and prints the next steps.
The CLI does not install dependencies or run a package manager. Review the
generated files, then follow their installation and run instructions yourself.
The `npx` invocation can fetch the package; the Canvas CLI itself does not make
network requests.

## Work in an existing project

After installing a release that contains the CLI, run these from the project
root to use the installed package:

```sh
npx --no-install canvas docs --list
npx --no-install canvas docs button
npx --no-install canvas doctor --json
npx --no-install canvas skills install --client codex
```

Choose `--client claude` or `--client both` for the other supported destinations.
The skill installer writes project-local guidance into `.agents/skills/canvas`
for Codex and `.claude/skills/canvas` for Claude Code. It refuses file collisions;
review and reconcile existing guidance before trying the installation again.
It does not change account settings. The doctor reports setup findings locally;
read its output before sharing it in a public issue.

Give your coding agent a concrete task, the target platforms and the installed
Canvas version. For example: “Build a settings form with Canvas components for
web and iOS. Read the installed Canvas skill and component documentation, keep
the existing app shell, and verify keyboard use and the native runtime.” Agent
guidance helps retrieve the right API; it does not guarantee a model's choices
or a working application without verification.

## Read the API

- [Discovery index](/llms.txt) and [combined documentation](/llms-full.txt)
- [Installation](/ai/4.3.1/installation.md)
- [Theming](/ai/4.3.1/theming.md)

- [Component catalog](/ai/4.3.1/catalog.json) and [source/content manifest](/ai/4.3.1/manifest.json)

Compose existing Canvas components. Use boolean styling such as
`<Button primary large>` and layout components such as `Container`, `Row`,
`Column` and `Grid`. Read each component's props before using it, preserve
accessible names and keyboard behavior, and test each target platform. Typechecks,
web bundles and native runtime checks provide different evidence.

## Package and source terms

Canvas ships as one npm package. The npm package's LICENSE covers its packaged
files, including the consumer skill and recipes. Repository source retains its
all-rights-reserved terms; a public source preview is not a separate source grant.
Use the license and copyright notice included with the installed tarball for
the distributed package's terms. The public onboarding and API references linked
above do not require access to the private source repository.

# Accordion

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/molecules/accordion/accordion.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/accordion

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Accordion } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A vertically stacked group of disclosure rows: each `items` entry is a header (its `title` plus a chevron that rotates when the row opens) over a collapsible content panel.

Single-open by default (opening one row closes the others); pass `multiple` to let any number stay open. Open state is controlled (`value` + `onValueChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`). An item's `description` adds a muted secondary line under its title;
`card` wraps the whole group in an outlined card surface on web and Android (on iOS the default look already is the inset-grouped card, so `card` is a no-op there).

## Usage

```tsx
<Accordion
  items={[
    { key: "what", title: "What is Canvas?", content: "A universal React Native UI kit for iOS, Android, and the web." },
    { key: "access", title: "Is it accessible?", content: "Yes. Each header is a button that exposes its expanded state." },
    { key: "theme", title: "Is it themed?", content: "Yes. Every color comes from the active theme tokens." }
  ]}
  defaultValue="what"
/>
```

## Variants

### Multiple open

```tsx
<Accordion
  multiple
  items={[
    { key: "billing", title: "Billing", content: "Manage your plan, payment method, and invoices." },
    { key: "team", title: "Team", content: "Invite teammates and set their roles." },
    { key: "security", title: "Security", content: "Two-factor authentication and active sessions." }
  ]}
  defaultValue={["billing", "security"]}
/>
```

### Card surface

`card` gives the group an outlined card container with inset headers and content on
web and Android. On iOS the default Accordion already renders as the inset-grouped
card, so `card` changes nothing there (a documented no-op).

```tsx
<Accordion
  card
  items={[
    { key: "ship", title: "Shipping", content: "Free 2-day shipping on orders over $50." },
    { key: "return", title: "Returns", content: "30-day returns, no questions asked." },
    { key: "warranty", title: "Warranty", content: "Two years, parts and labor." }
  ]}
  defaultValue="ship"
/>
```

### With descriptions

```tsx
<Accordion
  items={[
    { key: "billing", title: "Billing", description: "Plan, payment method, invoices.", content: "Manage your plan, payment method, and invoices." },
    { key: "team", title: "Team", description: "Members and roles.", content: "Invite teammates and set their roles." },
    { key: "security", title: "Security", description: "2FA and sessions.", content: "Two-factor authentication and active sessions." }
  ]}
  defaultValue="billing"
/>
```

### Disabled row

```tsx
<Accordion
  items={[
    { key: "general", title: "General", content: "Workspace name, language, and time zone." },
    { key: "advanced", title: "Advanced (coming soon)", content: "Not available yet.", disabled: true },
    { key: "danger", title: "Danger zone", content: "Delete this workspace permanently." }
  ]}
  defaultValue="general"
/>
```

### Controlled

Drive the open step from outside the accordion: a parent owns the active step and
passes it as `value`, so the group reflects that external state rather than toggling on
a header press. Here the Next step button is the trigger. (`Stateful` is a
docs-only helper standing in for your own state; in an app you would hold `step` with
`useState` and pass `value={step}` plus `onValueChange` if you also want header presses
to update it.)

```tsx
<Stateful initial="step-1">
  {(step, setStep) => (
    <Column relaxed>
      <Button small outline onPress={() => setStep(step === "step-1" ? "step-2" : step === "step-2" ? "step-3" : "step-1")}>Next step</Button>
      <Accordion
        value={step}
        items={[
          { key: "step-1", title: "Step 1: Connect", content: "Link your data source." },
          { key: "step-2", title: "Step 2: Map", content: "Map the incoming fields." },
          { key: "step-3", title: "Step 3: Review", content: "Confirm and import." }
        ]}
      />
    </Column>
  )}
</Stateful>
```

### Activity disclosure

`activity` retains the original Argus run surface, instant trace reveal, dense
header and 180-degree chevron transition. `compact` keeps the original phone
insets. `renderHeader` arranges domain content inside the component-owned trigger;
the supplied indicator carries the controlled disclosure state. Put nested actions
in that header as Canvas controls so they retain independent targets.

```tsx
<Accordion activity items={[{ key: "run", title: "Scout run", content: "Trace complete" }]} defaultValue="run" />
```


## Do & Don't

### Peer sections

**Do** — Keep one disclosure group for a set of related, peer sections, and let the chevron carry the open/closed affordance.

```tsx
<Accordion
  items={[
    { key: "ship", title: "Shipping", content: "Free 2-day shipping on orders over $50." },
    { key: "return", title: "Returns", content: "30-day returns, no questions asked." }
  ]}
  defaultValue="ship"
/>
```

**Don't** — Don't leave every panel open by default in single-open mode; the closed-by-default disclosure is the point of an accordion.

```tsx
<Accordion
  items={[
    { key: "a", title: "Section A", content: "..." },
    { key: "b", title: "Section B", content: "..." }
  ]}
  multiple
  defaultValue={["a", "b"]}
/>
```

## Supported props

### AccordionProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| activity | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Original Argus run disclosure surface, header and trace insets. |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Compact activity header and trace indentation. |
| renderHeader | ((item: AccordionItem, expanded: boolean, indicator: ReactNode) => ReactNode) \| undefined | no |  | Activity header content; the Accordion owns its trigger and indicator. |
| items | AccordionItem[] \| undefined | no |  | The disclosure rows, top to bottom. |
| value | string \| string[] \| undefined | no |  | Controlled open state. A single key in single-open mode, an array of keys in `multiple` mode. Pair with `onValueChange`. Omit for uncontrolled. |
| defaultValue | string \| string[] \| undefined | no |  | Initial open state for the uncontrolled case (read once). |
| onValueChange | ((value: string \| string[]) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Called with the next open value whenever a header toggles. |
| multiple | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Allow more than one panel open at once (default: single-open). |
| card | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Card surface: wraps the group in an outlined card container with inset headers and content (web/Android). On iOS the default Accordion already renders as the inset-grouped card, so `card` is a no-op there. |
| disabled | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Disable the whole group (every row stops toggling and dims). |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# ActionPanel

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/molecules/action-panels/action-panels.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/action-panels

## Public imports

```tsx
import { ActionPanel } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Section panel with headline, body text, and one action. Used to surface a single decision or call-to-action.

The panel is the v4 hand-off's on every platform (no platform ships an action panel): an 18 px inset at the card corner on a hairline over the card fill, a 600 15 title over a 13 px muted description. The action is an outline Button; `destructive` washes the panel in the danger tint, edges it in the destructive colour and makes the action destructive; `inline` pins the action beside the copy, wrapping it underneath when the panel is narrow. Embedded `children` sit under the copy, and the Button then closes the panel on the right as the primary action that commits them.

## Usage

The panel's single action fires `onAction`; wire it to your own handler and every
press runs it.

```tsx
<ActionPanel
  title="Export your data"
  description="Download everything in this workspace as a ZIP archive."
  actionLabel="Export"
/>
```

## Variants

### Destructive

```tsx
<ActionPanel
  title="Delete this project"
  description="Once you delete a project, there is no going back."
  actionLabel="Delete project"
  destructive
/>
```

### Inline

```tsx
<ActionPanel
  title="Weekly digest"
  description="A summary of workspace activity, sent every Monday."
  actionLabel="Subscribe"
  inline
/>
```

### Toggle

```tsx
<ActionPanel
  title="Two-factor authentication"
  description="Require a verification code on every login."
  toggle
/>
```

### Embedded fields

```tsx
<ActionPanel
  title="Workspace profile"
  description="These details appear on every invoice."
  actionLabel="Save changes"
>
  <Input label="Workspace name" defaultValue="Northwind" />
  <Input label="Billing email" defaultValue="billing@northwind.com" />
</ActionPanel>
```

### Fields under a pinned action

```tsx
<ActionPanel
  title="Two-factor authentication"
  description="Require a verification code on every login."
  toggle
>
  <Input label="Recovery phone" defaultValue="+1 555 0148" />
</ActionPanel>
```

### Confirm before delete

```tsx
<Stateful initial={false}>
  {(open, setOpen) => (
    <Container md>
      <ActionPanel
        title="Delete this project"
        description="Once you delete a project, there is no going back."
        actionLabel="Delete project"
        destructive
        onAction={() => setOpen(true)}
      />
      <AlertDialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        destructive
        title="Delete this project?"
        description="This permanently removes the project and its data."
        confirmLabel="Delete"
      />
    </Container>
  )}
</Stateful>
```

## Do & Don't

### Simple

**Do** — Spell out the consequence above the button so the stakes are clear before the click.

```tsx
<ActionPanel title="Delete this project" description="Once you delete a project, there is no going back. Please be certain." actionLabel="Delete project" destructive />
```

**Don't** — A destructive action with no consequence copy invites accidental, irreversible clicks.

```tsx
<ActionPanel title="Delete this project" actionLabel="Delete project" destructive />
```

### With toggle

**Do** — Pair the switch with a one-line explanation of what turning it on or off does.

```tsx
<ActionPanel title="Two-factor authentication" description="Add an extra layer of security to your account by requiring a verification code on login." toggle defaultChecked />
```

**Don't** — A bare switch with no description leaves the user guessing what flipping it actually changes.

```tsx
<ActionPanel title="Two-factor authentication" toggle defaultChecked />
```

## Supported props

### ActionPanelProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | string \| undefined | no |  | The headline: what the action acts on. |
| description | string \| undefined | no |  | The consequence copy beneath the title: what happens when the action fires. |
| actionLabel | string \| undefined | no |  | The action button label. |
| onAction | (() => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when the action button is pressed. |
| destructive | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tone (omit for the neutral, primary-action default). |
| inline | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Layout (pick one; default stacks the action below the copy). |
| toggle | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Affordance: render the action as an on/off Switch instead of a Button. The panel always lays out inline in this mode. |
| checked | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The Switch on/off state when `toggle` is set (CONTROLLED). Omit for uncontrolled use. |
| defaultChecked | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Initial Switch state for uncontrolled use (the toggle flips itself on press). |
| onToggle | ((next: boolean) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired with the next checked value when the toggle Switch is flipped. |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | Content embedded in the panel under the copy (a block of field rows in a settings panel, say). The Button then closes the panel on the right, under a hairline, as the action that commits it; a toggle stays pinned beside the copy. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# ActionSheet

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/action-sheet/action-sheet.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/action-sheet

## Public imports

```tsx
import { ActionSheet } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A modal sheet of contextual actions, the iOS action sheet idiom:
a bottom sheet
of choices summoned in response to a user action, over a dimmed scrim that glass
on the web also blurs.

It poses an optional title and message, lists a set of actions (any of which can
be destructive), and offers a Cancel. Selecting an action runs it and closes the
sheet; tapping the scrim or Cancel closes it without acting. Pass a `trigger`
label for a self-contained button that opens the sheet, or drive `open` /
`onOpenChange` yourself. For a small contextual menu anchored to a control,
reach for Dropdown or RowMenu instead.

On the web the sheet is two cards a little off the window's edges: a centered header
over full-width rows in the accent's ink (a destructive one in the error ink), each under
a hairline, and a separate Cancel card.
iOS keeps its Liquid Glass sheet with detached
capsules, and Android the Material 3 bottom sheet with a drag handle and list rows.

iOS accessibility escape and Android system back request cancellation without
running an action.
An open child overlay handles the request first. Disabled
actions do not disable cancellation, and a controlled owner can keep the sheet
open. The visible Cancel row remains available to assistive technology.

## Usage

```tsx
<ActionSheet
  trigger="Add photo"
  actions={[
    { label: "Take Photo", onPress: () => {} },
    { label: "Choose from Library", onPress: () => {} }
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### With a title and message

```tsx
<ActionSheet
  trigger="Discard draft…"
  title="Discard draft?"
  message="Your unsaved changes will be lost."
  actions={[
    { label: "Discard Changes", onPress: () => {} },
    { label: "Keep Editing", onPress: () => {} }
  ]}
/>
```

### Destructive action

```tsx
<ActionSheet
  trigger="File options"
  actions={[
    { label: "Move to Folder", onPress: () => {} },
    { label: "Delete File", destructive: true, onPress: () => {} }
  ]}
/>
```

### Disabled action

```tsx
<ActionSheet
  trigger="File options"
  actions={[
    { label: "Save", onPress: () => {} },
    { label: "Save As…", disabled: true, onPress: () => {} }
  ]}
/>
```

### Controlled

```tsx
<Stateful initial={false}>
  {(open, setOpen) => (
    <>
      <Button onPress={() => setOpen(true)}>Share…</Button>
      <ActionSheet
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        actions={[
          { label: "Copy Link", onPress: () => {} },
          { label: "Send by Email", onPress: () => {} }
        ]}
      />
    </>
  )}
</Stateful>
```

### Open in place

`embedded` draws the sheet open at the foot of its parent over the parent's own dim, for a
specimen or a preview: no modal, no focus trap, no Escape or hardware back, and a dim that
passes touches through. A `trigger` always opens the live modal sheet instead.

```tsx
<ActionSheet
  embedded
  open
  title="Share photo"
  actions={[
    { label: "Copy Link", onPress: () => {} },
    { label: "Send by Email", onPress: () => {} },
    { label: "Print", onPress: () => {}, disabled: true }
  ]}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### Right tool for the job

**Do** — Use an Action Sheet for a short list of choices triggered by a user action, with the dangerous option marked destructive.

```tsx
<ActionSheet
  trigger="Add photo"
  title="Photo"
  actions={[
    { label: "Take Photo", onPress: () => {} },
    { label: "Choose from Library", onPress: () => {} },
    { label: "Remove Photo", destructive: true, onPress: () => {} },
  ]}
/>
```

**Don't** — Use an Action Sheet for a single yes/no confirmation; an Alert Dialog is the focused tool for that.

```tsx
<ActionSheet
  trigger="Confirm"
  title="Are you sure?"
  actions={[{ label: "OK", onPress: () => {} }]}
/>
```

### Name the action, not a generic verb

**Do** — Label each row with the action it performs (Take Photo, Delete File, Move).

```tsx
<ActionSheet
  trigger="File options"
  actions={[
    { label: "Delete File", destructive: true, onPress: () => {} },
    { label: "Move to Folder", onPress: () => {} },
  ]}
/>
```

**Don't** — Generic labels force the user to re-read the title to know what each row does.

```tsx
<ActionSheet
  trigger="Delete file…"
  title="Delete file?"
  actions={[
    { label: "Yes", destructive: true, onPress: () => {} },
    { label: "No", onPress: () => {} },
  ]}
/>
```

## Supported props

### ActionSheetProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Controlled open state. Omit for uncontrolled (a `trigger` opens it). |
| onOpenChange | ((open: boolean) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when the open state changes (trigger press, scrim tap, Cancel, an action, back/escape). |
| trigger | string \| undefined | no |  | Label for an optional trigger button. When set, the sheet renders the button and opens itself on press (uncontrolled). Omit when you drive `open` yourself. |
| title | string \| undefined | no |  | Optional header title (a left-aligned primary-label heading on iOS, a short centered heading on web, left-aligned on Android). |
| message | string \| undefined | no |  | Optional header message under the title. |
| actions | ActionSheetAction[] | yes |  | The action rows. Each runs its `onPress` then closes the sheet. |
| cancelLabel | string \| undefined | no | "Cancel" | The Cancel row label (default "Cancel"). |
| embedded | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Show the open sheet as a non-modal specimen inside its parent, for a catalogue or a showcase: the stack rests against the parent's bottom edge (the parent gives it its height) over the dim, with no Modal, no rise, no focus trap and no close on Escape, native back or a tap on the dim. Its rows still run their actions. Ignored with `trigger`, which always opens a live sheet. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | StyleProp<ViewStyle> | no |  | Outer layout composition for the bottom-anchored stack, composed onto the stack container; not a restyle hook. (The device's bottom safe-area inset is applied automatically, so it clears the home indicator without a manual `paddingBottom`.) |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# AlertDialog

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/molecules/alert-dialog/alert-dialog.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/alert-dialog

## Public imports

```tsx
import { AlertDialog } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Catalyst-style confirmation dialog: a centered panel over a dimmed backdrop, which glass on the web also blurs, with a title, description, optional body, and action buttons. Reserve it for decisions that must block the rest of the app.

On the web and Android the panel leads with a tone tile (a trash glyph on the
destructive wash, otherwise an info glyph on the accent's), then a display title over
its description, and closes on two equal buttons: a secondary Cancel and the primary or
destructive confirm.
On iOS it is the system alert: centered text over a two-cell action
row under a hairline, the confirm in the error ink when destructive.

Browser Escape and iOS accessibility escape cancel the dialog,
clear its
confirmation field and request `open=false`. The confirmation text gates only
the confirm action; cancellation remains available while confirm is disabled.
An open child overlay handles dismissal first. A controlled owner can refuse
closure without passing that request to a parent or calling `onConfirm`.

Add `embedded` to show an open alert dialog in a page as a specimen, the way a
catalogue or a showcase does: it keeps its look, its alertdialog role and its
labelling, but it is not modal. It does not take focus when it opens, trap Tab,
return focus, set `aria-modal`, or cancel on Escape or native back, so the page
around it keeps its scroll position and its keyboard order. `embedded` is ignored
with `trigger`, which always opens a live modal.

## Usage

```tsx
<AlertDialog
  title="Delete this identity?"
  description="This permanently removes the identity and revokes any active sessions. This action cannot be undone."
  confirmLabel="Delete"
  destructive
  trigger="Delete identity…"
/>
```

## Variants

### Narrow

```tsx
<AlertDialog
  narrow
  title="Sign out?"
  confirmLabel="Sign out"
  trigger="Sign out…"
/>
```

### Small

```tsx
<AlertDialog
  small
  title="Transfer ownership?"
  description="You will lose admin access to this workspace."
  confirmLabel="Transfer"
  trigger="Transfer ownership…"
/>
```

### Large

```tsx
<AlertDialog
  large
  title="Transfer ownership?"
  description="You will lose admin access to this workspace, and the new owner can remove you from it. Billing, integrations, and the audit history move with the workspace."
  confirmLabel="Transfer"
  trigger="Transfer ownership…"
/>
```

### Body field

`withInput` renders a confirmation field that gates the confirm action: the user
must type the `confirmText` token (default `"DELETE"`) exactly before the confirm
button enables, so it is a real safety check rather than a decorative field. Pass
`confirmText` to require a different token.

```tsx
<AlertDialog
  title="Delete this identity?"
  description="This permanently removes the identity and revokes any active sessions. This action cannot be undone."
  confirmLabel="Delete"
  destructive
  withInput
  trigger="Delete identity…"
/>
```

### Controlled

Drive the open state from outside the dialog: omit `trigger`, own `open` yourself,
and pass `onOpenChange` so every way the dialog closes (confirm, cancel,
browser
Escape or iOS accessibility escape) reports back
and keeps your state in sync. (`Stateful` is a
docs-only state holder; in an app you would hold `open` with `useState`.)

```tsx
<Stateful initial={false}>
  {(open, setOpen) => (
    <Column relaxed>
      <Button onPress={() => setOpen(true)}>Transfer ownership…</Button>
      <AlertDialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        title="Transfer ownership?"
        description="You will lose admin access to this workspace."
        confirmLabel="Transfer"
      />
    </Column>
  )}
</Stateful>
```

## Do & Don't

### Reserve the dialog for blocking decisions

**Do** — Use an inline banner or toast for passive feedback; reserve the dialog for decisions that must be confirmed.

```tsx
<Alert success title="Saved" description="Your changes have been saved." />
```

**Don't** — A blocking alert dialog for passive confirmation interrupts the user for no reason.

```tsx
<AlertDialog small title="Saved" description="Your changes have been saved." confirmLabel="OK" trigger="Save changes" />
```

### Name the action on the confirm button

**Do** — Label the confirm button with the verb it performs (Delete, Archive, Sign out).

```tsx
<AlertDialog small destructive title="Delete this identity?" cancelLabel="Cancel" confirmLabel="Delete" trigger="Delete identity…" />
```

**Don't** — Generic Yes / No forces the user to re-read the title to know what they are confirming.

```tsx
<AlertDialog small destructive title="Delete this identity?" cancelLabel="No" confirmLabel="Yes" trigger="Delete identity…" />
```

### xs

**Do** — Reserve xs for a terse one-line question with short button labels and no body content.

```tsx
<AlertDialog narrow destructive title="Remove device?" cancelLabel="Cancel" confirmLabel="Remove" trigger="Remove device…" />
```

**Don't** — A long title, multi-line description, and wordy buttons get cramped in the xs width and wrap awkwardly.

```tsx
<AlertDialog narrow destructive title="Remove this trusted device?" description="It will need to re-authenticate, and any pending background syncs from it will be cancelled the next time it connects." cancelLabel="Cancel" confirmLabel="Remove device" trigger="Remove device…" />
```

### sm

**Do** — Use sm for a single short confirmation with a one-line description; move real forms to a full dialog.

```tsx
<AlertDialog small title="Transfer ownership?" description="You will lose admin access to this workspace." cancelLabel="Cancel" confirmLabel="Transfer" trigger="Transfer ownership…" />
```

**Don't** — Packing a multi-field form into sm makes it feel like a form crammed into a confirmation popup.

```tsx
<View style={{ alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", borderRadius: 8, backgroundColor: alpha("#000000", 0.5), padding: 32, minHeight: 200 }}>
  <View style={{ width: 384, maxWidth: "100%", borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.popover, padding: 24, boxShadow: "0 20px 25px -5px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)" }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 16, lineHeight: 24, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens["popover-foreground"] }}>Transfer ownership</Text>
    <View style={{ marginTop: 16, gap: 16 }}>
      <View>
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground, marginBottom: 6 }}>New owner email</Text>
        <Input placeholder="owner@example.com" />
      </View>
      <View>
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground, marginBottom: 6 }}>Reason</Text>
        <Input placeholder="Optional note" />
      </View>
      <View>
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground, marginBottom: 6 }}>Type TRANSFER to confirm</Text>
        <Input placeholder="TRANSFER" />
      </View>
    </View>
    <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", justifyContent: "flex-end", gap: 8, marginTop: 24 }}>
      <Button outline small>Cancel</Button>
      <Button primary small>Transfer</Button>
    </View>
  </View>
</View>
```

### md

**Do** — md is the default home for a typical destructive confirm with a sentence or two of description.

```tsx
<AlertDialog destructive title="Delete this identity?" description="This permanently removes the identity and revokes any active sessions. This action cannot be undone." cancelLabel="Cancel" confirmLabel="Delete" trigger="Delete identity…" />
```

**Don't** — Squeezing a description-carrying confirm into a smaller width crowds the copy against the edges.

```tsx
<AlertDialog narrow destructive title="Delete this identity?" description="This permanently removes the identity and revokes any active sessions. This action cannot be undone." cancelLabel="Cancel" confirmLabel="Delete" trigger="Delete identity…" />
```

### lg

**Do** — Reserve lg for dialogs that earn the width: a body field or a longer explanation to read.

```tsx
<AlertDialog large destructive withInput title="Delete this identity?" description="This permanently removes the identity and revokes any active sessions. This action cannot be undone." cancelLabel="Cancel" confirmLabel="Delete" trigger="Delete identity…" />
```

**Don't** — A bare yes/no in lg leaves a wide, empty panel that reads as heavier than the trivial decision it asks for.

```tsx
<AlertDialog large title="Sign out?" cancelLabel="Cancel" confirmLabel="Sign out" trigger="Sign out…" />
```

## Supported props

### AlertDialogProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | string \| undefined | no |  | Content (strings). |
| description | string \| undefined | no |  | Content (strings). |
| trigger | string \| undefined | no |  | Trigger button label. When set, the dialog renders the button and opens itself on press (uncontrolled). Omit when you drive `open` yourself. |
| confirmLabel | string \| undefined | no | "Continue" | Action labels. |
| cancelLabel | string \| undefined | no | "Cancel" | Action labels. |

The default is a contained overlay, which the docs catalogue needs to show one inside an example stage. An application asking to confirm a destructive action needs the opposite: inline, the scrim appears wherever the component happens to sit, the page behind stays scrollable and clickable, and the dialog still claims `aria-modal`. Teleports into the nearest `OverlayProvider`; with none in the tree it renders in place. |
| embedded | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Show the open dialog as a non-modal specimen in the page, for a catalogue or a showcase: it keeps its look, its alertdialog role and its labelling, but does not take focus when it opens, trap Tab, return focus, claim `aria-modal`, or cancel on Escape or native back. # Alert

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/molecules/alert/alert.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/alert

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Alert } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Inline notification banners: info, success, warning, and destructive, plus a full-width announcement bar. For a blocking confirmation prompt, see Alert Dialog.

A banner fills the parent it is given, so a column of alerts is the same measure top to bottom and a banner over a form lines up with the fields; a Container step sets the measure when the layout calls for one.

A banner is a soft callout: the tone's wash under a 1px edge of the tone's color, the tone's own glyph in that color, a foreground title and a muted body, from `statusColors` (the helper Badge and every toned surface read). The neutral banner is the quiet muted surface with an info glyph in the muted ink. Pass `icon` to draw another glyph (an `<Icon />` takes the tone's color and the banner's 18px size), or `icon={null}` to draw none.

## Usage

Pressing the trailing "×" (`dismissible`) hides the banner out of the box; `onDismiss` reports it, and a controlled `dismissed` prop hands that state to the parent instead. Action buttons are real Buttons: wire each one's `onPress`.

```tsx
<Alert
  info
  title="Heads up"
  description="Maintenance window scheduled for Sunday 2:00 UTC."
/>
```

## Variants

### Success

```tsx
<Alert
  success
  title="All set"
  description="Your changes have been saved successfully."
/>
```

### Warning

```tsx
<Alert
  warning
  title="Action required"
  description="Your trial expires in 3 days."
/>
```

### Destructive

```tsx
<Alert
  destructive
  title="Something went wrong"
  description="Could not save your changes. Please try again."
/>
```

### Neutral

```tsx
<Alert
  icon={<Icon bell />}
  title="Scheduled maintenance"
  description="The dashboard may be briefly unavailable on Sunday between 2:00 and 3:00 UTC."
/>
```

### Dismissible

```tsx
<Alert
  info
  title="Heads up"
  description="Maintenance window scheduled for Sunday 2:00 UTC."
  dismissible
/>
```

### Actions

```tsx
<Alert
  warning
  title="Action required"
  description="Your trial expires in 3 days."
  actions={<Button primary small>Upgrade plan</Button>}
/>
```

### Inline action

`action` is one quiet link in the banner's actions, for the single next step a notice offers.

```tsx
<Alert
  info
  title="New sign-in"
  description="A browser in Lisbon signed in to your account."
  action={{ label: "Review activity" }}
/>
```

### Announcement

`announcement` is the full-width product bar: the accent's gradient under its own ink, a
sparkles glyph, the message, an inline `action` link and the dismiss box. It has its own
look, so the tone booleans do not apply to it.

```tsx
<Alert
  announcement
  dismissible
  title="Canvas 4.0 is live: every component on lit glass."
  action={{ label: "See what moved" }}
/>
```

### Measures come from the parent

```tsx
<Column snug>
  <Container xs start>
    <Alert title="In an xs Container" description="The banner fills the 320px step, the measure of a short form." />
  </Container>
  <Alert title="Bare" description="No container of its own: the banner fills whatever parent it sits in." />
</Column>
```

### Rich body

```tsx
<Alert title="Design token renamed">
  <Typography small muted>
    The field underline now reads from <Typography code>--p-field-underline</Typography> instead of a raw hex value; update any local overrides before upgrading.
  </Typography>
</Alert>
```

## Do & Don't

### info

**Do**: Reserve info for passive, non-urgent context (notices, tips); escalate to warning or destructive when action is required.

```tsx
<Alert info title="Heads up" description="Maintenance window scheduled for Sunday 2:00 UTC." />
```

**Don't**: Dressing an act-now message in the neutral info tone hides the urgency; users skim past it like an FYI.

```tsx
<Alert info title="Trial expires today" description="Upgrade now or you'll lose access to your projects." />
```

### success

**Do**: Make confirmations transient: auto-dismiss or give a Dismiss control so the success state clears once acknowledged.

```tsx
<Alert
  success
  title="Saved"
  description="Your changes have been saved successfully."
  dismissible
/>
```

**Don't**: A success banner pinned with no way to dismiss it lingers as visual noise long after the action is done.

```tsx
<Alert success title="Saved" description="Your changes have been saved successfully." />
```

### warning

**Do**: State the consequence, the deadline, and the action: name what's wrong and give a button to resolve it.

```tsx
<Alert
  warning
  title="Action required"
  description="Your trial expires in 3 days. Upgrade to keep your projects."
  actions={<Button primary small>Upgrade plan</Button>}
/>
```

**Don't**: A warning with no specifics or next step leaves the user guessing what to fix and by when.

```tsx
<Alert warning title="Action required" description="Something needs your attention." />
```

### destructive

**Do**: Match the variant to the severity: reserve destructive for genuine failures, success for confirmations.

```tsx
<Alert destructive title="Something went wrong" description="Could not save your changes. Please try again." />
```

**Don't**: Using the destructive variant for non-errors cries wolf; users learn to tune out red and miss real failures.

```tsx
<Alert destructive title="Saved" description="Your changes have been saved successfully." />
```

## Supported props

### AlertProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | string \| undefined | no |  | Content. |
| description | string \| undefined | no |  | Content. |
| icon | ReactNode | no |  | The leading glyph: an element (an `<Icon />`, tinted to the tone's color unless it sets its own, and sized to the banner's glyph) or a single text character. Omitted, the banner draws its tone's own glyph (an info circle on info and neutral, a check on success, an alert circle on warning, a cross on destructive); `null` draws none. |
| info | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tone (pick one; omit for the neutral default). |
| success | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tone (pick one; omit for the neutral default). |
| warning | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tone (pick one; omit for the neutral default). |
| destructive | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The danger tone. This is the name the intent axis uses across the kit (Button, AlertDialog, and every chart) and the one the design hand-off uses here too. |
| announcement | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The announcement bar: one line on the accent gradient (the accent running into the cyan series hue) in the accent's own ink, under its glow, with its `action` inline at the end. For page-wide news ("v4 is live"), not for a status. It is its own look, so it ignores the tone axis. |
| action | { label: string; onPress?: () => void; } \| undefined | no |  | One action, as a label and a handler. On the announcement bar it sits inline at the end of the line, in the bar's ink; on the other looks it is a link Button in the actions region, before any `actions`. |
| dismissible | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Shows a trailing dismiss control. Pressing it hides the banner out of the box (uncontrolled); pass `dismissed` to own that state instead. |
| dismissed | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Controlled dismissal: `true` hides the banner. Omit to let the Alert manage it. |
| defaultDismissed | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Uncontrolled seed: start hidden. Rarely useful; defaults to false. |
| onDismiss | (() => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when the dismiss control is pressed (both modes). |
| children | ReactNode | no |  |  |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| actions | ReactNode | no |  | A footer action region rendered under the body. The Alert owns the layout: it separates the actions from the description above and lays the buttons out in a row, so a call site passes the buttons directly (`actions={<Button primary small>Upgrade plan</Button>}`) with no wrapper. Pass a fragment for more than one action. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

# AppFrame

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/app-frame/app-frame.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/app-frame

## Public imports

```tsx
import { AppFrame, Page } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

The app's root frame and its scrolling screens. `AppFrame` mounts the safe-area context and the app-root overlay host, pads all four safe-area edges over the theme background, renders the app's top chrome in a banner region and lets its body (a router's Stack) fill the height left. `Page` is one screen inside it: the main region, a scroller with page gutters whose content is capped and centered at a step of the width scale.

Mount `AppFrame` once, inside `ThemeProvider`, at the root of the app. It is the app-root `OverlayProvider` itself, so menus, sheets and toasts render above the whole window and keep clear of the status bar, the Dynamic Island and the home indicator; do not mount a second root host around it. The safe-area context comes from `react-native-safe-area-context` when the app installs it (Expo Router apps already do); without it the frame keeps its layout and the insets resolve to 0.

Each screen renders a `Page`. Its content stacks at the loose rhythm and is capped at `widest` (1152) by default, the reading width of an app page on a desktop window; below the cap it fills the window between its gutters, which is all a phone is. A measure step (`xxxs` through `page`) narrows or widens it, `start` pins it to the leading edge, and `fluid` removes the cap. The page is also an overlay host of its own, so an anchored menu opened in it is framed by the page.

## Usage

The examples below render the frame inside the docs stage, where its parent is the stage instead of the window: the header, the body and the page measure behave as they do at an app's root, and the safe-area insets are 0.

```tsx
<AppFrame header={<Navbar bordered brand="Acme" links={["Overview", "Reports"]} />}>
  <Page>
    <Typography h2>Overview</Typography>
    <Card title="Revenue" description="$48,250 this week" />
  </Page>
</AppFrame>
```

## Variants

### Narrower measure

A form or a settings screen reads better at a narrower step; the page centers it.

```tsx
<AppFrame header={<Navbar bordered brand="Acme" />}>
  <Page md>
    <Typography h2>Profile</Typography>
    <Input label="Display name" defaultValue="Rachel Chen" />
    <Button primary>Save</Button>
  </Page>
</AppFrame>
```

### Pinned to the start

```tsx
<AppFrame header={<Navbar bordered brand="Acme" />}>
  <Page md start>
    <Typography h2>Notifications</Typography>
    <Switch defaultChecked description="A daily summary of your projects.">Email digest</Switch>
  </Page>
</AppFrame>
```

### Overlays in an enclosing viewport host

A screen whose modals must center in the visible viewport, not in the page's full scrolled content, wraps the page in a viewport-measured `OverlayProvider` and passes `inheritOverlays`, so the page is a plain content box and its overlays go to that host.

```tsx
<OverlayProvider viewport>
  <Page inheritOverlays>
    <Typography h2>Billing</Typography>
    <Select label="Plan" options={["Starter", "Team", "Enterprise"]} />
  </Page>
</OverlayProvider>
```

## Do & Don't

### The page measure

**Do**: Name the measure with a step on the page; the content fills it and centers.

```tsx
<Page md>
  <Typography h2>Profile</Typography>
  <Input label="Display name" />
</Page>
```

**Don't**: Hand-roll the scroller and cap a raw View with a number of your own; the width drifts off the shared scale and the page loses its main region and overlay host.

```tsx
<ScrollView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
  <View style={{ width: "100%", maxWidth: 1120, alignSelf: "center", padding: 24 }}>
    <Typography h2>Profile</Typography>
    <Input label="Display name" />
  </View>
</ScrollView>
```

### The app frame

**Do**: Let AppFrame own the safe area, the background and the banner region.

```tsx
<AppFrame header={<Navbar bordered brand="Acme" />}>
  <Page>
    <Typography h2>Overview</Typography>
  </Page>
</AppFrame>
```

**Don't**: Paint the background and wrap the header by hand; the insets, the overlay host and the banner role are each one more thing every app gets wrong.

```tsx
<View style={{ flex: 1, backgroundColor: tokens.background }}>
  <Navbar bordered brand="Acme" />
  <Page>
    <Typography h2>Overview</Typography>
  </Page>
</View>
```

## Accessibility

The header renders inside a `role="banner"` region and each Page is the screen's `role="main"` region, so assistive technology can jump between the app's chrome and its content. The page scroller keeps taps on its controls while the software keyboard is up (`keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"`), so a field's submit button works on the first tap. The frame adds no focus stops of its own.

| children | ReactNode | no |  | The body, typically a router's Stack: it fills the height the header leaves. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the frame. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# AreaChart

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/charts/area-chart/area-chart.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/area-chart

## Public imports

```tsx
import { AreaChart } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Categorical-x series fills: overlapping translucent areas by default, or running-sum bands with `stacked`. Shares the line chart's curve, density, furniture, and scrub-to-inspect axes.

## Usage

```tsx
<AreaChart
  labels={["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug"]}
  series={[
    { label: "Total", values: [120, 138, 151, 149, 168, 184, 197, 212] },
    { label: "Paid", values: [42, 51, 58, 63, 71, 84, 92, 104] }
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Stacked

```tsx
<AreaChart
  stacked
  labels={["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug"]}
  series={[
    { label: "Direct", values: [37, 46, 49, 61, 53, 49, 54, 56] },
    { label: "Search", values: [77, 90, 83, 82, 82, 85, 85, 92] },
    { label: "Social", values: [18, 28, 34, 41, 48, 55, 50, 57] }
  ]}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### Stacking

**Do**: Stack series that are parts of one total, like sessions by device; the top edge is the total and each band is its share.

```tsx
<AreaChart
  stacked
  labels={["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"]}
  series={[
    { label: "Mobile", values: [42, 48, 51, 57, 63, 70] },
    { label: "Desktop", values: [35, 36, 38, 37, 40, 41] },
    { label: "Tablet", values: [8, 9, 9, 10, 11, 11] }
  ]}
/>
```

**Don't**: Stack rates that do not add up; conversion, bounce and churn rates summed into one band draw a total that means nothing.

```tsx
<AreaChart
  stacked
  labels={["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"]}
  series={[
    { label: "Conversion rate", values: [3.1, 3.4, 3.2, 3.8, 4.0, 4.2] },
    { label: "Bounce rate", values: [41, 39, 40, 37, 36, 35] },
    { label: "Churn rate", values: [2.4, 2.2, 2.5, 2.1, 2.0, 1.9] }
  ]}
/>
```

# Autocomplete

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/autocomplete/autocomplete.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/autocomplete

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Autocomplete } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Text input + dropdown: searchable single-select.

Pass `label` (and `required`) to name the field:
iOS and web render the label
above the field, while Android floats the Material 3 in-container label once the
list opens or a value fills the field. On Android the field grows with the
user's text size, and a label longer than the field truncates on one line clear
of the toggle while the field's accessible name stays the whole label.
The required
star is decorative: a screen reader hears the field as required,
from
`aria-required` on the web and from its name ("Assigned to, required") on iOS and
Android.
The field fills the parent it is given; a
step of its own (`xs`, `lg`, …, with `start` to pin it to the leading edge) or a
Container step sets its measure.

On web the field is the Canvas v4 search field: 40px tall (32 small, 48 large) on
the sunken fill behind the `field-border` hairline, a leading 16px search glyph, a
400 14px value (13 small) and a 15px chevrons-up-down 10px from its end. The
pointer darkens the edge to the subtle ink, and focus rings it in the accent with a
4px halo. The suggestions are a card 6px under the field with a 4px inset and 34px
rows; the typed letters are marked in each suggestion on the accent's soft wash, and
the chosen suggestion sits on the `muted` wash.
iOS ships no combo box, so it draws
the same field and card at the iOS corners.
Android keeps the Material 3 exposed
dropdown: the filled field with its active indicator and drop-down triangle, and the
Material menu whose active and chosen rows take the state layer.

In glass mode the suggestion list is a dense-layer glass card under the field (or
above it when it fits there); the field, its caret and its toggle stay in place,
and picking a suggestion commits the value at once. Solid mode paints the skin's
own list.

Arrow Down and Arrow Up open the list and highlight an option while focus stays in the text field. Navigation stops at the first and last matches. Home and End jump to those limits once an option is highlighted; otherwise they retain their text-editing behavior. Enter chooses the highlighted option, Escape closes the list without changing the query, and Tab closes it while moving focus. Typing resets the highlight. Confirming an input-method candidate does not select an option or submit a surrounding Form.

Use `value` with `onValueChange` to control the selection, and use `""` for a controlled empty value. The callback reports selections and clearing the field. `onSelect` remains a selection-only notification. The independent `query`/`onQueryChange` pair controls filtering; choosing an option resets the query to `""`.

The disclosure button has a real target of at least 24px on web, 44pt on iOS, and 48dp on Android.
The small iOS field keeps a 44pt height so its touch target fits inside the field; its typography remains compact.

An option can carry a short `detail` (a version, a platform, a count): pass
`{ label, detail }` objects in place of strings, and the detail sits at the row's end
in the 11px mono face in the subtle ink.
Android sets it in the row's type and muted ink.
The label is what the query matches and what `value` holds; the row is announced as
"label, detail".

## Usage

```tsx
<Autocomplete label="Assigned to" placeholder="Search a person…" options={["Ada Lovelace", "Grace Hopper", "Kira Tanaka", "Liang Bao", "Noor Park"]} />
```

  )}
</Stateful>

## Do & Don't

### When to use

**Do** — A plain select for short, fixed lists; reserve the autocomplete for long, searchable ones.

```tsx
<Select label="Size" options={["Small", "Medium", "Large"]} placeholder="Select a size" />
```

**Don't** — Type or click: a search field for three fixed options is overhead with nothing to filter.

```tsx
<Autocomplete label="Size" options={["Small", "Medium", "Large"]} placeholder="Search…" />
```

### Filtering

**Do** — Type a few letters: the list narrows as you go, so a long list stays usable.

```tsx
<Autocomplete label="Assigned to" options={[
    "Wade Cooper",
    "Arlene Mccoy",
    "Devon Webb",
    "Tom Cook",
    "Tanya Fox",
    "Hellen Schmidt"
  ]} defaultQuery="co" />
```

**Don't** — Try typing: a plain dropdown wearing a search placeholder ignores every keystroke, so a long list stays as long as it started.

```tsx
<Select label="Assigned to" options={[
    "Wade Cooper",
    "Arlene Mccoy",
    "Devon Webb",
    "Tom Cook",
    "Tanya Fox",
    "Hellen Schmidt"
  ]} placeholder="Search a person…" />
```

### Selection

**Do** — Click an option: it fills the input and stays marked as selected.

```tsx
<Autocomplete label="Assigned to" options={["Wade Cooper", "Arlene Mccoy", "Devon Webb", "Tom Cook"]} defaultValue="Devon Webb" />
```

**Don't** — Click an option: the field is pinned to an empty `value`, so the list closes on nothing and you can't tell what you picked.

```tsx
<Autocomplete label="Assigned to" options={["Wade Cooper", "Arlene Mccoy", "Devon Webb", "Tom Cook"]} value="" placeholder="Pick a person…" />
```

### With label

**Do** — A persistent label keeps the field named after a selection has filled the input.

```tsx
<Autocomplete label="Assigned to" options={["Wade Cooper", "Arlene Mccoy", "Devon Webb"]} defaultValue="Devon Webb" />
```

**Don't** — Once a value replaces the placeholder, an unlabeled field has nothing left to name it.

```tsx
<Autocomplete options={["Wade Cooper", "Arlene Mccoy", "Devon Webb"]} defaultValue="Devon Webb" />
```

### With helper text

**Do** — A short placeholder plus persistent helper text keeps the rule visible while you type.

```tsx
<Autocomplete label="Assigned to" options={["Wade Cooper", "Arlene Mccoy", "Devon Webb"]} placeholder="Search a person…" helperText="Deactivated users are hidden from the list." />
```

**Don't** — Type a letter: guidance crammed into the placeholder vanishes the moment you start.

```tsx
<Autocomplete label="Assigned to" options={["Wade Cooper", "Arlene Mccoy", "Devon Webb"]} placeholder="Pick an active teammate; deactivated users are hidden" />
```

### Disabled

**Do** — Show the locked value and say why it's fixed, so disabled reads as a settled choice.

```tsx
<Autocomplete label="Assigned to" options={["Wade Cooper", "Arlene Mccoy", "Devon Webb"]} defaultValue="Devon Webb" disabled helperText="Set by the project owner and can't be changed here." />
```

**Don't** — An empty, dimmed field with no value reads as broken, not as intentionally locked.

```tsx
<Autocomplete label="Assigned to" options={["Wade Cooper", "Arlene Mccoy", "Devon Webb"]} disabled placeholder="Search a person…" />
```

# Avatar

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/avatar/avatar.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/avatar

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup, AvatarMenu } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A photo when the account has one, falling back to one or two initials on an identity disc: the name resolves to one of ten hues (or `hue` picks one), and the disc is that hue's soft wash under initials in the same hue, so one person keeps one colour on every platform and stays distinct in a stack or list. The initials sit at weight 600, 38% of the disc, and their ink is held to 4.5:1 on the wash in both schemes.

Like a photo, the disc is identity content: it keeps its colours under glass, where only the neutral tile of an avatar with no name or initials takes the control material. `AvatarMenu` builds the signed-in account control on the same circle: one capsule trigger carrying the avatar, the name, and the email, opening the account menu under that same identity.

Argus identity sizes are available as `annotation` (16), `compact` (30), `account`
(32), `row` (36), `person` (38), `profile` (44), `detail` (52), `hero` (58),
`featured` (60), and `spotlight` (74), in that precedence order. These retain their
reference initials metrics, including the existing 9px annotation glyph.

`hue` selects a stage identity independently of its name. `whiteInk` preserves
white reference initials; `bold` uses the 700 weight. `sheen`, `mediumSheen`, and
`strongSheen` add the 2, 2.5 and 3px conic ring (strongest wins). `inverse` is the
translucent white identity disc, `orchid` the account gradient, and `glow` its
selected account ring. These reference discs keep the identity gradient. On the four
stock sizes, `glow` is a 2px gap in the page colour inside the accent's soft glow, and
`ring` stays the separator ring a stack draws between discs.

## Usage

```tsx
<Avatar name="AO" />
```

## Variants

### Brand mark

```tsx
<Avatar logo whiteInk initials="A" />
```

`logo` retains the original 30px Argus mark, nine-pixel corners, action-to-ring
gradient, 14px extra-bold initial, and selection-colored drop shadow.


### Photo

```tsx
<Avatar src="/rachel-chen.jpg" name="RC" />
```

### Identity colours

Each name resolves to one of ten hues through a stable hash, so the same person gets the same disc in every session and on every platform, and a list of people spreads across the set. The hue follows `name` when one is set, else the initials, so pass the full name: two people who share initials then usually get different discs.

```tsx
<Row snug wrap>
  <Avatar name="Ada Ito" />
  <Avatar name="Rachel Tanaka" />
  <Avatar name="Liang Kim" />
  <Avatar name="Kira Okafor" />
  <Avatar name="Marcus Singh" />
  <Avatar name="Noor Novak" />
  <Avatar name="Sofia Bao" />
  <Avatar name="Theo Lovelace" />
  <Avatar name="Omar Moreau" />
  <Avatar name="Priya Haddad" />
</Row>
```

### Sizes

Four steps: `tiny` (20px), `small` (28px), the default 40px row avatar, and `large` (56px). The initials take 38% of the disc (11, 15 and 21px), and 10px on `tiny`, the kit's smallest type. `rounded` squares the disc with corners at 28% of its size. `small` is the disc `AvatarMenu` builds its capsule around, so a standalone small avatar and the one inside a pill are the same circle. Precedence when several are passed: `tiny` beats `small` beats `large`.

```tsx
<Row relaxed alignCenter>
  <Avatar tiny name="NP" />
  <Avatar small name="AL" />
  <Avatar name="MA" />
  <Avatar large name="RC" />
</Row>
```

### Rounded

```tsx
<Avatar rounded name="LB" />
```

### Online

`online` marks presence: the success dot in a ring of the card at the disc's lower trailing edge. The dot is decorative, so say the presence in the label where it matters.

```tsx
<Avatar online name="Rachel Chen" accessibilityLabel="Rachel Chen, online" />
```

### Ring outline

```tsx
<Avatar ring name="AO" />
```

### Stacked

```tsx
<AvatarGroup max={3}>
  <Avatar name="Rachel Chen" />
  <Avatar name="Liang Bao" />
  <Avatar name="Marcus Allen" />
  <Avatar name="Kira Tran" />

```

### Topbar

A lone avatar as the account trigger: the Dropdown makes the disc its press target, so tapping it opens the account menu, no email or chevron needed.

```tsx
<Dropdown items={[{ label: "Your profile" }, { label: "Sign out" }]}>
  <Avatar small name="MA" />
</Dropdown>
```

### Argus account menu

`account` preserves the original Argus 32px orchid disc, glow, name and role
metrics, and compact menu. `triggerLabel` names the one press target;
`menuLabel` independently names its menu. Bounds use `menuWidth` and `maxHeight`.

```tsx
<AvatarMenu account name="Bobby" email="Principal Engineer" initials="B" triggerLabel="Viewing as Principal Engineer. Switch role" menuLabel="View as role" menuWidth={300} maxHeight={420} items={[{ label: "Principal Engineer", selected: true }, { label: "Architect" }]} />
```

### Account menu

Built on Dropdown, so in glass mode the menu is Dropdown's dense-layer glass card
under the capsule, which keeps its place, its press and its accessible name
throughout.

The whole account control in one component. `AvatarMenu` renders a single capsule trigger (the avatar in the viewer's violet glow ring, the name over the muted email, a chevron) and the account menu itself, with `name` and `email` repeated as the menu's own identity header. One press target covers the capsule, so nothing beside it has to be wired up. The capsule is the hand-off's identity pill on every platform: a hairline edge round the popover fill at rest, the accent fill under the pointer and while its menu is open; the menu is each platform's own Dropdown.

```tsx
<AvatarMenu
  name="Rachel Chen"
  email="rachel.chen@example.com"
  src="/rachel-chen.jpg"
  items={[
    { label: "Profile", icon: "user" },
    { label: "Settings", icon: "settings" },
    { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut", destructive: true, separatorBefore: true }
  ]}
/>
```

### Menu specimen

`inline` draws the menu open and in flow under the capsule rather than floating over the page, for a page that shows the menu itself. Rows still fire `onSelect`; nothing dismisses it.

```tsx
<AvatarMenu
  inline
  name="Rachel Chen"
  email="rachel.chen@example.com"
  menuWidth={240}
  items={[
    { label: "Profile", icon: "user" },
    { label: "Settings", icon: "settings" },
    { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut", destructive: true, separatorBefore: true }
  ]}
/>
```

### Compact menu

`compact` drops the name block for a bar with no room for it, leaving the 28px avatar alone. The identity still travels with the menu, so the name and email head the rows the moment it opens. A topbar parks the pill at the trailing edge, so the menu hangs from that edge by default; `alignStart` moves it to the leading edge for a pill that sits at the start of a bar.

```tsx
<AvatarMenu
  compact
  name="Marcus Allen"
  email="admin@example.com"
  src="/marcus-allen.jpg"
  items={[
    { label: "Profile", icon: "user" },
    { label: "Settings", icon: "settings" },
    { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut", destructive: true, separatorBefore: true }
  ]}
/>
```

### Menu alignment

The menu hangs from the pill's trailing edge by default, the edge a topbar parks the account control against and the only one a right-parked trigger can open from without running off the surface. `alignStart` swings it to the leading edge for a pill that sits at the start of a bar, and `alignEnd` spells the default out. Both are logical, so a right-to-left locale mirrors them. Press each pill to see which edge its menu meets.

```tsx
<Row between>
  <AvatarMenu
    compact
    alignStart
    name="Liang Bao"
    email="liang.bao@example.com"
    src="/liang-bao.jpg"
    items={[
      { label: "Profile", icon: "user" },
      { label: "Settings", icon: "settings" },
      { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut", destructive: true, separatorBefore: true }
    ]}
  />
  <AvatarMenu
    compact
    alignEnd
    name="Kira Tanaka"
    email="kira.tanaka@example.com"
    src="/kira-tanaka.jpg"
    items={[
      { label: "Profile", icon: "user" },
      { label: "Settings", icon: "settings" },
      { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut", destructive: true, separatorBefore: true }
    ]}
  />
</Row>
```

### Disabled menu

`disabled` takes the whole pill out of service: it dims to the platform's disabled treatment, the press is a no-op, the menu never opens, and the button announces itself disabled before anyone reaches for it. Reach for it while the session is still resolving, not to park a menu whose rows simply have nothing to offer.

```tsx
<AvatarMenu
  disabled
  name="Ada Lovelace"
  email="ada.lovelace@example.com"
  src="/ada-lovelace.jpg"
  items={[
    { label: "Profile", icon: "user" },
    { label: "Settings", icon: "settings" },
    { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut", destructive: true, separatorBefore: true }
  ]}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### Single

**Do** — One or two initials, about a third of the disc.

```tsx
<Avatar name="AO" />
```

**Don't** — Cramming in a full set of initials shrinks the type and crowds the circle.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexShrink: 0, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", overflow: "hidden", backgroundColor: tokens.muted, width: 40, height: 40, borderRadius: 9999 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontWeight: "500", color: tokens["muted-foreground"], fontSize: 12 }}>ABCD</Text>
</View>
```

### Stacked

**Do** — Cap the stack with `max` and let AvatarGroup summarize the rest as a +N count.

```tsx
<AvatarGroup small max={4} total={16}>
  <Avatar name="Ada Okafor" />
  <Avatar name="Rachel Chen" />
  <Avatar name="Liang Bao" />
  <Avatar name="Kira Tran" />
</AvatarGroup>
```

**Don't** — An unbounded stack (no `max`) runs off the row and stops being scannable.

```tsx
<AvatarGroup small>
  <Avatar name="AO" />
  <Avatar name="RC" />
  <Avatar name="LB" />
  <Avatar name="KT" />
  <Avatar name="JD" />
  <Avatar name="MA" />
  <Avatar name="AL" />
  <Avatar name="SK" />
</AvatarGroup>
```

### Topbar account menu

**Do**: Press the avatar: `AvatarMenu compact` makes it a real trigger in a bar with no room for a name, and the account is named in the menu header the moment the menu opens.

```tsx
<AvatarMenu compact name="Marcus Allen" email="admin@example.com" src="/marcus-allen.jpg" items={[
    { label: "Profile", icon: "user" },
    { label: "Settings", icon: "settings", shortcut: "⌘," },
    { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut", destructive: true, separatorBefore: true }
  ]} />
```

**Don't** — A bare avatar with no Dropdown around it is decorative, not a trigger, and opens nothing.

```tsx
<Avatar small src="/marcus-allen.jpg" name="MA" />
```

### Identity

**Do** — Name primary; email muted and secondary.

```tsx
<MediaObject center src="/rachel-chen.jpg" title="Rachel Chen" description="rachel.chen@example.com" />
```

**Don't** — Equal weight on the name and email flattens the hierarchy.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 16 }}>
  <Avatar src="/rachel-chen.jpg" name="RC" />
  <View>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens.foreground }}>Rachel Chen</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens.foreground }}>rachel.chen@example.com</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Menu header

**Do** — Keep one consistent circular avatar shape across contexts.

```tsx
<MediaObject compact center src="/ada-lovelace.jpg" title="Ada Lovelace" description="admin@example.com" />
```

**Don't** — Squaring the avatar here clashes with the circular avatars everywhere else.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 12 }}>
  <Avatar rounded src="/ada-lovelace.jpg" name="AL" />
  <View>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens.foreground }}>Ada Lovelace</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>admin@example.com</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Account identity

**Do**: Press the pill: `name` and `email` go through AvatarMenu, which owns both lines, the shared press target, and the identity header on the menu it opens.

```tsx
<AvatarMenu name="Rachel Chen" email="rachel.chen@example.com" src="/rachel-chen.jpg" items={[
    { label: "Profile", icon: "user" },
    { label: "Settings", icon: "settings", shortcut: "⌘," },
    { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut", destructive: true, separatorBefore: true }
  ]} />
```

**Don't**: Hand-composing the identity beside the trigger drifts from the pill's type and spacing, and the menu that opens names no account at all.

```tsx
<Dropdown items={[
    { label: "Profile", icon: "user" },
    { label: "Settings", icon: "settings" },
    { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut", separatorBefore: true }
  ]}>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
    <Avatar small src="/rachel-chen.jpg" name="RC" />
    <View>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens.foreground }}>Rachel Chen</Text>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens.foreground }}>rachel.chen@example.com</Text>
    </View>
    <Icon chevronDown muted size={12} />
  </View>
</Dropdown>
```

### Sign out

**Do**: Open the menu: keep the destructive sign out last and behind a separator, a reach away from the rows people press every day.

```tsx
<AvatarMenu name="Kira Tanaka" email="kira.tanaka@example.com" src="/kira-tanaka.jpg" items={[
    { label: "Profile", icon: "user" },
    { label: "Billing", icon: "creditCard" },
    { label: "Settings", icon: "settings", shortcut: "⌘," },
    { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut", destructive: true, separatorBefore: true }
  ]} />
```

**Don't**: Sign out buried mid-list, in the same tone as its neighbours, is one slip away on the path to Settings.

```tsx
<AvatarMenu name="Kira Tanaka" email="kira.tanaka@example.com" src="/kira-tanaka.jpg" items={[
    { label: "Profile", icon: "user" },
    { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut" },
    { label: "Billing", icon: "creditCard" },
    { label: "Settings", icon: "settings", shortcut: "⌘," }
  ]} />
```

### Compact trigger

**Do**: Press the pill: where the row has space, the full form says who is signed in before anything is opened.

```tsx
<AvatarMenu name="Noor Park" email="noor.park@example.com" src="/noor-park.jpg" items={[
    { label: "Profile", icon: "user" },
    { label: "Settings", icon: "settings", shortcut: "⌘," },
    { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut", destructive: true, separatorBefore: true }
  ]} />
```

**Don't**: `compact` on a roomy page that names the account nowhere else hides who is signed in behind a press, to save room the row never needed.

```tsx
<AvatarMenu compact name="Noor Park" email="noor.park@example.com" src="/noor-park.jpg" items={[
    { label: "Profile", icon: "user" },
    { label: "Settings", icon: "settings", shortcut: "⌘," },
    { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut", destructive: true, separatorBefore: true }
  ]} />
```

### Unavailable account

**Do**: `disabled` on the pill itself: the whole trigger dims, the press is inert, and the button announces itself disabled instead of inviting a press that goes nowhere.

```tsx
<AvatarMenu disabled name="Ada Lovelace" email="ada.lovelace@example.com" src="/ada-lovelace.jpg" items={[
    { label: "Profile", icon: "user" },
    { label: "Settings", icon: "settings", shortcut: "⌘," },
    { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut", destructive: true, separatorBefore: true }
  ]} />
```

**Don't**: Disabling every row instead leaves the pill live: it still opens, onto a menu where nothing can be pressed.

```tsx
<AvatarMenu name="Ada Lovelace" email="ada.lovelace@example.com" src="/ada-lovelace.jpg" items={[
    { label: "Profile", icon: "user", disabled: true },
    { label: "Settings", icon: "settings", shortcut: "⌘,", disabled: true },
    { label: "Sign out", icon: "logOut", destructive: true, separatorBefore: true, disabled: true }
  ]} />
```

## Supported props

### AvatarMenuProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| account | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Original Argus account control with a 32px orchid disc and compact role menu. |
| triggerLabel | string \| undefined | no |  | Explicit name for the trigger. |
| menuLabel | string \| undefined | no |  | Menu heading and accessible name, independent of the account's identity lines. |
| menuWidth | number \| undefined | no |  |  |
| maxHeight | number \| undefined | no |  |  |
| name | string \| undefined | no |  | The account holder's full name: the pill's first line, the avatar's initials fallback and colour identity, and the menu header's title. |
| email | string \| undefined | no |  | The secondary line under the name in the pill, and the menu header's description (typically the account's email address). |
| src | string \| undefined | no |  | The account photo. Falls back to the initials exactly like `Avatar`. |
| initials | string \| undefined | no |  | Ready-made initials for the avatar, used verbatim when there is no photo. |
| items | DropdownItem[] | yes |  | The menu rows, top to bottom. Same rows as `Dropdown` (icon, shortcut, destructive, disabled, separatorBefore). |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Avatar and chevron only, no name block: the topbar form of the pill. |
| alignStart | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Hang the menu from the pill's LEADING edge instead of its trailing one. |
| alignEnd | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The default, spelled out: the menu's trailing edge meets the pill's. |
| disabled | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Dimmed, non-opening pill: the menu never opens and the press is inert. |
| inline | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Draw the menu open and in flow under the pill instead of floating it over the page, a specimen of the account menu (Dropdown's `inline`): the pill reads as open and its press is inert, a row still fires `onSelect`, and `open` / `onOpenChange` have no effect. |
| open | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Controlled open state. Omit for uncontrolled (the pill opens/closes it). |
| onOpenChange | ((open: boolean) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when the open state changes (pill press, row select, dismissal). |
| onSelect | ((item: DropdownItem, index: number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired with the selected row and its index when a menu row is pressed. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Outer layout composition only (placement within a parent), never a restyle hook. |
