<!-- Source: https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/components/badge.md -->
# Badge

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/badge/badge.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/badge

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Badge, BadgeGroup } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Two families on one Badge component, picked by boolean props. The metadata badge labels a schema, role, or tag: with no tone it is the accent's soft pill, and the tones give `default` the solid call-to-action pill, `secondary` the quiet surface pill, `outline` a hairline pill and `destructive` the soft red pill; add `mono` for token names. A status tone (`success`, `warning`, `error`, `info`, `neutral`) paints the pill in that tone's wash and ink and leads it with a dot. The status badge (`status`) has no pill: a dot in the tone's color, ringed in its wash, beside a muted label, for live state like active, pending, or failed.

The tone colors come from `statusColors`, the helper every toned surface in the kit reads, so a warning badge and a warning alert are the same state, and every ink is the solved text role that keeps 4.5:1 on its wash.

`contrast` is the most prominent neutral: the scheme's ink (`foreground`) as the fill under the page colour as the label (under glass, the ink at the dense alpha, as the Tooltip bubble's). `dashed` is the placeholder outline: no fill inside a dashed `field-border` edge, the label in the second ink.

If more than one tone is passed, Badge resolves the highest-precedence one: `default` > `contrast` > `destructive` > `secondary` > `outline` > `dashed` for metadata (the accent's soft pill when none is passed), and `success` > `error` > `warning` > `info` > `neutral` for status (`neutral` when none is passed). The metadata tones win over a status tone's colors; the status tone's dot stays.

`cyan` and `mint` paint a metadata pill in a fixed series hue, the same whatever the palette (the hand-off's `--cyan` and `--mint`, the `chart-2` and `chart-3` tokens): the hue's 16% wash under its ink, solved to 4.5:1 on the wash, with no dot. They sit after the status tones in precedence (`success` > `warning` > `error` > `info` > `cyan` > `mint`), so a section can name three tiers mint, cyan and the accent and keep them apart under every palette.

Lay out a series of badges with `BadgeGroup`, a wrapping row that owns the gap (`tight` 4 / `compact` 6 / `snug` 8 / `cozy` 12, default `compact`, the hand-off's 6; the largest gap passed wins: `cozy` > `snug` > `compact` > `tight`) and centers its badges, so a call site never hand-rolls a flex row around them. Give it an `accessibilityLabel` (say, "Rachel Chen's roles") and it is announced as a named group that keeps its badges' text; without one it is a plain row.

The pill is 22 px tall with a 12 px label; `small` is 18 px with an 11 px label and `large` 26 px. `count` is the small pill with the heavier label, `navigationCount` the small solid count, and `reference` a linked key at the 6 px key corner in the code face, underlined, with an arrow when it has an `href`. `token` is a code token chip, the 22 px pill under the small 11 px label in the code face, for a role, a state or an attribute name listed beside its term; `tier` is a tier tag, a 24 px pill with a 10 px inset under an 11 px mono label in caps on its own line, the tag that names a component's tier beside its title, in whichever tone the tier takes. `tiny` is the 18 px pill under a 10 px label on its own line, at the regular weight even when `solid` (a navigation row's "New" tag). The metric precedence is `notification` > `marker` > `disc` > `step` > `reference` > `navigationCount` > `count` > `tier` > `band` > `tick` > `token` > `tiny` > `small`. `primary` and `action` take the accent's wash, `soft` names the soft wash every toned pill already has, `neutralFill` fills with the border color, `foreground` overrides the label ink, `dot` adds the leading dot without a status tone, and `inverse` and `solid` supply branded surfaces. `uppercase` tracks caps; `start` pins a badge in a host layout; `truncate` keeps the label on one line and lets the pill shrink in a tight row, ending the label with an ellipsis instead of overflowing its host.

`notification` is a destructive count: a 20 px pill with a 600 11 px label, soft by default and solid with `solid`, set off from the page by a ring of the background; `action` adds a halo of the destructive wash. Button carries its own count when passed a `count`.

`signal` is the original standalone 10px status marker. It uses the existing
status-tone precedence and announces its supplied status label.

`marker` is an anatomy figure's numbered disc: a 22 px pill with no inset, its number 600 11 px in the code face on the accent (the solid call-to-action fill under its ink), set off from the stage by a 3 px ring of the stage well's fill (`surface-sunken`) and a drop shadow, the way the component page's Anatomy section numbers a specimen's parts. It wins over the other metrics but `notification`.

`disc` is the same 22 px numbered disc in a legend: the marker's disc and 600 11 px code-face number, in the tone axis's fill (`default` the solid accent for a part the figure draws, `secondary` the quiet surface for one it does not) with no ring and no shadow, the way the Anatomy legend numbers its rows. It sits below `marker` in precedence and above the pills.

`tier` is the tier pill beside a page title (Atom, Molecule, Organism): 24 px tall with a 10 px inset and a 500 11 px label on its own line, tracked in caps with `uppercase` and in the code face with `mono`, in the tone axis's fill. It sits above `small` in precedence.

`band` is a group band's pill, the "pick one" beside an axis's title in a props table: 20 px tall with a 7 px inset, no border, and a 500 11 px label, in the code face with `mono`, in the tone axis's fill (the accent's soft pill with none). It sits between `tier` and `small` in precedence; like `tick`, it never leads with a tone's dot.

`tick` is a ruler tick's readout: 20 px tall with an 8 px inset, no border and a 500 10 px label in the code face on the pill's own 20 px line, usually `contrast` (the Layout page's "this window" pill under its marker).

`step` is a numbered step mark: a 32 px square at the 10 px step corner with its number 600 13 px in the code face, centred, in the tone axis's fill: `default` the solid accent with the accent's glow beneath, none the accent's soft wash, `secondary` the quiet surface inside the `field-border` edge in the second ink. Pass it as a MediaObject's `icon` with `bareIcon` to number a list of steps.

`keyCorners` sets any pill at the key cap's 6 px corner in place of the round one (the corner axis has this one member); `reference` and `step` keep their own corners.

## Usage

```tsx
<Badge>admin</Badge>
```

## Variants

### Notification count

```tsx
<Badge notification solid action>3</Badge>
```


### Solid

```tsx
<Badge default>admin</Badge>
```

### Outline

```tsx
<Badge outline>admin</Badge>
```

### Destructive

```tsx
<Badge destructive>admin</Badge>
```

### Mono (token / event names)

```tsx
<Badge mono>refresh_token</Badge>
```

### Status

```tsx
<Badge status>pending</Badge>
```

### Status tones

```tsx
<BadgeGroup>
  <Badge status success>active</Badge>
  <Badge status warning>degraded</Badge>
  <Badge status error>failed</Badge>
  <Badge status info>syncing</Badge>
  <Badge status neutral>archived</Badge>
</BadgeGroup>
```

### Bare dot

`dot` with no label is the 8 px dot alone, in the tone's ink with no pill: a marker beside
text that names it. Give it an `accessibilityLabel` when it carries meaning of its own.

```tsx
<Row snug alignCenter>
  <Badge dot />
  <Typography small>Live</Typography>
</Row>
```

### Hue tones

```tsx
<BadgeGroup>
  <Badge mint mono>compact</Badge>
  <Badge cyan mono>regular</Badge>
  <Badge mono>wide</Badge>
</BadgeGroup>
```

### Group

```tsx
<BadgeGroup>
  <Badge>employee</Badge>
  <Badge>engineering</Badge>
  <Badge status success>active</Badge>
</BadgeGroup>
```

### Reference link

```tsx
<Badge reference href="https://example.com">CORE-1842</Badge>
```

### Anatomy marker

```tsx
<BadgeGroup>
  <Badge marker>1</Badge>
  <Badge marker>2</Badge>
  <Badge marker>3</Badge>
</BadgeGroup>
```

### Legend disc

```tsx
<BadgeGroup>

```

### Tier pill

```tsx

</BadgeGroup>
```

### Band pill

```tsx
<BadgeGroup>
  <Badge band mono>pick one</Badge>
  <Badge band mono secondary>stacks</Badge>
</BadgeGroup>
```

### Contrast tick

```tsx
<Badge tick contrast>this window · 1440px</Badge>
```

### Step marks

```tsx
<BadgeGroup>
  <Badge step default>1</Badge>
  <Badge step>2</Badge>
  <Badge step secondary>3</Badge>
</BadgeGroup>
```

### Key corners and the dashed outline

```tsx
<BadgeGroup>
  <Badge band mono keyCorners>fill</Badge>
  <Badge band mono keyCorners cyan>hug</Badge>
  <Badge mono keyCorners dashed>View</Badge>
  <Badge mono keyCorners dashed>ScrollView</Badge>
</BadgeGroup>
```

### Token chips

```tsx
<BadgeGroup tight>
  <Badge token>busy</Badge>
  <Badge token>disabled</Badge>
  <Badge token>aria-expanded</Badge>
</BadgeGroup>
```

## Do & Don't

### Grouping

**Do**: Reach for `BadgeGroup` to lay out a series of badges; it owns the wrap, the gap, and the vertical centering.

```tsx
<BadgeGroup>
  <Badge secondary>employee</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>engineering</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>remote</Badge>
</BadgeGroup>
```

**Don't**: Hand-rolling a flex row for a badge series re-invents the gap and wrap and drifts from the kit's spacing scale.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
  <Badge secondary>employee</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>engineering</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>remote</Badge>
</View>
```

### Metadata badge

**Do**: Neutral tags for metadata; reserve color and the status-badge dot for live state.

```tsx
<BadgeGroup>
  <Badge secondary>employee</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>engineering</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>remote</Badge>
  <Badge status success>active</Badge>
</BadgeGroup>
```

**Don't**: Borrowing status colors for plain metadata reads as severity that isn't there; a red tag looks like an error.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "center", gap: 6 }}>
  <Badge default>employee</Badge>
  <Badge destructive>engineering</Badge>
  <Badge default>remote</Badge>
  <Badge destructive>active</Badge>
</View>
```

### Status badge

**Do**: Always pair the dot with a word: active, pending, failed.

```tsx
<Badge status error>Failed</Badge>
```

**Don't**: A bare colored dot isn't a label and fails for color-blind users.

```tsx
<Badge status error />
```

### Identity row

**Do**: Show only the one or two badges relevant to this view.

```tsx
<Row wrap alignCenter snug>
  <Typography lead semibold>Rachel Chen</Typography>
  <BadgeGroup>
    <Badge status success>active</Badge>
    <Badge secondary>employee</Badge>
  </BadgeGroup>
</Row>
```

**Don't**: A wall of badges after a name buries the one that matters.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 15, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens.foreground }}>Rachel Chen</Text>
  <Badge status success>active</Badge>
  <Badge status info>Verified</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>employee</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>engineering</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>remote</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>admin</Badge>
</View>
```

### Token / code badge

**Do**: Use the mono variant for tokens, scopes, and event names.

```tsx
<BadgeGroup tight>
  <Badge secondary mono>authorization_code</Badge>
  <Badge secondary mono>refresh_token</Badge>
  <Badge secondary mono>client_credentials</Badge>
</BadgeGroup>
```

**Don't**: Proportional type makes identifiers hard to scan and compare.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", gap: 4 }}>
  <Badge secondary>authorization_code</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>refresh_token</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>client_credentials</Badge>
</View>
```

### Default variant

**Do**: Reserve the default fill for the single tag you want noticed first; keep the rest secondary.

```tsx
<BadgeGroup>
  <Badge default>admin</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>engineering</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>remote</Badge>
</BadgeGroup>
```

**Don't**: The solid call-to-action fill is the loudest badge; using it for every tag makes the whole row shout and nothing leads.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "center", gap: 6 }}>
  <Badge default>employee</Badge>
  <Badge default>engineering</Badge>
  <Badge default>remote</Badge>
  <Badge default>admin</Badge>
</View>
```

### Secondary variant

**Do**: Keep secondary for static metadata (role, team) and switch to the status-badge for anything live.

```tsx
<BadgeGroup>
  <Badge secondary>employee</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>engineering</Badge>
  <Badge status success>active</Badge>
</BadgeGroup>
```

**Don't**: A muted gray pill reads as static metadata, so live state shown as a secondary badge looks inert and goes unnoticed.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "center", gap: 6 }}>
  <Badge secondary>active</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>pending</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>failed</Badge>
</View>
```

### Outline variant

**Do**: Use outline on a plain surface where the quiet border has contrast, for low-priority secondary tags.

```tsx
<Card padded>
  <BadgeGroup>
    <Badge outline>draft</Badge>
    <Badge outline>internal</Badge>
  </BadgeGroup>
</Card>
```

**Don't**: The thin border is the whole badge; on a colored or busy surface it disappears and the label floats unboxed.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "center", gap: 6, borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: tokens.primary, padding: 12 }}>
  <Badge outline>draft</Badge>
  <Badge outline>internal</Badge>
</View>
```

### Destructive variant

**Do**: Reserve destructive for genuinely destructive or error semantics like revoked or banned.

```tsx
<BadgeGroup>
  <Badge destructive>Revoked</Badge>
  <Badge destructive>Banned</Badge>
  <Badge secondary>marketing</Badge>
</BadgeGroup>
```

**Don't**: Solid red signals error or danger, so using it to color-code neutral categories raises a false alarm.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "center", gap: 6 }}>
  <Badge destructive>marketing</Badge>
  <Badge destructive>finance</Badge>
  <Badge destructive>legal</Badge>
</View>
```

# BarList

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/charts/bar-list/bar-list.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/bar-list

## Public imports

```tsx
import { BarList } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Ranked label and value rows: each row is a proportional tone wash behind a truncating label, with a right-aligned mono value and an optional delta.

Bars size against the largest row by default (the ranking idiom); `share` sizes them against the sum of the rows and appends percent readouts (the composition idiom). Rows become drill-in buttons with `onPressItem`. For comparing magnitudes on a shared axis without deltas or shares, reach for the bar `Chart` and its `horizontal` mode instead.

## Usage

```tsx
<BarList
  title="Top pages"
  items={[
    { label: "/pricing", value: 18400, delta: "+12%" },
    { label: "/docs", value: 12100, delta: "+4%" },
    { label: "/blog/launch", value: 8700, delta: "-2%", down: true },
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Share of total

```tsx
<BarList
  share
  items={[
    { label: "google", value: 412 },
    { label: "email", value: 318 },
    { label: "github", value: 142 },
  ]}
/>
```

### Drill-in rows

```tsx
<BarList
  onPressItem={() => {}}
  items={[
    { label: "news.ycombinator.com", value: 4210 },
    { label: "reddit.com", value: 2380 },
    { label: "linkedin.com", value: 1240 },
  ]}
/>
```

### Plain, inside a card

```tsx
<Card>
  <BarList
    plain
    items={[
      { label: "Deploys", value: 42 },
      { label: "Rollbacks", value: 3 },
      { label: "Incidents", value: 1 },
    ]}
  />
</Card>
```

## Do & Don't

### BarList

**Do** - Let the component own the whole row anatomy: label, value, delta, and the proportional wash.

```tsx
<BarList
title="Top pages"
items={[
  { label: "/pricing", value: 18400, delta: "+12%" },
  { label: "/docs", value: 12100, delta: "-4%", down: true },
]}
/>
```

**Don't** - A hand-rolled row of Text and colored Views splits the anatomy, drifts from the type scale, and hides its share from assistive tech.

```tsx
<View style={{ borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.card, padding: 20, maxWidth: 420, gap: 8 }}>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", justifyContent: "space-between" }}>
    <Text>/pricing</Text>
    <Text>18.4k</Text>
  </View>
  <View style={{ height: 3, backgroundColor: tokens.primary, width: "80%" }} />
</View>
```

## Supported props

### BarListProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | BreakdownRow[] | yes |  | The rows to render, in order. |
| title | string \| undefined | no |  | Optional heading shown above the rows. |
| share | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Bars proportional to the sum of all rows, with percent readouts, instead of relative to the largest row. |
| success | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tone (single-hue lists; pick one; default is the ramp by index). Precedence: success > destructive; a row's chartN slot beats the tone. |
| destructive | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tone (single-hue lists; pick one; default is the ramp by index). Precedence: success > destructive; a row's chartN slot beats the tone. |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Density (omit for the default row spacing). |
| plain | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Strip the card surface for nesting inside an existing card (mirrors Stats). |
| formatValue | ((v: number) => string) \| undefined | no |  | Formats row values (data formatting, not styling). |
| onPressItem | ((index: number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Rows become tappable drill-in targets when set. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# Board

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/board/board.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/board

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Board, applyBoardMove } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A data-driven kanban board: columns scroll horizontally, each column is a drop zone in a sunken well headed by its label and item count, and every card carries a drag grip, an optional trailing badge, a two-line description, a free-form chips slot, and an optional kebab menu.

Dragging is the kit's own drag-and-drop family,
so it runs on iOS, Android, and the web from one code path
and stays keyboard- and screen-reader-operable: press Space on a grip to grab, the arrow keys to move between positions and columns, Space to drop, Escape to cancel. The list stays controlled: a drop reports a `BoardMove` (source, target, insertion index, and the new neighbor ids) through `onMove`, and `applyBoardMove` is the standard reducer to apply it. Pass `defaultItems` instead of `items` for uncontrolled use, where the board applies each move itself.

For an action-driven work board, `plain` drops the lane wells and keeps the lane
headers and dashed empty slots. `renderItem` supplies the domain card with its
own controls. Add `draggable` to enable drag grips and drop targets while retaining
the plain layout. A custom `renderItem` receives `{ dragHandle }` as its second
argument; place that supplied grip in the card's header. `disabled` prevents moves
while a consumer saves a change. `bleed`
extends horizontal scrolling through the owning container's inset.
Plain lanes share the Board's measured width equally, with a 168px minimum per
lane. Narrow containers scroll horizontally; long card text stays within its lane.

Add `pageScroll` when the surrounding page or content pane owns horizontal scrolling.
The Board then renders an overflow-visible lane row without an inner scrollport.
Plain lanes still fill the available content width equally down to their 168px
minimum; standard lanes keep their configured width. The surrounding scroll area
must allow horizontal overflow and keyboard scrolling. Card actions and drag grips
retain their keyboard behavior. Omit `pageScroll` to keep the default local scroller.

## Usage

```tsx
<Board
  columns={[
    { id: "todo", label: "To do" },
    { id: "doing", label: "Doing" },
    { id: "done", label: "Done" },
  ]}
  defaultItems={[
    { id: "t1", columnId: "todo", title: "Rotate webhook secrets" },
    { id: "t2", columnId: "todo", title: "Draft the design review" },
    { id: "t3", columnId: "doing", title: "SSO rollout" },
    { id: "t4", columnId: "done", title: "Upgrade the CI runners" },
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Plain work lanes

```tsx
<Board plain emptyLabel="No work here" columns={[{ id: "ready", label: "Ready" }, { id: "review", label: "Review" }]} items={[{ id: "core-1", columnId: "ready", title: "Preserve the Argus experience" }]} />
```

### Draggable plain work lanes

The grip supports pointer dragging and Space/arrow/Enter keyboard moves. Drop
targets fill each column's height, including the space below an empty placeholder.
Controlled consumers persist `onMove` before replacing their saved `items`.

```tsx
<Board plain draggable
  columns={[{ id: "ready", label: "Ready" }, { id: "doing", label: "In progress" }, { id: "done", label: "Done" }]}
  defaultItems={[{ id: "core-1", columnId: "ready", title: "Preserve the Argus experience" }]}
  renderItem={(item, { dragHandle }) => (
    <Card compact>
      <Row between alignCenter><Typography bold>{item.title}</Typography>{dragHandle}</Row>
    </Card>
  )}
/>
```


### Compact

The density axis tightens the lane padding, the card gaps, and the card insets for a board that has to show more at once.

```tsx
<Board
  compact
  columns={[
    { id: "todo", label: "To do" },
    { id: "doing", label: "Doing" },
  ]}
  defaultItems={[
    { id: "t1", columnId: "todo", title: "Rotate webhook secrets" },
    { id: "t2", columnId: "todo", title: "Draft the design review" },
    { id: "t3", columnId: "doing", title: "SSO rollout" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Card menus and press

`onPressItem` makes each card's body pressable (the grip and the kebab stay separate controls), and a card with `menu` rows gains a kebab reported through `onSelectItemMenu`. `chips` is a free slot under the title for chips or avatars.

```tsx
<Board
  columns={[
    { id: "todo", label: "To do" },
    { id: "doing", label: "Doing" },
  ]}
  defaultItems={[
    { id: "t1", columnId: "todo", title: "Rotate webhook secrets", menu: [{ label: "Edit", icon: "pencil" }, { label: "Delete", icon: "trash", destructive: true }] },
    { id: "t2", columnId: "doing", title: "SSO rollout", chips: <Chip>identity</Chip> },
  ]}
  onPressItem={(item) => {}}
  onSelectItemMenu={(item, menuItem) => {}}
/>
```

### Empty column and explicit badges

An empty column shows `emptyLabel` in a dashed slot and stays a valid drop target. A column's `badge` prop replaces the automatic item count (a WIP limit, a status).

```tsx
<Board
  columns={[
    { id: "todo", label: "To do", badge: "WIP 2" },
    { id: "doing", label: "Doing" },
  ]}
  defaultItems={[
    { id: "t1", columnId: "todo", title: "Rotate webhook secrets" },
    { id: "t2", columnId: "todo", title: "Draft the design review" },
  ]}
  emptyLabel="Drop tasks here"
/>
```

### Controlled

`items` keeps the list in your hands: each drop reports a `BoardMove` through `onMove`, and `applyBoardMove` is the standard reducer to apply it.

```tsx
<Stateful initial={[
  { id: "t1", columnId: "todo", title: "Rotate webhook secrets" },
  { id: "t2", columnId: "doing", title: "SSO rollout" },
]}>
  {(items, setItems) => (
    <Board
      columns={[
        { id: "todo", label: "To do" },
        { id: "doing", label: "Doing" },
      ]}
      items={items}
      onMove={(move) => setItems(applyBoardMove(items, move))}
    />
  )}
</Stateful>
```

## Do & Don't

### Moves stay in the consumer's data

**Do** — Treat `items` as the single source of truth: apply every `onMove` to your own array (`applyBoardMove`), and persist `afterId`/`beforeId` if your backend ranks by neighbors.

```tsx
<Stateful initial={[
  { id: "t1", columnId: "todo", title: "Rotate webhook secrets" },
  { id: "t2", columnId: "doing", title: "SSO rollout" },
]}>
  {(items, setItems) => (
    <Board
      columns={[
        { id: "todo", label: "To do" },
        { id: "doing", label: "Doing" },
      ]}
      items={items}
      onMove={(move) => setItems(applyBoardMove(items, move))}
    />
  )}
</Stateful>
```

**Don't** — Don't pass a controlled `items` and drop the move on the floor: the drag completes, announces, and then the card snaps back because nothing updated the array.

```tsx
<Board
  columns={[
    { id: "todo", label: "To do" },
    { id: "doing", label: "Doing" },
  ]}
  items={[
    { id: "t1", columnId: "todo", title: "Rotate webhook secrets" },
    { id: "t2", columnId: "doing", title: "SSO rollout" },
  ]}
/>
```

## Supported props

### BoardProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| plain | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Unframed work lanes with custom domain cards. |
| pageScroll | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Let the surrounding page own horizontal overflow instead of an inner scroller. |
| draggable | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Enable drag handles and drop targets in plain lanes. |
| disabled | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Temporarily prevent moves, for example while the consumer saves a drop. |
| renderItem | ((item: BoardItem, controls: { dragHandle: ReactNode; }) => ReactNode) \| undefined | no |  | Custom plain card; place the supplied dragHandle alongside its domain actions. |
| bleed | number \| undefined | no |  | Extend the scroller through its parent's horizontal inset. |
| columns | BoardColumn[] | yes |  | The columns (lanes), left to right. |
| items | BoardItem[] \| undefined | no |  | CONTROLLED list; order within a column is array order filtered by `columnId`. The kit never mutates it: apply each `onMove` yourself (`applyBoardMove` is the standard reducer). Omit it (optionally passing `defaultItems`) for uncontrolled use. |
| defaultItems | BoardItem[] \| undefined | no |  | Initial list for UNCONTROLLED use; Board then applies each move internally. |
| onItemsChange | ((items: BoardItem[]) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired with the would-be next list after a drop, in both modes. |
| onMove | ((move: BoardMove) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired on every completed drop with the computed move (source, target, index, neighbors). |
| onPressItem | ((item: BoardItem) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Makes each card body pressable and reports the pressed item. |
| onSelectItemMenu | ((item: BoardItem, menuItem: RowMenuItem, menuIndex: number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when a row of a card's kebab menu (`item.menu`) is selected. |
| columnWidth | number \| undefined | no | 300 | Column width in px (default 300). |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Density axis (pass none for the default density). |
| emptyLabel | string \| undefined | no | "No items" | Message shown in an empty column (default "No items"). |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | StyleProp<ViewStyle> | no |  | Outer layout composition only (width/flex), never a restyle hook. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

Quartile boxes, whiskers, and outlier dots per category, computed by the chart from raw samples: quartiles by linear interpolation, whiskers at the most extreme data inside the 1.5 IQR fences, outliers beyond them. ## Do & Don't

### BoxPlot

**Do** - Compare distributions with the full five-number anatomy: box, whiskers, median, outliers.

```tsx
<BoxPlot
title="Latency by region"
data={[
  { label: "us-east", values: [42, 38, 51, 44, 47, 39, 58, 44, 41, 49, 96] },
  { label: "eu-west", values: [55, 61, 58, 64, 57, 63, 59, 66, 60, 62] },

```

**Don't** - A bar of averages hides the spread and the outliers, which are the point of comparing distributions.

```tsx
<Chart
```

# Breadcrumb

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/breadcrumb/breadcrumb.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/breadcrumb

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb, BreadcrumbItem } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Hierarchical navigation showing where you are.

## Usage

```tsx
<Breadcrumb items={["Projects", "Identity Platform", "Settings"]} />
```

## Variants

### Slash

```tsx
<Breadcrumb items={["Projects", "Identity Platform", "Settings"]} slash />
```

### Dot

```tsx
<Breadcrumb items={["Projects", "Identity Platform", "Settings"]} dot />
```

### Home icon

```tsx
<Breadcrumb items={["Projects", "Identity Platform", "Settings"]} homeIcon />
```

### Subtle

A page header's quieter trail: the ancestors in the subtle ink and the current page at the
regular weight, so the trail recedes under the title.

```tsx
<Breadcrumb items={["Library", "Controls", "Button"]} slash subtle />
```

## Do & Don't

### Current page

**Do** — Ancestors are links; the page you're on is plain text at the end of the trail.

```tsx
<Breadcrumb items={["Projects", "Identity Platform", "Settings"]} />
```

**Don't** — Linking the current page implies there's somewhere to go; it's a dead link to itself.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "center", gap: 6 }}>
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="link" style={({ pressed }) => (pressed ? { opacity: 0.7 } : null)}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Projects</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: alpha(tokens["muted-foreground"], 0.6) }}>/</Text>
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="link" style={({ pressed }) => (pressed ? { opacity: 0.7 } : null)}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Identity Platform</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: alpha(tokens["muted-foreground"], 0.6) }}>/</Text>
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="link" style={({ pressed }) => (pressed ? { opacity: 0.7 } : null)}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Settings</Text>
  </Pressable>
</View>
```

### Deep paths

**Do** — Collapse the middle to an ellipsis; keep the root and the last couple of levels.

```tsx
<Breadcrumb maxItems={3} items={["Projects", "Identity Platform", "Settings", "Avatar", "Edit"]} />
```

**Don't** — A fully expanded deep path wraps and competes with the page.

```tsx
<Breadcrumb items={[
    "Projects",
    "Identity Platform",
    "Settings",
    "Profile",
    "Avatar",
    "Edit"
  ]} />
```

### Separator

**Do** — Pick one separator and use it the whole way.

```tsx
<Breadcrumb items={["Projects", "Identity Platform", "Settings"]} />
```

**Don't** — Mixing separators in one trail looks broken.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "center", gap: 6 }}>
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="link" style={({ pressed }) => (pressed ? { opacity: 0.7 } : null)}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Projects</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: alpha(tokens["muted-foreground"], 0.6) }}>/</Text>
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="link" style={({ pressed }) => (pressed ? { opacity: 0.7 } : null)}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Identity Platform</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: alpha(tokens["muted-foreground"], 0.6) }}>›</Text>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Settings</Text>
</View>
```

### Home root

**Do** — Give the home icon an aria-label so the root is announced.

```tsx
<Breadcrumb homeIcon items={["Settings"]} />
```

**Don't** — An icon-only root with no label is unclear to screen readers.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "center", gap: 6 }}>
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="link" style={({ pressed }) => (pressed ? { opacity: 0.7 } : null)}>
    <Icon home muted size={14} />
  </Pressable>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: alpha(tokens["muted-foreground"], 0.6) }}>/</Text>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Settings</Text>
</View>
```

### Chevron

**Do** — Point the chevron in the reading direction (right in LTR) so each one means 'drill into the next level'.

```tsx
<Breadcrumb chevron items={["Projects", "Identity Platform", "Settings"]} />
```

**Don't** — A down (or back) chevron reads as a dropdown or a back affordance, not progression down the hierarchy.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "center", gap: 6 }}>
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="link" style={({ pressed }) => (pressed ? { opacity: 0.7 } : null)}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Projects</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: alpha(tokens["muted-foreground"], 0.6) }}>⌄</Text>
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="link" style={({ pressed }) => (pressed ? { opacity: 0.7 } : null)}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Identity Platform</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: alpha(tokens["muted-foreground"], 0.6) }}>⌄</Text>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Settings</Text>
</View>
```

### Slash

**Do** — Keep the slash muted and lighter than the text so it reads as a quiet path divider.

```tsx
<Breadcrumb slash items={["Projects", "Identity Platform", "Settings"]} />
```

**Don't** — A full-weight, foreground slash competes with the labels and can read as part of a link.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "center", gap: 6 }}>
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="link" style={({ pressed }) => (pressed ? { opacity: 0.7 } : null)}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Projects</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground, paddingHorizontal: 4 }}>/</Text>
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="link" style={({ pressed }) => (pressed ? { opacity: 0.7 } : null)}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Identity Platform</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground, paddingHorizontal: 4 }}>/</Text>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Settings</Text>
</View>
```

### Dot

**Do** — Use a centered middot (·) so the dot sits between the crumbs and clearly divides them.

```tsx
<Breadcrumb dot items={["Projects", "Identity Platform", "Settings"]} />
```

**Don't** — A baseline period looks like a typo or end-of-sentence, not a separator between crumbs.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "center", gap: 6 }}>
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="link" style={({ pressed }) => (pressed ? { opacity: 0.7 } : null)}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Projects</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: alpha(tokens["muted-foreground"], 0.6) }}>.</Text>
  <Pressable accessibilityRole="link" style={({ pressed }) => (pressed ? { opacity: 0.7 } : null)}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Identity Platform</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: alpha(tokens["muted-foreground"], 0.6) }}>.</Text>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Settings</Text>
</View>
```

## Supported props

### BreadcrumbProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| chevron | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Separator style (pick one; default is the chevron glyph). |
| slash | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Separator style (pick one; default is the chevron glyph). |

# BulletChart

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/charts/bullet-chart/bullet-chart.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/bullet-chart

## Public imports

```tsx
import { BulletChart } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Goal-attainment rows: each datum is a leading label, a track holding qualitative background bands (`ranges`, ascending bounds in fading washes), the tone-colored measure bar, an optional vertical target tick, and the trailing formatted value.

Following the classic bullet-graph anatomy each row carries its own scale, since goals rarely share units; pass `max` to force one shared scale when they do. The compact alternative to a dashboard of gauges: five goals read in five rows.

`detailed` expands each track, keeps its target marker inside the band and adds the target/ranges key.

## Usage

```tsx
<BulletChart
  title="Q3 targets"
  data={[
    { label: "Revenue", value: 275, target: 300, ranges: [200, 350, 500] },
    { label: "Profit", value: 42, target: 35, ranges: [30, 50, 70] },
    { label: "NPS", value: 61, target: 70, ranges: [40, 60, 80] },
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Success tone

```tsx
<BulletChart
  success
  data={[
    { label: "Web", value: 34, target: 30 },
    { label: "iOS", value: 18, target: 24 },
    { label: "Android", value: 21, target: 24 },
  ]}
/>
```

### Compact

```tsx
<BulletChart
  compact
  data={[
    { label: "Compute", value: 8200, target: 10000, ranges: [6000, 10000, 14000] },
    { label: "Storage", value: 4100, target: 5000, ranges: [3000, 5000, 8000] },
  ]}
/>
```

### Row tones

A datum takes its own `success`, `warning` or `destructive` tone (precedence success > warning > destructive): its measure bar is the solid status colour and its value the status ink.

```tsx
<BulletChart
  title="SLOs"
  max={100}
  formatValue={(v) => `${v}%`}
  data={[
    { label: "Availability", value: 99, target: 99, success: true },
    { label: "Latency p95", value: 82, target: 90, warning: true },
    { label: "Error budget", value: 41, target: 75, destructive: true }
  ]}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### BulletChart

**Do** - Give every goal its row, with the target as a tick and the qualitative context as bands.

```tsx
<BulletChart
title="Q3 targets"
data={[
  { label: "Revenue", value: 275, target: 300, ranges: [200, 350, 500] },
  { label: "Profit", value: 42, target: 35, ranges: [30, 50, 70] },
]}
/>
```

**Don't** - A bare progress bar per goal loses the target, the qualitative bands, and the shared scale that makes rows comparable.

```tsx
<View style={{ borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.card, padding: 20, maxWidth: 480, gap: 8 }}>
  <View style={{ height: 12, backgroundColor: tokens.muted, borderRadius: 6 }}>
    <View style={{ height: 12, width: "60%", backgroundColor: tokens.primary, borderRadius: 6 }} />
  </View>
</View>
```

## Supported props

### BulletChartProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data | BulletDatum[] | yes |  | The rows to render, in order, each on its own scale. |
| title | string \| undefined | no |  | Optional heading shown above the rows. |
| max | number \| undefined | no |  | Force one scale maximum shared by every row (only when the rows share a unit). Omit for the default per-row scale: each row's largest value, target, or range bound. |
| success | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Measure tone (pick one; default primary). Precedence: success > destructive. |
| destructive | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Measure tone (pick one; default primary). Precedence: success > destructive. |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Density (omit for the default row spacing). |
| detailed | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Expanded goal rows with inset markers and a qualitative-band key. |
| plain | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Strip the card surface for nesting inside an existing card (mirrors Stats). |
| formatValue | ((v: number) => string) \| undefined | no |  | Formats row values (data formatting, not styling). |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# ButtonGroup

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/button-group/button-group.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/button-group

## Public imports

```tsx
import { ButtonGroup } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Segmented controls, split buttons, attached groups.

On the web the segmented control is the v4 hand-off's: the options sit in a rounded track on the raised fill, and the selected one rides a flat card thumb with a small shadow, the rest in the muted ink. It is 30, 36 or 44 px tall at the small, default and large sizes. The split button is the green call-to-action pill with its chevron half, and the stepper and the spaced peers are hairline pills the height of a Button beside them.

Pass `rounded` for a capsule segmented track with equal cells and one sliding selection thumb. The small capsule is 32 px tall, as in the docs appearance picker. Its spring transition follows Reduce Motion.
On iOS and Android the groups keep their platform shapes (the iOS segmented control, the Material 3 segmented button) in the theme's colours.

All four kinds follow the theme's surface mode.
Toggle Liquid Glass in the docs,
or use `<ThemeProvider glass>` in an app:
segmented groups paint a glass
selection puck, in the segment's own corners, on the selected segment, a split group is its call to action's
brand-tinted glass (the action colour under the material, as a primary Button), a
stepper shares a glass capsule, and spaced peers get individual glass surfaces. Every
kind keeps its solid size under glass: the material covers the track or cell's whole
footprint and a hairline border gives way to the material's edge, so switching the surface
mode never moves the page. Solid mode keeps each platform's existing skin.
The material uses native Liquid Glass on supported iOS
versions, the native blur or tint fallback on Android and older iOS, and
the hand-off's frost in the browser.
Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast use the
shared material's opaque fallbacks.

A web segment is 8 px shorter than its track, padded 14 px a side (8 px for an icon
alone) with a 500 label of 12 px at the small size and 13 px otherwise. `compact` is the
hand-off component page's platform switch: the segments keep their size's height and take
the 12 px label on a 12 px inset, on the web alone (a platform that ships the control keeps
its one density; the split, stepper and spaced kinds ignore it). `steadyPress` preserves the resting opacity of a
segment while pressed; `start` pins the group in an app-owned host arrangement.

## Usage

```tsx
<ButtonGroup items={["Day", "Week", "Month"]} />
```

## Variants

### Small

```tsx
<ButtonGroup items={["Day", "Week", "Month"]} small />
```

### Large

```tsx
<ButtonGroup items={["Day", "Week", "Month"]} large />
```

### Compact

```tsx
<ButtonGroup compact items={["Day", "Week", "Month"]} defaultActive={0} accessibilityLabel="Range" />
```

### Disabled

```tsx
<ButtonGroup items={["Day", "Week", "Month"]} disabled />
```

### Block

```tsx
<ButtonGroup items={["Day", "Week", "Month"]} block />
```

### Block spaced

```tsx
<ButtonGroup spaced items={["Edit", "Duplicate", "Archive"]} block />
```

### Measure

```tsx
<Container>
  <Column>
    <ButtonGroup items={["Day", "Week", "Month"]} xs start />
    <ButtonGroup spaced items={["Edit", "Duplicate", "Archive"]} md />
  </Column>
</Container>
```

### Attached

`attached` joins the segments into one box: a single edge round the group, a hairline between the cells, and every cell its full height, the selected one on the raised fill. Use it for a toolbar's view or formatting choices. An item's `display` draws the cell's face from any node (a glyph set in a weight or a style), with the item's `label` kept as the cell's accessible name.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup
  attached
  defaultActive={0}
  items={[
    { label: "Bold", display: <Typography tileTitle bold>B</Typography> },
    { label: "Italic", display: <Typography tileTitle italic>I</Typography> },
    { label: "Underline", display: <Typography tileTitle underline>U</Typography> }
  ]}
/>
```

### Stepper

```tsx
<ButtonGroup stepper items={["Yesterday", "Today", "Tomorrow"]} />
```

### Stepper signs

`decrementIcon` and `incrementIcon` replace the stepper's back and forward glyphs with any icon, for a stepper that changes a value rather than moving through a list.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup stepper decrementIcon={<Icon zoomOut size={14} decorative />} incrementIcon={<Icon zoomIn size={14} decorative />} items={["100%"]} />
```

### Split

```tsx
<ButtonGroup split items={["Save"]} menu={["Save as draft", "Save and close", "Save a copy"]} />
```

In glass mode the split menu is a dense-layer glass card under the group, whose
shared glass, primary label, divider and chevron stay in place. The primary action
and the chevron stay two fixed targets throughout, and a group disabled while its
menu is open closes it. Solid mode paints the skin's own menu.

### Icon segments

An item may pair its label with a kit glyph (`{ label, icon }`); `iconsOnly`
renders each segment as the glyph alone, with the label as the segment's
accessible name. An icon-only segmented control: a view switcher, a
form-factor switcher.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup
  iconsOnly
  items={[
    { label: "Phone width", icon: "smartphone" },
    { label: "Tablet width", icon: "tablet" },
    { label: "Desktop width", icon: "monitor" }
  ]}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### Segmented

**Do** — Keep a segmented control to a few mutually-exclusive views.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup segmented defaultActive={0} items={["Day", "Week", "Month"]} />
```

**Don't** — Past ~4 options a segmented control gets cramped and hard to scan; reach for a select.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup segmented defaultActive={0} items={["Day", "Week", "Month", "Quarter", "Year", "5Y", "All"]} />
```

### Attached

**Do** — Reserve attached groups for closely-related actions like prev / today / next.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup stepper active={1} items={["Yesterday", "Today", "Tomorrow"]} />
```

**Don't** — Attaching unrelated actions implies they belong to one control.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup segmented defaultActive={-1} items={["Save", "Delete", "Export"]} />
```

### Split

**Do** — Separate the chevron with a hairline so the secondary menu reads as distinct.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup split items={["Save"]} menu={["Save as draft", "Save and close", "Save a copy"]} />
```

**Don't** — With no divider the chevron looks like part of one button, hiding the menu.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", alignSelf: "flex-start" }}>
  <Pressable
    style={({ pressed }) => [
      { flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", height: 36, paddingHorizontal: 18, borderTopLeftRadius: 9999, borderBottomLeftRadius: 9999, borderTopRightRadius: 0, borderBottomRightRadius: 0, backgroundColor: tokens.action },
      pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null
    ]}
  >
    <Text style={{ fontWeight: "800", fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, letterSpacing: 0.12, color: tokens["action-foreground"] }}>Save</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Pressable
    style={({ pressed }) => [
      { flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", height: 36, paddingLeft: 8, paddingRight: 12, borderTopRightRadius: 9999, borderBottomRightRadius: 9999, borderTopLeftRadius: 0, borderBottomLeftRadius: 0, backgroundColor: tokens.action },
      pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null
    ]}
  >
    <Icon chevronDown color={tokens["action-foreground"]} size={16} />
  </Pressable>
</View>
```

# Button

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/button/button.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/button

## Public imports

```tsx
import { AnatomyPart, AnatomyProvider, Button } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Six intents × three sizes (plus the icon square) × disabled / focus / hover states. Always semantic: the intent communicates what the button does (default = the primary action, destructive = irreversible, ghost = chrome).

On the web a button is 32, 40 or 48 tall (`small`, default, `large`) with the 10 px control corner, a 500-weight label at 13, 14 or 16 px, and an 8 px gap beside its icons. The call to action fills with the accent, `destructive` with the status red, both under a lit top edge; `secondary` is the quiet well with a boundary, `outline` the boundary alone, `ghost` and `link` bare (the link underlined). A filled button brightens and rises 1 px under the pointer over 150 ms and settles back when it leaves; the other looks take the well's wash at once. A press scales the button to 96% and darkens it, unless `steadyPress`. A disabled button fades to 40%; a loading one keeps its full look while its spinner runs. A disabled or loading button stays put, and Reduce Motion makes the lift instant.
On iOS the button is the 50 pt capsule with a semibold 17 pt label, on Android the 40 dp Material 3 stadium, both in the same colours.

Pass `ref` to access the interactive Pressable, including link buttons. Use `useRef<ComponentRef<typeof Button>>(null)` from React, or `useRef<View>(null)` with React Native's `View` type. Object and callback refs are supported and detach on unmount. Calling `ref.current?.focus()` or `.blur()` delegates to the host without activating the control. Browser focus is supported; native focus depends on the platform and React Native version, and is separate from accessibility focus.

`softHover` dims a link to 85% on hover in place of the wash. Inverse actions use
a translucent white hover wash over a branded surface.

Utility icon actions use `icon` with `compactIcon` (28), `mediumIcon` (32), or
`largeIcon` (34). `wideIcon` gives the compact box two extra pixels of
horizontal room; `circle` rounds it fully. Pair with `ghost` for a plain surface,
`outline` for a boundary, or `ghost inset` for a quiet fill. `steadyPress` keeps
the resting look while pressed, and `count` carries a notification badge over the
upper trailing corner. The button still owns its accessible name, hover wash, and
native touch-target extension.

Use `inlineLink link small` for an inline text action: an underlined 13-pixel
label with no box, read as a link and washed on hover. The default size is 14
pixels; `large` is 16. `extraBold`, `foreground`, and `inverse` set its weight and
ink. `external` opens `href` through the system browser on every platform, while
keeping its browser link semantics.

`plainLink` is a plain accent text action with no box and no underline, still read
as a button: a panel's Reset, a table's show-all row. On the web it is a 500 13 px
label in the accent text ink (12 px with `small`) that brightens to the foreground ink
under the pointer; natively it is the platform's own tint-coloured text button. Among
the bodies, `inlineLink` wins over `plainLink` when both are passed.

`scopeTrigger ghost steadyPress` is a bare 32 px menu trigger with a 600-weight
14px label; `filterTrigger ghost steadyPress` the same with a muted 13px label. Both
take the well's wash on hover. Supply the trailing chevron through `iconRight`, and
announce the menu with `expanded` and `haspopup`.

`identityAction` is a 28 px hairline pill around a leading avatar and its name;
`referenceLink` an underlined monospace key in the link ink; `inlineIcon` an unboxed
22 px icon action; `themeChoice` a 32 px pill around the theme's colour disc, a
`<Swatch tiny ring circle decorative>` passed through `iconLeft`, whose `selected` state is the
accent edge with a soft accent halo. `pageLink` is a page header's link, a 34 px hairline box
around a muted 13 px label (a page's section, its source); add `mono` when the label is a
path, which sets it in the 400 12 px mono face. `jumpLink` is a page's jump to one of its sections, a 28 px
hairline pill around a muted 500 12 px label. Both header links brighten their label to the
full ink and take the `secondary` wash under the pointer.

## Usage

A button's whole job is to fire `onPress`. Wire it to your own handler and every press runs it.

```tsx
<Button>Save changes</Button>
```

## Variants

The variant only changes how a button looks; every one of them fires `onPress` the same way.

### Attention required

Use `attention` for a required setup action. Soft red glow swells outward and returns
in a heartbeat rhythm: a strong beat, a softer beat, then a pause every 1.8 seconds.
Its inner edge, label and button dimensions stay still. Reduce Motion
keeps a steady halo; disabled and loading buttons suppress it. Remove the button
or the prop when the required setup is complete.

```tsx
<Button outline small attention>Configure AI</Button>
```

### Inline identity and reference actions

```tsx
<Row comfortable alignCenter>
  <Button identityAction ghost steadyPress iconLeft={<Avatar annotation initials="S" hue={20} />}>Scout v2.3</Button>
  <Button referenceLink inlineLink link steadyPress iconRight={<Icon externalLink size={10} heavyStroke muted />}>CORE-1790</Button>
  <Button inlineIcon inlineLink link steadyPress iconLeft={<Icon externalLink size={13} heavyStroke primary />} accessibilityLabel="Open repository" />
</Row>
```

### Theme choices

The disc is the theme's own colour, data the example carries rather than a token: the
hand-off's `THM` table (cv-kit-code.js line 67) gives blush `oklch(.8 .09 10)` and mint
`oklch(.84 .11 165)`, which are `#f1a6b0` and `#80e2b9` in sRGB.

```tsx
<Row snug>
  <Button themeChoice ghost steadyPress selected iconLeft={<Swatch tiny ring circle decorative color="#f1a6b0" />}>blush</Button>
  <Button themeChoice ghost steadyPress iconLeft={<Swatch tiny ring circle decorative color="#80e2b9" />}>mint</Button>
</Row>
```


### Scope and filter triggers

```tsx
<Row comfortable alignCenter>
  <Button scopeTrigger ghost steadyPress iconRight={<Icon chevronDown size={14} heavyStroke />}>All my projects</Button>
  <Button filterTrigger ghost steadyPress iconRight={<Icon chevronDown size={13} heavyStroke muted />}>Filter by</Button>
</Row>
```


### Utility icon

```tsx
<Button icon compactIcon ghost steadyPress accessibilityLabel="Open menu" iconLeft={<Icon menu size={15} boldStroke muted />} />
```

### Notification action

```tsx
<Button icon largeIcon circle ghost steadyPress count={3} accessibilityLabel="Approvals" iconLeft={<Icon bell size={17} mediumStroke muted />} />
```

### Unread mark

`unread` marks something new without a number: the accent dot inside the box's upper trailing corner, ringed in the card colour. The dot is decorative, so name the state in the accessible label; `count` wins when both are passed.

```tsx
<Button outline icon unread accessibilityLabel="Inbox, unread messages" iconLeft={<Icon inbox size={16} decorative />} />
```

### Outline

```tsx
<Button outline>Save changes</Button>
```

### Secondary

```tsx
<Button secondary>Save changes</Button>
```

### Ghost

```tsx
<Button ghost>Save changes</Button>
```

### Destructive

```tsx
<Button destructive>Save changes</Button>
```

### Link

```tsx
<Button inlineLink link small steadyPress>Save changes</Button>
```

### Plain link

```tsx
<Row snug alignCenter>
  <Button plainLink>Show all 54 props</Button>
  <Button plainLink small>Reset</Button>
</Row>
```

### Small

```tsx
<Button small>Save changes</Button>
```

### Large

```tsx
<Button large>Save changes</Button>
```

### Icon only

```tsx
<Button icon accessibilityLabel="Add item" iconLeft={<Icon plus size={16} />} />
```

### Disabled

A disabled button ignores presses: `onPress` never runs.

```tsx
<Button disabled>Save changes</Button>
```

### Loading

```tsx
<Button loading>Saving</Button>
```

### Raised

`raised` rests the page's main call to action on a soft glow in its own colour. Only a primary button takes it, and never while disabled.

```tsx
<Button raised>Mint agent</Button>
```

### Rounded

`rounded` gives a button fully rounded ends: the pill in place of the control corner, and a circle on an `icon` square. The special bodies keep their own corners.

```tsx
<Button secondary rounded>Rounded</Button>
```

### Block

```tsx
<Button block>Create account</Button>
```

### Dashed

`dashed` draws the edge dashed, for an add-a-row or drop-here action. It shows on the looks that draw an edge, `secondary` and `outline`.

```tsx
<Button secondary block dashed>Add a row</Button>
```

### Measure

Use `shrink` for a content-sized action in a narrow row. The button keeps its
normal width when space permits and wraps its full label when constrained.

```tsx
<Container>
  <Column>
    <Button xs start>xs step, pinned to the start (320)</Button>
    <Button md>md step, centered (448)</Button>
    <Button block>Block: fills the parent</Button>
  </Column>
</Container>
```

### With icon

An `Icon` in `iconLeft` or `iconRight` takes the button's label ink when it carries no
tone of its own: the primary's contrast ink on a primary button, the foreground on an
outline or ghost one, the muted ink on a quiet trigger, the link ink on a link, and it
dims with the label while the button is disabled. Size the glyph (16 at the base size,
14 small); pass a tone (`destructive`, `muted`) only to colour it apart from the label.

```tsx
<Button iconLeft={<Icon plus size={16} />}>Save changes</Button>
```

### Icon ink per intent

The same bare glyph on each intent, in that intent's label ink. The row wraps, so the
six buttons fold onto a second line inside a narrow card instead of running past its edge.

```tsx
<Row wrap relaxed alignCenter>
  <Button iconLeft={<Icon sparkles size={16} />} iconRight={<Icon chevronDown size={16} />}>Save changes</Button>
  <Button secondary iconLeft={<Icon sparkles size={16} />}>Save changes</Button>
  <Button outline iconLeft={<Icon sparkles size={16} />}>Save changes</Button>
  <Button destructive iconLeft={<Icon trash2 size={16} />}>Delete</Button>
  <Button disabled iconLeft={<Icon sparkles size={16} />}>Save changes</Button>
</Row>
```

## Do & Don't

### Default (primary)

**Do** — One clear primary action; everything else is supporting.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter snug>
  <Button primary>Save</Button>
  <Button outline>Cancel</Button>
</Row>
```

**Don't** — Multiple primaries compete; nothing stands out.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
  <Button primary>Save</Button>
  <Button primary>Apply</Button>
  <Button primary>Continue</Button>
</View>
```

### Outline

**Do** — Promote the main action to default; keep the rest outline.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter snug>
  <Button primary>Publish</Button>
  <Button outline>Save draft</Button>
  <Button outline>Schedule</Button>
</Row>
```

**Don't** — All-outline leaves no signal which action is primary.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
  <Button outline>Save</Button>
  <Button outline>Publish</Button>
  <Button outline>Schedule</Button>
</View>
```

### Secondary

**Do** — Default for the primary action; secondary for the next one down.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter snug>
  <Button primary>Create account</Button>
  <Button secondary>Import instead</Button>
</Row>
```

**Don't** — A secondary button as the main call to action under-sells it.

```tsx
<Button secondary>Create account</Button>
```

### Ghost

**Do** — Use ghost for tertiary and toolbar actions; keep the CTA filled.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter snug>
  <Button ghost>Cancel</Button>
  <Button primary>Save changes</Button>
</Row>
```

**Don't** — A ghost button is too quiet to carry the primary action.

```tsx
<Button ghost>Save changes</Button>
```

### Destructive

**Do** — Reserve the destructive variant for irreversible actions like delete.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter snug>
  <Button primary>Save changes</Button>
  <Button destructive>Delete account</Button>
</Row>
```

**Don't** — Red on a safe action cries wolf; users learn to ignore it.

```tsx
<Button destructive>Save changes</Button>
```

### Link

**Do** — Link variant for inline navigation; a filled button for the submit.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter cozy>
  <Button primary>Submit</Button>
  <Button link>Learn more</Button>
</Row>
```

**Don't** — A link-styled submit doesn't look pressable and gets lost.

```tsx
<Button link>Submit form</Button>
```

## Real links (href)

A button that NAVIGATES should be a real link, not a press handler that sets `location`. Pass `href` and the web render becomes a genuine browser link: middle-click, cmd-click, and open-in-new-tab all work, crawlers see the destination, and assistive tech hears a link. Native platforms have no anchors, so pair `href` with an `onPress` that runs the same navigation through your router; while `disabled` or `loading` the anchor is suppressed exactly like `onPress`. `hrefAttrs` carries the anchor attributes react-native-web forwards (`target`, `rel`, `download`).

```tsx
<Row alignCenter cozy>
  <Button link href="https://canvas.nannier.com">Read the docs</Button>
  <Button outline href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nannier/canvas" hrefAttrs={{ target: "_blank", rel: "noreferrer" }}>
    npm package
  </Button>
</Row>
```

## Anatomy

A Button registers its parts with an enclosing `AnatomyProvider`, in the hand-off's order: `Container` (the pressable box), `Label`, `Leading icon`, `Trailing icon` and `Count badge`. The provider (`AnatomyProviderProps`) fills its stage and centres the specimen, and reports each rendered part's rectangle (an `AnatomyRect`, relative to its own box and in the space the specimen is seen in) to its `onMeasure` callback as `AnatomyRects` by part name, with its own box as its parent laid it out, so a docs Anatomy section can number the parts with markers drawn over the specimen. `zoomed` draws the specimen at the hand-off's anatomy zoom (1.6, for a component that hugs its content): the provider lays its inner box out at the stage width over the zoom and scales it back up about its centre, reserves the scaled height so the stage grows with the figure, and maps the rectangles before reporting them. Outside a provider the registration costs one context read and adds no node. Every kit component registers its own parts the same way, under the names its docs page lists, and a part belongs to the outermost component that names it: the Badge inside a Button's count, or the Buttons in a Dialog's footer, register nothing of theirs. `AnatomyPart` registers an element of your own as a named part (`<AnatomyPart name="Child view">...</AnatomyPart>`), measured in a wrapping view inside a provider and rendered bare outside one; its `AnatomyPartProps` take the part's `name`, or a `part` a component already took, which renders its children bare when undefined.

## Workflow actions

Use `outline quiet` for a muted secondary operation and `outline inverse` on a dark
branded surface. `consistent` gives short workflow actions a shared minimum width;
`comfortable` supplies the roomier surround used for a compact featured action.

## Touch area

On iOS and Android a Button smaller than the platform's minimum touch target (44pt, 48dp) keeps its size
and extends only its touch area to the minimum, from its first frame, so nothing moves. React Native bounds that area by two rules of its own. It never reaches past a native container that does not contain it: a container of yours that clips (overflow hidden, a scroll view's edge) stops it at that edge. A container that paints, carries a `testID` or handles pointer events admits it, because such a container records the touch area at its layout and the Button has it from its first one. Every kit control does the same for itself; a control the kit lacks belongs in the kit, never in a Pressable of your own (see DESIGN.md, Shapes).
And where two touch areas overlap, the later sibling takes the tap: on Android two small icon Buttons 8 apart in a Row both reach across the gap between them, so a tap anywhere in it presses the second. Leave at least twice the extra touch area between small Buttons you place side by side (16 between two small icon Buttons on Android, 8 on iOS).
