# Calendar

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/calendar/calendar.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/calendar

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Calendar } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Month grid, week timeline, and day timeline in one component. Events mark their
days with a dot in the month grid and week strip, and timed events render as
blocks on the week/day hour timelines.

The view is a semantic boolean axis: pass `week` or `day`, or neither for the
month grid (`day` wins over `week` when both are set).

In glass mode the selected day is a brand-tinted control-layer puck behind its
number and event dot, in the month grid and along the week strip; in `range`
mode both endpoints carry the puck over the range band. The day peek and the
hover card are functional-layer glass cards beside their day. Solid mode keeps the
skin's own filled day.

## Usage

A bare calendar is uncontrolled: pressing a day selects it, and in the week/day views the chevrons page the selection a week or a day at a time (crossing into another month hands the press to `onPrev`/`onNext`, since the month itself is a prop).

```tsx
<Calendar
  month="May 2026"
  today={23}
  defaultSelected={24}
  daysInMonth={31}
  startWeekday={4}
/>
```

## Variants

### Events

Each event carries the `day` it falls on, plus an optional `title` and `start`/`end` hours. The month grid marks event days with a dot and reads the count to assistive tech.

```tsx
<Calendar
  month="May 2026"
  today={23}
  defaultSelected={24}
  daysInMonth={31}
  startWeekday={4}
  events={[
    { day: 8, title: "Design review" },
    { day: 14, title: "1:1 with manager" },
    { day: 24, title: "Sprint planning" }
  ]}
/>
```

### Day peek

With `dayPeek`, pressing a marked day opens that day's hour timeline (the same timeline the day view renders) beside the cell: at its trailing side (the right in a left-to-right layout), at its leading side when that lacks room, and above or below it when neither side fits. A tap anywhere else or Escape dismisses it.

```tsx
<Calendar
  dayPeek
  month="May 2026"
  today={23}
  defaultSelected={24}
  daysInMonth={31}
  startWeekday={4}
  events={[
    { day: 24, title: "Sprint planning", start: 9, end: 10.5 },
    { day: 24, title: "Team lunch", start: 12.5, end: 13.5 }
  ]}
/>
```

### Week

`week` renders the selected day's week: a strip of seven selectable day cells over an hour timeline, with each timed event as a block in its day column. The timeline spans the full day; the scroller opens on the 8 AM to 5 PM window and scrolls to the rest, and the 12h/24h control flips the hour labels (12-hour by default). Overlapping events split their column into side-by-side lanes, hovering a block floats its details, and the chevrons page a week at a time.

```tsx
<Calendar
  week
  month="May 2026"
  today={23}
  defaultSelected={20}
  daysInMonth={31}
  startWeekday={4}
  events={[
    { day: 19, title: "Design review", start: 11, end: 12.5 },
    { day: 20, title: "Sprint planning", start: 9.5, end: 11 },
    { day: 21, title: "User interviews", start: 10, end: 12 }
  ]}
/>
```

### Day

`day` renders a single day's hour timeline with each block carrying its title and time span. The timeline covers the whole day (narrow it with `startHour`/`endHour`); the scroller opens on 8 AM to 5 PM and scrolls to the remaining hours, and the 12h/24h control flips the labels. Hovering a block floats a detail card with the event's `description`. The chevrons page a day at a time.

```tsx
<Calendar
  day
  month="May 2026"
  today={23}
  defaultSelected={24}
  daysInMonth={31}
  startWeekday={4}
  events={[
    { day: 24, title: "Sprint planning", start: 9, end: 10.5, description: "Backlog grooming and capacity check for the next sprint." },
    { day: 24, title: "Design review", start: 11.5, end: 13 },
    { day: 24, title: "Team lunch", start: 12.5, end: 13.5 }
  ]}
/>
```

### Range

`range` turns the month grid into a check-in/check-out picker for booking flows: the first press sets the start day, a later press sets the end, and a tinted band spans the days between; pressing an earlier day restarts the pick. Control it with `rangeStart`/`rangeEnd` and `onRangeChange`, or seed it with the `default` pair.

```tsx
<Calendar
  range
  month="May 2026"
  today={23}
  daysInMonth={31}
  startWeekday={4}
  defaultRangeStart={14}
  defaultRangeEnd={20}
/>
```

### Compact

`compact` tightens the cells and type for dense surfaces, in every view.

```tsx
<Calendar
  compact
  month="May 2026"
  today={23}
  defaultSelected={24}
  daysInMonth={31}
  startWeekday={4}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### Single date

**Do**: Exactly one selected day (primary), with today marked separately in the accent tone.

```tsx
<Calendar month="May 2026" today={23} defaultSelected={24} daysInMonth={31} startWeekday={4} />
```

**Don't**: Painting several days with the primary selected style fakes a multi-select; when you mean a span of days, use `range` instead.

```tsx
<View style={{ width: "auto", borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, padding: 12 }}>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 2 }}>
    <Pressable style={{ height: 36, width: 36, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: tokens.primary }}>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["primary-foreground"] }}>8</Text>
    </Pressable>
    <Pressable style={{ height: 36, width: 36, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: tokens.primary }}>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["primary-foreground"] }}>14</Text>
    </Pressable>
    <Pressable style={{ height: 36, width: 36, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: tokens.primary }}>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["primary-foreground"] }}>23</Text>
    </Pressable>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Event marks

**Do**: A dot marks a day with events and the count lives in the accessible name; titles belong to the week/day timelines or a side panel.

```tsx
<Calendar
  month="May 2026"
  today={23}
  defaultSelected={24}
  daysInMonth={31}
  startWeekday={4}
  events={[{ day: 8, title: "Design review" }, { day: 14 }, { day: 24, title: "Sprint planning" }]}
/>
```

**Don't**: Cramming event titles into month cells clips them into unreadable slivers and breaks the grid's rhythm.

```tsx
<View style={{ width: "auto", borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, padding: 12 }}>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 2 }}>
    <View style={{ height: 40, width: 36, alignItems: "center", borderRadius: 6 }}>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens.foreground }}>8</Text>
      <Text numberOfLines={1} style={{ fontSize: 7, maxWidth: 34, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Design review</Text>
    </View>
    <View style={{ height: 40, width: 36, alignItems: "center", borderRadius: 6 }}>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens.foreground }}>9</Text>
    </View>
    <View style={{ height: 40, width: 36, alignItems: "center", borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: tokens.primary }}>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["primary-foreground"] }}>10</Text>
      <Text numberOfLines={1} style={{ fontSize: 7, maxWidth: 34, color: tokens["primary-foreground"] }}>Sprint planning meeting</Text>
    </View>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Day details

**Do**: `dayPeek` reveals a pressed day's schedule in place, anchored beside the cell, so detail arrives on demand and the grid stays the single source of truth.

```tsx
<Calendar
  dayPeek
  month="May 2026"
  today={23}
  defaultSelected={24}
  daysInMonth={31}
  startWeekday={4}
  events={[
    { day: 14, title: "1:1 with manager", start: 14, end: 15 },
    { day: 24, title: "Sprint planning", start: 9, end: 10.5 },
    { day: 24, title: "Team lunch", start: 12.5, end: 13.5 }
  ]}
/>
```

**Don't**: Selecting May 24 but leaving a detached panel on a placeholder breaks the link between the grid and its day.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", alignItems: "flex-start", gap: 24 }}>
  <Calendar month="May 2026" today={23} defaultSelected={24} daysInMonth={31} startWeekday={4} />
  <Column fill style={{ minWidth: 240 }}>
    <Card flush>
      <View style={{ paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingVertical: 12 }}>
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Pick a date to see events.</Text>
      </View>
    </Card>
  </Column>
</View>
```

### Hour bounds

**Do**: Keep the full-day timeline and let the scroller do the work: it opens on the 8 AM to 5 PM window, and every event stays reachable.

```tsx
<Calendar
  day
  month="May 2026"
  defaultSelected={24}
  daysInMonth={31}
  startWeekday={4}
  events={[
    { day: 24, title: "Sprint planning", start: 9, end: 10.5 },
    { day: 24, title: "Evening review", start: 18.5, end: 19.5 }
  ]}
/>
```

**Don't**: Narrowing `startHour`/`endHour` below the real schedule silently clips events out of view; the 6:30 PM review never renders here.

```tsx
<Calendar
  day
  month="May 2026"
  defaultSelected={24}
  daysInMonth={31}
  startWeekday={4}
  startHour={9}
  endHour={12}
  events={[
    { day: 24, title: "Sprint planning", start: 9, end: 10.5 },
    { day: 24, title: "Evening review", start: 18.5, end: 19.5 }
  ]}
/>
```

### Booking a stay

**Do**: One `range` calendar carries the whole check-in/check-out pick: the endpoints fill, the nights between band together, and an earlier press restarts.

```tsx
<Calendar
  range
  month="May 2026"
  today={23}
  daysInMonth={31}
  startWeekday={4}
  defaultRangeStart={14}
  defaultRangeEnd={20}
/>
```

**Don't**: Splitting the stay across two single-date calendars doubles the interaction cost and never shows the span at a glance.

```tsx
<Row loose wrap alignStart>
  <Column tight>
    <Typography small muted>Check-in</Typography>
    <Calendar month="May 2026" defaultSelected={14} daysInMonth={31} startWeekday={4} />
  </Column>
  <Column tight>
    <Typography small muted>Check-out</Typography>
    <Calendar month="May 2026" defaultSelected={20} daysInMonth={31} startWeekday={4} />
  </Column>
</Row>
```

## Supported props

### CalendarProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| month | string \| undefined | no | "June 2026" | Month + year label shown in the header, e.g. "June 2026". |
| selected | number \| undefined | no |  | The day number currently selected (CONTROLLED, primary highlight). Omit for uncontrolled use. |
| defaultSelected | number \| undefined | no |  | Initial selected day for uncontrolled use (a bare calendar highlights the day on press). |
| today | number \| undefined | no |  | The day number that is today (primary highlight when unselected). |
| daysInMonth | number \| undefined | no | 30 | Number of days in the month. |
| startWeekday | number \| undefined | no | 0 | Weekday (0=Sun .. 6=Sat) the 1st falls on; sets leading blank cells. |
| events | CalendarEvent[] \| undefined | no |  | Events to mark: dots on their days in the month grid and week strip, timed blocks in the week/day timelines. |
| onSelect | ((day: number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired with the day number when a day cell is pressed (and when week/day chevron paging moves the selection). |
| onEventPress | ((event: CalendarEvent) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired with the event when a timed block in the week/day timeline is pressed. |
| onPrev | ((event: GestureResponderEvent) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when the previous chevron is pressed in the month view, or when week/day paging would cross into the previous month. |
| onNext | ((event: GestureResponderEvent) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when the next chevron is pressed in the month view, or when week/day paging would cross into the next month. |
| week | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Seven-day strip over an hour timeline; chevrons page by week. |
| day | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Single-day hour timeline; chevrons page by day. |
| dayPeek | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Month view: pressing a day that has events also opens that day's hour timeline in an anchored overlay (a tooltip-style day peek) beside the cell, at its trailing side (the right in a left-to-right layout), at its leading side when that lacks room, and above or below it when neither side fits; dismissed by an outside tap or Escape. |
| range | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Month view: two-tap range selection — the first press sets the start day, the second (later) press the end; a press before the start restarts. Days between carry a tinted band. |
| rangeStart | number \| undefined | no |  | The range's start day (CONTROLLED with `rangeEnd`). Omit both for uncontrolled use. |
| rangeEnd | number \| undefined | no |  | The range's end day (CONTROLLED with `rangeStart`). |
| defaultRangeStart | number \| undefined | no |  | Initial range start for uncontrolled use. |
| defaultRangeEnd | number \| undefined | no |  | Initial range end for uncontrolled use. |
| onRangeChange | ((start?: number, end?: number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired as the range is picked: with (start, undefined) after the first press, (start, end) after the second. |
| startHour | number \| undefined | no |  | First hour of the week/day timeline (0-24; default 0, the full day). |
| endHour | number \| undefined | no |  | Last hour of the week/day timeline (0-24; default 24). The scroller initially windows 8 AM–5 PM and scrolls to the rest. |
| hour24 | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Timeline labels in 24-hour format (CONTROLLED). Omit to let the built-in 12h/24h toggle manage it. |
| defaultHour24 | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Initial hour format for uncontrolled use (default false = 12-hour AM/PM). |
| onHour24Change | ((hour24: boolean) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when the hour format changes (true = 24-hour). |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tighter cells and smaller type, for dense surfaces. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

# CandlestickChart

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/charts/candlestick-chart/candlestick-chart.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/candlestick-chart

## Public imports

```tsx
import { CandlestickChart } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

The trading instrument view: OHLC candles colored by direction from the success/destructive tokens, an optional docked volume pane, and optional overlay series (moving averages) in the series tokens. Press or scrub a candle to read its Open/High/Low/Close and volume.

```tsx
    { open: 63.6, high: 65.2, low: 62.4, close: 64.2 },
    { open: 64.2, high: 64.4, low: 64.0, close: 64.2 },
    { open: 64.2, high: 65.3, low: 62.8, close: 64.4 },
    { open: 64.4, high: 65.4, low: 63.8, close: 64.4 },
    { open: 64.4, high: 64.5, low: 62.6, close: 63.8 },
    { open: 63.8, high: 65.8, low: 63.6, close: 64.7 },
    { open: 64.7, high: 65.1, low: 63.9, close: 64.6 }
```

## Do & Don't

### OHLC data

**Do**: Feed the candles real open, high, low and close prices; each body shows the session's move and each wick its range.

```tsx
<CandlestickChart
  compact
  labels={["D1", "D2", "D3", "D4", "D5", "D6"]}
  candles={[
    { open: 64.0, high: 64.3, low: 62.7, close: 63.5 },
    { open: 63.5, high: 64.6, low: 63.2, close: 63.9 },
    { open: 63.9, high: 64.9, low: 62.4, close: 63.6 },
    { open: 63.6, high: 65.2, low: 62.4, close: 64.2 },
    { open: 64.2, high: 65.3, low: 62.8, close: 64.4 },
    { open: 64.4, high: 65.4, low: 63.8, close: 65.1 }
  ]}
/>
```

**Don't**: Fill the candles from a close-only series by repeating the close as open, high and low; every candle collapses to a flat tick, and the chart shows less than a line of the closes would.

```tsx
<CandlestickChart
  compact
  labels={["D1", "D2", "D3", "D4", "D5", "D6"]}
  candles={[
    { open: 63.5, high: 63.5, low: 63.5, close: 63.5 },
    { open: 63.9, high: 63.9, low: 63.9, close: 63.9 },
    { open: 63.6, high: 63.6, low: 63.6, close: 63.6 },
    { open: 64.2, high: 64.2, low: 64.2, close: 64.2 },
    { open: 64.4, high: 64.4, low: 64.4, close: 64.4 },
    { open: 65.1, high: 65.1, low: 65.1, close: 65.1 }
  ]}
/>
```

<!-- Source: https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/components/card.md -->
# Card

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/molecules/card/card.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/card

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardMedia, CardSeparator, CardTitle } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A content surface, used three ways: a stat card (a single metric, a big number and a delta), a section card (a labeled surface with an optional eyebrow, header and footer), and the generic card that brings its own structure. It is the Canvas v4 panel: the card fill under a hairline at the card corner (16 px on the web, 12 natively), the small shadow at rest and the large one `raised`; `flat` drops the shadow and steps the fill up a surface, `sunken` drops the shadow and sinks the fill to the well beneath the page (`surface-sunken`, the hand-off's `--bg2` tiles, stages and panels set into a card) under the hairline, and `outlined` drops the shadow and keeps the card fill under the hairline (the hand-off's page cards; a platform whose card control draws an outline instead of a shadow draws both the same), and `heroShadow` is the medium shadow (the hand-off's `--sh-md`, its section hero's stage), between the resting card and the raised one. Precedence is `raised`, `flat`, `sunken`, `outlined`, `heroShadow`.
On Android `sunken` is the Material 3 filled card: the well's fill with no outline.
A pressable card lifts 2 px on hover and takes the raised shadow. `selected` draws the primary border with a ring of the accent's soft wash around it.

Corners (pick one; the smaller step wins): the card corner by default, `smallCorners` for the tile corner (12), and the three steps the hand-off's component page frames with, `calloutCorners` (14: a note under a table, a compact link tile), `largeCorners` (18: a card framing a section of a page) and `stageCorners` (20: a staging frame, a figure and its legend), and the two its section pages frame with, `showcaseCorners` (20: a section page's showcase card) and `heroCorners` (24: the section hero's stage). The web skin draws each from its row; the native skins keep their own card corner on every step but the tile.

A card with content is padded by default, and a padded surface also spaces its flat children (the card owns the vertical rhythm, so a stack of Typography lines needs no layout wrapper); pass `flush` to opt out of both, the inset and the spacing, for edge-to-edge content (a table, a nav bar) or when you compose the self-padding `CardHeader`/`CardContent`.

The section props (`eyebrow` / `badge` / `title` / `description` / `icon` / `actions` / `footer`) render self-padding sections, so a sectioned card needs no `padded`: a tracked mono eyebrow with a badge opposite, the 20 px title in the display face over its muted description, the body, and a footer under a hairline in the subtle ink. They compose with a string `body` OR with raw children, so a panel can carry a titled header above a table or a form; children win when both are passed. For a cover image, `CardMedia` is the full-bleed top slot: it spans the card edge to edge, its top corners follow the card's corner, and its bottom edge stays flat; compose it with `flush` and let `CardContent` pad the text below.

Density: the card's own inset is 20 px with an 8 px rhythm; pass `compact` (14 / 8) or `comfortable` (28 / 8) to tighten or relax the card's own padding and the gap between flat children (`compact` takes precedence, and a density prop pads the surface on its own). On a sectioned card (an eyebrow, a title or a footer) the surface never pads, so a density moves its inset and rhythm onto the sections instead: the first section takes the inset above, every section the inset beside, the last the inset below, and each section sits the rhythm under the one before it. `grow` fills the height a parent Row or Column hands the card (the body takes the slack, so a footer stays on its floor); inside a `Grid` cell it is implied, so the tiles of one row are equal-height without being asked.

The hand-off's component page insets are their own density steps, the same on every platform: `panel` (18 with a 12 px rhythm: a section panel, an accessibility card, a figure's legend), `guide` (18×20 with 10: a guidance card), `linkTile` (14×16 with 6: a link tile) and `pager` (16×18 with 4: a previous or next card); the section pages add `well` (16 with a 12 px rhythm: a loading-state well, a wizard's preview).

Gap-free content densities preserve dense application layouts: `dense` (12),
`snug` (18), `cozy` (20), `relaxed` (22×24), `spacious` (28), `insetContent` (14),
`rail` (12×14), `summary` (14×16), `metric` (14×18), `request` (18/22/18/20),
and `menu` (12 vertical). `roomy` sits between `relaxed` and `spacious` and keeps a
rhythm: a 24 px inset with 20 px between flat children, the Canvas v4 section page's
showcase card, the same on every platform. Precedence follows that order, then the
page steps (`panel`, `guide`, `linkTile`, `pager`, `well`), before compact/comfortable.
`gapless` removes flat-child spacing; `borderless`, `inset`,
`dimmed` and `clip` control surface anatomy. `tileShadow`, `rowShadow`, and
`emptyShadow` extend the elevation axis after raised/flat/outlined/heroShadow. Accessible names and
hover-lift reporting are supported on interactive cards.

`interactiveContents` keeps a clickable card from nesting a button role around its
own buttons and links. `steadyPress` preserves its resting opacity while keeping
the hover lift and native ripple.

`gatePanel`, `versionPanel` and `notePanel` preserve the original Argus inset
content surfaces. Precedence is note, version, then gate; they own their secondary
fill, exact insets and corners.

## Usage

```tsx
<Card>
  <Typography caption medium>Active identities</Typography>
  <Typography h3 bold>12,348</Typography>
  <Typography tiny muted>+142 today</Typography>
</Card>
```

## Variants

### Featured approval

`featured` washes the card with the accent's soft tint from its top-left corner and
rims it in the accent. Supply the identity, eyebrow, stage badge, summary, gate
caption, metadata and domain action controls. `stacked` sets a second card behind
it. A pressable featured card lifts two pixels on hover.

```tsx
<Card featured stacked hue={285} initials="B" title="Blueprint" description="v3.0" eyebrow="Awaiting approval · Architect gate" badge="Architecture" body="Proposes service boundaries for pricing and money paths." caption="A human signs every money path." metadata="Commerce · $2.1k / 30d" actions={<Button primary small>Approve</Button>} />
```

### Artwork alone

Give `artwork` a parent with definite height. It paints two radial blooms, the
accent and the brand cyan (swapped on `promo`), over the quiet surface, without
text, padding or shadow. Add `illustration` with children for a 12px inset around
an identity.

```tsx
<Row cozy>
  <Column fill flush style={{ height: 100 }}><Card featured artwork /></Column>
  <Column fill flush style={{ height: 100 }}><Card promo artwork /></Column>
</Row>
```

### Promotional artwork

```tsx
<Card promo title="Gates come down only with receipts." body="Autonomy charter, circuit breakers, all as code." actions={<Button inlineLink link small>Read the charter</Button>} />
```

`promo` sweeps from the accent to the brand cyan, each mixed into the card fill,
under the card's own inks. It stays opaque content in glass mode.


### Linked references

`referenceInline`, `referenceStacked`, `referenceTile` and `referenceDetail`
preserve the original Argus reference layouts. `referenceKey` is the key, `title`
the summary and `description` the status/context. `referenceSource` adds the
source affordance in the detail panel. An `href` opens through the system browser.

```tsx
<Column cozy>
  <Card referenceInline referenceKey="CORE-1790" title="Size the pricing bet" description="In Progress" />
  <Card referenceStacked referenceKey="CORE-1790" title="Size the pricing bet" description="In Progress" />
  <Card referenceTile referenceKey="CORE-1790" title="Size the pricing bet" />
  <Card referenceDetail referenceKey="CORE-1790" title="Size the pricing bet" description="In Progress · Platform Core" referenceSource="Jira" />
</Column>
```


### Board tickets

`board` owns the ticket anatomy while retaining Card's existing surface, corner,
elevation and press behavior. It reads `ticketNumber`, `priorityLabel`, `title`,
`description`, `statusLabel` and `typeLabel`. Priority and type appear in compact rounded Badge pills without
visible field-name prefixes; accessible names retain their field context. High
and Critical priorities use the soft error treatment, Medium uses warning, and
other priorities use a quiet secondary pill. Types use the soft primary treatment.
Type comes first, then priority, in one 18 px metadata row below the status on
every platform. `noticeLabel` adds a quiet outline pill after them for a short
notice, such as "Workflow v1" on a ticket that follows an older workflow; its
text is its accessible name. It is the only pill that gives way in a narrow
card, ending in an ellipsis while type and priority keep their size. Omitted labels render no pill; the shared row
retains its height.
The header contains only the ticket number and move handle. Pass the Board render callback's
`moveHandle` unchanged; Card places it at the top right beside the ticket number.
`blocked` displays “Blocked by Discovery” when `blockedReason` is “Discovery”,
or just “Blocked” when there is no reason. `aiActive` reveals
“AI work in progress” with a shimmer in the text and cycling dots. Reduced motion
keeps that label static. Title and description clamp to two lines; each other
text row has one line. The metadata row and optional progress keep their
reserved slots, so short and long tickets have the same text height.

`imageSource` accepts an actual React Native image source (including authentication
headers), with `imageLabel` for its accessible name. It adds a taller, full-bleed
header, with matching top corners and the number and move handle over
an opaque, legible backing. Images use contain fitting. A failed image collapses
to the compact metadata header; a new source retries. Only the image header adds
height. Board anatomy takes precedence over raw children and section props.

```tsx
<Card board compact smallCorners tileShadow borderless
  ticketNumber="ARGUS-123" priorityLabel="High" title="Preserve saved work"
  description="Keep the current project state when returning to the board."
  statusLabel="In Progress" typeLabel="Task" noticeLabel="Workflow v1" aiActive />
```

```tsx
  <Card heroCorners heroShadow>
    <Typography small medium>Hero stage</Typography>
    <Typography small subtle>The 24 corner under the medium shadow.</Typography>
  </Card>
</Column>
```

### Media

```tsx
<Card flush>
  <CardMedia src="/kira-tanaka.jpg" alt="Portrait of Kira Tanaka" />
  <CardContent>
    <Typography h5 semibold>Kira Tanaka</Typography>
  </CardContent>
</Card>
```

### Specimen well

Given children instead of `src`, `CardMedia` is a sunken well that stages live content: the page's sunken fill (an ink tint under glass), the content centered, at least 160 px tall with a 28 x 20 inset, growing with what it holds. `compact` takes the 130 px well with a 24 x 16 inset and `tall` the 240 px one with a 32 x 20 inset; `stage` is a figure's stage, 320 px with an 80 x 40 inset, and `playground` a live specimen's, 340 px with a 44 x 28 inset that also grows to the height and the remaining width of a panel beside it (precedence `compact`, `tall`, `stage`, `playground`). `height` sizes the image band only. Children win over `src`.

```tsx
<Card flush>
  <CardMedia>
    <Button primary>Save changes</Button>
  </CardMedia>
  <CardSeparator />
  <CardContent>
    <Typography small medium>Primary</Typography>
  </CardContent>
</Card>
```

### Caption density

`CardContent` pads its body 20 px on every side. Under a media well a caption takes a
tighter inset: `dense` is 10 x 14 (a one-line label), `compact` 12 x 16 (a title over a
meta line) and `cozy` 14 x 16 (a title, a note and a code line). Precedence is `dense`,
then `compact`, then `cozy`.

```tsx
<Card flush>
  <CardMedia compact>
    <Button small>Save</Button>
  </CardMedia>
  <CardSeparator />
  <CardContent dense>
    <Typography caption mono medium muted>size small</Typography>
  </CardContent>
</Card>
```

### Specimen well sizes

```tsx
<Column relaxed>
  <Card flush>
    <CardMedia compact>
      <Button small>Small</Button>
    </CardMedia>
    <CardSeparator />
    <CardContent>
      <Typography small medium>compact</Typography>
    </CardContent>
  </Card>
  <Card flush>
    <CardMedia tall>
      <Button large>Large</Button>
    </CardMedia>
    <CardSeparator />
    <CardContent>
      <Typography small medium>tall</Typography>
    </CardContent>
  </Card>
</Column>
```

### Actions

```tsx
    <Button primary small>Save</Button>
  </CardFooter>

```

### Pressable

Pass `onPress` and the whole card becomes a control, with the button role. On the web it lifts under the pointer: it rises 2 px over 180 ms while its resting shade deepens to the raised one in step, and settles back when the pointer leaves (a `raised` or `flat` card rises with its shade unchanged). While it lifts and settles it stacks above the cards around it, so its deeper shade falls over the next one. Reduce Motion makes the change instant.
iOS and Android keep their own press feedback.

```tsx
<Column relaxed>
  <Card onPress={() => {}} title="Scout" description="Research agent, v2.3" />
  <Card onPress={() => {}} title="Mint" description="Release agent, v1.8" />
</Column>
```

### Selectable

```tsx
<Card selected onPress={() => {}}>
  <Typography lead semibold>Pro</Typography>
</Card>
```

## Do & Don't

### stat

**Do** — One big number, a short label, a small delta. The metric is scannable in a glance.

```tsx
<Card padded>
  <Row between alignStart>
    <Column tight>
      <Typography caption medium>Active identities</Typography>
      <Typography h3 bold>12,348</Typography>
      <Typography tiny muted>+142 today</Typography>
    </Column>
    <Emblem primary label="U" />
  </Row>
</Card>
```

**Don't** — Prose where the number should be: the eye has nothing big to land on, so the card stops being a stat.

```tsx
<Card padded>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, fontWeight: "500", textTransform: "uppercase", letterSpacing: 0.4, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>This month</Text>
  <Text style={{ marginTop: 4, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens["card-foreground"] }}>We onboarded 12,348 active identities, up 142 today, with churn holding steady.</Text>
</Card>
```

### section

**Do** — Give the header its title and description through the card's own parts; the header's spacing sets it apart from the body.

```tsx
<Card flush>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Recent activity</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Events from the last 24 hours.</CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>
    <Typography small>Two events today.</Typography>
  </CardContent>
</Card>
```

**Don't** — Hand-style a title in the body; it loses the card's title type and the header's spacing.

```tsx
<Card flush>
  <CardContent>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 18, fontWeight: "700", color: tokens["card-foreground"] }}>Recent activity</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["card-foreground"] }}>Two events today.</Text>
  </CardContent>
</Card>
```

### generic

**Do** — Use the surface once and layout the content with plain spacing inside it.

```tsx
<Card padded>
  <Column tight>
    <Typography lead semibold>Anything goes here</Typography>
    <Typography small muted>The card surface gives you the border, radius, and shadow. You bring the content.</Typography>
  </Column>
</Card>
```

**Don't** — Nesting one card surface inside another stacks border on border and shadow on shadow; the inner block looks dropped in.

```tsx
<Card padded>
  <Card padded>
    <Text style={{ marginBottom: 4, fontSize: 15, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens["card-foreground"] }}>Nested surface</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>A card inside a card doubles the border and shadow.</Text>
  </Card>
</Card>
```

# Carousel

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/carousel/carousel.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/carousel

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Carousel } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A horizontally paged slide viewer: swipe (or use the prev/next arrows and the
dot indicators) to move one slide at a time.

Paging snaps to the viewport width, the current slide drives the dots, and the
arrows step the index (clamped, or wrapped when `loop`). Slides hold any
content; pass an `items` array of `{ key, content }`.

Each slide is itself the card: it paints the surface, rounds the corners and
clips its content to them. So pass the slide's content, not a Card. A plain
string renders in the slide's own type, inset from its edge; any other node
fills the slide inside its 1px edge, so a picture is masked to the slide's
shape. A
Card nested inside frames the slide
twice, and on Android the Material 3
item's 28dp corners cut the Card's own 12dp edge.

The prev and next arrows sit beside the slides, never over them, so nothing
near a slide's edge is hidden behind an arrow; the slides narrow by the two
arrow gutters instead.

Every slide is mounted from the first frame and stays mounted, so a slide's own
state (a field's text, a playing video) survives the carousel measuring its
viewport, on the first layout and whenever a hidden carousel is shown again.
Until it has measured, the current slide fills the viewport on its own. A
carousel does not window its slides, so a long gallery loads every slide's
content up front.

On web, Tab visits the carousel in the order it reads: the previous arrow, the
slide viewport, the next arrow, then the slide picker (an arrow disabled at the
end of a non-looping carousel is skipped). Tab reaches the viewport while its
slides overflow it, and the focused viewport draws the theme's focus ring around
the slide. Left and Right move between
slides, while Home and End reach the first and last. Controls inside a slide
keep their own keyboard behavior. The named slide-picker buttons report the
current slide and its position in the set; activating the current slide does
nothing.
Picker targets measure at least 24px on web, 44pt on iOS, and 48dp on
Android, independently of the small painted dots.

The active dot follows the committed slide (a dot press, the arrows, the
keyboard, a controlled `index`, a finished swipe) in both surface modes; the
strip is absent with one slide,
with `showDots={false}`, and by default on
Android.

## Usage

```tsx
<Carousel
  items={[
    { key: "one", content: "Slide 1" },
    { key: "two", content: "Slide 2" },
    { key: "three", content: "Slide 3" }
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Arrows hidden (dots only)

Hide the prev/next chevrons with `showArrows={false}`; swipe and the dots still
page the carousel, the iOS page-control idiom.

```tsx
<Carousel
  showArrows={false}
  items={[
    { key: "a", content: "Featured" },
    { key: "b", content: "Popular" }
  ]}
/>
```

### Default index

Start on a later slide with `defaultIndex`; the matching dot reads selected.

```tsx
<Carousel
  defaultIndex={1}
  items={[
    { key: "x", content: "First" },
    { key: "y", content: "Second" },
    { key: "z", content: "Third" }
  ]}
/>
```

### Arrows and dots everywhere

The chrome defaults are platform-adaptive (web shows both, iOS dots only,
Android neither);
pass `showArrows` and `showDots` to force the full
arrows-plus-dots anatomy on every platform.

```tsx
<Carousel
  showArrows
  showDots
  items={[
    { key: "p", content: "Photos" },
    { key: "q", content: "Albums" },
    { key: "r", content: "Shared" }
  ]}
/>
```

### Loop

With `loop` the index wraps: both arrows stay enabled at the ends, and next on the
last slide returns to the first.

```tsx
<Carousel
  loop
  showArrows
  items={[
    { key: "first", content: "Start" },
    { key: "mid", content: "Middle" },
    { key: "last", content: "End" }
  ]}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### Current slide

**Do** — Keep one current slide and let the dots mirror it, so the position in
the set is always clear.

```tsx
<Carousel
  items={[
    { key: "do1", content: (
      <Column alignCenter center style={{ height: 140, backgroundColor: tokens.muted }}>{/* docgen-allow-style: demo placeholder slide surface */}
        <Typography lead medium>Step 1</Typography>
      </Column>
    ) },
    { key: "do2", content: (
      <Column alignCenter center style={{ height: 140, backgroundColor: tokens.muted }}>{/* docgen-allow-style: demo placeholder slide surface */}
        <Typography lead medium>Step 2</Typography>
      </Column>
    ) }
  ]}
  defaultIndex={0}
  onIndexChange={() => {}}
/>
```

**Don't** — Stack the slides yourself with a manual row of pressables; it loses
the snap paging, the synced dots, and the per-slide accessibility.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 8 }}>
  <View style={{ width: 200, height: 140, borderRadius: 8, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", backgroundColor: tokens.muted }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 16, color: tokens.foreground }}>Slide 1</Text>
  </View>
  <View style={{ width: 200, height: 140, borderRadius: 8, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", backgroundColor: tokens.muted }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 16, color: tokens.foreground }}>Slide 2</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

## Supported props

### CarouselProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | CarouselItem[] | yes |  | The slides, left to right. |
| index | number \| undefined | no |  | Controlled current slide. Pair with `onIndexChange`. Omit for uncontrolled. |
| defaultIndex | number \| undefined | no | 0 | Initial current slide for the uncontrolled case (read once; default 0). |
| onIndexChange | ((index: number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Called with the next current index whenever the slide changes. |
| loop | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Wrap from the last slide to the first (and first to last) on arrow nav. |
| showArrows | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Show the prev/next chevron buttons beside the slides. Default is platform-adaptive: on for web, off for iOS + Android (swipe idioms); pass `true` to opt in. |
| showDots | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Show the centered dot indicators below the slides. Default is platform-adaptive: on for web + iOS (UIPageControl), off for Android M3. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# Chart

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/charts/chart/chart.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/chart

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Chart } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A single- or multi-series bar chart: vertical columns (or horizontal rows) sized against the axis max, with per-category values and labels.

Pass `labels` + `series` for grouped clusters colored by the `chart-1`..`chart-8` tokens, add `stacked` to accumulate those series within one column per category, or give a series its own `success` / `destructive` tone when it means success or failure; press or scrub a category to inspect it.

## Usage

```tsx
<Chart
  title="Signups"
  data={[
    { label: "Mon", value: 45 },
    { label: "Tue", value: 60 },
    { label: "Wed", value: 35 },
    { label: "Thu", value: 70 },
    { label: "Fri", value: 55 },
    { label: "Sat", value: 80 },
    { label: "Sun", value: 95 }
  ]}
  max={100}
/>
```

## Variants

### Grouped bars

```tsx
<Chart
  labels={["Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"]}
  series={[
    { label: "Revenue", values: [62, 70, 84, 89] },
    { label: "Costs", values: [41, 48, 55, 59] },
    { label: "Profit", values: [21, 22, 29, 30] }
  ]}
/>
```

### Stacked columns

```tsx
<Chart
  stacked
  labels={["acme", "globex", "initech", "umbrella"]}
  series={[
    { label: "Authorization code", values: [1840, 1210, 960, 640] },
    { label: "Client credentials", values: [920, 1480, 340, 1120] },
    { label: "Refresh token", values: [610, 380, 720, 290] }
  ]}
/>
```

### Success vs failure

```tsx
<Chart
  labels={["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]}
  series={[
    { label: "Granted", values: [812, 905, 874, 961, 1024, 640, 588], success: true },
    { label: "Denied", values: [41, 38, 56, 47, 62, 29, 24], destructive: true }
  ]}
/>
```

### Horizontal rows

```tsx
  horizontal
  data={[
    { label: "Atoms", value: 92 },
    { label: "Molecules", value: 78 },
    { label: "Organisms", value: 64 },

  ]}
/>
```

### Tones

```tsx
    success
    data={[
      { label: "Mon", value: 82 },

      { label: "Fri", value: 94 }
    ]}
  />
  <Chart
    destructive
    data={[
      { label: "Mon", value: 14 },
      { label: "Tue", value: 9 },
      { label: "Wed", value: 22 },

      { label: "Fri", value: 7 }
    ]}
  />
</Column>
```

### Formatted values

`formatValue` formats the value axis, the inspected value and the accessible values; it is data formatting, not styling.

```tsx
<Chart
  title="Requests"
  data={[
    { label: "Mon", value: 12400 },
    { label: "Tue", value: 15100 },
    { label: "Wed", value: 13800 },
    { label: "Thu", value: 16900 }
  ]}
  formatValue={(v) => v.toLocaleString("en-US")}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### Bar

**Do** — Keep a labelled axis row and a single bar tone so the buckets read at a glance.

```tsx
<Chart title="Signups" max={100} data={[
  { label: "Mon", value: 45 },
  { label: "Tue", value: 60 },
  { label: "Wed", value: 35 },
  { label: "Thu", value: 70 },
  { label: "Fri", value: 55 },
  { label: "Sat", value: 80 },
  { label: "Sun", value: 95 }
]} />

```

**Don't** — Every bar the same full-strength fill and no labels: nothing is emphasized and the axis is unreadable.

```tsx
<View style={{ borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.card, padding: 20, maxWidth: 560 }}>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "flex-end", gap: 4, height: 120, width: 520, maxWidth: "100%" }}>
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderTopLeftRadius: 4, borderTopRightRadius: 4, backgroundColor: tokens.primary, height: 63 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderTopLeftRadius: 4, borderTopRightRadius: 4, backgroundColor: tokens.primary, height: 84 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderTopLeftRadius: 4, borderTopRightRadius: 4, backgroundColor: tokens.primary, height: 49 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderTopLeftRadius: 4, borderTopRightRadius: 4, backgroundColor: tokens.primary, height: 98 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderTopLeftRadius: 4, borderTopRightRadius: 4, backgroundColor: tokens.primary, height: 77 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderTopLeftRadius: 4, borderTopRightRadius: 4, backgroundColor: tokens.primary, height: 112 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderTopLeftRadius: 4, borderTopRightRadius: 4, backgroundColor: tokens.primary, height: 118 }} />
  </View>
```

## Supported props

### ChartProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data | ChartDatum[] \| undefined | no |  | The bars to render, in order (single-series mode). |
| labels | string[] \| undefined | no |  | Category labels along the x axis (grouped mode, with `series`). |
| series | ChartSeries[] \| undefined | no |  | Multiple series rendered as grouped columns per category, colored by the chart-1..8 tokens (or a series' own `success`/`destructive` tone). |
| stacked | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Stack the grouped series within one column per category (composition) instead of clustering them side by side. |
| title | string \| undefined | no |  | Optional heading shown above the plot. |
| max | number \| undefined | no |  | Axis maximum. Defaults to the largest value in the data (the largest category TOTAL when `stacked`). |
| success | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tone (pick one; default is the primary fill). Single-series only. |
| destructive | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tone (pick one; default is the primary fill). Single-series only. |
| horizontal | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Orientation (default is a vertical column chart). Single-series only. |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Density (default is the standard plot size). |
| plain | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Strip the card surface for nesting inside an existing card (mirrors Stats). |
| hideLegend | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Hide the series legend (grouped mode shows one by default). |
| selected | number \| null \| undefined | no |  | Press-to-inspect: the selected category index (controlled). Pass null for none. Vertical charts only. |
| defaultSelected | number \| undefined | no |  | Press-to-inspect: the initially selected category (uncontrolled). |
| onSelect | ((index: number \| null) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when a press selects a category (or clears it with null). |

<!-- Source: https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/components/chat.md -->
# Chat

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/chat/chat.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/chat

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Chat, ChatComposer, ChatMessage, ChatThread, Markdown } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A controlled assistant conversation with independently scrolling messages, clear author and provider identities, and an anchored multiline composer. The parent supplies the bounds; Chat fills the available height without choosing a fixed height of its own.

Messages remain application-owned `ChatMessageData`: keep each `id` stable while updating `content` during streaming. `pending` shows a three-dot thinking indicator until an explicitly `streaming` message arrives; pass `pendingIcon` to identify its provider. Streaming replies retain their own Responding indicator. Both animations stop when their state ends and stay still under Reduce Motion. `providerIcon` accepts an application-supplied provider logo beside the author; label the image or icon with the provider name for assistive technology. `provider` remains an optional supplementary text label such as the transport name. `error` adds a visible failure label; `notice` preserves delivery or fallback information. `footer` anchors connection, review, or other actions below the composer and outside the scrollport.

Chat draws the conversation as a card: messages 14 points apart inside a 16 point inset, assistant replies as plain 14 point text with no author line unless the app names an `author` or a provider (several AIs in one conversation), the person's own turns as a bubble in the accent's soft wash on the trailing side, and the composer under a hairline, its sunken field holding the draft and a round send button. Set `flush` to drop the card frame so the conversation sits directly on its host's fill, for example inside a Drawer or a Wizard body.

Set `assistant` to lay the conversation out like a desktop assistant's window instead. The thread and the composer share one centered column whose composer box is 768 points wide at most, with the user's bubble 16 points in from its edge. Assistant replies are plain 15 / 21 text across the column, 20 points in from the composer's edge, with list items on the line rhythm and paragraphs 12 apart. The person's own turns are a neutral bubble, 12 by 16 points in. Turns that change speaker sit 40 points apart and the blocks of one turn 20 apart. The composer is one raised, rounded 44 point box with no divider: a bare add icon, the draft, and a send control that stays quiet until there is something to send. The thread and the composer keep 24 point gutters; when either is narrower than 480 points (a phone, a side panel, a wizard body) the gutters shrink to 12 so the composer's text keeps its room. With `assistant`, `meta` names what will answer (a model, a provider) in one muted line at the end of the column under the composer. `assistant` and `flush` combine: a Wizard `assistant` body or a Drawer usually wants both.

Set `activity` on a message for work the assistant did rather than said, such as a command, a tool call or a process log. It shows as one muted line, its `author` then its `notice`, flush with the reply text, and expands to its markdown `content` when pressed. Consecutive activity messages fold into a single line naming each step ("Ran the tests, Process finished"), the way a desktop assistant folds its tool use; pressing it shows each step's own line.

Pass `actions` on any message for app-owned choices beneath its content: each has a stable `id`, a literal `label`, and optional `primary`. Chat, ChatThread, and ChatMessage call `onAction(messageId, actionId)` when chosen. Choices wrap at narrow widths and use each platform’s Button. `disabled`, `pending`, any streaming message in the thread, or an absent callback prevents activation. The app owns saving the choice, setting busy state while it is accepted, duplicate prevention, and removing resolved or historical actions. Actions do not send a composer draft or submit question answers.

Assistant content supports paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, fenced code, bold, emphasis, and inline code through React Native text. HTML, images, and links stay literal text and never load or execute remote content. `plain` renders all source punctuation literally; user messages are always plain text. This is a small safe markdown subset rather than a complete CommonMark renderer.

`ChatThread` follows new content while the reader is within 48 points of the bottom. Scrolling up to read older messages pauses following; returning to the bottom resumes it. Message updates, streaming text, question-height changes, and viewport resizing coalesce into a tail adjustment after layout settles. Scrolling is immediate and never animated, so it does not add motion when text streams or Reduce Motion is enabled. The overflowing thread is keyboard focusable with a visible focus frame. The native app or owning Dialog handles safe areas and keyboard avoidance.

`ChatComposer` keeps Enter available for newlines. Its explicit Send control receives the trimmed draft through `onSend`; empty, disabled, pending, or uploading sends are blocked. An attached file permits an empty text draft. `sendDisabled` blocks only Send while leaving drafts, attachment controls, and message choices interactive; use it when a saved choice must be made before another freeform message. Pending replies leave the draft editable. The app owns draft clearing, transport, cancellation, persistence, and retry behavior.

Pass `terminal` to Chat or its standalone pieces for a flat, left-aligned monospace transcript. Messages use `❯` for the user and `●` for the assistant beside their author, preserving provider text and current delivery state. No user bubble or conversation card is added. The bare composer places `❯` and its multiline editor between two full-width hairlines, with an explicit rectangular Send action. Hardware Enter sends; Shift+Enter inserts a newline. IME composition and native soft-keyboard Enter retain their normal text-entry behavior. Sending returns focus to the editor; `autoFocus` optionally focuses it on mount. The app still owns clearing the draft, delivery, and preventing duplicate requests. Pending replies keep the draft editable and block sending.

`Markdown terminal` preserves the same safe document grammar with 13px monospace text, compact spacing, and semantic headings. Tables remain aligned table rows in a horizontal scrollport instead of becoming stacked cards. Fenced code and tabs remain literal whitespace. `Textarea terminal` supplies the prompt's bare monospace metrics and implies `embedded`; existing Textarea defaults remain unchanged.

Set `onAttach` to show the accessible paperclip action. The app owns file picking and uploading, passes composer `attachments`, and removes a staged file through `onRemoveAttachment(id)`. A `ChatAttachmentData` has an `id`, `name`, optional `uploading` or `error` flags, and optional `notice` text. Uploading and failed files block sending; remove a failed file or replace it after retrying. `attaching` also blocks attaching and sending while the app opens a picker or uploads. Saved message attachments use the same metadata; `onOpenAttachment(attachment)` on Chat, ChatThread, or ChatMessage delegates opening or downloading to the app. Canvas never requests, uploads, or opens file URLs itself.

An assistant message can include `questions`: each `ChatQuestionData` has a stable `id`, `title`, optional `multiple`, and `options` with an `id`, `label`, and optional `description`. Supply controlled `ChatQuestionAnswerData` entries in `questionAnswers` containing `questionId`, `optionId` for a single choice or `optionIds` for multiple choices, and optional `customText`. Set `multiple` on the question for checkboxes; a custom answer can be combined with regular choices. A single-choice question also offers Select multiple at the bottom-right of its action row: switching it on records `multiple: true` in its answer and uses `optionIds`, preserving the original question metadata. The switch retains existing selections and custom text. Switching it off returns to the first selected choice, or clears an empty draft. Every question offers Write my own answer under the reserved `__custom` option id, limited to 1000 characters.

The active form shows one question with a counter derived from the actual question count. Selecting an ordinary radio saves and advances before the last question. Custom text stays on the current question and uses Next; a blank custom answer cannot advance. Back is a neutral outline button that preserves saved selections and text. Revisited valid single choices offer Next. Checkboxes use Submit to advance; Submit appears only for multiple-choice questions and the last question. The last question always requires explicit Submit before the complete batch is sent, and every question must have a real answer. An incomplete earlier answer returns the reader to the first unresolved question instead of submitting. Submitted custom text is trimmed.

Chat, ChatThread, and ChatMessage expose `onQuestionAnswerChange(messageId, answers)`, `onQuestionIndexChange(messageId, index)`, and `onSubmitQuestionAnswers(messageId, answers)`. Record answer changes in message data and pass the zero-based `questionIndex` to control navigation, including saved continuation after reload. Omitting `questionIndex` uses local navigation state. The position is clamped to the actual list. The final callback receives fresh answers for the whole batch, including the current answer; set `questionsSubmitted` after accepting it. Repeated activations are guarded while navigation or submission settles. A busy state that ends without a saved receipt permits retry. The app owns persistence, transport, and duplicate prevention across requests.

Both answer callbacks and an enabled form are required for interaction. `disabled`, `pending`, and active streaming lock the current question. Use `questionsDisabled` for an inactive earlier batch: it shows every original question and option read-only, without navigation actions. `questionsSubmitted` shows saved answers with an Answers sent receipt. Multiple-choice receipts include every selected label and custom text; an answer-mode override is identified as Multiple answers selected by you. Question labels and descriptions remain literal text; RadioGroup supplies arrow navigation and accessible group names. The counter is announced as Question X of N in a polite live region; navigation moves focus there through the kit's shared browser and native accessibility focus mechanism.

The current question is framed by the existing compact, flat selected Card: a soft theme tint and primary border distinguish its counter, answers and actions from the surrounding conversation. Saved receipts and inactive question history remain unframed. The Card is visual only, so answer controls retain their own accessible roles and focus behavior.

`Markdown` reuses Chat's safe grammar and renderer for standalone documents. It preserves heading levels one through six, emphasis, inline and fenced code, quotes, ordered and unordered lists, nested indentation, static checked/unchecked task lists, horizontal rules, and pipe tables.
Tables use Canvas DataTable's container-responsive stacked layout on narrow surfaces, retaining every column on iOS too.
Checklists are read-only Canvas selection controls; reading a document never changes its source. HTML, links and image syntax remain inert text: no source is executed and no remote image is requested. `MarkdownProps` accepts the source as children, an optional accessibility label and test ID; `compact` uses dense document typography. The parent supplies width.


## Usage

```tsx
<Chat
  style={{ height: 360 }}
  messages={[
    { id: "question", role: "user", content: "Help me plan the release." },
    { id: "answer", role: "assistant", author: "Planner", provider: "OpenAI", content: "Start with **scope** and a release checklist.\n\n1. Confirm acceptance criteria\n2. Run the affected checks\n3. Review the rollout" }
  ]}
  value=""
  onChangeText={() => {}}
  onSend={() => {}}
/>
```

### Selectable questions

Move through one question at a time. This example controls the saved position and answer draft separately so navigation and answer callbacks can update together.

```tsx
<Stateful initial={{ answers: [] as { questionId: string; optionId?: string; optionIds?: string[]; customText?: string; multiple?: boolean }[], submitted: false }}>
  {(state, setState) => (
    <Stateful initial={0}>
      {(questionIndex, setQuestionIndex) => (
        <ChatThread
          style={{ height: 420 }}
          messages={[{
            id: "planning-questions",
            role: "assistant",
            content: "Which release approach should we plan?",
            questions: [{ id: "scope", title: "What should the first release include?", options: [
              { id: "focused", label: "A focused first release", description: "Ship the essential workflow, then expand from feedback." },
              { id: "complete", label: "The complete workflow", description: "Include reporting, collaboration, and administration in the first release." }
            ] }, { id: "checks", title: "Which checks should we include?", multiple: true, options: [
              { id: "desktop", label: "Desktop browser testing" },
              { id: "mobile", label: "Mobile layout and accessibility testing" }
            ] }],
            questionAnswers: state.answers,
            questionIndex,
            questionsSubmitted: state.submitted
          }]}
          onQuestionAnswerChange={(_messageId, answers) => setState({ ...state, answers })}
          onQuestionIndexChange={(_messageId, index) => setQuestionIndex(index)}
          onSubmitQuestionAnswers={(_messageId, answers) => setState({ answers, submitted: true })}
        />
      )}
    </Stateful>
  )}
</Stateful>
```

## Do & Don't

### Bound the thread

**Do** — Give the conversation a bounded parent or an explicit composition height so only its messages scroll.

```tsx
<ChatThread style={{ height: 240 }} label="Planning conversation" messages={[{ id: "one", role: "assistant", content: "Keep the composer outside the scrolling thread." }]} />
```

**Don't** — An unbounded thread grows with every message and pushes its composer away.

```tsx
<Column><ChatThread messages={[{ id: "one", role: "assistant", content: "An unbounded parent cannot provide a scrolling viewport." }]} /><ChatComposer value="" onChangeText={() => {}} onSend={() => {}} /></Column>
```

## Supported props

### ChatMessageProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |

# Checkbox

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/checkbox/checkbox.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/checkbox

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Multi-select option, single yes/no, grouped lists.

One job, a platform's own control: a Checkbox that is one setting (a yes/no, a consent, an opt-in)
renders the platform's switch on iOS and Android, where a single setting is a switch (Material 3 on phones included), and stays a checkbox on the web; its role follows what renders (`switch` there, `checkbox` here).
A Checkbox that selects items in a list, a table's rows or a "select all" parent takes `selection`:
the web keeps the checkbox, Android the Material 3 checkbox, and iOS draws the edit-mode selection circle.
`indeterminate` implies `selection`, since a mixed state belongs to a "select all" parent and a switch has none. In glass mode the box keeps its solid look on every platform: it is a small mark inside content, not a surface, so it draws with no pane and no rim, a checked box in its solid brand fill under its check and an empty box with its solid outline.

Pass `ref` to access the interactive checkbox row, including its label. Use `useRef<ComponentRef<typeof Checkbox>>(null)` from React, or `useRef<View>(null)` with React Native's `View` type. Object and callback refs are supported and detach on unmount. Calling `ref.current?.focus()` or `.blur()` delegates to the host without activating the control. Browser focus is supported; native focus depends on the platform and React Native version, and is separate from accessibility focus.

On the web, Space activates the focused control on key release, and Enter also activates it. Holding Space does not repeat the change. Moving focus away, disabling the control, or composing text cancels a pending Space press.

## Usage

```tsx
<Checkbox defaultChecked>Email notifications</Checkbox>
```

## Variants

### Unchecked

```tsx
<Checkbox>Email notifications</Checkbox>
```

### Disabled

```tsx
<Checkbox disabled>Email notifications</Checkbox>
```

### Sizes

```tsx
<Column>
  <Checkbox small defaultChecked>Small</Checkbox>
  <Checkbox defaultChecked>Default</Checkbox>
  <Checkbox large defaultChecked>Large</Checkbox>
</Column>
```

### With description

```tsx
<Checkbox defaultChecked description="Get notified when activity happens on your account.">
  Email notifications
</Checkbox>
```

### Nested group

A parent "select all" over a group of children: a list selection, so every box takes
`selection`. Wire the parent's `checked` and `indeterminate` from the children's
state: `checked` when every child is on, `indeterminate` when only some are, and
toggling the parent selects or clears the whole group. (`Stateful` is a docs-only
state holder so this fence can show the controlled wiring; in an app that state lives
in your own component.)

```tsx
<Stateful initial={["Read"]}>
  {(selected, setSelected) => {
    const perms = ["Read", "Write", "Delete"];
    const all = perms.every((p) => selected.includes(p));
    const some = selected.length > 0 && !all;
    return (
      <Column>
        <Checkbox
          selection
          checked={all}
          indeterminate={some}
          onChange={(next) => setSelected(next ? perms : [])}
        >
          Select all
        </Checkbox>
        <Column indent>
          {perms.map((p) => (
            <Checkbox
              key={p}
              selection
              checked={selected.includes(p)}
              onChange={(next) =>
                setSelected(next ? [...selected, p] : selected.filter((x) => x !== p))
              }
            >
              {p}
            </Checkbox>
          ))}
        </Column>
      </Column>
    );
  }}
</Stateful>
```

## Do & Don't

### Unchecked

**Do**: Leave opt-in consent unchecked so agreeing is a deliberate act the user takes.

```tsx
<Checkbox>Email me product news, offers, and survey invitations.</Checkbox>
```

**Don't**: A consent box that starts checked opts users in by default; under GDPR pre-ticked consent is not consent.

```tsx
<Checkbox defaultChecked>Email me product news, offers, and survey invitations.</Checkbox>
```

### Checked

**Do**: Show the parent indeterminate (a dash, not a tick) when only some children are checked.

```tsx
<Column snug>
  <Checkbox selection indeterminate>Select all</Checkbox>
  <Column snug indent>
    <Checkbox selection defaultChecked>Read</Checkbox>
    <Checkbox selection>Write</Checkbox>
    <Checkbox selection>Delete</Checkbox>
  </Column>
</Column>
```

**Don't**: A fully checked parent claims every child is selected when only one is, so the state reads as a lie.

```tsx
<View style={{ gap: 8 }}>
  <Checkbox selection defaultChecked>Select all</Checkbox>
  <View style={{ marginLeft: 24, gap: 8 }}>
    <Checkbox selection defaultChecked>Read</Checkbox>
    <Checkbox selection>Write</Checkbox>
    <Checkbox selection>Delete</Checkbox>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Disabled

**Do**: Say why it's unavailable, like a plan gate, or don't show it at all.

```tsx
<Checkbox disabled description="Available on the Pro plan">Export to CSV</Checkbox>
```

**Don't**: A disabled option with no reason leaves users stuck and guessing.

```tsx
<Checkbox disabled>Export to CSV</Checkbox>
```

### Selection

**Do**: Radios for one-of-many; reserve checkboxes for independent multi-select.

```tsx
<Column snug>
  <Typography small semibold>Plan</Typography>
  <RadioGroup defaultValue="pro">
    <Radio value="free">Free</Radio>
    <Radio value="pro">Pro</Radio>
    <Radio value="enterprise">Enterprise</Radio>
  </RadioGroup>
</Column>
```

**Don't**: Checkboxes allow multiple selections; for a one-of choice they let users pick contradictory options.

```tsx
<View style={{ gap: 8 }}>
  <Text style={{ marginBottom: 4, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens.foreground }}>Plan</Text>
  <Checkbox>Free</Checkbox>
  <Checkbox defaultChecked>Pro</Checkbox>
  <Checkbox>Enterprise</Checkbox>
</View>
```

### With description

**Do**: Pass a `description` and the control stacks the title over its secondary line for you, box aligned to the first text line and the whole row tappable.

```tsx
<Checkbox defaultChecked description="Get notified when activity happens on your account.">
  Email notifications
</Checkbox>
```

**Don't**: A detached checkbox makes only the 18px box tappable; the label text does nothing.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "flex-start", gap: 8 }}>
  <View style={{ marginTop: 2 }}>
    <Checkbox defaultChecked />
  </View>
  <View>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Email notifications</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Get notified when activity happens on your account.</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

## Supported props

### CheckboxProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | Label text (the option's title) shown beside the box. |
| description | ReactNode | no |  | Optional muted secondary line rendered under the label, for the common title-plus-description option (a notification setting, a consent row). Supplying it builds the stacked title/description layout inside the control, so the caller never hand-composes a Row + Column + two Typography nodes and the whole row stays tappable. |
| checked | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Controlled checked state; omit for uncontrolled use. |
| defaultChecked | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Initial state for uncontrolled use (a bare <Checkbox /> is interactive). |

The web draws the checkbox, iOS the edit-mode selection circle, Android the Material 3 checkbox. Without it a Checkbox is one setting, which iOS and Android render as their switch (role `switch`), so a settings row reads the way each platform writes it. |

| onValueChange | ((next: boolean) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Alias of onChange, for parity with RN's value-style callbacks. |
| accessibilityLabel | string \| undefined | no |  | Accessible name for a LABEL-LESS checkbox (one with no `children`, e.g. a row selector in a table). With a visible label the label itself is the name; without one this is what a screen reader announces. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the pressable row. |
| small | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Size (pick one; default is the base box). |
| large | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Size (pick one; default is the base box). |
| disabled | boolean \| undefined | no | false | State. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |
| ref | React.Ref<View> | no |  | Ref to the interactive checkbox row, including its label. Typed as a React Native View. On web, React Native Web exposes its DOM host; focus() and blur() move browser focus. Native host behavior depends on the platform and React Native version. Calling focus() does not activate the control or call accessibility focus APIs. |
