
### Column weights

A column without a fixed `width` takes an equal share of what the fixed columns leave; `grow` weights that share (`grow: 2` takes twice a `grow: 1` column's) and `minWidth` floors the column's box, as a grid's `minmax(150px, 2fr)` track does. Weights, floors and fixed widths mix freely. Once the declared floors add up to more than the table's width, the table pans horizontally at any width rather than crushing them.

```tsx
<DataTable
  columns={[
    { label: "Prop", minWidth: 150 },
    { label: "Type", grow: 1.2, minWidth: 150 },
    { label: "Default", width: 100 },
    { label: "Description", grow: 2.2, minWidth: 220 }
  ]}
  rows={[
    ["primary", "boolean", "false", "The filled accent button, for the one main action on a surface."],
    ["small", "boolean", "false", "The 32 px control height."],
    ["loading", "boolean", "false", "Shows a spinner in place of the label and blocks presses."]
  ]}
/>
```

### Grouped rows

Pass `groups` in place of `rows` to title runs of rows: each group draws a band spanning every column (its `label`, an optional `adornment` node and an optional `count`, on the sunken fill) above its own rows. Sorting reorders rows within their group, paging draws the band of every group a page shows, and row indices count through the groups in order.

```tsx
<DataTable
  columns={["Prop", "Type", "Default"]}
  groups={[
    {
      label: "Intent",
      adornment: <Badge soft small>pick one</Badge>,
      count: 3,
      rows: [
        ["primary", "boolean", "false"],
        ["destructive", "boolean", "false"],
        ["ghost", "boolean", "false"]
      ]
    },
    {
      label: "State",
      count: 2,
      rows: [
        ["loading", "boolean", "false"],
        ["disabled", "boolean", "false"]
      ]
    }
  ]}
/>
```

### Reference sheet

Pass `reference` for the reference sheet, a component page's props table: the column headings as the page's small uppercase mono label (PROP, TYPE, DEFAULT and DESCRIPTION) on a header row with no fill of its own, 12 px above and below whatever the density; rows 10 px above and below with a rule above each; the columns 16 px apart and 16 px in from the frame's sides; and the frame at the panel corner on the `border` hairline over the card fill. `bordered` only firms the hairline, and `attached` still drops the frame. Pair it with `alignTop` when a cell wraps.
On iOS the table keeps its own look and the prop changes nothing.

```tsx
<DataTable
  reference
  columns={["Prop", "Type", "Default"]}
  rows={[
    ["primary", "boolean", "false"],
    ["small", "boolean", "false"],
    ["loading", "boolean", "false"]
  ]}
/>
```

### Bare table

Pass `bare` for the hairline table with no frame and no fill: the headings in the reference sheet's small uppercase mono label over a `field-border` rule 10 px below them, a `border` rule under every row, the first column flush with the table's start, each cell keeping 12 px clear at its end inside its column's width (so a fixed `width` is the whole column), and 12 px above and below whatever the density. `reference` wins when both are passed.
On iOS the table keeps its own look and the prop changes nothing.

```tsx
<DataTable
  bare
  alignTop
  columns={["Family", "Height", "Floor"]}
  rows={[
    ["Controls", "32 · 40 · 48", "—"],
    ["Fields", "40", "—"],
    ["Data", "hug · scrolls", "320"]
  ]}
/>
```

### Matrix

Pass `matrix` for a specimen grid: no frame, no fill and no rules, the headings in the reference sheet's small uppercase mono label, the cells unpadded, the rows 12 px apart and the columns 20 px apart. A column with `fit` takes its widest cell's width, its heading included (a grid's `max-content` track), so a column of buttons lines up at its longest label; a table with `fit` columns pans once they add up to more than it has. `reference` and `bare` win over `matrix`.
On iOS the table keeps its own look and the prop changes nothing.

```tsx
<DataTable
  matrix
  columns={[{ label: "", width: 110 }, { label: "Default", fit: true }, { label: "Disabled", fit: true }]}
  rows={[
    ["primary", <Button primary>Save changes</Button>, <Button primary disabled>Save changes</Button>],
    ["outline", <Button outline>Preview</Button>, <Button outline disabled>Preview</Button>]
  ]}
/>
```

### Top-aligned cells

Pass `alignTop` when a cell may wrap to several lines: every cell sits at the top of its row, so a row's name, type and default stay beside the first line of its description instead of drifting to the row's middle. The selection box and the row actions center on that first line, as they do in a stacked row.

```tsx
<DataTable
  alignTop
  columns={[
    { label: "Prop", minWidth: 150 },
    { label: "Type", grow: 1.2, minWidth: 150 },
    { label: "Description", grow: 2.2, minWidth: 220 }
  ]}
  rows={[
    ["iconLeft", "ReactNode", "An icon before the label. It takes the label's ink and size, and the button keeps its height, so a leading icon never grows a row of buttons."],
    ["href", "string", "Renders the button as a link to this address on the web, and opens it natively elsewhere."]
  ]}
/>
```

### Footer row

Pass `footer` to draw a row inside the table's frame under the last row, and under the pagination bar when the table is `paginated`: 44 px tall with its content centered, for a "Show all" control or a note. One hairline separates it from what sits above it.

```tsx
<DataTable
  columns={["Prop", "Type", "Default"]}
  rows={[
    ["primary", "boolean", "false"],
    ["small", "boolean", "false"],
    ["loading", "boolean", "false"]
  ]}
  footer={<Button link small>Show all 58 props</Button>}
/>
```

### Sparkline trend column

```tsx
<DataTable
  columns={["Page", "7D", "Visits"]}
  rows={[
    ["/pricing", <Sparkline values={[52, 60, 55, 71, 68, 84, 96]} />, "12,480"],
    ["/docs", <Sparkline values={[88, 74, 70, 66, 58, 49, 41]} />, "8,102"],
    ["/blog", <Sparkline values={[34, 42, 39, 51, 60, 66, 78]} />, "5,914"]
  ]}
/>
```

### Avatar identity cells

```tsx
<DataTable
  columns={["Member", "Role"]}
  rows={[
    [<MediaObject compact avatar="AJ" title="Alice Johnson" />, "Admin"],
    [<MediaObject compact avatar="BS" title="Bob Smith" />, "Editor"],
    [<MediaObject compact avatar="RC" title="Rachel Chen" />, "Admin"]
  ]}
/>
```

### Row actions

```tsx
<Stateful initial={[
  ["Alice Johnson", "alice@example.com", "Admin"],
  ["Bob Smith", "bob@example.com", "Editor"],
  ["Rachel Chen", "rachel@example.com", "Viewer"]
]}>
  {(rows, setRows) => (
    <DataTable
      columns={["Name", "Email", "Role"]}
      rows={rows}
      onRowEdit={() => {}}
      onRowCommit={(i, cells) => setRows(rows.map((row, r) => (r === i ? cells.map(String) : row)))}
      onRowDelete={(i) => setRows(rows.filter((_row, r) => r !== i))}
    />
  )}
</Stateful>
```

### Inline editing

```tsx
<Stateful initial={[
  ["/pricing", "12,480"],
  ["/docs", "8,102"],
  ["/blog", "5,914"]
]}>
  {(rows, setRows) => (
    <DataTable
      columns={["Page", "Visits"]}
      rows={rows}
      inlineEdit
      onCellCommit={(i, c, next) =>
        setRows(rows.map((row, r) => (r === i ? row.map((cell, ci) => (ci === c ? next : cell)) : row)))
      }
    />
  )}
</Stateful>
```

### Stacked

Pass `stacks` when the cells carry long text. When the table's own container is at or below `stackBreakpoint` (default `sm`, 640), each row lays its cells out top to bottom at the full width: the first cell leads as the row's title and every later cell sits under its column label, so a paragraph reads at the table's width instead of a column's share of it. The header row stays only while it holds a control (a sortable column, as here, or the box that selects every row),
the selection box and row actions keep their places, and on iOS the table stacks instead of collapsing to its first column.
Above the breakpoint it is the ordinary table.

```tsx
<DataTable
  stacks
  sortable
  columns={["Setting", "Default", "Description"]}
  rows={[
    ["Session timeout", "30 minutes", "Signs a member out after this long without activity. Shorter timeouts suit shared devices; longer ones suit a personal laptop."],
    ["Password length", "12 characters", "The shortest password a member can choose. Longer minimums resist guessing, and a passphrase meets them easily."],
    ["Recovery codes", "10 codes", "One-time codes a member can use when their authenticator is unavailable. Each code works once."]
  ]}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### default

**Do** — Use the built-in paginated footer so the search result is always anchored to the total.

```tsx
<Card flat flush style={{ overflow: "hidden" }}>
  <Row snug alignCenter between pad>
    <Input small placeholder="Search users..." />
    <Button outline small>Export</Button>
  </Row>
  <Divider />
  <DataTable attached paginated pageSize={3} columns={["Name", "Email"]} rows={[
    ["Alice Johnson", "alice@example.com"],
    ["Bob Smith", "bob@example.com"],
    ["Rachel Chen", "rachel@example.com"],
    ["Dan Wright", "dan@example.com"],
    ["Eve Park", "eve@example.com"]
  ]} />
</Card>
```

**Don't** — Wiring search but dropping the footer leaves the user with no result count or way to page through 142 rows.

```tsx
<View style={{ overflow: "hidden", borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, maxWidth: 520 }}>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8, borderBottomWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, padding: 12 }}>
    <Container xs start><Input small placeholder="Search users..." /></Container>
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%" }} />
    <Button outline small>Export</Button>
  </View>
  <DataTable columns={["Name", "Email"]} rows={[
    ["Alice Johnson", "alice@example.com"],
    ["Bob Smith", "bob@example.com"],
    ["Rachel Chen", "rachel@example.com"]
  ]} />
</View>
```

### bulk

**Do** — Pair the selection with a bulk bar that leads with the non-destructive action and keeps Delete visually distinct.

```tsx
<Card flat flush style={{ overflow: "hidden" }}>
  <Row snug alignCenter between pad>
    <Typography tiny muted>2 selected</Typography>
    <Row snug alignCenter>
      <Button outline small>Bulk edit</Button>
      <Button destructive small>Delete</Button>
    </Row>
  </Row>
  <Divider />
  <DataTable attached selectable defaultSelectedKeys={[0, 2]} columns={["Name", "Email"]} rows={[
    ["Alice Johnson", "alice@example.com"],
    ["Bob Smith", "bob@example.com"],
    ["Rachel Chen", "rachel@example.com"]
  ]} />
</Card>
```

**Don't** — Surfacing only the destructive Delete on a selection invites accidental data loss with no safer path.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8, borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, padding: 12, maxWidth: 520 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>3 selected</Text>
  <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%" }} />
  <Button destructive small>Delete</Button>
</View>
```

### filter

**Do** — Echo the live result count next to the filter so its effect is visible.

```tsx
  <Card flat padded>
    <Row snug alignCenter between>
      <Row snug alignCenter>
        <Typography tiny muted>Status:</Typography>
        <Column><Select value="All" options={["All", "Active", "Inactive"]} small /></Column>
      </Row>
      <Typography tiny muted>142 results</Typography>
    </Row>
  </Card>
```

**Don't** — A filter control with no result count leaves the user guessing whether the filter narrowed anything.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8, borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, padding: 12, maxWidth: 520 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Status:</Text>
  <Select value="All" options={["All", "Active", "Inactive"]} small />
</View>
```

### empty

**Do** — Keep the header and let the built-in emptyMessage span a centered row so the structure stays intact.

```tsx
  <DataTable bordered columns={["Name", "Email", "Status"]} rows={[]} emptyMessage="No results found." />
```

**Don't** — Hiding the body entirely on no results collapses the table and looks broken.

```tsx
  <DataTable bordered columns={["Name", "Email", "Status"]} rows={[]} />
```

### loading

**Do** — Use the built-in loading skeletons so the load reads as the table taking shape in place.

```tsx
  <DataTable bordered loading columns={["Name", "Email", "Status"]} rows={[]} />
```

**Don't** — A bare "Loading…" string gives no sense of progress and reads like static content.

```tsx
<View style={{ overflow: "hidden", borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, maxWidth: 520 }}>
  <DataTable columns={["Name", "Email", "Status"]} rows={[]} />
  <View style={{ alignItems: "center", paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingVertical: 32 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Loading…</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

## Supported props

### DataTableProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| columns | (string \| DataTableColumn)[] | yes |  | Columns: a header label per column, or a `DataTableColumn` descriptor for per-column alignment (`numeric`/`centered`), a fixed `width`, and sorting (`sortable`, `sortValue`). Strings and descriptors mix freely. Treat the array and descriptors as immutable: replace both when a column changes. |
| rows | ReactNode[][] \| undefined | no |  | Row data: an array of rows, each an array of cells (one per column). A cell is a string (rendered in the default cell type) or any ReactNode for a custom cell, such as a link, a `Badge`, or a monospace name (rendered directly). Treat this data as immutable: replace the outer array and each changed row when data changes, so cached sorting and pagination update correctly. |
| groups | DataTableGroup[] \| undefined | no |  | Group the rows under titled bands (the props table's "Intent", "Size" and "State" groups): each group draws a band spanning every column, its label, an optional adornment and an optional count on the sunken fill, then its own rows. Given `groups`, the table's rows are the groups' rows in order and `rows` is ignored; every row index a callback reports (`onRowPress`, `onRowEdit`, `rowKey` and the rest) counts through them in that order. Sorting reorders rows within their group and never moves a group; paging pages the rows, and each page draws the band of every group it shows. A group with no rows draws no band. |
| striped | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tint every other data row for easier horizontal scanning. |
| bordered | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Draw the table's frame on the firmer field boundary rather than the hairline. |
| attached | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The table sits flush inside a frame its parent draws (a `flush` Card, a bordered panel that clips to its corners), so it draws no frame of its own. Without it a standalone table frames itself (on the web and Android, a hairline at the table corner over the card fill), which is the standalone look. |
| stacks | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Responsive: when the table's own CONTAINER is at or below `stackBreakpoint` (default `sm` = 640), each row lays its cells out top to bottom at the full width instead of side by side, so long text reads at the width of the table rather than a column's share of it. The first cell leads the row as its title; every later cell carries its column label above its value. The header row is drawn only while it holds a control (a sortable column, or the box that selects every row), as a band of its labels that wraps; the selection box and the row actions stay at the row's leading and trailing edges. A stacked table never pans, and on iOS it stacks instead of collapsing to its first column. Container-measured with a viewport seed for the first frame, like Row `stacks`; crossing the breakpoint changes the layout only. |
| stackBreakpoint | BreakpointKey \| undefined | no |  | The breakpoint at and below which `stacks` stacks the rows (default `"sm"`). Only meaningful with `stacks` (DEV warns without it). |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tighter vertical padding on header and data cells. |
| comfortable | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Looser vertical padding on header and data cells. |
| reference | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The reference sheet (a component page's props table): the column headings as the page's small uppercase mono label on a header row with no fill of its own, 12 px above and below whatever the density; rows 10 px above and below with a rule above each; the columns 16 px apart and 16 px in from the frame's sides; and the frame at the panel corner on the `border` hairline over the card fill, so `bordered` only firms the hairline and `attached` still drops the frame. On iOS the table keeps its own look and this changes nothing. |
| bare | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The bare hairline table: no frame and no fill, a `field-border` rule under the headings (the reference sheet's mono uppercase label) and a `border` rule under every row, the first column flush with the table's start, each cell keeping 12 px clear at its end inside its column's width, and 12 px above and below whatever the density. `reference` wins over it. On iOS the table keeps its own look and this changes nothing. |
| matrix | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The specimen matrix (a section page's states grid): no frame, no fill and no rules, the headings as the page's small uppercase mono label in the third ink, the cells unpadded, the rows 12 px apart and the columns 20 px apart. Pair it with `fit` columns for the hand-off's content-sized tracks. `reference` and `bare` win over it. On iOS the table keeps its own look and this changes nothing. |
| alignTop | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Align every cell to the top of its row rather than its middle, so a row whose description wraps keeps its name, type and default beside the description's first line. The selection box and the row actions center on that first line, as they do in a stacked row. |
| footer | ReactNode | no |  | A row drawn inside the table's frame under the last row (and under the pagination bar when `paginated`): 44 px tall with its content centered, for a "Show all" control or a note. A hairline separates it from what sits above it: the one the last row draws already, or its own where nothing above it draws one. |
| sortable | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Make every column sortable: pressing a header cycles ascending, descending, off. A column descriptor opts back out with `sortable: false`. Sorting is self-managed out of the box; control it via `sort`/`onSortChange`. |
| sort | DataTableSort \| null \| undefined | no |  | Controlled sort state (`null` = unsorted). Omit for uncontrolled use. |
| defaultSort | DataTableSort \| null \| undefined | no |  | Initial sort for uncontrolled use. |
| onSortChange | ((sort: DataTableSort \| null) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired with the next sort (or `null` when cleared) on header press. |
| selectable | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Row selection: a leading checkbox column with a select-all header checkbox (indeterminate on a partial selection). Selection is keyed by `rowKey` (the row's original index when omitted) and self-managed out of the box; control it via `selectedKeys`/`onSelectionChange`. When no `onRowPress` is set, pressing anywhere on a row toggles it. |
| selectedKeys | (string \| number)[] \| undefined | no |  | Controlled selected row keys. Omit for uncontrolled use. |
| defaultSelectedKeys | (string \| number)[] \| undefined | no |  | Initial selected row keys for uncontrolled use. |
| onSelectionChange | ((keys: Array<string \| number>) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired with the next selected keys when a row or the select-all is toggled. |
| paginated | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Page the rows through a built-in footer (the kit Pagination): a "Showing X-Y of N" range with Prev/Next, plus the selection count when `selectable`. Sorting applies before paging. Self-managed out of the box; control the page via `page`/`onPageChange`. |
| pageSize | number \| undefined | no |  | Rows per page (CONTROLLED; default 10, or the first of `pageSizes`). |
| defaultPageSize | number \| undefined | no |  | Initial rows per page for uncontrolled use. |
| pageSizes | number[] \| undefined | no |  | Selectable rows-per-page values. Supplying them upgrades the footer to the Pagination `withSize` variant (a "Rows per page" selector). |
| onPageSizeChange | ((size: number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired with the next rows-per-page value when the footer selector changes it. |
| page | number \| undefined | no |  | Current page, 1-based (CONTROLLED). Omit for uncontrolled use. |
| defaultPage | number \| undefined | no |  | Initial page for uncontrolled use. |
| onPageChange | ((page: number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired with the next 1-based page when the footer pagination navigates. |
| loading | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Loading state: the body renders pulsing skeleton placeholder rows (one per would-be row on the page) instead of data. |
| emptyMessage | ReactNode | no |  | What to render, centered under the header, when `rows` is empty (and not `loading`). A string gets the muted caption type; any ReactNode renders as given (an `EmptyState`, a retry Button). Omitted = just the header row, as before. |
| onRowPress | ((row: ReactNode[], index: number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | When set, each data row is pressable, reporting the row data and its index in `rows`. A press anywhere on the row acts; the keyboard and screen-reader path is a button inside the row's FIRST column, named from the row's plain text cells (or, when it has none, by that cell's own content). The row itself stays a `row`, so keep your own controls out of the first column here: a control there would nest inside the activator. |
| onRowEdit | ((rowIndex: number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Row editing: passing this adds a trailing actions column with a pencil button per row. Pressing the pencil opens the row's edit mode (its string cells become fields with a trailing Save/Cancel pair) and fires this with the row's original index in `rows`. Save reports the edited cells through `onRowCommit`; Cancel (or Escape in a field) closes without committing. |
| onRowDelete | ((rowIndex: number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Row deletion: passing this adds a delete (bin) button to the trailing actions column. Delete is second-press confirm: the first press ARMS it (the bin turns destructive and its accessible name says confirm), a second press within the confirm window fires this with the row's original index, and pressing anywhere else in the table (or the window lapsing) disarms. |
| inlineEdit | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Let string cells be edited in place: pressing one swaps it to a field. Enter or blur commits through `onCellCommit`; Escape restores the cell. Custom ReactNode cells (badges, links) are not editable. |
| onCellCommit | ((rowIndex: number, colIndex: number, next: string) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when an `inlineEdit` cell commits (Enter or blur) with a changed value: the row's original index in `rows`, the column index, and the next text. Data stays yours: re-render with updated `rows` to keep the edit. |
| onRowCommit | ((rowIndex: number, cells: ReactNode[]) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when a pencil-opened row edit is saved: the row's original index in `rows` and the full cells array with the edited strings in place (custom ReactNode cells pass through unchanged). |
| virtualized | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Render the data rows through a windowed `FlatList` instead of mounting every row up front, for large tables. The header row stays fixed above it. Give the table a bounded height (via `style`, e.g. `{ maxHeight: 400 }`) so the body can scroll; without one it warns and renders eagerly. Default mounts all rows. |
| rowKey | ((row: ReactNode[], index: number) => string \| number) \| undefined | no |  | Stable key for a row, derived from the row data and its index in `rows`. Selection is keyed by it, and it keeps React row identity stable when rows reorder (sorting, live data) and a cell is a stateful custom ReactNode. When omitted, rows key off their original array index (safe for string/number cells and stateless custom cells; selection then tracks row POSITIONS, so supply a real key when the data itself can be reordered, inserted, or deleted). Keep this function pure; replace its identity when external data changes how keys are derived, so the cached selection summary updates. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# DepthChart

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/charts/depth-chart/depth-chart.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/depth-chart

## Public imports

```tsx
import { DepthChart } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

The order-book view: cumulative bid and ask step areas mirrored around the spread, bids in the success tone and asks in destructive, on a numeric price axis.

## Usage

```tsx
<DepthChart
  title="OLY order book"
  bids={[
    { price: 191.3, size: 80 },
    { price: 191.15, size: 120 },
    { price: 191.0, size: 116 },
    { price: 190.85, size: 118 },
    { price: 190.7, size: 176 },
    { price: 190.55, size: 190 },
    { price: 190.4, size: 210 },
    { price: 190.25, size: 236 }
  ]}
  asks={[
    { price: 191.6, size: 90 },
    { price: 191.75, size: 122 },
    { price: 191.9, size: 110 },
    { price: 192.05, size: 154 },
    { price: 192.2, size: 154 },
    { price: 192.35, size: 210 },
    { price: 192.5, size: 222 },
    { price: 192.65, size: 240 }
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Compact

```tsx
<DepthChart
  compact
  bids={[
    { price: 191.3, size: 90 },
    { price: 191.15, size: 150 },
    { price: 191.0, size: 220 },
    { price: 190.85, size: 310 },
    { price: 190.7, size: 420 }
  ]}
  asks={[
    { price: 191.6, size: 110 },
    { price: 191.75, size: 180 },
    { price: 191.9, size: 260 },
    { price: 192.05, size: 350 },
    { price: 192.2, size: 470 }
  ]}
/>
```

### Spread guide

`spread` draws a dashed guide midway between the best bid and the best ask, with its label in a pill at the guide's top.

```tsx
<DepthChart
  title="OLY order book"
  spread="spread 0.16%"
  bids={[
    { price: 191.3, size: 80 },
    { price: 191.0, size: 116 },
    { price: 190.7, size: 176 }
  ]}
  asks={[
    { price: 191.6, size: 90 },
    { price: 191.9, size: 110 },
    { price: 192.2, size: 154 }
  ]}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### Both sides of the book

**Do**: Pass the bids and the asks together; the two sides meet at the spread, the gap a trader reads first.

```tsx
<DepthChart
  compact
  bids={[
    { price: 191.3, size: 90 },
    { price: 191.15, size: 150 },
    { price: 191.0, size: 220 },
    { price: 190.85, size: 310 },
    { price: 190.7, size: 420 }
  ]}
  asks={[
    { price: 191.6, size: 110 },
    { price: 191.75, size: 180 },
    { price: 191.9, size: 260 },
    { price: 192.05, size: 350 },
    { price: 192.2, size: 470 }
  ]}
/>
```

**Don't**: Plot one side alone: with no asks the price axis covers only the bids, nothing marks the spread, and the Asks legend entry labels nothing.

```tsx
<DepthChart
  compact
  bids={[
    { price: 191.3, size: 90 },
    { price: 191.15, size: 150 },
    { price: 191.0, size: 220 },
    { price: 190.85, size: 310 },
    { price: 190.7, size: 420 }
  ]}
  asks={[]}
/>
```

## Supported props

### DepthChartProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bids | DepthLevel[] | yes |  | Bid levels (any order; sorted internally). |
| asks | DepthLevel[] | yes |  | Ask levels (any order; sorted internally). |
| title | string \| undefined | no |  | Optional heading shown above the plot. |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Density (omit for the default plot size). |
| plain | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Strip the card surface for nesting inside an existing card (mirrors Stats). |
| hideLegend | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Furniture visibility. |
| hideGrid | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Furniture visibility. |
| hideAxes | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Furniture visibility. |
| formatValue | ((v: number) => string) \| undefined | no |  | Formats tick labels and accessible values (data formatting, not styling). |
| spread | string \| undefined | no |  | The spread's label ("spread 0.12%"): drawn as a dashed guide midway between the best bid and the best ask, with this label in a pill at its top. Omit for no guide. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

# DescriptionList

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/molecules/description-lists/description-lists.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/description-lists

## Public imports

```tsx
import { DescriptionList } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Key-value pairs in stacked, two-column, or inline-edit layouts. Used for detail panels, settings, and profile views. Rows flagged `update` carry a working in-place editor: Update opens it, Enter or Save commits the new value and fires `onUpdate`, Escape or Cancel dismisses it. `muted` sets each text value as a note beside its term, in the small type and the muted ink, for a list that explains its terms (a key and its effect) rather than reporting data; a node value renders as given, and a platform skin whose value detail is already the secondary ink keeps its type.

The rows axis (pick one; `ruled` wins over `divided`): `divided` draws a hairline under every row but the last, the two-column detail look. `ruled` draws the v4 hand-off's accessibility-card rows: a 1 px top rule on every row, the first included, so the list reads as a table that starts under its caption, each row padded 9 above and below with nothing beside, and in the two-column layout the term hugging its content over a 120 floor with 14 to the value.

The density axis: `compact` tightens the ruled rows to the hand-off's semantics-card rows, each padded 8 above and below with 12 to the value, the two-column term a fixed 110 column, and the value at the top of its row (so a wrapping row of badges starts level with its term); the plain and divided rows have no compact step, so `compact` without `ruled` changes nothing.

## Usage

```tsx
<DescriptionList
  items={[
    { term: "Full name", value: "Rachel Chen" },
    { term: "Email", value: "rachel.chen@example.com" },
    { term: "Role", value: "Admin" }
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Card

```tsx
<DescriptionList
  card
  title="Application details"
  subtitle="Personal information and credentials."
  items={[
    { term: "Full name", value: "Rachel Chen" },
    { term: "Email", value: "rachel.chen@example.com" },
    { term: "Role", value: "Admin" }
  ]}
/>
```

### Inline

Each value sits on the right of its term. A value too wide to fit beside its term (a long id with its Copy button in a narrow sidebar) wraps onto its own line under the term, still at the trailing edge, so the list never runs past its container.

```tsx
<DescriptionList
  inline
  items={[
    { term: "Status", value: "Active" },
    { term: "Seats", value: "12 of 20" },
    { term: "Renews", value: "Mar 1, 2026" }
  ]}
/>
```

### Rich values

A row's value can compose real atoms: `status`/`badge` render Badges, `avatars` renders an overlapping AvatarGroup (`overflow` folds the rest into its "+N" chip), and `copyValue` appends a ghost Copy button that hands the string to `onCopy` (wire your clipboard there).

```tsx
<DescriptionList
  twoColumn
  items={[
    { term: "Status", value: "Active", status: true },
    { term: "Plan", value: "Pro", badge: true },
    { term: "Members", value: "8 members", avatars: [{ name: "Rachel Chen" }, { name: "Alan Turing" }, { name: "Grace Hopper" }], overflow: 5 },
    { term: "Client ID", value: "clnt_01H2X8K9", mono: true, copyValue: "clnt_01H2X8K9" }
  ]}
/>
```

### Node values

A `term` or `value` may be any node, as a DataTable cell may: a string or number takes the list's own type and the per-item forms (`badge`, `status`, `mono`, `copyValue`, `update`), and any other node renders as given in its place, here a row of Badges. A node value yields to its cell, so a wrapping Row wraps at the cell's width instead of running past the list. An `update` row needs a text value to edit.

```tsx
<DescriptionList
  twoColumn
  divided
  items={[
    { term: "Role", value: <Row snug wrap><Badge soft>button</Badge></Row> },
    { term: "States", value: <Row snug wrap><Badge soft>disabled</Badge><Badge soft>busy</Badge><Badge soft>loading</Badge><Badge soft>pressed</Badge><Badge soft>focused</Badge><Badge soft>hovered</Badge></Row> },
    { term: "Keyboard", value: "Enter and Space activate it" }
  ]}
/>
```

### Ruled

Every row carries a top rule, the first included, under a caption the parent sets; the term hugs its content over a 120 floor.

```tsx
<DescriptionList
  twoColumn
  ruled
  items={[
    { term: <Kbd>Enter</Kbd>, value: "Activates" },
    { term: <Kbd>Space</Kbd>, value: "Activates" },
    { term: <Kbd>Tab</Kbd>, value: "Moves focus to the next control" }
  ]}
/>
```

### Compact ruled

The semantics-card rows: 8 above and below, 12 to the value, the term a fixed 110 column and the value at the top of its row.

```tsx
<DescriptionList
  twoColumn
  ruled
  compact
  items={[
    { term: "Roles", value: <Row compact wrap><Badge mono small>button</Badge></Row> },
    { term: "States", value: <Row compact wrap><Badge mono small>disabled</Badge><Badge mono small>busy</Badge><Badge mono small>loading</Badge><Badge mono small>pressed</Badge><Badge mono small>focused</Badge><Badge mono small>hovered</Badge></Row> },
    { term: "ARIA on web", value: <Row compact wrap><Badge mono small>aria-busy</Badge><Badge mono small>aria-disabled</Badge></Row> }
  ]}
/>
```

### Inline-edit

```tsx
<DescriptionList
  twoColumn
  items={[
    { term: "Name", value: "Rachel Chen", update: true },
    { term: "Email", value: "rachel.chen@example.com", update: true }
  ]}
/>
```

### Muted notes

Each value explains its term: a key and what it does, the value in the small type and the muted ink.

```tsx
<DescriptionList
  twoColumn
  divided
  muted
  items={[
    { term: <Kbd comfortable>Enter</Kbd>, value: "Activates" },
    { term: <Kbd comfortable>Space</Kbd>, value: "Activates" },
    { term: <Kbd comfortable>Tab</Kbd>, value: "Moves focus on" }
  ]}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### Two-column

**Do** — Fix the label column wide enough for the longest term so every value lines up on one edge.

```tsx
<DescriptionList twoColumn divided items={[
  { term: "Client identifier", value: "clnt_01H2X8K9P3Q7VN4W6R5T0JYMZF", mono: true },
  { term: "Status", value: "Active", status: true }
]} />
```

**Don't** — A too-narrow label column wraps the longest term and knocks the two columns out of alignment.

```tsx
<View>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "baseline", gap: 16, borderBottomWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, paddingVertical: 12 }}>
    <Text style={{ width: 64, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Client identifier</Text>
    <Text style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", fontSize: 12.5, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground, fontFamily: "monospace" }}>clnt_01H2X8K9P3Q7VN4W6R5T0JYMZF</Text>
  </View>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "baseline", gap: 16, paddingVertical: 12 }}>
    <Text style={{ width: 64, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Status</Text>
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%" }}>
      <Badge status success>Active</Badge>
    </View>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Inline-edit

**Do** — Give every editable row a trailing Update affordance so the inline editor is discoverable; pressing it opens the editor in place, and Enter or Save commits.

```tsx
<DescriptionList twoColumn items={[
  { term: "Name", value: "Rachel Chen", update: true },
  { term: "Email", value: "rachel.chen@example.com", update: true }
]} />
```

**Don't** — Editable rows that look identical to read-only ones give no hint a value can be changed.

```tsx
<DescriptionList twoColumn items={[
  { term: "Name", value: "Rachel Chen" },
  { term: "Email", value: "rachel.chen@example.com" }
]} />
```

### Stacked

**Do** — Keep the label small, uppercase, and muted above a full-weight value so the data stays primary.

```tsx
<DescriptionList stacked items={[
  { term: "Full name", value: "Rachel Chen" },
  { term: "Email", value: "rachel.chen@example.com" }
]} />
```

**Don't** — Muting the value and bolding nothing inverts the hierarchy; the label outweighs the data it describes.

```tsx
<View style={{ maxWidth: 320, gap: 16 }}>
  <View style={{ gap: 4 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens.foreground }}>Full name</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Rachel Chen</Text>
  </View>
  <View style={{ gap: 4 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens.foreground }}>Email</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>rachel.chen@example.com</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

# Dialog

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/dialog/dialog.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/dialog

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Dialog } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A modal dialog: a centered panel over a dimmed backdrop, which glass on the web also blurs, with a title, an optional description, a body for real content like a form, and right-aligned actions. Use it for a focused task that warrants interrupting the page; reach for the Alert Dialog for a terse yes/no confirmation.

On light glass, the description and currency prefix use the stronger foreground color. For custom body content, use the default `Typography` foreground for message copy over the dimmed background.

Browser Escape and iOS accessibility escape cancel the foremost open child
overlay before the dialog.
Cancelling the dialog calls `onCancel` and requests
`open=false`, including destructive dialogs and dialogs with custom children.
A controlled owner may keep it open; that request never confirms an action.

Pass `dismissible` to let a backdrop press follow the same cancel policy. It is
off by default, so existing dialogs and destructive confirmations keep their
current outside-press behavior. The scrim is excluded from keyboard navigation.

Use `form overlay dismissible` for the original Argus application dialog: a
persistent title and optional `description`, a close action, and scrolling body
and `footer` content. `panelWidth` bounds the form (560 pixels by default), and
the viewport keeps a twenty-pixel safe-area inset. The web treatment preserves
Argus’s 28-pixel content inset, 17-pixel title, rounded card, shadow, and lightly
frosted dim. A form with no trigger contributes no layout wrapper to its caller.
Nested menus receive Escape before the dialog; focus stays in the open modal.

For a conversation or other workspace with its own scroll region, use
`form workspace overlay`. The dialog measures a safe-area-bounded viewport
height; its header and optional `footer` stay fixed while `children` fill the
remaining space. Put the workspace's scrollable content inside `children` and
keep its composer or other controls as siblings of that scroll region. The
workspace body does not add an outer scrollport. `workspaceHeader` adds content
below the title and description in the fixed header, such as a step indicator.
This mode is intended for an overlay form; ordinary forms keep their existing
scrolling body.

Add `compact` to a workspace when short content should determine the panel's
height: `form workspace compact overlay`. The panel hugs the conversation and
composer, then grows up to the same safe-area-bounded viewport maximum. A long
conversation scrolls inside its own thread while the header, composer, and dialog
footer remain visible. The default workspace still fills its available height;
`compact` has no effect without `form workspace`.

Add `embedded` to show an open dialog in a page as a specimen, the way a catalogue
or a showcase does: it keeps its look, its dialog role and its labelling, but it is
not modal. It does not take focus when it opens, trap Tab, return focus, set
`aria-modal`, or cancel on Escape, native back or a backdrop press, so the page
around it keeps its scroll position and its keyboard order. `embedded` is ignored
with `trigger`, which always opens a live modal.

## Usage

```tsx
<Dialog
  trigger="Open dialog"
  title="Refund payment"
  description="The refund posts to the original card in 2 to 3 business days."
  withBody
/>
```

## Variants

### Application form

```tsx
<Dialog form trigger="Edit project" title="Project details" description="Update the project name." footer={<Button primary>Save changes</Button>}>
  <Input label="Name" defaultValue="Platform Core" />
</Dialog>
```


### Banded with an icon

`banded` draws a form dialog in three bands: the header (the `icon`, the title row with
the close and any `workspaceHeader`) over a rule, the body, and the footer under a rule.
`icon` draws its glyph in the accent's soft tile above the title.

```tsx
<Dialog form banded icon={<Icon arrowUpRight decorative />} trigger="Publish" title="Publish release" description="Ship the changes to everyone in the workspace." footer={<Button primary>Publish</Button>}>
  <Input label="Release name" defaultValue="Canvas 4.0" />
</Dialog>
```

### Toolbar header

`toolbar` with `banded` turns the header into a 44 point top bar like a desktop app
window's: the title in the 14 medium face on one line, `headerAccessory` after it, and
`headerActions` before the close action. The description is not drawn, so name the
dialog's purpose in its title. With `workspace` the sidebar runs the full height beside
the bar and the body.

```tsx
<Dialog open embedded banded toolbar onOpenChange={() => {}} title="Plan pacman"
  headerAccessory={<Typography small muted>Autosaved</Typography>}
  headerActions={<Button small ghost>Reset</Button>}>
  <Typography body>The conversation fills the body.</Typography>
</Dialog>
```

### Dismissible

```tsx
<Dialog trigger="Open details" title="Workspace details" dismissible />
```

### Extra small

```tsx
<Dialog trigger="Open dialog" title="Refund payment" xs />
```

### Small

```tsx
<Dialog trigger="Open dialog" title="Refund payment" small />
```

### Medium

```tsx
<Dialog trigger="Open dialog" title="Refund payment" medium />
```

### Large

```tsx
<Dialog trigger="Open dialog" title="Refund payment" large />
```

### Wide

```tsx
<Dialog trigger="Open dialog" title="Refund payment" wide />
```

### Destructive action

```tsx

```

## Do & Don't

### When to use

**Do** — Use the Dialog for a focused task with real content, like a short form.

```tsx
<Dialog open embedded large>
  <Column relaxed>
    <Column tight>
      <Typography lead semibold>Edit profile</Typography>
      <Typography>Update how your name and email appear to teammates.</Typography>
    </Column>
    <Column relaxed>
      <Input label="Name" defaultValue="Ada Lovelace" />
      <Input label="Email" defaultValue="ada@example.com" />
    </Column>
    <Row end snug alignCenter>
      <Button outline small>Cancel</Button>
      <Button primary small>Save changes</Button>
    </Row>
  </Column>
</Dialog>
```

**Don't** — A bare yes/no question does not need the roomier Dialog; that is what the Alert Dialog is for.

```tsx
<Dialog open embedded title="Delete file?" small destructive confirmLabel="Delete" cancelLabel="Cancel" />
```

### Description

**Do** — Keep the description to one supporting line; link out for the full policy.

```tsx
<Dialog open embedded title="Refund payment" description="The refund posts to the original card in 2 to 3 business days." medium confirmLabel="Refund" cancelLabel="Cancel" />
```

**Don't** — A multi-sentence policy dump in the description buries the task under reading.

```tsx
<Dialog open embedded title="Refund payment" description="Refunds are processed through the original payment method. Depending on the bank, the amount can take 2 to 3 business days to appear. Partial refunds are supported. Once submitted a refund cannot be cancelled, and the payout for this period will be adjusted on your next statement." medium confirmLabel="Refund" cancelLabel="Cancel" />
```

### Body form

**Do** — Keep the body to the few fields the task needs; send long forms to a full page.

```tsx
<Dialog open embedded large>
  <Column relaxed>
    <Typography lead semibold>Create project</Typography>
    <Column relaxed>
      <Input label="Name" placeholder="Acme website" />
      <Input label="Key" placeholder="ACME" />
    </Column>
    <Row end snug alignCenter>
      <Button outline small>Cancel</Button>
      <Button primary small>Create</Button>
    </Row>
  </Column>
</Dialog>
```

**Don't** — A seven-field form crammed into a small dialog feels like a page stuffed into a popup.

```tsx
<Dialog open embedded small>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 16, lineHeight: 24, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens["popover-foreground"] }}>Create project</Text>
  <View style={{ marginTop: 20 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground, marginBottom: 6 }}>Name</Text>
    <Input accessibilityLabel="Name" />
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground, marginBottom: 6, marginTop: 12 }}>Key</Text>
    <Input accessibilityLabel="Key" />
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground, marginBottom: 6, marginTop: 12 }}>Description</Text>
    <Input accessibilityLabel="Description" />
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground, marginBottom: 6, marginTop: 12 }}>Lead</Text>
    <Input accessibilityLabel="Lead" />
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground, marginBottom: 6, marginTop: 12 }}>Team</Text>
    <Input accessibilityLabel="Team" />
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground, marginBottom: 6, marginTop: 12 }}>Visibility</Text>
    <Input accessibilityLabel="Visibility" />
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground, marginBottom: 6, marginTop: 12 }}>Template</Text>
    <Input accessibilityLabel="Template" />
  </View>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", justifyContent: "flex-end", gap: 8, marginTop: 24 }}>
    <Button outline small>Cancel</Button>
    <Button primary small>Create</Button>
  </View>
</Dialog>
```

### Actions

**Do** — One primary plus quieter secondaries, right-aligned and labeled with their verb.

```tsx
<Dialog open embedded medium>
  <Column relaxed>
    <Column tight>
      <Typography lead semibold>Unsaved changes</Typography>
      <Typography>You have edits that are not saved.</Typography>
    </Column>
    <Row end snug alignCenter wrap>
      <Button ghost small>Discard</Button>
      <Button outline small>Keep editing</Button>
      <Button primary small>Save</Button>
    </Row>
  </Column>
</Dialog>
```

**Don't** — Three look-alike primary buttons give no signal about the default, safe choice.

```tsx
<Dialog open embedded medium>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 16, lineHeight: 24, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens["popover-foreground"] }}>Unsaved changes</Text>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"], marginTop: 8 }}>You have edits that are not saved.</Text>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", justifyContent: "flex-end", gap: 8, marginTop: 24 }}>
    <Button primary small>Save</Button>
    <Button primary small>Discard</Button>
    <Button primary small>Keep editing</Button>
  </View>
</Dialog>
```

### Destructive action

**Do** — Reserve the destructive tone for the irreversible action it names.

```tsx
<Dialog open embedded title="Delete workspace" description="This removes all projects and cannot be undone." medium destructive confirmLabel="Delete" cancelLabel="Cancel" />
```

**Don't** — A red button on a routine Save trains users to ignore the colour that should mean danger.

```tsx
<Dialog open embedded title="Save changes" description="Update the profile with your edits." medium destructive confirmLabel="Save" cancelLabel="Cancel" />
```

### Size

**Do** — Size the dialog to its content: a single field belongs in xs or sm.

```tsx
<Dialog open embedded small>
  <Column relaxed>
    <Typography lead semibold>Rename</Typography>
    <Input label="Name" defaultValue="Untitled" />
    <Row end snug alignCenter>
      <Button outline small>Cancel</Button>
      <Button primary small>Save</Button>
    </Row>
  </Column>
</Dialog>
```

**Don't** — A 2xl panel around a single field leaves a vast empty expanse beside the input.

```tsx
<Dialog open embedded wide>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 16, lineHeight: 24, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens["popover-foreground"] }}>Rename</Text>
  <View style={{ marginTop: 20 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground, marginBottom: 6 }}>Name</Text>
    <Input accessibilityLabel="Name" value="Untitled" />
  </View>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", justifyContent: "flex-end", gap: 8, marginTop: 24 }}>
    <Button outline small>Cancel</Button>
    <Button primary small>Save</Button>
  </View>
</Dialog>
```

## Supported props

### DialogProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| form | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Structured form: a named header and close action above scrolling body/footer content. |
| workspace | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Give an overlay form a viewport-bounded body that fills between its fixed header and footer. |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Let a workspace hug short content and grow only up to its viewport bound. |

| footer | ReactNode | no |  | Custom actions after the form body; fixed below the body in workspace mode. |
| banded | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Draw the reference's shared workflow panel as three bands split by hairline rules: the header (title, `headerAccessory` and optional `workspaceHeader`), body, and footer. A `workspaceSidebar` stays beside the body. Embedded panels keep their opaque in-page surface without a veil or close action; live panels keep modal presentation. |

| withBody | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Body: render a short form (Amount + Reason fields) inside the panel for the data-driven case. |

| confirmLabel | string \| undefined | no | "Confirm" | Action labels. |
| cancelLabel | string \| undefined | no | "Cancel" | Action labels. |
| open | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Controlled open state. Omit for uncontrolled (the trigger opens it). |
| onOpenChange | ((open: boolean) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when the open state changes (trigger press, confirm, cancel). |
| destructive | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Confirm intent (default is a primary confirm). |
| xs | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Width (pick one; default is the standard panel width). First-match precedence: xs, small, medium, large, wide. |
| small | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Width (pick one; default is the standard panel width). First-match precedence: xs, small, medium, large, wide. |

| overlay | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Presents the dialog OVER the page instead of inline where it is mounted. The default is a contained overlay: a scrim with its own height, sitting in normal flow, which is what the docs catalogue needs to show a dialog inside an example stage. An application confirming a destructive action needs the opposite, and the inline form is actively wrong there: it appends a scrim wherever the component happens to sit, leaves the page behind scrollable and clickable, and still claims `aria-modal`. With `overlay`, the dialog teleports into the nearest `OverlayProvider` and fills it, so `aria-modal` becomes true rather than aspirational. | dismissible | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Cancel when the backdrop is pressed. Off by default, including destructive dialogs. |
| embedded | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Show the open dialog as a non-modal specimen in the page, for a catalogue or a showcase: it keeps its look, its dialog role and its labelling, but does not take focus when it opens, trap Tab, return focus, claim `aria-modal`, or cancel on Escape, native back or a backdrop press. Ignored with `trigger`, which always opens a live modal. |
| accessibilityLabel | string \| undefined | no |  | The dialog's accessible name, for the case where `children` supply the panel body. # Divider

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/divider/divider.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/divider

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Divider } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Horizontal, vertical, with label, with action.

## Usage

A divider spans the width of its parent, so give it a bounded container.

```tsx
<Column>
  <Typography>Profile</Typography>
  <Divider />
  <Typography>Account</Typography>
</Column>
```

## Variants

### Vertical

```tsx
<Row>
  <Typography>Edit</Typography>
  <Divider vertical />
  <Typography>Delete</Typography>
</Row>
```

### Inset

A vertical rule of its own short length, centred in its row with a little space on each
side: the separator between groups in a toolbar or a floating bar, where a rule the row's
full height would read as a wall.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter flush>
  <Button ghost small>Bold</Button>
  <Button ghost small>Italic</Button>
  <Divider vertical inset />
  <Button ghost small>Link</Button>
</Row>
```

### Emphasis

The hairline by default; `strong` for a firmer line, `soft` for a quieter one.

```tsx
<Column snug>
  <Divider soft />
  <Divider />
  <Divider strong />
</Column>
```

### Label

```tsx
<Divider>Or continue with</Divider>
```

### Action

```tsx
<Divider>
  <Button ghost small>Show more</Button>
</Divider>
```

## Do & Don't

### Plain

**Do** — Click a row: group with spacing and reserve a divider for a real break like Sign out.

```tsx
<Column tight>
  <Typography small>Profile</Typography>
  <Typography small>Account</Typography>
  <Typography small>Notifications</Typography>
  <Divider />
  <Typography small>Sign out</Typography>
</Column>
```

**Don't** — Click a row: a divider between every one is noise that competes with the content.

```tsx
<View>
  <Text style={{ borderRadius: 6, paddingHorizontal: 8, paddingVertical: 6, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20 }}>Profile</Text>
  <Divider />
  <Text style={{ borderRadius: 6, paddingHorizontal: 8, paddingVertical: 6, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20 }}>Account</Text>
  <Divider />
  <Text style={{ borderRadius: 6, paddingHorizontal: 8, paddingVertical: 6, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20 }}>Notifications</Text>
  <Divider />
  <Text style={{ borderRadius: 6, paddingHorizontal: 8, paddingVertical: 6, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20 }}>Billing</Text>
</View>
```

### With label

**Do** — Click a provider: keep the label to a few words and let the buttons carry the options.

```tsx
<Column snug>
  <Button primary block>Sign in</Button>
  <Divider>or continue with</Divider>
  <Row snug>
    <Column fill>
      <Button outline block>Google</Button>
    </Column>
    <Column fill>
      <Button outline block>GitHub</Button>
    </Column>
  </Row>
</Column>
```

**Don't** — Click Sign in: a full sentence in the label divider buries the choice.

```tsx
<View style={{ width: 320, maxWidth: "100%", flexDirection: "column", gap: 8 }}>
  <Button primary block>Sign in</Button>
  <Divider>or continue with one of your previously linked third-party accounts</Divider>
</View>
```

### With action

**Do** — Click Show more: the button toggles its label and reveals the rest.

```tsx
<Column snug>
  <Typography small muted>Logged in from 2 new devices · 3 more entries</Typography>
  <Divider>
    <Button ghost small>Show less</Button>
  </Divider>
</Column>
```

**Don't** — Click the button: an action divider that does nothing is just decoration.

```tsx
<Divider>
  <Button ghost small>Show more</Button>
</Divider>
```

### Vertical

**Do** — Click an action: the vertical rule separates inline actions in a row.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter cozy>
  <Typography small>Edit</Typography>
  <Divider vertical inset />
  <Typography small>Delete</Typography>
  <Divider vertical inset />
  <Typography small>Share</Typography>
</Row>
```

**Don't** — Click an action: a vertical rule between stacked items reads as a glitch.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "column", alignItems: "flex-start", gap: 8 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20 }}>Edit</Text>
  <Divider vertical inset />
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20 }}>Delete</Text>
</View>
```

## Supported props

### DividerProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | Optional middle content. With children, a horizontal divider renders a flanking-line + centered-label row (the "with label" / "with action" patterns). A string renders as the uppercase mono caption label; arbitrary nodes (e.g. a button) render as-is for the action pattern. Ignored when `vertical`. |
| horizontal | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Orientation (pick one; default is horizontal). |
| vertical | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Orientation (pick one; default is horizontal). |
| soft | boolean \| undefined | no | false | A quieter rule: the hairline at 60% of its strength. |
| strong | boolean \| undefined | no | false | A firmer rule: the `field-border` line, twice the hairline's strength. |
| inset | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Vertical only: a short rule (18 px) centred in its row with 4 px kept on each side, instead of a rule that stretches to the row's height. The separator between groups in a toolbar or a floating bar. A horizontal divider ignores it. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

<!-- Source: https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/components/drag-drop.md -->
# Drag & drop

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/drag-drop/drag-drop.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/drag-drop

## Public imports

```tsx
import { DragDropProvider, DragHandle, Draggable, DropZone } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A reusable drag-and-drop context: wrap a surface in a `DragDropProvider`, mark droppable regions with `DropZone`, and make items draggable with `Draggable` plus a `DragHandle` grip.

Items lift into a floating ghost and reorder within or across zones, position-aware.
It runs on iOS, Android, and the web from one PanResponder + Animated code path,
and the grip is keyboard- and screen-reader-operable: press Space to grab, the arrow keys to move, Space to drop, Escape to cancel.

The reading direction is respected throughout. In a right-to-left locale a `horizontal` zone lays its items out right to left, so the first position is the rightmost one, the drop indicator meets the row's right edge, and the two horizontal arrows swap roles (Left Arrow moves forward, Right Arrow back, per the WAI-ARIA practices). Vertical lists and the up/down arrows read the same way in both directions.

## Usage

```tsx
<Stateful initial={[
  { id: "a", zone: "list", title: "Design review" },
  { id: "b", zone: "list", title: "Write the tests" },
  { id: "c", zone: "list", title: "Ship the release" },
]}>
  {(cards, setCards) => (
    <DragDropProvider>
      <DropZone bordered id="list" label="Tasks" onDrop={(e) => setCards(applyDrop(cards, e))}>
        <Column snug>
          {cards.map((c) => (
            <Draggable key={c.id} id={c.id} data={c} label={c.title}>
              <Card>
                <Row between alignCenter>
                  <Typography>{c.title}</Typography>
                  <DragHandle label={`Reorder ${c.title}`} />
                </Row>
              </Card>
            </Draggable>
          ))}
        </Column>
      </DropZone>
    </DragDropProvider>
  )}
</Stateful>
```

## Variants

### Bordered zone

Pass `bordered` to a `DropZone` to draw it as a visible drop well: a dashed, sunken surface
with the zone's `label` as an eyebrow over its items. While a drag is over it, its edge and
fill take the accent. Without `bordered` the zone is only a drop target around its children
(a Board lane or a StackedList draws its own surface), and a drag over it lays the same
accent edge and wash across it.

```tsx
<DragDropProvider>
  <DropZone bordered id="queue" label="Queue">
    <Draggable id="tokens" data={{ id: "tokens", zone: "queue" }} label="Tokens">
      <Card compact>
        <Row between alignCenter>
          <Typography small>Tokens</Typography>
          <DragHandle label="Reorder Tokens" />
        </Row>
      </Card>
    </Draggable>
  </DropZone>
</DragDropProvider>
```

### Locked item

Pass `disabled` to a `Draggable` to pin it in place: its grip dims and becomes inert while the
rest of the list stays draggable.

```tsx
<DragDropProvider>
  <DropZone bordered id="list" label="Tasks">
    <Column snug>
      <Draggable id="a" data={{ id: "a", zone: "list" }} label="Design review">
        <Card>
          <Row between alignCenter>
            <Typography>Design review</Typography>
            <DragHandle label="Reorder Design review" />
          </Row>
        </Card>
      </Draggable>
      <Draggable id="b" data={{ id: "b", zone: "list" }} disabled label="Locked task">
        <Card>
          <Row between alignCenter>
            <Typography>Locked task</Typography>
            <DragHandle label="Locked task" />
          </Row>
        </Card>
      </Draggable>
    </Column>
  </DropZone>
</DragDropProvider>
```

### Between columns

A `DropZone` per column; dragging a card moves it into another column at the drop position. The
shared list is a flat array with a `zone` field, and `applyDrop` re-homes the card.

```tsx
<Stateful initial={[
  { id: "t1", zone: "todo", title: "Rotate secrets" },
  { id: "t2", zone: "todo", title: "Draft the review" },
  { id: "t3", zone: "doing", title: "SSO rollout" },
  { id: "t4", zone: "doing", title: "Audit log export" },
]}>
  {(cards, setCards) => (
    <DragDropProvider>
      <Grid columns={2} relaxed>
        {["todo", "doing"].map((zone) => (
          <DropZone bordered key={zone} id={zone} label={zone === "todo" ? "To do" : "Doing"} onDrop={(e) => setCards(applyDrop(cards, e))}>
            <Column snug>
              {cards.filter((c) => c.zone === zone).map((c) => (
                <Draggable key={c.id} id={c.id} data={c} label={c.title}>
                  <Card>
                    <Row between alignCenter>
                      <Typography>{c.title}</Typography>
                      <DragHandle label={`Reorder ${c.title}`} />
                    </Row>
                  </Card>
                </Draggable>
              ))}
            </Column>
          </DropZone>
        ))}
      </Grid>
    </DragDropProvider>
  )}
</Stateful>
```

## Do & Don't

### Grip and fallback

**Do** — Give each item a labeled `DragHandle` and keep a non-drag way to move it. The grip is a keyboard tab stop that grabs on Space and moves with the arrows; a `RowMenu` "Move to" beside it is a good extra path for pointer and assistive-tech users.

```tsx
<DragDropProvider>
  <DropZone id="list" label="Tasks" style={{ width: 280, maxWidth: "100%", minHeight: 96 }}>
    <Draggable id="a" data={{ id: "a", zone: "list" }} label="Design review">
      <Card compact>
        <Row between alignCenter>
          <Typography small>Design review</Typography>
          <Row snug alignCenter>
            <DragHandle label="Reorder Design review" />
            <RowMenu items={[{ label: "Move to Doing", icon: "arrowRight" }]} triggerLabel="Move Design review" />
          </Row>
        </Row>
      </Card>
    </Draggable>
  </DropZone>
</DragDropProvider>
```

**Don't** — Don't make a bare card the only drag surface with no grip and no alternative: whole-card dragging fights taps and scrolling, and it leaves keyboard and screen-reader users with no way to move the item at all.

```tsx
<Card compact>
  <Pressable onPress={() => {}}>
    <Typography small>Design review (drag the whole card?)</Typography>
  </Pressable>
</Card>
```

| style | StyleProp<ViewStyle> | no |  | Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook. |

| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | StyleProp<ViewStyle> | no |  | Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook. |

<!-- Source: https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/components/drawer.md -->
# Drawer

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/drawer/drawer.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/drawer

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Drawer } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A full-screen panel that slides in from an edge: a navigation drawer, a mobile menu, or a bottom action sheet. Built on React Native's Modal,
so it floats over the whole app on iOS, Android, and the web,
over a dimmed scrim that glass on the web also blurs. For a small contextual menu, reach for Dropdown or RowMenu instead.

Drawer provides an overlay host inside its own window. Dropdown, Select, and other anchored children render above the panel without being clipped by its corners; no additional OverlayProvider is needed inside the drawer. A tap outside an open child menu dismisses that menu, and Escape dismisses the child before the drawer. Nested drawers each keep their overlays in their own window.

On iOS, VoiceOver's accessibility escape gesture requests dismissal of the
foremost open child before the drawer.
Android system back uses the same child
ownership.
A controlled child that stays open continues to own later requests;
one request never falls through to its parent. The scrim remains a pointer
target, and the built-in trigger opens the drawer. Sidebar drill-down navigation
has its own back behavior; accessibility escape dismisses the overlay rather
than navigating a sidebar level. Focus restoration remains platform-dependent.

Give a controlled drawer an `accessibilityLabel` when it has no built-in
`trigger`. A drawer with a trigger uses the trigger label as its modal name.

`header` and `footer` pin content around an independently scrolling body. Its
application inset is 20 pixels vertically and 24 horizontally, with 22 between
children. `navigation` gives that body no inset or gap and fills its height.
`plain` preserves the original square Argus side panel and lightly frosted dim on
web; native skins retain their platform panel. `instant` presents and dismisses
without a slide or fade. Existing drawers retain their animated default.

## Usage

```tsx
<Drawer trigger="Open menu">
  <Column padLoose cozy>
    <Typography lead semibold>Menu</Typography>
    <Button ghost block>Home</Button>
    <Button ghost block>Components</Button>
    <Button ghost block>Settings</Button>
  </Column>
</Drawer>
```

## Variants

### Terminal sidebar

`terminal` opens a solid execution screen at the right edge, using the active
light or dark theme even under glass. All four corners round to 12 pixels; the
screen sits 12 pixels inside wider windows and 8 pixels inside windows up to
640 pixels wide. Its width is capped to the available viewport. Header and footer
remain pinned around the scrolling body; `navigation` removes the body inset.
`terminal` wins over edge flags and `plain`. The existing slide, Escape, focus and
Reduced Motion behavior remain in effect (`instant` still skips animation).
`onClosed` fires once after a completed dismissal, allowing a parent to retain the
drawer through its exit animation; an initially closed drawer does not fire it.

```tsx
<Drawer terminal navigation width={820} trigger="Execution" header={<Typography h5>Execution</Typography>}>
  <CodeBlock transcript code={"$ bun test\nRan 42 tests across 6 files.\n42 pass, 0 fail"} />
</Drawer>
```

### Application panel

```tsx
<Drawer plain instant right width={440} trigger="Agent details" header={<Typography h3 bold>Scout</Typography>} footer={<Button secondary>Pause</Button>}>
  <Typography>Recent work and trace details.</Typography>
</Drawer>
```


### Right

```tsx
<Drawer trigger="Right drawer" right>
  <Column padLoose snug>
    <Typography lead semibold>Details</Typography>
    <Typography small muted>A full-height panel on the right.</Typography>
  </Column>
</Drawer>
```

### Open in place

`embedded` draws the drawer open inside its parent (the panel at its edge over the parent's
own dim) for a specimen or a preview: it is a labelled region, not a modal, so it traps no
focus, takes no Escape or hardware back, and its dim passes touches through. It needs no
trigger and fills the parent it is given.

```tsx
<Drawer embedded open right accessibilityLabel="Invite people" header={<Typography h5>Invite people</Typography>}>
  <Input label="Email" placeholder="name@company.com" />
</Drawer>
```

### Bottom sheet

```tsx
<Drawer trigger="Bottom sheet" bottom>
  <Column padLoose snug>
    <Typography lead semibold>Actions</Typography>
    <Typography small muted>A sheet that rises from the bottom edge.</Typography>
  </Column>
</Drawer>
```

### Top sheet

```tsx
<Drawer trigger="Top sheet" top>
  <Column padLoose snug>
    <Typography lead semibold>What's new</Typography>
    <Typography small muted>A sheet that drops down from the top edge.</Typography>
  </Column>
</Drawer>
```

## Do & Don't

### Right tool for the job

**Do** — Use a Drawer for primary navigation or a full sheet of actions that should take over the screen on a phone.

```tsx
<Drawer trigger="Open navigation" left width={260}>
  <Column padLoose snug>
    <Typography lead semibold>Navigation</Typography>
    <Typography small muted>Home</Typography>
    <Typography small muted>Components</Typography>
  </Column>
</Drawer>
```

**Don't** — Use a full-screen Drawer for a small contextual menu; covering the whole screen for two choices is disorienting. Use a Dropdown or RowMenu anchored to the trigger.

```tsx
<Drawer trigger="Edit" right width={240}>
  <View style={{ padding: 20, gap: 10 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, color: tokens.foreground }}>Rename</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, color: tokens.foreground }}>Delete</Text>
  </View>
</Drawer>
```

### DrawerProps

# Dropdown

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/dropdown/dropdown.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/dropdown

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Dropdown } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Floating menus triggered by a button: actions, options, navigation.

On the web the menu is the v4 panel: a card with a hairline and a soft shadow, 36-pixel
rows with quiet icons that take a raised wash under the pointer at once, a mono uppercase
eyebrow over a section, mono shortcuts in their own column, destructive rows in the
destructive ink, and a disabled row in the muted ink rather than faded.
iOS and Android keep their platform
menus (the iOS pull-down menu, the Material 3 menu) in the theme's colours.

In glass mode the menu is a dense-layer glass card under its trigger (or above it
when it fits there); the trigger keeps its place, its press and its accessible
name and state, and a selection commits and closes the menu the moment a row is
pressed. AvatarMenu and the collapsed Navbar menu are built on Dropdown. Solid
mode paints the skin's own menu.

`compact` tightens the web rows to 30 pixels and lets the menu scroll inside
`maxHeight`; with `steadyPress` a press does not tint the row. Selected rows take the
action ink.
Items can carry a stored `value`, `detail`, `description`, `selected` state, and a
`sectionBefore` heading. `keepOpen` leaves refresh-style commands open. A `note`
adds a muted footer. `menuWidth` and `maxHeight` bound the scrolling menu.
Pass `anchorRef` to use an existing trigger without adding another control or
layout wrapper; `accessibilityLabel` names the menu independently of its heading.
Checked choices use browser menu-radio semantics and the native radio trait.

## Usage

```tsx
<Dropdown
  trigger="Actions"
  items={[
    { label: "Edit profile" },
    { label: "Duplicate" },
    { label: "Settings" }
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Project menu

```tsx
<Dropdown compact steadyPress menuWidth={250} trigger="Projects" label="Your projects" note="Only projects you can access appear."
  items={[
    { label: "All my projects", value: "all", detail: "11", selected: true },
    { label: "Platform Core", value: "core", detail: "6", selected: false },
    { label: "Add project", value: "add", sectionBefore: "Manage projects", description: "Open project setup" },
  ]} />
```


### Disabled trigger

```tsx
<Dropdown

  items={[

    { label: "Duplicate" },
    { label: "Settings" }
  ]}
/>
```

```tsx
    { label: "Duplicate" },
    { label: "Archive", disabled: true }
  ]}
/>
```

### Destructive item

```tsx
  ]}
/>
```

### Section label

### Choices and submenus

A `selected` item is the menu's current choice: on the web it takes the accent's soft wash
and a leading check, and the menu keeps the check's column on its other rows. A `submenu`
item draws a trailing chevron, the hint that its `onSelect` opens another menu.

```tsx
<Dropdown
  trigger="View"
  items={[
    { label: "Grid", selected: true },
    { label: "List" },
    { label: "Sort by", submenu: true }
  ]}
/>
```

### Custom trigger

### End alignment

```tsx

  alignEnd
  items={[
```
