# Icon

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/icon/icon.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/icon

## Public imports

```tsx
import { ICON_CATEGORIES, ICON_NAMES, Icon } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Lucide-style outline. 1.75 stroke width, rounded caps. The stroke defaults to the theme foreground token and tracks light and dark automatically; pick other hues with the semantic color booleans (`primary`, `destructive`, `success`, `warning`, `muted`, `subtle`; that order is the precedence). `muted` is the third ink (`subtle-foreground`) and `subtle` the second (`muted-foreground`), the names Typography gives the same two inks. Inside a control that owns a label ink (a Button's `iconLeft` and `iconRight` slots) a glyph with no tone takes that ink instead, the way the hand-off's icons inherit `currentColor`: the primary's contrast ink on a primary button, the muted ink on a quiet one. The precedence is the explicit tone, then the host's ink, then the foreground, so a toned glyph keeps its tone anywhere.

## Usage

```tsx
<Icon shield />
```

## Variants

### Primary

```tsx
<Icon shield primary />
```

### Destructive

```tsx
<Icon shield destructive />
```

### Success

```tsx
<Icon circleCheck success />
```

### Warning

```tsx
<Icon alertTriangle warning />
```

### Muted

```tsx
<Icon shield muted />
```

### Subtle

The second ink, a glyph that reads quieter than the foreground but louder than `muted`.

```tsx
<Icon shield subtle />
```

### Cell

`cell` centres the glyph in a square cell that fills its parent at a 10 px corner, the
tile of a glyph gallery laid out by a `Grid`. On the web a hovered cell takes the
accent's soft wash and its glyph the accent ink.

```tsx
<Grid minTileWidth={40} compact>
  <Icon cell subtle search size={20} accessibilityLabel="search" />
  <Icon cell subtle bell size={20} accessibilityLabel="bell" />
  <Icon cell subtle settings size={20} accessibilityLabel="settings" />
  <Icon cell subtle user size={20} accessibilityLabel="user" />
</Grid>
```

### Disclosure indicator

`disclosure` turns the glyph 180 degrees over the original Argus 180ms ease when
`expanded` changes. Reduce Motion snaps to the target. The existing glyph, color
and stroke props keep their usual meaning.

```tsx
<Icon disclosure expanded decorative chevronDown muted heavyStroke size={14} />
```

### Gallery

`ICON_NAMES` lists every glyph in gallery order, each with its prop `key`, its
typed `label` and its `category`, for an icon picker or a catalog like this one.
`ICON_CATEGORIES` lists the categories in menu order, typed `IconCategory`. This
gallery filters by both: search a name, or pick a category.

```tsx
<IconGallery />
```


## Do & Don't

### Stroke coherence

**Do** — One outline style at 1.75 stroke across the whole set.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter relaxed>
  <Icon home size={28} />
  <Icon search size={28} />
  <Icon bell size={28} />
</Row>
```

**Don't** — Mixed stroke weights and a stray filled glyph make a set look incoherent.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 20 }}>
  <Icon home muted size={20} />
  <Icon search destructive size={34} />
  <Icon bell primary size={28} />
</View>
```

### foreground

**Do** — Leave the stroke at its default: it paints the theme foreground and follows light and dark on its own, no color prop needed.

```tsx
<Icon mail size={28} />
```

**Don't** — Hard-coding a hex stroke pins the icon to one theme; it stays black on a dark surface and disappears.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: tokens.foreground, padding: 12 }}>
  <Icon mail size={28} />
</View>
```

### primary

**Do** — Reserve text-primary for the one active or selected icon; keep the rest muted.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter relaxed>
  <Icon home muted size={22} />
  <Icon star primary size={22} />
  <Icon settings muted size={22} />
</Row>
```

**Don't** — Painting a whole toolbar primary spends the accent on everything, so nothing reads as emphasized.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 20 }}>
  <Icon home primary size={22} />
  <Icon search primary size={22} />
  <Icon settings primary size={22} />
</View>
```

### destructive

**Do** — Keep text-destructive for genuinely destructive actions like delete, so red always means consequence.

```tsx
<Icon trash destructive size={28} />
```

**Don't** — A red download icon implies danger on a perfectly safe action and trains users to ignore the warning color.

```tsx
<Icon download destructive size={28} />
```

### muted

**Do** — Use the muted tone for secondary, inline hint icons where its color matches the helper text.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter snug>
  <Icon info muted size={16} />
  <Typography small muted>Optional, used only for recovery</Typography>
</Row>
```

**Don't** — A muted icon inside a solid primary button reads as disabled and clashes with the high-contrast label.

```tsx
<Pressable style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", gap: 8, borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: tokens.primary, paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingVertical: 8 }}>
  <Icon plus muted size={16} />
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens["primary-foreground"] }}>New project</Text>
</Pressable>
```

### IconProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| disclosure | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Rotate the glyph as an Argus disclosure indicator. |
| expanded | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Open state of a disclosure indicator. |
| heavyStroke | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Strong action/link stroke from the Argus reference. |
| boldStroke | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Standard emphasized metadata stroke. |
| mediumStroke | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The medium toolbar stroke. |
| regularStroke | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The fine navigation stroke. |
| primary | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Color axis: pass one (default foreground). First match wins. |
| primaryForeground | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Contrast color for a glyph on a primary surface (e.g. a primary button). |
| destructive | boolean \| undefined | no | false |  |
| success | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Positive/green status (matches Alert's success tone, scheme-aware). |
| warning | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Caution/amber status (the warning token, scheme-aware; matches Alert/Toast warning). |
| muted | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The third ink (`subtle-foreground`, the hand-off's `--tx3`): a glyph that recedes. |
| subtle | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The second ink (`muted-foreground`, the hand-off's `--tx2`), as Typography's `subtle`. |
| cell | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The glyph centred in a square cell that fills its parent (a Grid tile of a glyph gallery) at a 10 px corner. On the web a hovered cell takes the accent's soft wash and its glyph the accent ink. |

# Image

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/image/image.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/image

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Image } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Displays a local or remote image. Set the `source` (`{ uri }`) and a size, then choose how it fills its box with a fit prop: `cover` (the default) fills the box and crops the overflow, while `contain` fits the whole image inside and letterboxes the spare space.

`stretch`, `center`, `repeat`, and `none` cover the rarer fits. `repeat` tiles a bundled asset (or a `{ uri, width, height }` source) at its point size on every platform, drawing the density variant that matches the screen (`grain@2x.png` on a 2x screen) into each tile; a box with no size of its own is one tile. A remote image with no stated size keeps React Native's own repeat. Remote images load over the network; bundle local assets with `require`. Name an image that carries content with `alt`, and it is announced as an image with that name on every platform; an image with no name is decorative, and assistive tech skips it. The v4 hand-off rounds a standalone photo at 12 (`radius="xl"`); Image draws no corner of its own, so a photo inside a Card or a Video keeps its host's corner. For a circular identity photo with an initials fallback, reach for `<Avatar src="…" name="…" />` rather than rounding a bare Image.

## Usage

```tsx
<Image source={{ uri: "/kira-tanaka.jpg" }} alt="Portrait of Kira Tanaka" width={120} height={120} radius="xl" />
```

## Variants

### Contain

```tsx
<Image source={{ uri: "/liang-bao.jpg" }} alt="Portrait of Liang Bao" contain width={160} height={120} radius="xl" />
```

### Cover

```tsx
<Image source={{ uri: "/ada-lovelace.jpg" }} alt="Portrait of Ada Lovelace" cover width={240} height={96} radius="xl" />
```

## Do & Don't

### Fitting a photo

**Do**: Fill a box of another shape with `cover`: the photo keeps its proportions and crops what falls outside the box.

```tsx
<Image source={{ uri: "/grace-hopper.jpg" }} cover width={240} height={96} accessibilityLabel="Grace Hopper" />
```

**Don't**: Stretch a photo to a box of another shape; `stretch` scales each axis on its own, so the picture squashes out of proportion.

```tsx
<Image source={{ uri: "/grace-hopper.jpg" }} stretch width={240} height={96} accessibilityLabel="Grace Hopper" />
```

# InputOTP

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/input-otp/input-otp.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/input-otp

## Public imports

```tsx
import { InputOTP } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A segmented one-time-code field: `length` cells display the typed characters while one underlying text input captures the keystrokes, so native SMS autofill, the one-time-code keyboard suggestion, and paste all flow into a single value.

Because that one input spans the whole row, the caret is pinned to the end of the code: tap any cell and the next character still lands in the first unfilled one, so a keystroke can never drop into the middle of a partly-entered code. It works controlled (`value` + `onChangeText`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`, or a bare `<InputOTP />` that is typeable out of the box); `onComplete` fires once the code reaches `length` characters. Style and shape it with semantic props: `groups` splits the run into dash-separated chunks, `alphanumeric` accepts letters as well as digits, and `small`, `large`, `masked`, `disabled` and `autoFocus` do what they say.

## Usage

```tsx
<InputOTP />
```

## Variants

### Length

```tsx
<InputOTP length={4} />
```

### Grouped

```tsx
<InputOTP groups={3} />
```

### Alphanumeric

```tsx
<InputOTP alphanumeric defaultValue="G" />
```

### Masked

```tsx
<InputOTP masked defaultValue="1234" />
```

### Sizes

```tsx
<Column relaxed>
  <InputOTP small />
  <InputOTP />
  <InputOTP large />
</Column>
```

### Disabled

```tsx
<InputOTP disabled defaultValue="1234" />
```

## Do & Don't

### Readable codes

**Do** — Size the field to the real code length with `length`, and split a long code with `groups` so the eye can chunk it the way the sender wrote it.

```tsx
<InputOTP length={6} groups={3} />
```

**Don't** — Use `masked` for a code the user is meant to read back from an SMS; the bullets hide whether they typed it correctly.

```tsx
<InputOTP masked defaultValue="123456" />
```

## Supported props

### InputOTPProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| length | number \| undefined | no | 6 | Number of segment cells (and the max code length). Default 6. |
| value | string \| undefined | no |  | Current code (controlled). Only the typed characters, e.g. "123". Omit for uncontrolled use; a bare <InputOTP /> is typeable out of the box. |
| defaultValue | string \| undefined | no | "" | Starting code for the uncontrolled field. Defaults to empty. |
| onChangeText | ((code: string) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Called with the new code (cleaned, sliced to `length`) on each change (both modes). |
| onComplete | ((code: string) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired once when the code reaches `length` digits. |
| groups | number \| undefined | no |  | Split the run into groups of this many cells, separated by a dash: `length={6}` with `groups={3}` reads 123-456. Omit for one unbroken run. |
| alphanumeric | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Accept letters as well as digits, and ask for the text keyboard instead of the number pad. Off by default: a one-time code is digits only. |
| autoFocus | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Focus the field on mount. |
| disabled | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Disable input and dim the cells. |
| masked | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Render a bullet (●) instead of the character, for passcode entry. |
| small | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Size (pick one; default is the medium cell). |
| large | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Size (pick one; default is the medium cell). |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |
| ref | React.Ref<RNTextInput> | no |  | Ref to the underlying React Native host. Supports object refs and callback refs; native methods follow the platform's behavior. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# Input

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/input/input.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/input

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Input } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

The Input component is a React Native text field with semantic boolean props
(`error`, `small`, `large`, `compact`, `disabled`), plus prefix/suffix addons, overlaid
icons (`leadingIcon` / `trailingIcon` with any Canvas glyph as `icon`), a
`passwordToggle` eye for a `secureTextEntry` value, a `clearable` clear
button, and a `shortcut` keycap. Input is single-line; for multi-line entry use the
dedicated Textarea.

On the web the eye shows what pressing it does: the open eye while the value is masked,
the struck-through eye once it is revealed. A field held
focused by an `InteractionOverride` (a docs specimen) draws the web's 1.5px accent caret,
blinking once a second, just after its value, since no real caret shows there.

`shortcut` shows a keyboard shortcut hint at the field's end, the key that focuses a
search field: a compact flat keycap (`<Kbd small flat>`, the 22 px cap; `tiny`, the 20 px
cap, on a `small` field) after the value and any inline suffix and before the trailing
glyphs, 8 px from the field's end and 10 px from the value (8 on a small field). It takes
the keys as Kbd's `keys` does: `"⌘K"` is one cap, `"⌘ K"` two. It is a hint only; bind
the key yourself.

Pass `label` (and `required`) to name the field:
iOS and web render the label
above the control, while Android floats the Material 3 in-container label. On
Android the field grows with the user's text size so the floated label never
meets the value, and a label longer than the field truncates on one line inside
it while the field's accessible name stays the whole label.
The required star is
decorative: a screen reader hears the field as required,
from `aria-required` on
the web and from its name ("Full name, required") on iOS and Android.
A field fills the parent it is given; a step of its own (`xs`, `lg`, …, with
`start` to pin it to the leading edge) or a Container step sets its measure.
Select and the search field share its look, and Field and Form compose that
label with helper and error text.
On iOS the field is the native text field in
Canvas's colors: a card-colored box with a hairline, a muted title above, a glyph
that tints with focus and error, and in solid mode an error wash. Under glass a
wash would cost the field's ink its contrast over the material, so the iOS field
takes none (the web's field a trace in dark only), and the error border, the tinted
glyph and a Field's message carry the state.
A prefix or suffix addon's fill is held to
the same bar: under glass it is only as dense as keeps its text at 4.5:1 over the field,
so in the browser's light palettes and on the iOS field in dark it is a faint trace.

Inside an overlay, Escape follows the overlay's cancellation policy. A supplied
`onKeyPress` runs first and can call `preventDefault()` to handle Escape locally.
Cancelling an IME candidate keeps the overlay open.

On web, the field is a sunken well: 40 pixels tall (32 small, 48 large) at the
10-pixel field corner, a hairline edge, a 12-pixel inset, a regular 14-pixel value
(13 small) and a medium 13-pixel muted label above. The edge darkens under the
pointer, takes the accent with a soft accent halo on focus, and turns red with a
red halo for an error; a read-only field is a dashed edge on no fill, and a
disabled one dims. A prefix sits in a muted box behind a divider, a passive
suffix is inline monospace text before the clear button (a small raised disc with
an x), and an action suffix is a button box at the end.

On iOS the clear button is the system's gray disc with an x, inside the boxed
suffix segment, and the action suffix's label is a semibold 15-point brand label.
On Android the suffix is inline text before the circled-x clear glyph, an errored
field shows a red alert glyph at its end (in place of a clear or eye button), and
a read-only field drops its fill under a dashed frame with a subtle underline.

`eyebrow` uses the original dense uppercase web field label, preserving its
9.5/12.35 metrics and tracking. Other platform label treatments retain their skin.

`soft` uses the brand’s entry-well fill where the skin provides it.
`systemFocus` preserves the platform’s system focus outline. An explicit
`accessibilityLabel` takes precedence over the visible label’s accessible name.

Pass `search` for the toolbar search: a magnifier, a borderless editor, and a
uppercase prompt while empty on web. The prompt names the editor unless
`accessibilityLabel` or `label` supplies its purpose.
iOS draws its search field
(a 36-point muted well) and Android the Material 3 search bar (a 56-dp muted
stadium).
`systemFocus` preserves the system
focus outline for the borderless editor.

## Usage

```tsx
<Input placeholder="rachel.chen@example.com" />
```

## Variants

### Compact

`compact` is an outlined well with a 12px inset and the platform's field corner.
Its default is 40px high with a 14px value; `small` is 32px/13px and `large` is
48px/16px. Labels sit above the well on every platform.

```tsx
<Input compact placeholder="noor@nannier.com" accessibilityLabel="Teammate email" />
```

### Toolbar search

```tsx
<Input search systemFocus placeholder="Search work items" />
```

## Do & Don't

### text

**Do** — Pass `label` so every field carries a persistent, programmatically-linked name.

```tsx
<Input label="Email" placeholder="ada@acme.dev" />
```

**Don't** — A placeholder is not a label; it vanishes the moment the user types and screen readers may skip it.

```tsx
<Input placeholder="Email" />
```

### number

**Do** — Park the unit in a suffix addon so the value stays purely numeric.

```tsx
<Input label="Storage" defaultValue="1024" suffix="GB" />
```

**Don't** — A plain text field lets users type the unit into the value, breaking parsing and validation.

```tsx
<Input label="Storage" defaultValue="1024 GB" />
```

### Read only or disabled

**Do**: Pass `readOnly` for a value people still need to reach. On the web it stays in the tab order and its text stays selectable.
On iOS and Android, React Native maps a read-only field to a disabled native view, so VoiceOver and TalkBack announce it as dimmed and Android cannot select its text.

```tsx
<Input label="Workspace ID" readOnly defaultValue="ws_8f2k1" />
```

**Don't**: Disable a field whose value people must read or copy. `disabled` takes it out of the tab order and announces it as unavailable on every platform.

```tsx
<Input label="Workspace ID" disabled defaultValue="ws_8f2k1" />
```

# Kbd

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/kbd/kbd.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/kbd

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Kbd } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Keyboard shortcut indicator: a raised 24 px key cap with a mono label. `keys`
composes a whole shortcut, one cap per key; `sequence` says "then" between the
caps of keys pressed one after another. A shortcut reads as one accessible name
("⌘+K", "G then C"). `comfortable` pads the cap 3 px above and below its label and
8 px at the sides (25 px tall) for a key set beside what it does, as a reference's
keyboard table lists it; omit it for the 24 px cap with 6 px sides.

Two compact sizes take the cap down for a hint beside a field or a menu: `small`, the
22 px cap with 6 px sides at a 5 px corner and a 500 11 px label, and `tiny`, the 20 px cap
with 5 px sides at a 4 px corner and a 500 10 px label. Size precedence is `small`, then
`tiny`, and a size step wins over `comfortable`. `flat` is the hint cap's edge: one pixel
all round instead of the raised 2 px bottom, and the label in the secondary ink. An
`Input` draws its `shortcut` hint as `<Kbd small flat>` (`tiny` on a small field).

## Usage

```tsx
<Kbd keys="⌘ K" />
```

## Variants

### Single

```tsx
<Kbd>Esc</Kbd>
```

### Combo

```tsx
<Kbd keys="⌘ ⇧ P" />
```

### Sequence

```tsx
<Kbd keys="G C" sequence />
```

### Comfortable

```tsx
<Row alignCenter snug>
  <Kbd comfortable>Enter</Kbd>
  <Typography small muted>Activates</Typography>
</Row>
```

### Compact hint

```tsx
<Row alignCenter snug>
  <Kbd small flat>⌘K</Kbd>
  <Kbd tiny flat>⌘K</Kbd>
  <Kbd small flat>esc</Kbd>
</Row>
```

### In a button

```tsx
<Button outline iconRight={<Kbd keys="⌘ K" />}>Search…</Button>
```

### In a sentence

```tsx
<Row alignCenter tight>
  <Typography small>Press </Typography>
  <Kbd keys="⌘ K" />
  <Typography small> to search.</Typography>
</Row>
```

## Do & Don't

### Single

**Do**: Use `children` for one real key; give each cap exactly one key.

```tsx
<Kbd>Esc</Kbd>
```

**Don't**: Packing a whole shortcut into one key cap reads as a single keystroke that does not exist.

```tsx
<Kbd>⌘K</Kbd>
```

### Combo

**Do**: Pass every key to `keys`; Kbd lays out the caps and reads as one shortcut to a screen reader.

```tsx
<Kbd keys="⌘ ⇧ P" />
```

**Don't**: Hand-assembling caps and separators is verbose and drops the combined accessible name; let `keys` compose the chord.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter tight>
  <Kbd>⌘</Kbd>
  <Typography tiny muted>+</Typography>
  <Kbd>⇧</Kbd>
  <Typography tiny muted>+</Typography>
  <Kbd>P</Kbd>
</Row>
```

### In a sentence

**Do**: Drop a `keys` Kbd inline so the shortcut reads as physical keys.

```tsx
<Row wrap alignCenter tight>
  <Typography small>Press </Typography>
  <Kbd keys="Ctrl K" />
  <Typography small> to search.</Typography>
</Row>
```

**Don't**: Plain-text shortcuts blend into the prose and are easy to miss.

```tsx
<Typography small>Press Ctrl+K to search.</Typography>
```

## Supported props

### KbdProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | A single key label, rendered as one cap. Ignored when `keys` is set. |
| keys | string \| string[] \| undefined | no |  | A multi-key shortcut (a combo, pressed together), rendered as one cap per key. Pass a whitespace-separated string (`"⌘ K"`) or an array (`["⌘", "K"]`). A single entry renders one cap, identical to passing that key as `children`. When set, `keys` takes precedence over `children`. |
| sequence | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Render a key SEQUENCE (press one, then the next): the caps are separated by "then". Only affects the `keys` form. |
| comfortable | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The comfortable cap: padded 3 px above and below its label and 8 px at the sides (25 px tall), the key the hand-off's component page sets beside a key's effect. Omit for the 24 px cap with 6 px sides. |
| small | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The compact 22 px cap: 6 px sides on the small key corner, a 500 11 px label on a 20 px line (the hint a search field or a command palette shows, `<Kbd small flat>`). Size precedence: `small` > `tiny`; a size step wins over `comfortable`. |
| tiny | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The compact 20 px cap: 5 px sides on the tiny key corner, a 500 10 px label on an 18 px line. |
| flat | boolean \| undefined | no | false | The hint cap's edge: one pixel all round (no raised 2 px bottom) and the label in the secondary ink, the keycap a field or a menu shows beside what it opens. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# LineChart

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/charts/line-chart/line-chart.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/line-chart

## Public imports

```tsx
import { LineChart } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Categorical-x series lines with nice y ticks, gridlines, and a legend for multiple series.

`curved` draws a monotone cubic that never overshoots the data, `dots` marks each datum, and `baseline` + `fade` give the trading-app price idiom (dashed previous close, gain/loss auto tone, gradient fill). A series that means success or failure carries its own `success` / `destructive` tone instead of a ramp color. Press or scrub the plot to inspect a category.

## Usage

```tsx
<LineChart
  title="Active users"
  labels={["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul"]}
  series={[
    { label: "Web", values: [119, 122, 131, 147, 157, 176, 182] },
    { label: "Mobile", values: [63, 93, 101, 121, 162, 207, 251] }
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Curved

```tsx
  title="Signups"
  labels={["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]}

  curved
/>
```

```tsx
/>
```

```tsx
/>
```

### Dashed series

A series marked `dashed` draws its line dashed with flat ends, and its legend swatch is a dashed rule: a target or a forecast beside the measured line.

```tsx
<LineChart
  title="Signups vs target"
  labels={["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri"]}
  series={[
    { label: "Signups", values: [42, 48, 45, 61, 58] },
    { label: "Target", values: [50, 50, 50, 50, 50], dashed: true }
  ]}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### Line

**Do** — Compare series that share one scale, and let the legend plus the fixed series colors carry identity.

```tsx
<LineChart
title="Signups"
labels={["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"]}
series={[
  { label: "Web", values: [120, 180, 150, 240, 300, 280] },
  { label: "Mobile", values: [60, 90, 140, 160, 220, 260] }
]}
curved
/>

```

**Don't** — Mix measures of different scales on one axis: the smaller series flatlines against the baseline and reads as noise. Normalize, or use two charts.

```tsx
<LineChart
title="Revenue vs conversion"
labels={["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"]}
series={[
  { label: "Revenue", values: [12000, 18000, 15000, 24000, 30000, 28000] },
  { label: "Conversion rate", values: [2.1, 2.4, 2.2, 2.8, 3.1, 3] }
]}
/>

```

# Listbox

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/listbox/listbox.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/listbox

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Listbox } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A custom select whose options stay on screen: single or multi-select, an optional detail line under each option, and a checkmark on the chosen items. Reach for it when the options need rich rows; prefer `Select` for a simple short list.

The list fills the parent it is given; a step of its own (`xs`, `lg`, …, with `start` to pin it to the leading edge) or a Container step sets its measure.

Neither iOS nor Material 3 ships a listbox, so every platform draws the Canvas v4 list, in its own face:
a chosen row sits on the accent's soft wash with a 16px check at its end in the accent ink, in single and multi select alike, and the check's slot is kept on every row so a choice never reflows a label.

The rows are 10px in with a 500 14/18.2px label (13px small) over a 400 12/16.2px detail in the subtle ink, rounded concentric inside a bordered list, which is the `popover` fill behind the `field-border` hairline at the tile corner with a 4px inset. A pressed row takes the `muted` wash, and on the web a row under the pointer takes the hover wash at once.

Single-select exposes a list of selectable options. With `multi`, it exposes a checkbox group: each row owns its label, checked state, and tap target. Give either mode a meaningful `accessibilityLabel`; the fallback is "Options". Arrow keys and Home/End move focus within one tab stop. Single-select follows focus, while multi-select keeps the current selection until Enter or Space toggles the focused row.

## Usage

```tsx
<Listbox
  accessibilityLabel="Teams"
  items={[
    { label: "Backend", selected: true },
    { label: "Frontend" },
    { label: "Design" }
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Multi

```tsx
<Listbox
  accessibilityLabel="Teams"
  items={[
    { label: "Backend", selected: true },
    { label: "Frontend" },
    { label: "Design", selected: true }
  ]}
  multi
/>
```

### Small

```tsx

  accessibilityLabel="Teams"
  items={[
    { label: "Backend", selected: true },
    { label: "Frontend" },
    { label: "Design" }
  ]}
  small
/>
```

### Large

```tsx

  accessibilityLabel="Teams"
  items={[
    { label: "Backend", selected: true },
    { label: "Frontend" },
    { label: "Design" }
  ]}
  large
/>
```

### Disabled

```tsx

    { label: "Frontend" },
    { label: "Design" }
  ]}
  disabled
/>
```

### Detail line

```tsx
    { label: "Rachel Chen", detail: "rachel@acme.io", selected: true },
    { label: "Ada Lovelace", detail: "ada@acme.io" },
    { label: "Kevin Turner", detail: "kevin@acme.io" }
  ]}
```

### Measure

```tsx
  <Listbox lg start bordered items={[{ label: "lg step, pinned to the start (512)", selected: true }, { label: "Frontend" }]} />
  <Container lg start><Listbox bordered items={[{ label: "Bare, in an lg Container: fills it (512)", selected: true }, { label: "Frontend" }]} /></Container>
</Column>
```

## Do & Don't

### Prefer a native select for simple lists

**Do**: For short, plain lists a native select is lighter, accessible, and uses the platform picker on mobile.

```tsx
<Select defaultValue="Yes" options={["Yes", "No"]} />
```

**Don't**: A custom listbox for two short options is heavier than it needs to be and worse on mobile.

```tsx
<Listbox bordered items={[
    { label: "Yes", selected: true },
    { label: "No" }
  ]} />
```

### single

**Do**: Show exactly one checkmark, mirror it in the trigger value, and close the panel on pick.

```tsx
<Listbox bordered items={[
    { label: "Backend", selected: true },
    { label: "Frontend" },
    { label: "Design" },
    { label: "Platform" }
  ]} />
```

**Don't**: Single-select with two checkmarks lies about state: only one option can be the value.

```tsx
<Listbox bordered items={[
    { label: "Backend", selected: true },
    { label: "Frontend", selected: true },
    { label: "Design" },
    { label: "Platform" }
  ]} />
```

### multi

**Do**: Keep the panel open, toggle each option's own checkmark, and summarize the count in the trigger.

```tsx
<Column tight>
  <Select defaultValue="3 selected" />
  <Listbox multi bordered items={[
    { label: "Backend", selected: true },
    { label: "Frontend", selected: true },
    { label: "Design" },
    { label: "Platform", selected: true }
  ]} />
</Column>
```

**Don't**: Don't close on each pick or echo only the last choice: multi-select needs to keep all selections visible.

```tsx
<View style={{ width: 224, gap: 4 }}>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "space-between", borderRadius: 6, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.input, backgroundColor: tokens.background, paddingHorizontal: 12, height: 36 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens.foreground }}>Backend</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>▾</Text>
  </View>
  <Listbox multi bordered items={[
    { label: "Backend", selected: true },
    { label: "Frontend", selected: true },
    { label: "Design" },
    { label: "Platform", selected: true }
  ]} />
</View>
```

# MediaObject

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/molecules/media-objects/media-objects.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/media-objects

## Public imports

```tsx
import { MediaObject } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Image or icon paired with text content. The fundamental building block for list items, notifications, and comment layouts.

## Usage

```tsx
<MediaObject
  avatar="RC"
  title="Rachel Chen"
  description="Engineering Lead"
  body="Reviewed the latest pull request and left comments on the auth middleware changes."
  bordered
/>
```

## Variants

### Compact

```tsx
<MediaObject compact avatar="RC" title="Rachel Chen" description="rachel.chen@example.com" />
```

### Bare row with meta

```tsx
<MediaObject avatar="RC" title="Rachel Chen" description="Commented on the deploy pipeline." meta="1h" />
```

### Icon

```tsx
<MediaObject bordered title="Security first" description="End-to-end encryption with automatic key rotation." icon={<Icon shield primary size={18} />} />
```

### Action

The trailing `action` slot takes any control; the button's `onPress` is yours to
wire.

```tsx
<MediaObject bordered src="/ada-lovelace.jpg" title="Ada Lovelace" description="ada@example.com" action={<Button outline small>Invite</Button>} />
```

### Numbered step

`bareIcon` draws the `icon` node as it is, with no tinted box around it, for a lead that is its own mark: a numbered `<Badge step>` numbers a list of steps.

```tsx
<MediaObject bareIcon icon={<Badge step default>1</Badge>} title="Intrinsic · no JavaScript" description="Fill or hug inside the parent's bounds, a minWidth floor, wrapping." />
```

### Tappable

Passing `onPress` makes the whole row a single tap target; wire it to your own
handler and every tap runs it.

```tsx
<MediaObject onPress={() => {}} bordered avatar="RC" title="Rachel Chen" description="Engineering Lead" />
```

## Do & Don't

### Avatar

**Do** — Top-align with `start` so the avatar anchors to the first line of the title.

```tsx
<MediaObject bordered start src="/rachel-chen.jpg" title="Rachel Chen" description="Engineering Lead" body="Reviewed the latest pull request and left comments on the auth middleware changes. Need to discuss the token rotation approach before merging." />
```

**Don't** — Centering the avatar against a multi-line body leaves it floating beside the middle of the text.

```tsx
<MediaObject bordered center src="/rachel-chen.jpg" title="Rachel Chen" description="Engineering Lead" body="Reviewed the latest pull request and left comments on the auth middleware changes. Need to discuss the token rotation approach before merging." />
```

### Icon

**Do** — Keep the lead icon box compact with an 18px glyph so it reads as a tidy lead affordance.

```tsx
<MediaObject bordered start title="Security first" description="End-to-end encryption with automatic key rotation." icon={<Icon shield primary size={18} />} />
```

**Don't** — An oversized icon box throws off the optical balance with the two-line text.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "flex-start", gap: 12, borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.card, padding: 16, maxWidth: 480 }}>
  <View style={{ flexShrink: 0, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.15), padding: 8 }}>
    <Icon shield primary size={32} />
  </View>
  <View style={{ minWidth: 0, flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", gap: 2 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens.foreground }}>Security first</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 18, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>End-to-end encryption with automatic key rotation.</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Action

**Do** — Pass `truncate` so long text clips in place and the trailing action stays pinned right.

```tsx
<MediaObject bordered center truncate src="/ada-lovelace.jpg" title="Ada Lovelace" description="ada.lovelace@analytical-engine.example.com" action={<Button outline small>Invite</Button>} />
```

**Don't** — Without truncation a long email wraps and pushes the trailing button out of alignment.

```tsx
<MediaObject bordered center src="/ada-lovelace.jpg" title="Ada Lovelace" description="ada.lovelace@analytical-engine.example.com" action={<Button outline small>Invite</Button>} />
```

## Supported props

### MediaObjectProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | string \| undefined | no |  | Primary line: the bold heading (e.g. a person's name). |
| description | string \| undefined | no |  | Secondary line: muted supporting text under the title (e.g. a role or email). |
| body | ReactNode | no |  | Optional longer body paragraph rendered below the description. |
| meta | string \| undefined | no |  | Trailing metadata text pinned to the right (e.g. "2h ago", "admin"). |

| src | string \| number \| undefined | no |  | Photo for the leading avatar (a URI string or a bundled `require(...)` image); takes precedence over initials. |
| icon | ReactNode | no |  | A leading icon glyph rendered in a tinted square box (stands in for an SVG icon). |
| bareIcon | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Draw the `icon` node as it is, with no tinted box around it: a lead that is its own mark, such as a numbered `<Badge step>` (the Layout page's "try in this order" list). |
| action | ReactNode | no |  | A trailing action node (e.g. a <Button>), pinned to the right edge. |
| onPress | (() => void) \| undefined | no |  | Make the whole row a tappable target (navigate to a detail, select a row). When set, the row renders as a Pressable with a button role and a pressed affordance, so you never hand-roll a Pressable for a tappable media row. |
| center | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Alignment (pick one; default top-aligns with items-start). |
| start | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Alignment (pick one; default top-aligns with items-start). |
| reversed | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Direction (pick one; default leads with the media on the left). |
| leading | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Direction (pick one; default leads with the media on the left). |
| bordered | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Surface. |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Menu-header density: a smaller leading avatar (28px) and title/description type stepped down one size, for a compact identity row (e.g. a menu or dropdown header). Backward-compatible; without it the row keeps its default 40px avatar and type. |
| truncate | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Layout. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# MetricBreakdown

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/charts/metric-breakdown/metric-breakdown.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/metric-breakdown

## Public imports

```tsx
import { MetricBreakdown } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

The decomposed-metric dashboard card: headline value, tone-aware rate, Sparkline trend, per-category share rows, and a chip footer.

It holds a preformatted headline `value` with its caption, an optional secondary `rate` readout under the headline (toned by `rateSuccess`, `rateWarning`, or `rateDestructive`), an optional trend strip drawn by the kit Sparkline at the header's end with a latest-value caption above it, per-category `breakdown` rows with proportional share meters and Stats-style deltas, and a `chips` footer for recent notable codes. Every section is independently optional, so one layout backs OAuth token issuance, API request volume, sign-up sources, and any metric that needs decomposition plus trend in one card.

`detailed` emphasizes the value without repeating its caption, shows a trend arrow beside the rate and places the share rows under a divider. Its spark values are percentages from zero to one hundred; `rateLabel` supplies the period comparison.

## Usage

```tsx
<MetricBreakdown
  value="3,771"
  label="Tokens issued"
  breakdown={[
    { label: "authorization_code", value: 1842, delta: "+12%" },
    { label: "refresh_token", value: 1264, delta: "+4%" },
    { label: "client_credentials", value: 618, delta: "-3%", down: true },
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Rate and trend

```tsx
<MetricBreakdown
  value="25,874"
  label="Requests"
  rate="0.74%"
  rateLabel="4xx + 5xx rate"
  rateSuccess
  spark={[180, 196, 188, 204, 210, 202, 214, 220]}
  sparkUnit="req/s"
/>
```

### Plain, inside a card

```tsx
<Card>
  <MetricBreakdown
    plain
    value="25,874"
    label="Requests"
    breakdown={[
      { label: "GET", value: 18248, delta: "+8%" },
      { label: "POST", value: 6104, delta: "+21%" },
      { label: "PATCH", value: 1212, delta: "-2%", down: true },
    ]}
  />
</Card>
```

### Trend strip without its tag

`hideSparkTag` drops the latest-value tag over the trend strip, when the headline already carries the figure.

```tsx
<MetricBreakdown
  value="$48,210"
  label="Revenue"
  spark={[31, 34, 33, 38, 41, 40, 46, 48]}
  hideSparkTag
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### MetricBreakdown

**Do** - Pass preformatted strings and semantic tone booleans; the card owns the header, trend, rows, and chip anatomy.

```tsx
<MetricBreakdown
value="12.4k"
label="Requests"
rate="0.74%"
rateLabel="Error rate"
rateSuccess
breakdown={[
  { label: "GET", value: 8, delta: "+8%" },
  { label: "POST", value: 4, delta: "+21%" },
]}
/>
```

**Don't** - Rebuilding the header and trend from Text and Sparkline at the call site splits the anatomy the card owns and loses the rows' accessible shares.

```tsx
<View style={{ borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.card, padding: 20, maxWidth: 420, gap: 8 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 22, fontWeight: "600" }}>12.4k</Text>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 11, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>REQUESTS</Text>
  <Sparkline line values={[96, 104, 110, 108, 116]} />
</View>
```

# Navbar

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/navbars/navbars.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/navbars

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Navbar } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Topbars with a brand, navigation links, and an action button. Used as the
primary app-level navigation.

The bar measures its own width: at and below the `sm` breakpoint (640) the links
row automatically collapses into a menu button opening a dropdown of the same
links (the active one checkmarked), so links never clip off a phone screen;
`active` and `onSelect` keep their contract in both renderings.
The menu button
leads the bar, ahead of the logo and brand, where Material 3's top app bar puts
its navigation icon.
Pass `scrolls` to keep every link at every width instead: the bar's content row
then pans sideways inside the bar, with no scroll indicator, and the links never
fold into the menu. `onMenu` still replaces the links when both are passed.

On the web the bar is the v4 hand-off's: 56px tall with a 16px gutter, 32px
capsule links in the interface face, the active one (and a hovered one) on the
`secondary` fill. `floating` lifts it as a pill on the stronger hairline with the
md shade.
On iOS and Android the bar keeps the platform's own navigation bar and
top app bar shape.

In glass mode the active link paints a control-layer pane
(iOS keeps its
inactive capsules and carries the brand fill as glass, web and Android carry
their tinted tile),
and the collapsed menu is Dropdown's dense-layer glass card
under the hamburger. Solid mode keeps the skin's own active tile.

Either cluster takes a caller-supplied element beside its built-in parts:
`brandContent` leads the left one with a logo mark (beside or instead of the
`brand` wordmark) and `actions` leads the right one with free-form trailing
controls (a search button, icon buttons), ahead of `actionLabel` and `avatar`.
`links` is optional, so a console topbar with no middle nav renders neither the
links row nor the menu button that stands in for it.

## Usage

```tsx
<Navbar
  brand="Canvas"
  links={["Dashboard", "Users", "Settings"]}
  actionLabel="New"
  avatar="RC"
/>
```

## Variants

### Bordered

```tsx
<Navbar bordered brand="Canvas" links={["Dashboard", "Users", "Settings"]} />
```

### Floating

```tsx
<Navbar floating brand="Canvas" links={["Dashboard", "Users", "Settings"]} />
```

### Compact

`compact` is the density axis's one member: the tight bar, 44px with a 5px inset
and 2px between every item on the web (a shorter bar with tighter gaps natively).

```tsx
<Navbar compact floating brand="Canvas" links={["Docs", "Components", "Templates"]} />
```

### Scrolls

With `scrolls` the links never fold into the narrow menu: the content row scrolls
sideways inside the bar once it no longer fits. With `floating` and `compact` it is
the hand-off's docs pill.

```tsx
<Navbar scrolls floating compact brand="Canvas" links={["Foundations", "Controls", "Inputs", "Navigation", "Overlays", "Data", "Charts", "Layout", "Templates"]} />
```

### Brand divider

`brandDivider` sets the brand apart from the links with a short vertical rule (the kit
`Divider vertical inset strong`), as the hand-off's floating docs pill does. It shows
only while the links row is on the bar.

```tsx
<Navbar brandDivider scrolls floating compact brand="Canvas" links={["Foundations", "Controls", "Inputs", "Navigation"]} />
```

### Links with destinations

`hrefs` gives the links their destinations, by index. On the web each becomes a real
anchor, so middle-click and open-in-new-tab work, while a plain click still selects
the link and calls `onSelect` with the press event (call `event.preventDefault()`
there to route on the client). A modifier or middle click is left to the browser.
Natively `hrefs` is ignored and `onSelect` does the navigating.

```tsx
<Navbar bordered brand="Canvas" links={["Docs", "Components", "Templates"]} hrefs={["/docs", "/components", "/templates"]} />
```

### Bare

A bare bar paints no surface and no hairline, so it sits clear on what is behind it.
Pass it at the scroll edge, while nothing has scrolled under the bar, and drop it once
content does: the bar's own surface then returns to keep its labels legible,
as iOS's
navigation bar and Material 3's top app bar do.
A framed bar (`bordered`, `floating`)
keeps its frame over `bare`.

```tsx
<Navbar bare brand="Canvas" links={["Dashboard", "Users", "Settings"]} />
```

### App menu

An app with more destinations than a bar can hold (a component catalog, a settings
tree) passes `onMenu`: the bar leads with a menu button at every width and the app
opens its own navigation, such as a Drawer of grouped sections. It replaces `links`.

```tsx
<Stateful initial={false}>
  {(open, setOpen) => (
    <View>
      <Navbar bordered brand="Catalog" onMenu={() => setOpen(true)} />
      <Drawer open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} accessibilityLabel="Catalog menu">
        <Column padLoose loose>
          <Typography h3>Components</Typography>
          <Button ghost onPress={() => setOpen(false)}>Button</Button>
          <Button ghost onPress={() => setOpen(false)}>Card</Button>
        </Column>
      </Drawer>
    </View>
  )}
</Stateful>
```

### Console topbar

```tsx
<Navbar
  brandContent={<Icon layers />}
  actions={<Button ghost small icon accessibilityLabel="Search" iconLeft={<Icon search size={16} />} />}
  avatar="RC"
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### Brand element

**Do**: Pass the mark through `brandContent`, so the bar owns the whole brand group and the wordmark keeps its own type.

```tsx
<Navbar bordered brandContent={<Icon layers size={20} />} brand="Console" links={["Overview", "Access", "Audit"]} avatar="RC" />
```

**Don't**: Folding the mark into the wordmark string leaves it as text, stuck in the title's size and color.

```tsx
<Navbar bordered brand="◆ Console" links={["Overview", "Access", "Audit"]} avatar="RC" />
```

### Standard topbar

**Do** — Keep a few primary links inline and fold the rest behind a More menu.

```tsx
<Navbar bordered brand="Canvas" defaultActive={0} links={["Dashboard", "Users", "Settings"]} actionLabel="New" avatar="RC" />
```

**Don't** — Cramming every destination into the bar wraps the row and buries the primary links.

```tsx
<Navbar bordered brand="Canvas" defaultActive={0} links={[
    "Dashboard",
    "Users",
    "Settings",
    "Billing",
    "Reports",
    "Integrations",
    "Audit",
    "Webhooks"
  ]} avatar="RC" />
```

### With search bar

**Do** — Use a button that opens the command palette and advertise the ⌘K shortcut.

```tsx
<Card flat flush style={{ overflow: "hidden" }}>
  <Row alignCenter snug pad style={{ height: 56 }}>
    <Typography small semibold>Canvas</Typography>
    <Container sm start>
      <Button outline block iconLeft={<Icon search muted size={13} />} iconRight={<Kbd>⌘K</Kbd>}>Search…</Button>
    </Container>
  </Row>
</Card>
```

**Don't** — A live text field in the bar reads as a form input and offers no keyboard affordance.

```tsx
<View style={{ width: "100%", overflow: "hidden", borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border }}>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", height: 56, alignItems: "center", gap: 8, backgroundColor: tokens.card, paddingHorizontal: 16 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens.foreground }}>Canvas</Text>
    <View style={{ marginHorizontal: 16, maxWidth: 400, flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%" }}>
      <TextInput placeholder="Search…" style={{ height: 36, width: "100%", borderRadius: 6, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.background, paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 4, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens.foreground }} />
    </View>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Mobile

**Do** — Collapse the links into a hamburger and keep only the logo and avatar in the bar.

```tsx
<Card flat flush style={{ overflow: "hidden" }}>
  <Row alignCenter snug pad style={{ height: 56 }}>
    <Button ghost iconLeft={<Icon menu muted size={18} />} accessibilityLabel="Open menu" />
    <Typography small semibold>Canvas</Typography>
    <Column grow />
    <Avatar small src="/rachel-chen.jpg" name="RC" />
  </Row>
</Card>
```

**Don't** — A full horizontal nav at phone width wraps onto a second row and crowds out the logo.

```tsx
<View style={{ width: "100%", maxWidth: 360, overflow: "hidden", borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border }}>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", height: 56, alignItems: "center", gap: 4, backgroundColor: tokens.card, paddingHorizontal: 12 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 13, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens.foreground }}>Canvas</Text>
    <View style={{ marginLeft: 8, flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", gap: 4 }}>
      <Pressable style={({ pressed }) => [{ borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: tokens.accent, paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 6 }, pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null]}>
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Dashboard</Text>
      </Pressable>
      <Pressable style={({ pressed }) => [{ borderRadius: 6, paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 6 }, pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null]}>
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Users</Text>
      </Pressable>
      <Pressable style={({ pressed }) => [{ borderRadius: 6, paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 6 }, pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null]}>
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Settings</Text>
      </Pressable>
      <Pressable style={({ pressed }) => [{ borderRadius: 6, paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 6 }, pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null]}>
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Billing</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  </View>
</View>
```

### NavbarProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |

| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |

<!-- Source: https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/components/pagination.md -->
# Pagination

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/pagination/pagination.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/pagination

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Page-of-N navigation for tables and lists.

Neither iOS nor Android has a numbered pagination control, so every platform shows the
same pager:
rounded hairline cells at 28, 34 or 40 (small, default, large), the page
numbers in 13px mono numerals, and the current page in the accent fill with a soft glow
beneath it. Previous and Next carry a chevron and a "Prev" / "Next" label beside the
numbers (the chevron alone at the small size and in the compact row), the truncation gap
is a quiet text ellipsis (…), and the rows-per-page trigger sits on the field edge. A resting page
or arrow takes the hover wash at once; a disabled pager dims as one, and in an enabled
pager the arrow at either end dims on its own.

In glass mode the current page is a brand-tinted control-layer puck behind its number;
the other pages and the hairline arrows paint no surface, so they stay bare. Beyond
seven pages a page change also shifts the window (an ellipsis moves, a number appears or
drops out). Solid mode keeps the accent fill.

## Usage

```tsx
<Pagination defaultPage={2} total={12} />
```

## Variants

### With item range

```tsx
<Pagination compact defaultPage={2} total={12} itemCount={118} />
```

### With size

```tsx
<Pagination defaultPage={2} total={12} withSize defaultPageSize={10} pageSizes={[10, 25, 50]} />
```

### Sizes

```tsx
<Column relaxed>
  <Pagination small defaultPage={2} total={12} />
  <Pagination defaultPage={2} total={12} />
  <Pagination large defaultPage={2} total={12} />
</Column>
```

### First and last page

```tsx
<Column relaxed>
  <Pagination defaultPage={1} total={3} />
  <Pagination defaultPage={3} total={3} />
</Column>
```

## Do & Don't

### compact

**Do** — Pass `itemCount` so the buttons carry a "Showing X-Y of N" range and position and total are always visible.

```tsx
<Pagination compact defaultPage={2} total={12} itemCount={118} />
```

**Don't** — Bare Previous/Next with no range label leaves the user unable to tell where they are or how much is left.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "flex-end", gap: 4 }}>
  <Pressable style={{ alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", width: 36, height: 36, borderRadius: 9999, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border }} accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel="Previous page">
    <Icon chevronLeft size={16} />
  </Pressable>
  <Pressable style={{ alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", width: 36, height: 36, borderRadius: 9999, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border }} accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel="Next page">
    <Icon chevronRight size={16} />
  </Pressable>
</View>
```

### numbered

**Do** — Truncate the middle with an ellipsis; keep first, last, and a window around the current page.

```tsx
<Pagination defaultPage={2} total={12} />
```

**Don't** — Rendering every page number overflows and stops being scannable past a handful.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 4 }}>
  <Pressable style={{ alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", width: 36, height: 36, borderRadius: 9999, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border }} accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel="Previous page">
    <Icon chevronLeft muted size={16} />
  </Pressable>
```

### with-size

**Do** — Show "Page X of N" beside the size selector and reset to page 1 when the size changes.

```tsx
<Pagination withSize defaultPage={2} total={12} defaultPageSize={10} pageSizes={[10, 25, 50]} />
```

**Don't** — Offering a page-size selector without a page indicator hides which page the new size landed on.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 16 }}>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Rows per page</Text>
    <Pressable style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 4, height: 36, paddingHorizontal: 12, borderRadius: 9999, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border }} accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel="Rows per page">
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, fontWeight: "700", color: tokens.foreground }}>10</Text>
      <Icon chevronDown muted size={16} />
    </Pressable>
  </View>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 4 }}>
    <Pressable style={{ alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", width: 36, height: 36, borderRadius: 9999, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border }} accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel="Previous page">
      <Icon chevronLeft muted size={16} />
    </Pressable>
    <Pressable style={{ alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", width: 36, height: 36, borderRadius: 9999, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border }} accessibilityRole="button" accessibilityLabel="Next page">
      <Icon chevronRight size={16} />
    </Pressable>
  </View>
</View>
```

# PhoneInput

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/molecules/phone-input/phone-input.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/phone-input

## Public imports

```tsx
import { PHONE_COUNTRIES, PhoneInput, flagOf } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A phone number field: the Input's box with a country segment at its start (the
chosen country and a caret, which open a list of countries with their names and
dial codes) and that country's dial code inline before the number. On the web the
segment is a small chip inside the field naming the country by its ISO code, and
the dial code and the number are set in the mono face, and in the country list each
row is a 16px flag 10px from the name with the dial code a 12px mono note at its end;
on iOS and Android it is the
country's flag.

The number and the country are each controlled (`value` / `country`) or
self-managed (`defaultValue` / `defaultCountry`), the segment defaults to the
kit's curated `PHONE_COUNTRIES` list (pass `countries` for a full or localized
one), and the number field asks for the phone keypad. Pass `label` (and
`required`) to name it; `error` paints the whole box, segment included, and
Field delegates its label, required mark and error into it. The required star is
decorative: a screen reader hears the number field as required,
from
`aria-required` on the web and from its name ("Phone number, required") on iOS and
Android.
On iOS the field is
drawn to the iOS input-field reference: the white box, the flag and gray caret
segment with its state-coloured divider, the dial code in the placeholder gray.

In glass mode the country list is a dense-layer glass card under the box; the
box, its segment and its number stay in place. A pick commits the country and
returns focus to the number at once, and a field that becomes disabled or
read-only while the list is open closes it. Solid mode paints the skin's own list.

## Usage

```tsx
<PhoneInput label="Phone number" placeholder="Add your phone number" />
```

## Variants

### Pre-filled

```tsx
<PhoneInput label="Phone number" defaultCountry="US" defaultValue="(415) 728-3046" />
```

### Another country

```tsx
<PhoneInput label="Phone number" defaultCountry="GB" placeholder="Add your phone number" />
```

### Error

```tsx
<Field label="Phone number" error="Invalid phone number.">
  <PhoneInput defaultCountry="US" defaultValue="(415) 72" />
</Field>
```

### Required

```tsx
<PhoneInput label="Phone number" required placeholder="Add your phone number" />
```

### Controlled country

```tsx
<Stateful initial="CA">
  {(country, setCountry) => (
    <Column snug>
      <PhoneInput label="Phone number" country={country} onCountryChange={setCountry} placeholder="Add your phone number" />
      <Typography small muted>Selected: {country}</Typography>
    </Column>
  )}
</Stateful>
```

### Custom country list

```tsx
<PhoneInput
  label="Phone number"
  countries={[
    { code: "FR", name: "France", dialCode: "+33" },
    { code: "DE", name: "Germany", dialCode: "+49" },
    { code: "ES", name: "Spain", dialCode: "+34" },
  ]}
  defaultCountry="DE"
  placeholder="Add your phone number"
/>
```

### Disabled

```tsx

```

```tsx
  <PhoneInput small label="Small" placeholder="Add your phone number" />
  <PhoneInput label="Default" placeholder="Add your phone number" />
  <PhoneInput large label="Large" placeholder="Add your phone number" />
</Column>
```

## Do & Don't

### The country segment

**Do** — Let the segment carry the country so the number stays national and the dial code is never typed twice.

```tsx
<PhoneInput label="Phone number" defaultCountry="US" defaultValue="(415) 728-3046" />
```

**Don't** — A plain Input makes the user type the prefix, and nothing tells the app which country the digits belong to.

```tsx
<Input label="Phone number" defaultValue="+1 (415) 728-3046" />
```

### Errors

**Do** — Wrap the field in a Field so the message sits under the box and the box, segment included, paints the error border.

```tsx
<Field label="Phone number" error="Invalid phone number.">
  <PhoneInput defaultCountry="US" defaultValue="(415) 72" />
</Field>
```

**Don't** — A loose red caption beside a neutral box reads as unfinished, and a screen reader never hears it with the field.

```tsx
<Column tight>
  <PhoneInput label="Phone number" defaultCountry="US" defaultValue="(415) 72" />
  <Typography tiny destructive>Invalid phone number.</Typography>
</Column>
```

# PieChart

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/charts/pie-chart/pie-chart.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/pie-chart

## Public imports

```tsx
import { PieChart } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Proportional composition as arc slices in the `chart-1`..`chart-8` token colors, with a percent legend. `donut` centers the total (or the selected slice while inspecting); pressing a slice dims the others.

## Usage

```tsx
<PieChart
  label="Traffic"
  slices={[
    { label: "Direct", value: 42 },
    { label: "Organic search", value: 28 },
    { label: "Social", value: 18 },
    { label: "Other", value: 12 }
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Donut

```tsx
<PieChart
  donut
  label="Traffic"
  slices={[
    { label: "Direct", value: 42 },
    { label: "Organic search", value: 28 },
    { label: "Social", value: 18 },
    { label: "Other", value: 12 }
  ]}
/>
```

### Detailed composition

```tsx
<PieChart donut detailed label="Sessions" slices={[{label: "Direct", value: 42}, {label: "Search", value: 28}, {label: "Other", value: 30}]} />
```

## Do & Don't

### Pie

**Do** — Keep slices to a handful and fold the tail into an "Other" slice; the legend carries exact shares.

```tsx
<Card padded>
  <PieChart
    label="Traffic"
    slices={[
      { label: "Direct", value: 42 },
      { label: "Organic search", value: 28 },
      { label: "Social", value: 18 },
      { label: "Other", value: 12 }
    ]}
  />
</Card>

```

**Don't** — A dozen sliver slices cycle the palette and become unreadable; nothing is comparable at a glance.

```tsx
<Card padded>
  <PieChart
    label="Traffic"
    slices={[
      { label: "Direct", value: 22 },
      { label: "Organic", value: 18 },
      { label: "Social", value: 11 },
      { label: "Referral", value: 9 },
      { label: "Email", value: 8 },
      { label: "Paid", value: 7 },
      { label: "Video", value: 6 },
      { label: "Affiliates", value: 6 },
      { label: "Push", value: 5 },
      { label: "SMS", value: 4 },
      { label: "Podcasts", value: 2 },
      { label: "Misc", value: 2 }
    ]}
  />
</Card>

```

## Supported props

### PieChartProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| slices | StackedSegment[] | yes |  | The slices, in order; each takes its share of the circle. |
| label | string \| undefined | no |  | What the pie measures (e.g. "Traffic sources"); leads the accessible name. |
| donut | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Draw an annular ring with the total and label centered inside. |
| hideLegend | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Hide the legend (the labelled dots beside percentages). |
| detailed | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Spread names and shares into a value column beside a compact composition disc. |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Smaller diameter. |
| plain | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Strip the card surface for nesting inside an existing card (mirrors Stats). |
| selected | number \| null \| undefined | no |  | Press-to-inspect: the selected slice index (controlled). Pass null for none. |
| defaultSelected | number \| undefined | no |  | Press-to-inspect: the initially selected slice (uncontrolled). |
| onSelect | ((index: number \| null) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when a press selects a slice (or clears it with null). |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | For sizing/composition only. |
