# Popover

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/popover/popover.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/popover

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Popover } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Floating panel with a title, supporting text, rich content such as form fields, and a single follow-up action, anchored to its trigger. Pass children to host custom content in the panel body, between the description and the action.

On the web and Android the panel is the v4 card:
280 wide at the menu corner, the field
hairline and the large shadow, a 15px display heading over its 14px description in the
muted ink, and in solid mode a small diamond beak on the edge facing its trigger.
iOS
keeps the iPad popover, a rounder borderless card with a tapered beak toward its
trigger.

The triggered card opens below its button by default and above it with `top`; either
way it flips to the other side when its own lacks room, and the beak follows the
side it took. At phone width a triggered card that can close is presented as a sheet
on the bottom edge of the window, over the tab bar and a dimming scrim that glass on the
web also blurs,
its content kept clear of the home indicator: Dark Factory's sheet on the web, the iOS sheet on iPhone and
the Material 3 bottom sheet on Android.

In glass mode the triggered card is a functional-layer glass panel beside its
button, and the sheet a dense-layer one, legible over its scrim; focus enters once the
card's placement has committed, and the `inline` card is a static in-flow panel. Solid
mode paints the skin's own panel.

An existing control can own the trigger: pass its `anchorRef` and drive `open`
with `onOpenChange`. The popover then adds no trigger or layout wrapper. Name
custom content with `accessibilityLabel`. `compact` uses the original Argus panel
inset and outside hairline on web, with scrolling contents; `comfortable` gives
its filter panel more room. `panelWidth` and `maxHeight` bound the overlay.
`anchored` keeps a floating card at narrow widths, and `alignEnd` follows the
trigger’s trailing edge.

## Usage

```tsx
<Popover
  trigger="Open popover"
  title="Rename project"
  description="Choose a name your team will recognize."
  actionLabel="Rename"
>
  <Input label="Project name" defaultValue="Identity Platform" />
</Popover>
```

## Variants

### Compact panel

```tsx
<Popover compact comfortable anchored panelWidth={320} trigger="Filters" accessibilityLabel="Filters">
  <Typography small muted>Choose the roles and pods to include.</Typography>
</Popover>
```


### Inline

```tsx
<Popover inline title="Draft saved" description="Your changes are kept as a draft until you publish them." actionLabel="Publish" />
```

### Above

```tsx
<Popover top trigger="Filter" title="Filter results" description="Show only the projects you own." actionLabel="Apply" />
```

### Inline with a beak

An inline panel draws its beak when it is given a side: with `top` the panel sits above
what it belongs to and points down at it, with `bottom` below it and points up, and
`alignEnd` moves the beak to the panel's end, over a trigger that sits there.

```tsx
<Popover inline top alignEnd title="Share link" description="Anyone with the link can view." actionLabel="Copy link" />
```

### Description only

```tsx
<Popover trigger="What is a workspace?" description="A workspace groups your projects, members, and billing under one plan." />
```

### Controlled

```tsx
<Stateful initial={false}>
  {(open, setOpen) => (
    <Column snug>
      <Typography small muted>{open ? "The share popover is open." : "The share popover is closed."}</Typography>
      <Popover
        trigger="Share"
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        title="Share this project"
        description="Anyone with the link can view it."
        actionLabel="Copy link"
      />
    </Column>
  )}
</Stateful>
```

## Do & Don't

### Compact content

**Do** — Keep popovers compact: a focused prompt with one input and a clear action.

```tsx
<Popover inline title="Rename this project?" actionLabel="Rename">
  <Input label="Project name" defaultValue="Identity Platform" />
</Popover>
```

**Don't** — A full form belongs in a dialog; in a floating popover it is cramped and easy to dismiss by accident.

```tsx
<View style={{ borderRadius: 12, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.popover, padding: 16, boxShadow: "0px 26px 50px -20px rgba(121, 100, 214, 0.22)", alignSelf: "flex-start", minWidth: 260 }}>
  <Input label="Name" placeholder="Ada Lovelace" style={{ marginBottom: 8 }} />
  <Input label="Email" placeholder="ada@canvas.dev" style={{ marginBottom: 8 }} />
  <View style={{ marginBottom: 8 }}>
    <Text style={{ marginBottom: 6, fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 17, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens.foreground }}>Role</Text>
    <Select defaultValue="Engineer" options={["Engineer", "Designer", "Manager"]} />
  </View>
  <Input label="Team" placeholder="Identity Platform" style={{ marginBottom: 8 }} />
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", justifyContent: "flex-end", gap: 8 }}>
    <Button outline small>Cancel</Button>
    <Button primary small>Save</Button>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Triggered

**Do** — Wrap the trigger in a relative anchor and dismiss on outside click so the panel positions and closes predictably.

```tsx
<Popover trigger="Open popover" open description="Anchored to the trigger, closes on outside click." actionLabel="Close" />
```

**Don't** — A trigger with no relative anchor and no way to dismiss leaves the panel floating loose and stuck open.

```tsx
<View style={{ alignSelf: "flex-start" }}>
  <Button outline small>Open popover</Button>
  <View style={{ borderRadius: 12, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.popover, padding: 16, boxShadow: "0px 26px 50px -20px rgba(121, 100, 214, 0.22)", marginTop: 8, minWidth: 240 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 12.5, lineHeight: 19, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens["popover-foreground"] }}>No anchor, no dismiss, no Close.</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Inline

**Do** — Reserve the static panel for a brief always-on message with a single follow-up action.

```tsx
<Popover inline description="Saved to drafts. Publish when ready." actionLabel="Publish" />
```

**Don't** — An always-visible panel that scrolls internally is doing a card's or section's job; use the panel chrome only for short content.

```tsx
<View style={{ borderRadius: 12, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.popover, padding: 16, boxShadow: "0px 26px 50px -20px rgba(121, 100, 214, 0.22)", maxHeight: 120, minWidth: 260, overflow: "hidden" }}>
  <ScrollView style={{ maxHeight: 88 }}>
    <Input label="Street" placeholder="100 Market St" style={{ marginBottom: 8 }} />
    <Input label="City" placeholder="San Francisco" style={{ marginBottom: 8 }} />
    <Input label="Region" placeholder="California" style={{ marginBottom: 8 }} />
    <Input label="Postal code" placeholder="94105" style={{ marginBottom: 8 }} />
  </ScrollView>
</View>
```

## Accessibility

The trigger is a button that announces its popup as a dialog and whether it is expanded. Opening the card moves keyboard focus into the panel, once its placement has settled: a dialog named by its title (by the trigger's label when it has none) and described by its supporting line. A card pinned open (a controlled `open` with no change handler) is part of the page and takes no focus as it appears.

With a keyboard, Tab moves through the panel's controls as if the card sat right after its trigger, then on to the control after the trigger, and the card stays open: the anchored popover is non-modal on the web. Shift+Tab from the panel returns to the trigger, and Tab from the trigger re-enters the card. Escape closes it, and focus goes back to whatever opened it.

The sheet on phones is modal, as it covers and dims the page: its dialog is announced as modal, Tab and Shift+Tab keep to its controls and wrap at their ends, and a Tab from anywhere on the page behind it goes into it. Escape, the action or a tap on the scrim closes it, and focus goes back to whatever opened it.

On iOS and Android the open card is modal to VoiceOver and TalkBack: the page behind it is hidden from them, their focus moves to the card's first line, and when the card closes it returns to the trigger. The escape gesture and the Android back button close the card.
Touch closes it with a tap anywhere outside it, and on phones a tap on the scrim above the sheet.

## Supported props

### PopoverProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| anchorRef | RefObject<View \| null> \| undefined | no |  | An existing trigger to anchor against; omits the built-in trigger and wrapper. |
| accessibilityLabel | string \| undefined | no |  | Explicit name for a panel with custom content. |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Compact web application panel with an outside hairline and scrolling content. |
| comfortable | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Roomier compact-panel content inset. |
| anchored | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Keep the card anchored on narrow windows instead of adapting to a sheet. |
| alignEnd | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Align the trailing edge of the card to its trigger. |
| panelWidth | number \| undefined | no |  | Floating card width, clamped inside the overlay outlet. |
| maxHeight | number \| undefined | no |  | Maximum height of the floating card; its compact contents scroll within it. |
| trigger | string \| undefined | no |  | Label for the trigger button. |
| title | string \| undefined | no |  | Heading shown at the top of the floating card. |
| description | string \| undefined | no |  | Supporting line beneath the title. |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | Custom panel content (an input, a form row, any node), rendered in the card body between the description and the action row. Composes with the data-driven props. |
| actionLabel | string \| undefined | no |  | When set, renders a primary action button at the bottom of the card. |
| top | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Anchor the card ABOVE the trigger (it flips below when the room above is short). Placement axis: `top` > `bottom`. |
| bottom | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Anchor the card BELOW the trigger, the default (it flips above when the room below is short). |
| inline | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Static mode: render the card on its own with no trigger button (an always-visible inline panel). When set, the card is always shown and `open` is ignored. With `top` or `bottom` it points its beak at what it belongs to (below it with `top`, above it with `bottom`), from the end edge with `alignEnd`. |
| open | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Controlled open state. Omit for uncontrolled (the trigger toggles it). |
| onOpenChange | ((open: boolean) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when the open state changes. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | StyleProp<ViewStyle> | no |  | Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook. |

# Pressable

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/pressable/pressable.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/pressable

## Public imports

```tsx
import { InteractionOverride, Pressable } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

The touchable primitive: wraps content, fires `onPress`, and exposes the press state to its style for feedback.

The kit's interactive components (Button, plus the tappable Card, Stats, GridList, MediaObject, and StackedList rows) cover the common cases and keep branding consistent, so prefer them; Pressable stays for full flexibility when you need a custom interaction the kit doesn't provide. Its style prop accepts a function of the press state, `({ pressed }) => style`, so you can show press feedback with no extra wrapper; style it with tokens to stay on-brand.

Pass `focusable={false}` for a surface only a pointer should reach, such as a row whose keyboard path is a button inside it: it still presses, and it leaves the tab order on the web too, where react-native-web's own Pressable would keep it a tab stop. A Pressable with the `link` role presses on Enter (and not on Space), as a link does, on the web too: react-native-web's own Pressable leaves that key to the browser, which activates only a link that has an `href`.

## Usage

Wire `onPress` to your own handler. The background dims while the button is held, straight from the `({ pressed }) => style` function.

```tsx
<Pressable style={({ pressed }) => ({ padding: 12, borderRadius: 8, backgroundColor: pressed ? alpha(tokens.primary, 0.8) : tokens.primary })}>
  <Text style={{ color: tokens["primary-foreground"] }}>Press and hold</Text>
</Pressable>
```

## Variants

### Opacity

The style function dims the whole surface to 50% opacity while pressed.

```tsx
<Pressable style={({ pressed }) => ({ opacity: pressed ? 0.5 : 1 })}>
  <Text style={{ color: tokens.foreground }}>Press and hold</Text>
</Pressable>
```

### Disabled

A disabled Pressable ignores presses.

```tsx
<Pressable disabled style={{ padding: 12, borderRadius: 8, backgroundColor: tokens.muted, opacity: 0.5 }}>
  <Text style={{ color: tokens.foreground }}>Disabled</Text>
</Pressable>
```

## Do & Don't

### Press feedback

**Do**: Answer the press with a style function: `({ pressed }) => style` changes the surface while the finger is down, so the tap visibly lands.

```tsx
<Pressable accessibilityRole="button" style={({ pressed }) => ({ padding: 12, borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: pressed ? tokens.accent : tokens.card })}>
  <Typography small>Open the weekly report</Typography>
</Pressable>
```

**Don't**: Give the surface a fixed style; nothing changes under the finger, so a tap feels dropped and a slow response reads as a missed press.

```tsx
<Pressable accessibilityRole="button" style={{ padding: 12, borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.card }}>
  <Typography small>Open the weekly report</Typography>
</Pressable>
```

### Kit controls first

**Do**: Use the kit's control when one fits the job: a Button already carries the brand fill, press feedback, focus ring, role and disabled state on every platform.

```tsx
<Button primary onPress={() => {}}>Save changes</Button>
```

**Don't**: Rebuild a button from Pressable and a style object; it drifts from the brand the moment the kit's Button changes, and it misses every state the kit draws for you.

```tsx
<Pressable style={({ pressed }) => ({ alignSelf: "flex-start", paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingVertical: 10, borderRadius: 8, backgroundColor: pressed ? alpha(tokens.primary, 0.8) : tokens.primary })}>
  <Text style={{ color: tokens["primary-foreground"], fontWeight: "600" }}>Save changes</Text>
</Pressable>
```

## Pinned states

`InteractionOverride` pins hover, keyboard focus or the pressed state for every kit control inside it, so a docs specimen or a visual test shows that state without a pointer or a key. Pass `hovered`, `focused` or `pressed` (its `InteractionOverrideProps`); they combine, and passing none gives the subtree back its real states. The kit's Pressable draws its focus ring and reports `pressed` to its style and children functions, the hover primitive reports a hover, and a field shows its focused look, so Button, Input, Checkbox, Switch, Pagination and every other kit control honour it without a prop of their own. It pins the look only: no handler fires, assistive technology hears the control as it is, a disabled control stays at rest, and natively a pinned focus draws no ring, as a real one draws none there. Portaled overlay content keeps its real states.

```tsx
<Row wrap alignCenter cozy>
  <Button outline>Rest</Button>
  <InteractionOverride hovered>
    <Button outline>Hover</Button>
  </InteractionOverride>
  <InteractionOverride focused>
    <Button outline>Focus</Button>
  </InteractionOverride>
  <InteractionOverride pressed>
    <Button outline>Pressed</Button>
  </InteractionOverride>
</Row>
```

## Supported props

### InteractionOverrideProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hovered | boolean \| undefined | no |  | Every kit control in the subtree renders as if a pointer hovered it. |
| focused | boolean \| undefined | no |  | Every kit control in the subtree renders its keyboard focus (the focus ring, or the field's own focused look). |
| pressed | boolean \| undefined | no |  | Every kit control in the subtree renders as if it were held down. |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | The subtree that resolves the pinned states. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# ProgressRing

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)

## Public imports

```tsx
import { ProgressRing } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A full-circle completion ring, the Gauge's sibling: a muted track ring, a tone-colored value arc revealed clockwise from 12 o'clock with rounded caps, the whole-percent readout centered inside, and an optional label below the graphic. The same 0-100 value contract, tone axis, and rounding rules as Gauge, in the circular anatomy that reads as "completion" rather than "level".

## Usage

```tsx
<ProgressRing value={72} label="Complete" />
```

## Variants

### Success tone

```tsx
<ProgressRing value={92} success />
```

### Warning tone

```tsx
<ProgressRing value={81} warning />
```

### Compact

```tsx
<ProgressRing value={72} compact />
```

### Stacked label

`stacked` sets the label under the ring, centred, for a row of rings each named underneath.

```tsx
<ProgressRing value={64} label="Storage" stacked />
```

## Do & Don't

### ProgressRing

**Do** - Put a muted track behind the value arc, the percent readout in the ring's center, and the label below the graphic.

```tsx
<Card padded>
  <Column alignCenter>
    <ProgressRing value={72} label="Complete" />
  </Column>
</Card>
```

**Don't** - A bordered circle with no track and no readout gives no baseline to read the fill against and no exact value.

```tsx
<View style={{ borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.card, padding: 20, maxWidth: 200, alignItems: "center" }}>
  <View style={{ borderRadius: 9999, borderWidth: 10, borderColor: tokens.primary, height: 120, width: 120 }} />
</View>
```

## Supported props

### ProgressRingProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | number | yes |  | The value to display, 0-100. |
| label | string \| undefined | no |  | A short caption beneath the number (e.g. "Complete"). |
| primary | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tone of the value arc (pick one; default primary). Precedence when several are passed: success > warning > destructive (first match wins). |
| success | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tone of the value arc (pick one; default primary). Precedence when several are passed: success > warning > destructive (first match wins). |
| warning | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tone of the value arc (pick one; default primary). Precedence when several are passed: success > warning > destructive (first match wins). |
| destructive | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tone of the value arc (pick one; default primary). Precedence when several are passed: success > warning > destructive (first match wins). |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Density (omit for the default 168 ring; compact is 106). |
| stacked | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Set the label under the ring, centred, instead of beside it (a row of rings, each named underneath). |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | For sizing/composition only. |

# Progress

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/progress/progress.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/progress

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Determinate and indeterminate progress bars: a rounded bar that reports how far a task has gotten, or that work is underway.

The bar fills the parent it is given; a step of its own (`xs`, `lg`, …, with `start` to pin it to the leading edge) or a Container step sets its measure.

Name the task with string `children`, or pass `accessibilityLabel` when the visible title is omitted or contains rich content.

`segments` displays a fixed number of discrete 13×5 dashes with three pixels
between them. It uses the same 0–1 `value`, intent fill and accessible percentage.
Indeterminate wins over discrete segments; a labelled segmented meter retains its header.

## Usage

```tsx
<Progress accessibilityLabel="Uploading files" value={0.6} />
```

## Variants

### Labeled

```tsx
<Progress showValue description="3 of 5 files" value={0.6}>Uploading files</Progress>
```

### Status

`status` puts a short word on the title line, in the percent's place and type: what the
bar means now, where `description` is a sentence under the title. It shows while
indeterminate too, and wins the slot over `showValue`.

```tsx
<Progress indeterminate status="indexing">Indexing components</Progress>
```

### Indeterminate

```tsx
<Progress accessibilityLabel="Connecting" indeterminate />
```

### Small

```tsx
<Progress small accessibilityLabel="Uploading files" value={0.6} />
```

### Large

```tsx
<Progress large accessibilityLabel="Uploading files" value={0.6} />
```

### Warning

The tone axis recolors the fill when a metric crosses a soft threshold. Pass `warning` for an
amber bar; the track stays neutral.

```tsx
<Progress warning value={0.85}>Storage used</Progress>
```

### Danger

Pass `danger` for a red bar when a hard limit is exceeded, e.g. a work-in-progress cap. Reinforce
the state with copy, since the tone carries no new accessible value on its own.

```tsx
<Progress danger value={1}>Over the WIP limit</Progress>
```

### Live

The determinate fill eases to each new `value` instead of jumping, so a bar wired to real
progress fills smoothly. (Reduce Motion snaps instead.)

```tsx
<Ticker values={[0, 0.15, 0.4, 0.65, 0.85, 1]}>
  {(value) => (
    <Progress showValue value={value}>Uploading…</Progress>
  )}
</Ticker>
```

### Measure

```tsx
<Column snug>
  <Progress xs start value={0.6}>xs step, pinned to the start (320)</Progress>
  <Progress lg start value={0.6}>lg step, pinned to the start (512)</Progress>
  <Container lg start><Progress value={0.6}>Bare, in an lg Container: fills it (512)</Progress></Container>
</Column>
```

## Do & Don't

### Determinate

**Do** — Use a determinate bar when you know the share of work done, and pass `showValue` so the control renders the percent on the label line; the number and the bar always agree.

```tsx
<Progress showValue value={0.72}>Uploading…</Progress>
```

**Don't** — Don't park a determinate bar at a hard-coded value as a decorative divider; a frozen fill reads as a stalled task.

```tsx
<View style={{ gap: 8 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens.foreground }}>Section</Text>
  <Progress accessibilityLabel="Section progress" value={0.5} />
</View>
```

### Indeterminate

**Do** — Reach for `indeterminate` only when the duration is genuinely unknown. Pass the label as children;
on the web and Android a short bar sweeps the track; on iOS the control renders the kit Spinner, the platform's unknown-duration idiom (iOS has no linear indeterminate bar).

```tsx
<Progress indeterminate>Connecting…</Progress>
```

**Don't** — Don't fake indeterminate progress when you do have a measurable value;
hiding a known value behind a sweep (or a spinner on iOS) hides information you could show.

```tsx
<View style={{ gap: 8 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Step 3 of 4</Text>
  <Progress accessibilityLabel="Connecting" indeterminate />
</View>
```

### Context

**Do** — Give the bar a label through its own `children`; it fills the parent it is given, and a Container step sets its measure when the layout calls for it.

```tsx
<Progress value={0.35}>Importing contacts</Progress>
```

**Don't** — Don't hand-roll a bar from raw views; the kit's `Progress` already adapts its thickness, ends, and track anatomy per platform and stays themed.

```tsx
<View style={{ width: 320, maxWidth: "100%", height: 8, borderRadius: 4, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.2), overflow: "hidden" }}>
  <View style={{ height: "100%", width: "35%", borderRadius: 4, backgroundColor: tokens.primary }} />
</View>
```

## Supported props

### ProgressProps

Includes `MeasureProps`; their supported fields are expanded below.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | number \| undefined | no |  | Completion as a 0..1 fraction (clamped). Ignored when `indeterminate`. Defaults to 0. |
| segments | number \| undefined | no |  | A fixed number of discrete dashes, filled by the same fractional value. |
| indeterminate | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Indeterminate mode: ignore `value` and animate a sliding bar (a spinner on iOS). |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | Optional title line rendered ABOVE the bar. Supplying it (with or without a `description`/`showValue`) builds the stacked header inside the control, so the caller never hand-composes a Row/Column + Typography around the bar. This is the "components own their label anatomy" contract, mirroring Checkbox/Radio/Switch's `description` slot. |
| description | ReactNode | no |  | Optional muted secondary line rendered under the title. |
| showValue | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Render the percent (derived from `value`) as a right-aligned readout on the title line. Indeterminate has no measurable value, so this renders nothing then. |
| status | ReactNode | no |  | A short status word on the title line, in the percent readout's place and type ("indeterminate", "strong", "paused"): what the bar means right now, where `description` is a sentence under the title. It shows while indeterminate too, and when both are passed the status wins the readout slot over `showValue`. |

# QRCode

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Encodes a string as a scannable QR code. Built on react-native-svg,
so it renders the same on iOS, Android, and the web.
The code stays a fixed dark-on-white card so any camera can read it, whatever the app theme.

## Usage

```tsx
<QRCode value="https://canvas.nannier.com" />
```

## Variants

### Small

```tsx
<QRCode value="https://canvas.nannier.com" small />
```

### Large

```tsx
<QRCode value="https://canvas.nannier.com" large />
```

## Do & Don't

### Keep it scannable

**Do** — Leave the fixed dark-on-white card in place so the code stays high-contrast for any camera.

```tsx
<QRCode value="https://canvas.nannier.com" />
```

**Don't** — Shrinking a data-dense value to the small size drops the modules below a reliably scannable density.

```tsx
<QRCode value="https://canvas.nannier.com/get/the/app?ref=docs&utm=homepage&v=2" small />
```

# RadarChart

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/charts/radar-chart/radar-chart.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/radar-chart

## Public imports

```tsx
import { RadarChart } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A polygonal multi-axis comparison: concentric rings at nice tick fractions, a spoke per axis, and one closed polygon per series (ramp stroke over a soft matching wash), with the spoke labels just beyond the outer ring. Values align to `axes` by index and the accessible name folds every axis and value; press-to-inspect is deferred scope for this chart.

## Usage

```tsx
<RadarChart
  title="Candidate comparison"
  axes={["Coding", "Design", "Comms", "Ops", "Product"]}
  series={[
    { label: "Casey", values: [8, 6, 9, 5, 7] },
    { label: "Jordan", values: [6, 9, 7, 8, 5] },
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Single series, toned

```tsx
<RadarChart
  success
  axes={["Latency", "Uptime", "Errors", "Cost", "Coverage"]}
  series={[{ label: "API", values: [7, 9, 8, 6, 7] }]}
/>
```

### Compact, no grid

```tsx
<RadarChart
compact
hideGrid
axes={["Spd", "Pwr", "Def", "Mag", "Luck", "HP"]}
series={[{ label: "Build A", values: [12, 18, 9, 15, 7, 14] }]}
/>
```

### Compact with spokes

```tsx
<RadarChart compact spokes axes={["Speed", "Contrast", "Motion", "Density", "Reach", "A11y"]} max={10} series={[{label: "Current", values: [9, 7, 8, 6, 7.5, 5]}, {label: "Previous", values: [6, 8.5, 5, 8, 4.5, 7]}]} />
```

## Do & Don't

### RadarChart

**Do** - Compare a small number of profiles over the same axes, on one shared scale.

```tsx
<RadarChart
title="Candidate comparison"
axes={["Coding", "Design", "Comms", "Ops", "Product"]}
series={[
  { label: "Casey", values: [8, 6, 9, 5, 7] },
  { label: "Jordan", values: [6, 9, 7, 8, 5] },
]}
max={10}
/>
```

**Don't** - Radar axes are unordered categories; a time series belongs on a LineChart, where the x axis carries the order.

```tsx
<RadarChart
axes={["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"]}
series={[{ label: "Revenue", values: [4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9] }]}
/>
```

## Supported props

### RadarChartProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| title | string \| undefined | no |  | Optional heading shown above the plot. |
| max | number \| undefined | no |  | Outer-ring maximum. Defaults to a nice bound above the data max. |
| success | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tone (single-series only; pick one; default primary). Precedence: success > destructive. |
| destructive | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Tone (single-series only; pick one; default primary). Precedence: success > destructive. |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Density (omit for the default plot size). |
| plain | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Strip the card surface for nesting inside an existing card (mirrors Stats). |
| hideLegend | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Hide the series legend (multi-series charts show one by default). |
| hideGrid | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Hide the rings and spokes (the labels always render). |
| spokes | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Join each outer vertex to the center with a radial guide. |
| formatValue | ((v: number) => string) \| undefined | no |  | Formats accessible values (data formatting, not styling). |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.


The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Concentric arc rings, one per category, outermost first: each pairs a muted full-circle track with a ramp-colored value arc revealed clockwise from 12 o'clock, and a column legend carries the formatted values. Every ring sweeps against the same `max` (the largest entry by default), so the chart compares attainment, not shares. Press a ring to select it (the others dim); press elsewhere to clear.

## Usage

```tsx
<RadialBarChart
  label="Platform activation"
  max={100}
  data={[
    { label: "iOS", value: 64 },
    { label: "Android", value: 48 },

  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

```tsx
<RadialBarChart

    { label: "Q2", value: 71 }
  ]}
/>
```

### Inspected

```tsx
<RadialBarChart
  defaultSelected={1}
  data={[
    { label: "Hot", value: 420 },
    { label: "Warm", value: 260 },
    { label: "Cold", value: 890 }
  ]}
/>
```

### Detailed attainment

```tsx
<RadialBarChart detailed max={80} formatValue={(v) => `${v}k`} data={[{label: "Phone", value: 64}, {label: "Tablet", value: 41}, {label: "Web", value: 23}]} />
```

## Do & Don't

### RadialBarChart

**Do** - Compare attainment on rings that share one sweep maximum, with the values in the legend.

```tsx
<Card padded>
  <RadialBarChart
    label="Platform activation"
    data={[
      { label: "iOS", value: 64 },
      { label: "Web", value: 82 },
    ]}
    max={100}
  />
</Card>
```

**Don't** - Rings encoding shares of a whole belong on PieChart; nested rings without a shared maximum cannot be compared by eye.

```tsx
<Card padded>
  <RadialBarChart
    label="Traffic split"
    data={[
      { label: "Direct", value: 60 },
      { label: "Search", value: 40 },
    ]}
  />
</Card>
```

# Radio

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/radio/radio.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/radio

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Radio, RadioGroup } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Single-pick selection: stacked, inline, card-style.

One job, a platform's own control: iOS has no radio button, so there a single choice is a checkmark list, the inline picker of a grouped form. Each option's label leads and the chosen option carries a trailing check, and a RadioGroup's options form one inset-grouped section with a hairline between two rows. The web and Android keep the ring, and the role is `radio` on every platform: on the web an 18 px ring (16 `small`, 22 `large`) whose edge thickens in the accent around a hollow center when chosen, on Android Material 3's 20dp ring around an accent dot.
In glass mode the ring keeps its solid look on every platform: a ring is a small mark inside content, not a surface, so it draws with no pane and no rim. A `card` option is a content-layer pane, as a selectable Card is.
On iOS the list stays vertical when the group asks for a `row` (a list has no row form), and `card` options stay tiles that mark the choice with the same trailing check.

Pass `ref` to access the interactive radio row, preserving group navigation. Use `useRef<ComponentRef<typeof Radio>>(null)` from React, or `useRef<View>(null)` with React Native's `View` type. Object and callback refs are supported and detach on unmount. Calling `ref.current?.focus()` or `.blur()` delegates to the host without activating the control. Browser focus is supported; native focus depends on the platform and React Native version, and is separate from accessibility focus.

On the web, Space activates the focused control on key release, and Enter also activates it. Holding Space does not repeat the change. Moving focus away, disabling the control, or composing text cancels a pending Space press. RadioGroup arrow keys continue to move focus and selection.

## Usage

```tsx
<RadioGroup defaultValue="pro">
  <Radio value="hobby">Hobby</Radio>
  <Radio value="pro">Pro</Radio>
  <Radio value="enterprise">Enterprise</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

## Variants

### Inline

`row` lays the options out in a wrapping row. The group fills its parent's width (the parent provides the bounds, as for any list or field), so the row wraps onto another line when the options run out of room instead of running past its container.

```tsx
<RadioGroup row defaultValue="hobby">
  <Radio value="hobby">Hobby</Radio>
  <Radio value="pro">Pro</Radio>
  <Radio value="enterprise">Enterprise</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Card

```tsx
<RadioGroup row defaultValue="pro">
  <Radio card value="hobby" description="For personal projects.">Hobby</Radio>
  <Radio card value="pro" description="For growing teams.">Pro</Radio>
  <Radio card value="enterprise" description="Advanced security and support.">Enterprise</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Card icon and meta

A `card` radio takes an `icon` over its title, which turns the accent when it is chosen, and `equal` on a `row` group gives every option the same share of the row. Any radio takes `meta`, a short trailing note on the title's line (a version, a price, a badge).

```tsx
<RadioGroup row equal defaultValue="stable">
  <Radio card value="stable" icon={<Icon shieldCheck size={18} decorative />} meta="v4.0" description="Tested releases.">Stable</Radio>
  <Radio card value="beta" icon={<Icon gitBranch size={18} decorative />} meta="v4.1" description="Early features.">Beta</Radio>
  <Radio card value="canary" icon={<Icon bird size={18} decorative />} meta="nightly" description="Every commit.">Canary</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Inline label

`inlineLabel` sets a `row` group's `label` at the start of the row, before the options, in place of the heading above them.

```tsx
<RadioGroup row inlineLabel label="Digest" defaultValue="weekly">
  <Radio value="daily">Daily</Radio>
  <Radio value="weekly" meta={<Badge success small>default</Badge>}>Weekly</Radio>
  <Radio value="never">Never</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

### With description

```tsx
<RadioGroup defaultValue="pro">
  <Radio value="hobby" description="For personal projects and experiments.">Hobby</Radio>
  <Radio value="pro" description="For growing teams that need more control.">Pro</Radio>
  <Radio value="enterprise" description="Advanced security, compliance, and support.">Enterprise</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

## Do & Don't

### Default selection

**Do**: Pre-select a sensible default so the common path needs no clicks, and name the set with the group's own `label`.

```tsx
<RadioGroup label="Plan" defaultValue="pro">
  <Radio value="hobby">Hobby</Radio>
  <Radio value="pro">Pro</Radio>
  <Radio value="enterprise">Enterprise</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

**Don't**: Leaving a radio group with nothing selected forces an extra decision and can submit empty.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "column", gap: 8 }}>
  <Text style={{ marginBottom: 4, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens.foreground }}>Plan</Text>
  <Radio>Hobby</Radio>
  <Radio>Pro</Radio>
  <Radio>Enterprise</Radio>
</View>
```

### Stacked

**Do**: Pass a `description` and the control stacks the title over its secondary line for you, the mark aligned to the title
(the ring to its first line on the web and Android, the check centered on the row on iOS).

```tsx
<Radio checked description="For growing teams that need more control.">Pro</Radio>
```

**Don't**: Center-aligning the control floats it to the vertical middle of a two-line label, leaving it visually unattached to the title it controls.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "column", gap: 10 }}>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
    <Radio checked />
    <View>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 13, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Pro</Text>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>For growing teams that need more control.</Text>
    </View>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Inline

**Do**: Keep generous spacing between options and tighter spacing inside each so every label clearly pairs with its own control.

```tsx
<RadioGroup row defaultValue="hobby">
  <Radio value="hobby" small>Hobby</Radio>
  <Radio value="pro" small>Pro</Radio>
  <Radio value="enterprise" small>Enterprise</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

**Don't**: Cramped spacing between options makes each label blur into the next radio, so it is hard to tell which dot belongs to which choice.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", gap: 6 }}>
  <Radio checked small>Hobby</Radio>
  <Radio small>Pro</Radio>
  <Radio small>Enterprise</Radio>
</View>
```

### Card

**Do**: Give the selected card a primary border and tinted fill so the whole tile reads as chosen, not just the dot. Pass `card` and the control derives that treatment from its checked state automatically.

```tsx
<RadioGroup row defaultValue="pro">
  <Radio card value="pro" description="For growing teams.">Pro</Radio>
  <Radio card value="enterprise" description="Advanced security.">Enterprise</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

**Don't**: When the selected card keeps the same plain border, only the tiny native dot signals the choice and the active card is easy to miss.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 8 }}>
  <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", flexDirection: "column", borderRadius: 6, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, padding: 14 }}>
    <Radio checked style={{ marginBottom: 8 }} />
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 13, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens.foreground }}>Pro</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>For growing teams.</Text>
  </View>
  <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", flexDirection: "column", borderRadius: 6, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, padding: 14 }}>
    <Radio style={{ marginBottom: 8 }} />
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 13, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens.foreground }}>Enterprise</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Advanced security.</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

## Supported props

### RadioGroupProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | string \| number \| undefined | no |  | The selected option's value (CONTROLLED). Omit for uncontrolled use. |
| defaultValue | string \| number \| undefined | no |  | Initial selected value for uncontrolled use (a bare group selects on press). |
| onChange | ((value: string \| number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired with the newly selected option's value. |
| disabled | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Disable every radio in the group. |
| row | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Lay the options out in a wrapping row instead of the default column. iOS keeps its checkmark list vertical (a list has no row form); `card` options still sit in a row there. |
| equal | boolean \| undefined | no | false | With `row`: the options share the row equally and never wrap, a tile picker's even columns (card tiles 10 apart, plain options 20). |
| inlineLabel | boolean \| undefined | no | false | With `row` and a `label`: the label sits at the start of the row, before the options and centred on them, in the 500 13 px muted ink (a short setting's inline choice: "Digest ( ) Daily (o) Weekly"), instead of as a heading above. The `description` is not shown inline. |
| label | string \| undefined | no |  | The group's name, rendered as a heading above the options. It also becomes the radiogroup's accessible name, so a screen reader announces what the set of options is about before reading them. The group owns this label anatomy; never hand-compose a heading Text beside a bare group. |
| description | ReactNode | no |  | Optional muted supporting line rendered under the label. |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | The `<Radio value="…">` options that make up the group. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the group container. |
| style | StyleProp<ViewStyle> | no |  | Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook. |

### RadioProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | string \| number \| undefined | no |  | This option's value within a RadioGroup. When the radio sits inside a `<RadioGroup>`, its checked state and selection are driven by the group matching this value; ignored for a standalone radio. |
| checked | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Whether this control is the selected option (controlled; standalone use). |
| selected | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Alias for `checked`, for callers that think in terms of "selected". |
| onChange | ((checked: boolean, event: GestureResponderEvent) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired on press with the next checked value (always true for a radio). Web keyboard activation supports Space on release and Enter; RadioGroup also handles arrows. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the pressable row. |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | Label text (the option's title) shown beside the control. |
| description | ReactNode | no |  | Optional muted secondary line rendered under the label, for the common title-plus-description option (a plan picker, a settings choice). Supplying it builds the stacked title/description layout inside the control, so the caller never hand-composes a Row + Column + two Typography nodes per option. |
| card | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Render the whole control as a selectable option CARD: the mark (the ring, or the trailing check on iOS) plus the title and description sit inside Card chrome (bordered, padded), and the ENTIRE card is the tap target. When this radio is the chosen option, the card takes Card's own `selected` treatment (a primary border and a soft primary tint), so the whole tile reads as chosen, not just the mark. Pairs with `description` for a plan/tier picker, and is still group-wired through `value` inside a `<RadioGroup>`. |
| meta | ReactNode | no |  | A trailing detail on the title's line (a version, a price, a status pill): a string is set in the small mono meta type in the subtle ink, a node (a `Badge`) as it is. The title takes the row, so in a full-width option the detail sits at its end; in a `row` group's hugging option it follows the title. |
| icon | ReactNode | no |  | A `card` tile's icon (a kit `Icon` with no tone of its own): the tile stacks the icon and the mark on one line above the title and description. The icon takes the accent text ink while the option is chosen and the subtle ink otherwise. Ignored without `card`. |
| small | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Size (pick one; default is the 18px control on the web). |
| large | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Size (pick one; default is the 18px control on the web). |
| disabled | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Dim the control and block presses. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |
| ref | React.Ref<View> | no |  | Ref to the interactive radio row, preserving group navigation. Typed as a React Native View. On web, React Native Web exposes its DOM host; focus() and blur() move browser focus. Native host behavior depends on the platform and React Native version. Calling focus() does not activate the control or call accessibility focus APIs. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# RangeAreaChart

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/range-area-chart

## Public imports

```tsx
import { RangeAreaChart } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A min/max envelope: a translucent band between each label's `low` and `high`, an optional solid `mid` line through it, and the standard scrub-to-inspect flag showing High, Mid, and Low. The y domain hugs the data rather than anchoring at zero, since an envelope is a range idiom, not a magnitude bar. Forecast bands, error envelopes, and daily temperature ranges all read this way.

## Usage

```tsx
<RangeAreaChart
  label="p50 to p99"
  labels={["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]}
  data={[
    { low: 42, high: 118, mid: 61 },
    { low: 38, high: 102, mid: 55 },
    { low: 44, high: 131, mid: 66 },
    { low: 40, high: 95, mid: 52 },
    { low: 47, high: 144, mid: 71 },
    { low: 36, high: 88, mid: 49 },
    { low: 34, high: 81, mid: 46 },
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Band only

## Do & Don't

### RangeAreaChart

**Do** - Encode uncertainty as the band and the estimate as the mid line, in one mark.

```tsx
<RangeAreaChart

label="Confidence band"
labels={["W1", "W2", "W3", "W4"]}

  { low: 90, high: 110, mid: 100 },
  { low: 95, high: 125, mid: 108 },
  { low: 100, high: 140, mid: 118 },
```

**Don't** - Two separate lines for low and high leave the envelope unreadable as a region and double the legend.

```tsx
<LineChart
```

# Reveal

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/reveal/reveal.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/reveal

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Reveal, RevealGroup } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

An entrance for page content: what it wraps starts slightly offset and transparent, then travels into place and fades in when it reaches the viewport. It fires once and stays, so content that has arrived never leaves again.

Direction chooses the axis it travels from, with `fromBelow` the default and `fromAbove`, `fromLeft`, `fromRight` the alternatives (that is also the precedence order if more than one is passed). `pronounced` travels further, `brisk` arrives faster, and `deepInView` holds the entrance until the element is properly inside the viewport instead of firing as it enters.

Stagger is structural rather than numeric: wrap a set in `RevealGroup` and each child arrives after the one before it, so no call site ever computes a delay. `RevealGroup` renders no box of its own, so it can sit between a grid and the items the grid lays out.

The trigger is measured against the window rather than the nearest scrolling parent, so content sitting inside a short inner scroller can arrive before that scroller has been scrolled to it; reveal on the page scroll, which is what this is for. Under Reduce Motion the content renders its final frame immediately, with no measuring and no timers, and the stagger is skipped along with the motion.

## Usage

```tsx
<Reveal>
  <Card>
    <Typography>Rises into place</Typography>
  </Card>
</Reveal>
```

## Variants

### From above

```tsx
<Reveal fromAbove>
  <Card>
    <Typography>Descends into place</Typography>
  </Card>
</Reveal>
```

### From the left

```tsx
<Reveal fromLeft>
  <Card>
    <Typography>Slides in from the left</Typography>
  </Card>
</Reveal>
```

### From the right

```tsx
<Reveal fromRight>
  <Card>
    <Typography>Slides in from the right</Typography>
  </Card>
</Reveal>
```

### Pronounced

```tsx
<Reveal pronounced>
  <Card>
    <Typography>Travels further before settling</Typography>
  </Card>
</Reveal>
```

### Brisk

```tsx
<Reveal brisk>
  <Card>
    <Typography>Arrives faster</Typography>
  </Card>
</Reveal>
```

### Deep in view

```tsx
<Reveal deepInView>
  <Card>
    <Typography>Waits until it is properly in view</Typography>
  </Card>
</Reveal>
```

### Staggered group

```tsx
<Row wrap>
  <RevealGroup>
    <Reveal>
      <Container xxxs>
        <Card>
          <Typography>Measure</Typography>
        </Card>
      </Container>
    </Reveal>
    <Reveal>
      <Container xxxs>
        <Card>
          <Typography>Reveal</Typography>
        </Card>
      </Container>
    </Reveal>
    <Reveal>
      <Container xxxs>
        <Card>
          <Typography>Settle</Typography>
        </Card>
      </Container>
    </Reveal>
  </RevealGroup>

```

```tsx
  )}
</Ticker>
```

## Do & Don't

### stagger

**Do** - Wrap the set in a `RevealGroup` and let each item's position set its own rhythm.

```tsx
<Row cozy wrap>
  <RevealGroup>
    <Reveal>
      <Container xxxs>
        <Card padded>
          <Typography small semibold>First</Typography>
        </Card>
      </Container>
    </Reveal>
    <Reveal>
      <Container xxxs>
        <Card padded>
          <Typography small semibold>Second</Typography>
        </Card>
      </Container>
    </Reveal>
    <Reveal>
      <Container xxxs>
        <Card padded>
          <Typography small semibold>Third</Typography>
        </Card>
      </Container>
    </Reveal>
  </RevealGroup>
</Row>
```

**Don't** - Leave a set ungrouped: every card fires at the same instant, so the row lands as one slab instead of a cascade.

```tsx
<Row cozy wrap>
  <Reveal>
    <Container xxxs>
      <Card padded>
        <Typography small semibold>First</Typography>
      </Card>
    </Container>
  </Reveal>
  <Reveal>
    <Container xxxs>
      <Card padded>
        <Typography small semibold>Second</Typography>
      </Card>
    </Container>
  </Reveal>
  <Reveal>
    <Container xxxs>
      <Card padded>
        <Typography small semibold>Third</Typography>
      </Card>
    </Container>
  </Reveal>
</Row>
```

### direction

**Do** - Give a set one direction, so it arrives as a single gesture.

```tsx
<Row cozy wrap>
  <RevealGroup>
    <Reveal fromBelow>
      <Container xxxs>
        <Card padded>
          <Typography small semibold>Rises</Typography>
        </Card>
      </Container>
    </Reveal>
    <Reveal fromBelow>
      <Container xxxs>
        <Card padded>
          <Typography small semibold>Rises</Typography>
        </Card>
      </Container>
    </Reveal>
  </RevealGroup>
</Row>
```

**Don't** - Mix a direction per item; the set reads as scattered rather than as one movement.

```tsx
<Row cozy wrap>
  <RevealGroup>
    <Reveal fromLeft>
      <Container xxxs>
        <Card padded>
          <Typography small semibold>Left</Typography>
        </Card>
      </Container>
    </Reveal>
    <Reveal fromRight>
      <Container xxxs>
        <Card padded>
          <Typography small semibold>Right</Typography>
        </Card>
      </Container>
    </Reveal>
  </RevealGroup>
</Row>
```

### scope

**Do** - Reveal the block, so its contents arrive together as one piece of content.

```tsx
<Reveal>
  <Card padded>
    <Column tight>
      <Typography h4 semibold>One entrance</Typography>
      <Typography small muted>The card and its lines arrive as a single object.</Typography>
    </Column>
  </Card>
</Reveal>
```

**Don't** - Reveal each leaf inside one card; the card assembles itself in pieces in front of the reader.

```tsx
<Card padded>
  <Column tight>
    <Reveal>
      <Typography h4 semibold>Three entrances</Typography>
    </Reveal>
    <Reveal>
      <Typography small muted>Every line arrives on its own schedule.</Typography>
    </Reveal>
  </Column>
</Card>
```

### the real thing

**Do** - Use the atom, so the entrance is one prop, plays on scroll, and honors Reduce Motion.

```tsx
<Reveal pronounced>
  <Card padded>
    <Typography small semibold>Reveals itself</Typography>
  </Card>
</Reveal>
```

**Don't** - Hand-roll it with a wrapper and a hard-coded opacity: it never arrives, never watches the scroll position, and ignores Reduce Motion.

```tsx
<View style={{ opacity: 0.35, width: 300, maxWidth: "100%" }}>
  <Card padded>
    <Typography small semibold>Stuck half-arrived</Typography>
  </Card>
</View>
```

## Supported props

### RevealGroupProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | The Reveals to stagger. Each direct child receives the next ordinal in document order, so a mapped list arrives one item after another with no per-item props. |

### RevealProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| fromBelow | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Rise into place from below. The default. |
| fromAbove | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Descend into place from above. |
| fromLeft | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Slide in from the left. Physical, and does not mirror under RTL (see above). |
| fromRight | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Slide in from the right. Physical, and does not mirror under RTL (see above). |
| pronounced | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Travel further before settling, for a hero or a section header. Omit for the default, shorter travel. |
| brisk | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Arrive faster, for dense sets where the eye should not wait. Omit for the default duration. |
| deepInView | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Wait until the element is properly inside the viewport before starting, instead of firing as it enters. |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | The content to reveal. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Outer layout composition ONLY: how this wrapper sits in its parent (a `minWidth` of 0 so a grid child may shrink below its content, a `height` of 100% so cards in a row stay even, a flex share). It is NOT a restyle hook: the entrance itself is chosen entirely with the boolean props above, and the revealed content styles itself. A wrapper that cannot be told how to sit in its parent forces callers to add a second wrapper around it, which is worse. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the wrapper. |

<!-- Source: https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/components/row-column.md -->
# Row & Column

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/layout/layout.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/row-column

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Column, Row } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

The layout primitives. `Row` lays children out horizontally, `Column`
vertically. Both own arrangement through semantic boolean axes, a gap scale
(`flush` / `tight` / `snug` / `cozy` / `relaxed` / `loose`), main-axis
distribution (`center`, `between`, …), cross-axis alignment (`alignCenter`,
`baseline`, …), and `wrap` / `fill` / `grow` / `shrink`, so a call site never
hand-rolls `flexDirection`, `gap`, or `alignItems`.

The Argus reference adds intermediate spacing steps without rounding its layout:
`fine` 3, `dense` 5, `compact` 6, `close` 7, `nested` 9, `comfortable` 10,
`balanced` 11, `roomy` 14, `airy` 18, `spacious` 20, `generous` 22,
`section` 26, `panel` 28, `page` 30, `apart` 32 (the space between the side-by-side
panels of one composition), `ample` 40 (between a section page's hero and the body under
it, and between the hero's halves) and `broad` 48 (between the two halves of a page-wide split). Existing named steps keep their values.
Larger active steps take precedence.

`ample` (40) is the step between a section page's hero and the body under it, and between
the hero's halves (the Canvas v4 section pages). `chapter` (64) is the widest step: the
space between a page's chapters, the major sections of a long page (a component detail
page's Playground, Props and Examples). It wins over every other gap step, so the
precedence runs `chapter` > `broad` > `ample` > `apart` > `page` > `panel` > `section` >
`loose` and on down the scale to `flush`. Row, Column and Grid all take them.

`rowsTight`, `rowsComfortable`, `rowsSnug`, `rowsCozy`, `rowsSection` and `rowsPanel` set a
wrapped or stacked row's vertical gap to 4, 10, 8, 12, 26 and 28 independently of its main
gap (a stacked `Row stacks` lays its children down that vertical gap, so a hero whose
halves sit 40 apart beside each other and 28 apart stacked is `ample rowsPanel`). Application inset
roles preserve identity headers (24 top/horizontal, 18 bottom), action footers
(16 vertical, 24 horizontal), theme controls (14 top, 26 horizontal), status bands
(10 vertical, 28 horizontal), and navigation close controls (12 top/horizontal):
`insetIdentity`, `insetActions`, `insetTheme`, `insetStatus`, and `insetTabs`.

## Usage

```tsx
<Row>
  <Button primary>Save</Button>
  <Button ghost>Cancel</Button>
</Row>
```

## Variants

### Vertical stack

```tsx
<Column>
  <Button primary>Save</Button>
  <Button ghost>Cancel</Button>
</Column>
```

### Chapters

The widest gap, between the major sections of a long page.

```tsx
<Column chapter>
  <Typography h3 level={2}>Playground</Typography>
  <Typography h3 level={2}>Props</Typography>
  <Typography h3 level={2}>Examples</Typography>
</Column>
```

### Centered row

```tsx
<Row center>
  <Badge>schema</Badge>
  <Badge>role</Badge>
</Row>
```

### Space between

```tsx
<Row between>
  <Typography small>Request ID</Typography>
  <Typography mono>req_8f2c10ab</Typography>
</Row>
```

### Wrap

```tsx
<Row wrap>
  <Badge>alpha</Badge>
  <Badge>beta</Badge>
  <Badge>gamma</Badge>
  <Badge>delta</Badge>
  <Badge>epsilon</Badge>
  <Badge>zeta</Badge>
</Row>
```

### Shrink a child to the row

React Native gives every box `flexShrink: 0`, the opposite of the web's flex
default, so a Row child sized by a long sentence keeps that sentence's full
single-line width and spills past the row's edge, where the nearest clipping
ancestor cuts it mid-word. `shrink` hands the row's width back to the text: the
child gives way and the copy wraps. Reach for it on the copy in a
heading-beside-actions row, or any Row child whose width should follow the row
rather than its own longest line. It is not `fill`: `fill` also zeroes the flex
basis, so in a `wrap` row every child then fits on one line and the actions stop
wrapping below the copy.

```tsx
<Row between alignEnd wrap>
  <Column tight shrink>
    <Typography h3>Dashboard</Typography>
    <Typography small muted>Identity platform overview. Each widget reports its own window.</Typography>
  </Column>
  <Button outline small>Export</Button>
</Row>
```

### Padded surround

```tsx
<Card flush>
  <Row pad>
    <Typography>Padded surround</Typography>
  </Row>
</Card>
```

### Stacks at narrow widths

`stacks` renders the Row as a Column when the row's own container is at or
below `stackBreakpoint` (default `sm` = 640): container-measured, so it stacks
inside a narrow desktop column too, and the same gap, distribution, alignment,
and padding props apply to the new axes. Children keep their own sizing, which
makes `stacks` the tool for content-sized rows (a toolbar, a label beside its
actions); equal-width tiles that should renumber columns belong to `Grid`. A
Column never needs the inverse: a Column that must become a Row is a Row that
stacks.

```tsx
<Row stacks>
  <Input placeholder="Search runs" />
  <Button primary>New run</Button>
</Row>
```

### Spans (twelfths of the Row)

A direct child's `span` is its width in twelfths of the Row, Bootstrap's
`col-n`: `span={6}` is half, `span={4}` a third, `span={8}` two thirds. The Row
measures its own width and hands each spanning child a px cell with the gaps
accounted for, so two `span={6}` children and the gap between them fill the row
exactly, and spans past twelve wrap onto the next line. Fill components inside a
span (a field, a card) fill the cell.

```tsx
<Row>
  <Column span={8}>
    <Card>
      <Typography medium>Eight of twelve</Typography>
    </Card>
  </Column>
  <Column span={4}>
    <Card>
      <Typography medium>Four</Typography>
    </Card>
  </Column>
</Row>
```

### Spans that stack

`stacks` and spans compose: below the breakpoint the Row becomes a Column and
every child is full width, the `col-12 col-md-6` idiom without a second prop.
Crossing the breakpoint changes the layout only: every child stays mounted, so
a field keeps its text and focus when a window is resized across it or a phone
switches from the server's desktop layout after hydration. This is why a
two-pane screen is a `Row stacks` of spans rather than a Row on one side of a
`useFormFactor()` branch and a Column on the other, which remounts everything
inside.

```tsx
<Row stacks>
  <Column span={6}>
    <Card>
      <Typography medium>Left</Typography>
    </Card>
  </Column>
  <Column span={6}>
    <Card>
      <Typography medium>Right</Typography>
    </Card>
  </Column>
</Row>
```

### Weights (a share of the free width)

A direct child's `weight` is its share of the Row's width after the gaps, CSS
grid's `fr`: `weight={1.7}` beside `weight={1}` splits the row 1.7 to 1 whatever
either side holds, for the ratios twelfths cannot name. A weighted box has no
content floor, so text inside it wraps rather than pushing its neighbour. It
replaces `fill` and `grow` on the same box, a box takes a `span` or a `weight`,
not both, and once a `stacks` Row has stacked every weighted child is the whole
line.

```tsx
<Row stacks>
  <Column weight={1.7}>
    <Card>
      <Typography medium>The figure</Typography>
    </Card>
  </Column>
  <Column weight={1}>
    <Card>
      <Typography medium>Its legend</Typography>
    </Card>
  </Column>
</Row>
```

## Do & Don't

### Gap

**Do** — Use the gap scale so spacing tracks the kit's spacing tokens.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter snug>
  <Button primary>Save</Button>
  <Button ghost>Cancel</Button>
</Row>
```

**Don't** — Hand-roll `flexDirection` and a raw `gap`; that is a styling escape hatch.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
  <Button primary>Save</Button>
  <Button ghost>Cancel</Button>
</View>
```

### Alignment

**Do** — Reach for the main- and cross-axis booleans (`between`, `alignCenter`).

```tsx
<Row between alignCenter>
  <Typography small>Total</Typography>
  <Typography h5>$1,240.00</Typography>
</Row>
```

**Don't** — Push content around with raw `justifyContent` and `marginLeft`.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row" }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, color: "#71717a" }}>Total</Text>
  <Text style={{ marginLeft: "auto", fontWeight: "600" }}>$1,240.00</Text>
</View>
```

### Overflow

**Do** — Mark the child that may give way with `shrink`, so its text wraps to the row.

```tsx
<Row between alignEnd wrap snug>
  <Column tight shrink>
    <Typography h5>Sessions</Typography>
    <Typography small muted>Every session Kratos is holding open, newest first.</Typography>
  </Column>
  <Button primary small>Revoke all</Button>
</Row>
```

**Don't** — Reach into the raw view to unstick it; that is a styling escape hatch.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", justifyContent: "space-between", gap: 8 }}>
  <View style={{ flexShrink: 1, minWidth: 0 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 16, fontWeight: "600" }}>Sessions</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 13, color: "#71717a" }}>Every session Kratos is holding open, newest first.</Text>
  </View>
  <Button primary small>Revoke all</Button>
</View>
```

| shrink | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Let this box shrink below its own content width when the line runs out of room (`flexShrink: 1`), so a long text child wraps instead of overflowing. React Native gives every box `flexShrink: 0`, which is the opposite of the web's flex default: inside a Row, a Column holding a sentence keeps its MAX-CONTENT width and spills past the row's edge, where the nearest clipping ancestor cuts it mid-word. `shrink` is the opt-in that hands the row's width back to the text. Reach for it on the copy in a heading-beside-actions row, a label beside a control, any Row child whose width should follow the row rather than its own longest line. It is not `fill`. `fill` (flex: 1) also zeroes the flex BASIS, so in a `wrap` row every child then fits on one line and the actions stop wrapping below the copy; `shrink` leaves the basis at the content size, so the row still breaks where it did and only the over-wide child gives way. Redundant alongside `fill`, which already shrinks. |

Container-measured with a viewport seed for the first frame, so a Row inside a narrow desktop column stacks too, not just on phones. When stacked, the Row IS the Column with the same props: gap, justify, align, and padding apply to the new axes, the default `stretch` cross-axis makes children full width, and `wrap` is inert. Ignored (with a DEV warning) on Column: a Column that must become a Row is a Row that stacks. |
| stackBreakpoint | BreakpointKey \| undefined | no |  | The breakpoint at and below which `stacks` flips to a column (default `"sm"`). Only meaningful with `stacks` (DEV warns without it). |
| span | number \| undefined | no |  | Width in twelfths of the parent Row (Bootstrap `.col-n`): `span={6}` is half the row, `span={4}` a third, `span={12}` the full width. The Row measures its own width and gives this box a px cell, gaps included in the arithmetic, so two `span={6}` children plus the gap between them fill the row exactly. Spans over twelve wrap onto the next line. A Row with `stacks` ignores spans once it has stacked (every child is then full width). Only meaningful on a direct child of a Row (DEV warns elsewhere); in a Column, a width is a Container step. A child without a span, `fill`, or `grow` hugs its content (`.col-auto`): a fill component inside it collapses, so give it one of those. |
| weight | number \| undefined | no |  | A share of the parent Row's free width, CSS grid's `minmax(0, Nfr)`: siblings with `weight={1.7}` and `weight={1}` split the row 1.7 to 1 after the gap, whatever their content, and neither holds a content floor. It is the split a ratio of twelfths cannot name (the Canvas v4 component page's anatomy is 1.7 to 1, where `span` gives 7 to 5). A positive number; it replaces `fill` and `grow` on the same box, and a box takes a `span` or a `weight`, not both. Only meaningful on a direct child of a Row (DEV warns elsewhere); once a `stacks` Row has stacked, the box is the whole line and the weight is ignored. |
| indent | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Indent the whole stack by one control gutter (24: a control box plus the row gap), so a nested option group lines up under its parent control's label instead of its box. For nesting checkboxes/radios under a "select all" parent. |
| padTight | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Padding scale (pick one; omit for none). |
| pad | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Padding scale (pick one; omit for none). |
| padLoose | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Padding scale (pick one; omit for none). |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | StyleProp<ViewStyle> | no |  | Layout containers are the exception to the no-sizing rule: for sizing and composition only (a `maxWidth` on a shell, a `flex` inside an app frame), never for styling or spacing. Gap, margin, padding, and flex layout come from the props above, and the codegen guardrail rejects those keys in `style`. Prefer a Container step or a `span` where one fits. |
