# Stats

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/molecules/stats/stats.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/stats

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Stats } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Single value, grouped row, with sparkline, with comparison. Used for dashboards and overview pages.

Under the value each tile can draw one strip: its trend (`spark`) or its composition (`share`). Both reserve the same height, so a row that mixes them keeps one card height and no tile is left half empty. `framed` puts every strip on a muted track, which is what makes a ROW of them scan evenly.

The metrics sit edge to edge inside one bordered surface, a hairline between each: a 16px
inset, a 13px label, a 28px figure and a 12px delta led by its direction arrow. `framed`
separates them into tiles 12px apart. A trend draws as a small line beside the figure and
a composition as a thin bar over its legend. `compact` renders value-first rail tiles with
a 12px inset and 20px figures; `large` renders 36px dashboard headlines; compact wins if
both are set. Each item may include a muted `description`.

## Usage

```tsx
<Stats
  items={[
    { label: "Active users", value: "71,897", delta: "+12.3% vs. last 30 days" }
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Group

```tsx
<Stats
  items={[
    { label: "Total users", value: "12,847", delta: "+12.5%" },
    { label: "Error rate", value: "0.12%", delta: "+0.03%", down: true },
    { label: "Avg. session", value: "4m 32s", delta: "last 30 days", steady: true }
  ]}
/>
```

### Plain

```tsx
<Stats
  plain
  items={[
    { label: "Revenue", value: "$48.2k" },
    { label: "Orders", value: "842" },
    { label: "Conversion", value: "3.6%" }
  ]}
/>
```

### Per-tile icon, control and accent

```tsx
<Stats
  items={[
    { label: "Active users", value: "12,348", icon: <Icon users muted size={16} />, chart1: true },
    { label: "Sessions", value: "489", actions: <Button ghost small>7d</Button>, chart2: true }
  ]}
/>
```

### Sparkline

```tsx
<Stats
  items={[
    { label: "Requests", value: "24.5k", delta: "+8.2%", spark: [4, 8, 6, 12, 10, 16, 14, 18] }
  ]}
/>
```

### Composition strip

A metric that has no trend to plot usually still decomposes. `share` draws that
composition over a muted rail, in the same slot and at the same height as the
sparkline, so it fills the tile with something true rather than with padding.

```tsx
<Stats
  items={[
    { label: "Verified identities", value: "81.3%", delta: "1,502 of 1,847 verified", steady: true, share: [{ label: "Verified", value: 1502 }, { label: "Unverified", value: 345 }] }
  ]}
/>
```

### Framed strips

Without a frame each strip draws only its marks, so a quiet series shows a
near-empty band beside a full bar and the row's densities range from blank to
solid. `framed` gives every strip the same track whatever its data: a flat
series then reads as a chart sitting at zero, and the fill is the only thing
that varies.

```tsx
<Stats
  framed
  items={[
    { label: "Requests", value: "24.5k", delta: "+8.2%", spark: [4, 8, 6, 12, 10, 16, 14, 18] },
    { label: "Errors", value: "0", delta: "None in the last hour", steady: true, spark: [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] }
  ]}
/>
```

### Mixed strips in one row

```tsx
<Stats
  framed
  items={[
    { label: "Requests", value: "24.5k", delta: "+8.2%", spark: [4, 8, 6, 12, 10, 16, 14, 18] },
    { label: "Verified identities", value: "81.3%", delta: "1,502 of 1,847 verified", steady: true, share: [{ label: "Verified", value: 1502 }, { label: "Unverified", value: 345 }] }
  ]}
/>
```

### Tappable

```tsx
<Stats
  onPressItem={() => {}}
  items={[
    { label: "Active users", value: "71,897" },
    { label: "Revenue", value: "$48.2k" }
  ]}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### Single

**Do** — Name the comparison and the period so the delta is unambiguous.

```tsx
<Stats items={[
  { label: "Active users", value: "71,897", delta: "+12.3% vs. last 30 days" }
]} />
```

**Don't** — A bare delta with no baseline leaves the reader asking: up against what, and over what window?

```tsx
<Stats items={[
  { label: "Active users", value: "71,897", delta: "+12.3%" }
]} />
```

### Group

**Do** — Use the auto-fit grid and round headline numbers so cards wrap and stay scannable.

```tsx
<Stats items={[
    { label: "Revenue", value: "$48.2k", delta: "+12.5%" },
    { label: "Orders", value: "842", delta: "+3.2%" },
    { label: "Conversion", value: "3.6%", delta: "+0.4%" }
  ]} />
```

**Don't** — A fixed flex row of full-precision numbers overflows on narrow viewports and crowds the cards.

```tsx
<Stats items={[
    { label: "Revenue", value: "$48,250.00", delta: "+12.5%" },
    { label: "Orders", value: "842", delta: "+3.2%" },
    { label: "Conversion", value: "3.6%", delta: "+0.4%" }
  ]} />
```

### Plain (no border)

**Do** — On a parent surface drop the border and radius; let the number stacks stand on their own.

```tsx
<Stats plain items={[
    { label: "Revenue", value: "$48.2k" },
    { label: "Orders", value: "842" }
  ]} />
```

**Don't** — Bordered cards inside a card surface double the chrome: a box drawn around boxes.

```tsx
<View style={{ borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.card, boxShadow: "0px 16px 32px -22px rgba(121, 100, 214, 0.22)", padding: 24 }}>
  <Stats items={[
    { label: "Revenue", value: "$48.2k" },
    { label: "Orders", value: "842" }
  ]} />
</View>
```

### With sparkline

**Do** — Pair the sparkline with an explicit delta so the headline reads without decoding the curve.

```tsx
<Stats
  items={[
    { label: "Requests", value: "24.5k", delta: "+8.2%", spark: [4, 8, 6, 12, 10, 16, 14, 18, 16, 20, 24] }
  ]}
/>
```

**Don't** — A trend line with no current delta makes you eyeball the slope to guess the direction.

```tsx
<View style={{ borderRadius: 8, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.card, boxShadow: "0px 16px 32px -22px rgba(121, 100, 214, 0.22)", maxWidth: 220, padding: 20 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Requests</Text>
  <Text style={{ marginTop: 4, fontSize: 24, lineHeight: 32, fontWeight: "600", letterSpacing: -0.4, color: tokens.foreground }}>24.5k</Text>
  <View style={{ marginTop: 12, flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "flex-end", gap: 2, height: 24 }}>
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderRadius: 2, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.7), height: 4 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderRadius: 2, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.7), height: 8 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderRadius: 2, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.7), height: 6 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderRadius: 2, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.7), height: 12 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderRadius: 2, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.7), height: 10 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderRadius: 2, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.7), height: 16 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderRadius: 2, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.7), height: 14 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderRadius: 2, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.7), height: 18 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderRadius: 2, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.7), height: 16 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderRadius: 2, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.7), height: 20 }} />
    <View style={{ flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", borderRadius: 2, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.7), height: 24 }} />
  </View>
</View>
```

### A strip on every tile in a row

**Do** — Give every tile in a row a strip: the trend where one exists, the composition where it does not, and frame them so the row reads as one finished set.

```tsx
<Stats framed items={[
    { label: "Requests", value: "24.5k", delta: "+8.2%", spark: [4, 8, 6, 12, 10, 16, 14, 18, 16, 20, 24] },
    { label: "Cache hit rate", value: "94.1%", delta: "23.5k of 25k served warm", steady: true, share: [{ label: "Hit", value: 23525 }, { label: "Miss", value: 1475 }] }
  ]} />
```

**Don't** — Give one tile a strip and leave its neighbour without: cards stretch to the tallest sibling, so the bare tile ends up with a band of blank space that reads as unfinished.

```tsx
<Stats items={[
    { label: "Requests", value: "24.5k", delta: "+8.2%", spark: [4, 8, 6, 12, 10, 16, 14, 18, 16, 20, 24] },
    { label: "Cache hit rate", value: "94.1%", delta: "23.5k of 25k served warm", steady: true }
  ]} />
```

## Supported props

### StatsProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | StatItem[] | yes |  | The metrics to render, in order. |
| plain | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Borderless metric stacks on a shared surface, for nesting inside a card. |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Dense value-first tile for a navigation rail: a 12px inset and a 20px headline. |
| large | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Value-first dashboard tile with a 36px headline. |
| title | string \| undefined | no |  | Optional heading shown above the metrics (mainly for the plain surface). |
| framed | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Draw every metric's strip on a muted track, in one bounded band. For a ROW of metrics, where the strips are read against each other. Without it each strip draws only its marks, so a metric with a quiet series shows a near-empty band beside one with a full bar and the row's densities range from blank to solid with nothing tying them together; the eye lands on the fullest tile rather than scanning the row. The track gives every strip the same frame whatever its data, so a flat series reads as a chart sitting at zero and the fill is the only thing that varies. |
| onPressItem | ((index: number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Make each metric a tappable target (drill into the underlying detail). When set, every metric renders as a Pressable with a button role and a pressed affordance, so a tappable stat needs no hand-rolled Pressable. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

# Stepper

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/stepper/stepper.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/stepper

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Stepper } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Increment, decrement, or type a number in a bounded range. A − button, an editable numeric center field, and a + button, controlled by `value` and clamped to `min` / `max` by `step`.
This is the ± numeric control (the iOS UIStepper idiom); for a multi-step progress indicator see Steps.

On the web the control is one 40 px box (32 `small`, 48 `large`) at the control corner with square ± cells and the value in the mono face; on iOS the capsule [ − | + ] pill with the value to its left; on Android Material 3's outlined circular icon buttons around the value.

Pass `label` to title the control from above, `description` for a secondary line under it, and `required` to mark it: the label takes a decorative destructive star, and a screen reader hears the control as required,
from `aria-required` on the web's numeric field and from its name ("Quantity, required") on iOS and Android.

## Usage

```tsx
<Stepper defaultValue={3} max={10} />
```

## Variants

### With label

```tsx
<Stepper label="Quantity" defaultValue={1} min={1} max={9} />
```

### With description

```tsx
<Stepper label="Quantity" description="Up to 10 per order." defaultValue={1} min={1} max={10} />
```

### With suffix

`suffix` sets a unit beside the control, in the subtle ink.

```tsx
<Stepper label="Spacing" suffix="× 4px" defaultValue={2} min={0} max={99} />
```

### Sizes

```tsx
<Row alignCenter relaxed>
  <Stepper small defaultValue={2} max={10} />
  <Stepper defaultValue={2} max={10} />
  <Stepper large defaultValue={2} max={10} />
</Row>
```

### With min / max

```tsx
<Row alignCenter relaxed>
  <Stepper defaultValue={0} min={0} max={5} />
  <Stepper defaultValue={5} min={0} max={5} />
</Row>
```

### Stepped

```tsx
<Stepper defaultValue={20} max={100} step={10} />
```

### Disabled

```tsx
<Stepper disabled defaultValue={4} max={10} />
```

## Do & Don't

### Bounds

**Do**: Set `min` and `max` so the buttons disable at the edges and the value can never leave the valid range.

```tsx
<Stepper label="Quantity" defaultValue={1} min={1} max={9} onChange={() => {}} />
```

**Don't**: Leaving the range unbounded lets the user push the count below zero or past what the form can accept.

```tsx
<Stepper defaultValue={1} onChange={() => {}} />
```

### Step

**Do**: Match `step` to the real increment, so each tap moves the value by an amount that makes sense for the field.

```tsx
<Stepper defaultValue={30} min={0} max={120} step={5} onChange={() => {}} />
```

**Don't**: A step of 1 on a field that only takes round numbers makes the user tap many times to reach a usable value.

```tsx
<Stepper defaultValue={30} min={0} max={120} step={1} onChange={() => {}} />
```

## Supported props

### StepperProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | number \| undefined | no |  | Controlled numeric value (clamped to [min, max] for display); omit for uncontrolled use. |
| defaultValue | number \| undefined | no |  | Initial value for uncontrolled use (a bare <Stepper /> steps out of the box). Default `min`. |
| onChange | ((next: number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired with the next clamped value when buttons, adjustment keys, or direct entry change it (both modes). |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the group container. |
| min | number \| undefined | no | 0 | Lower bound. Default 0. The − button disables when value <= min. |
| max | number \| undefined | no |  | Upper bound. Default Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. The + button disables when value >= max. |
| step | number \| undefined | no | 1 | Increment/decrement amount for the ± buttons and adjustment keys. Default 1. |
| label | string \| undefined | no |  | The control's persistent, component-owned label. When set it renders as a VISIBLE title ABOVE the ± control (mirroring Input's above-field placement, per-OS type from the skin) and becomes the group's programmatic name (wired via accessibilityLabel + aria-labelledby). When omitted, the control keeps the invisible "Number" accessible-name fallback and renders no visible label, so a bare `<Stepper />` looks exactly as before. |
| description | ReactNode | no |  | Optional muted secondary line rendered under the label (parity with Input). Takes effect only alongside `label`. |
| required | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Marks the control required: appends a destructive "*" to the label (decorative, never in the accessible name) and announces the control as required, through aria-required on the web's numeric field and with the word in its name ("Quantity, required") on iOS and Android. The star takes effect only alongside `label`. |
| suffix | ReactNode | no |  | A unit or note beside the control, 16 px after it on the same line ("× 4px", "items"): a string is set in the 400 13 px subtle ink, a node as it is. Unlike `description`, it reads as part of the value's line. |
| small | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Size (pick one; default is the medium control). Precedence: large > small. |
| large | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Size (pick one; default is the medium control). Precedence: large > small. |
| disabled | boolean \| undefined | no | false | State. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |
| ref | React.Ref<RNTextInput> | no |  | Ref to the underlying React Native host. Supports object refs and callback refs; native methods follow the platform's behavior. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# Steps

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/steps/steps.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/steps

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Steps } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Multi-step progress indicators: horizontal, vertical, with progress.

## Usage

```tsx
<Steps
  steps={[{ label: "Account" }, { label: "Profile" }, { label: "Review" }]}
  defaultCurrent={1}
/>
```

## Variants

### Compact sidebar

`compact` with `vertical` renders short 22px markers without connector lines, as a
workflow sidebar. The current row is announced as the current step. Pressable steps
retain their normal controlled and uncontrolled behavior.

```tsx
<Steps vertical compact defaultCurrent={1}
  steps={[{ label: "Name" }, { label: "Members" }, { label: "Theme" }, { label: "Review" }]} />
```

### Sidebar rows

`rows` with `vertical` draws each step as a 32 point row like a desktop app's sidebar
list: the current step's row is filled, done steps carry a check, and the row reads
", done" or ", current" to assistive technology. With `onStepPress` each row is a button.

```tsx
<Steps vertical rows defaultCurrent={1}
  steps={[{ label: "Plan project" }, { label: "Review project plan" }, { label: "Plan workforce" }, { label: "Review team" }]} />
```

### Vertical

```tsx
<Steps
  vertical
  steps={[
    { label: "Account", description: "Email verified and password set." },
    { label: "Profile", description: "Add your name and avatar." },
    { label: "Review", description: "Invite collaborators." }
  ]}
  defaultCurrent={1}
/>
```

### Step progress

A vertical step's title sits on an 18.2 px line over its 12 px description in the third
ink; the current step's description takes the accent's text ink. A step with `progress`
(0 to 100) draws its own 6 px bar 8 px under its text, the fill running from the accent
into the cyan series hue with the accent's glow; the other layouts ignore it.

```tsx
<Steps
  vertical
  steps={[
    { label: "Create workspace", description: "Northwind · EU Frankfurt" },
    { label: "Import components", description: "Restyling 72 of 107", progress: 67 },
    { label: "Invite your team", description: "Optional" }
  ]}
  defaultCurrent={1}
/>
```

### Segmented

`segmented` lays the steps out as equal segments 8 px apart: each a 4 px bar (the
accent once reached, glowing on the current step, the raised surface ahead) over its
500 13 px label and, from its `description`, a status line inked by the step's state:
the success ink once done, the accent's text ink on the current step, the third ink
ahead. The layout precedence is `progress` > `segmented` > `vertical`.

```tsx
<Steps
  segmented
  steps={[
    { label: "Account", description: "Done" },
    { label: "Workspace", description: "Current" },
    { label: "Invite team", description: "Next" }
  ]}
  defaultCurrent={1}
/>
```

### Progress bar

```tsx
<Steps progress steps={[]} value={68} />
```

### Stacks at narrow widths

`stacks` renders the horizontal layout as the vertical one when the component's
own container is at or below `stackBreakpoint` (default `sm` = 640):
container-measured, like Row `stacks`, so a wizard header inside a narrow
column stacks too.

```tsx
<Steps
  stacks
  steps={[{ label: "Account" }, { label: "Profile" }, { label: "Review" }]}
  defaultCurrent={1}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### Horizontal

**Do** — Mark exactly one step active; show completed steps filled and the rest pending.

```tsx
<Steps defaultCurrent={1} steps={[
    { label: "Account" },
    { label: "Profile" },
    { label: "Review" }
  ]} />
```

**Don't** — Styling several steps as active at once hides which step the user is actually on.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "flex-start" }}>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "flex-start", flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%" }}>
    <View style={{ alignItems: "center", gap: 6 }}>
      <View style={{ height: 32, width: 32, flexShrink: 0, flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", borderRadius: 9999, borderWidth: 2, borderColor: tokens.primary, backgroundColor: "transparent" }}>
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.primary }}>1</Text>
      </View>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Account</Text>
    </View>
    <View style={{ marginHorizontal: 8, marginTop: 16, height: 1, flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", backgroundColor: tokens.border }} />
  </View>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "flex-start", flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%" }}>
    <View style={{ alignItems: "center", gap: 6 }}>
      <View style={{ height: 32, width: 32, flexShrink: 0, flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", borderRadius: 9999, borderWidth: 2, borderColor: tokens.primary, backgroundColor: "transparent" }}>
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.primary }}>2</Text>
      </View>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Profile</Text>
    </View>
    <View style={{ marginHorizontal: 8, marginTop: 16, height: 1, flexGrow: 1, flexShrink: 1, flexBasis: "0%", backgroundColor: tokens.border }} />
  </View>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "flex-start" }}>
    <View style={{ alignItems: "center", gap: 6 }}>
      <View style={{ height: 32, width: 32, flexShrink: 0, flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", borderRadius: 9999, borderWidth: 2, borderColor: tokens.primary, backgroundColor: "transparent" }}>
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.primary }}>3</Text>
      </View>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Review</Text>
    </View>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Vertical

**Do** — Pair each vertical step with a one-line description so the extra width earns its place.

```tsx
<Steps vertical defaultCurrent={1} steps={[
  { label: "Account created", description: "Email verified and password set." },
  { label: "Profile setup", description: "Add your name and avatar." },
  { label: "Team invite", description: "Invite collaborators to your workspace." },
  { label: "Done", description: "You're all set." }
]} />
```

**Don't** — A vertical step with only a title wastes the space the layout is built to use.

```tsx
<Steps vertical defaultCurrent={1} steps={[
  { label: "Account created" },
  { label: "Profile setup" },
  { label: "Team invite" },
  { label: "Done" }
]} />
```

### Progress bar

**Do** — Label the bar and show the exact percentage so progress is legible at a glance.

```tsx
<Steps progress current={0} steps={[]} label="Setup progress" value={68} />
```

**Don't** — A bare progress bar with no percentage leaves users guessing how far along they are.

```tsx
<View style={{ height: 6, overflow: "hidden", borderRadius: 9999, backgroundColor: tokens.muted }}>
  <View style={{ height: "100%", borderRadius: 9999, backgroundColor: tokens.primary, width: "68%" }} />
</View>
```

## Supported props

### StepsProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps | Step[] | yes |  | Ordered steps to render. Each is a label with an optional one-line note. |
| current | number \| undefined | no |  | Index of the active step (CONTROLLED). Earlier steps read completed, later ones muted. Omit for uncontrolled use. |
| defaultCurrent | number \| undefined | no |  | Initial active step for uncontrolled use (pressing a step, with `onStepPress`, moves it). |
| vertical | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Layout (pick one; default is horizontal). Precedence: progress, segmented, vertical. |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | A short vertical list with 22px markers and no connector lines, for a workflow sidebar. |
| rows | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Vertical only: each step a 32 px row like a desktop app's sidebar list (the Claude desktop window's), the current step's row filled, done steps marked with a check. |
| segmented | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Equal segments in a row: each step a 4 px bar (the accent once reached, glowing on the current step) over its label and, from its `description`, a status line inked by the step's state (the success ink once done, the accent's text ink on the current step). |
| progress | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Render a labeled percentage progress bar instead of discrete steps. |
| stacks | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Responsive (horizontal layout only): render the EXISTING vertical layout when the component's own CONTAINER is at or below `stackBreakpoint` (default `sm` = 640). Container-measured with a viewport seed, mirroring Row `stacks`. `vertical` and `progress` are unaffected (a progress bar is already fluid). |
| stackBreakpoint | BreakpointKey \| undefined | no |  | The breakpoint at and below which `stacks` goes vertical (default `"sm"`). Only meaningful with `stacks`. |
| value | number \| undefined | no |  | Progress mode only: filled fraction, 0-100 (clamped). Defaults to 0. |
| label | string \| undefined | no |  | Progress mode only: caption shown left of the percentage. |
| onStepPress | ((index: number) => void) \| undefined | no |  | When set, each step circle is pressable, reporting the step index. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

# Swatch

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/swatch/swatch.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/swatch

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Swatch } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A color sample: a filled rounded block with the token's name and value beneath
it, the anatomy a design-system color sheet repeats down a page. Swatch owns the
whole lockup, so a sheet never sets a bare block next to a hand-built text
column and drifts row to row.

Pass a live theme token as `color` and the sample follows the active scheme; a
hairline edge keeps a white or near-black sample visible on the surface behind
it. The chip is 48px at a 12px corner (32 `small`, 72 `large`, and 20 `tiny`,
the disc of a token Chip), the name a 13px line and the value lines 11px mono
in the subtle ink; the lockup also comes as a `circle`, `inline` (the label
beside the block), or as a `block` (a full-width ramp bar). `ring` draws the
edge as a 1px inset ring in the field border instead of the hairline, the token
chip's swatch. `selected` marks the chosen sample with the selection ring, a
2px gap in the page color and then a 2px accent band, and adds "selected" to
its accessible name. `decorative` hides a sample from assistive tech when text
beside it already names it (a theme choice's disc before its label), so the
name is read once.

A palette picker takes one of the kit's five accent palettes, `violet`, `cyan`,
`mint`, `rose` or `amber` (ThemeProvider's precedence: cyan, mint, rose, amber,
violet), with `selected` and `onPress`. It is a 16px disc of the palette's hue,
the same in both schemes, and a radio named for its palette ("Violet"). The
palette in force wears the selection ring, a 2px gap in the card color and then
a 2px muted-foreground band; the others draw none. On the web a hovered disc
grows to 1.25 times its size. A size boolean sizes the disc to that sample edge
(`small` is a 32px disc, the size a form's hue choice takes). Put the pickers in
a `radiogroup` so the set reads as one choice. A plain sample still uses `color`.

The section page's samples come as forms and lockups of the same component. `tile` is
the labelled colour tile, the parent's width and 64 px tall (40 `small`), its name set
inside the fill on one line (ellipsized where it outgrows the tile, its accessible name
whole) in the 11 px code face at an 8 px inset, at the foot (centred `small`),
in the `ink` it is given. `bar` is a colour bar, the parent's width at 26 px and a 7 px
corner. `steps` takes a list of colours in place of `color` and draws one bar of them,
flush and clipped at a 10 px corner at the size's height; `segmented` stands them 4 px
apart in a 28 px bar, each at a 3 px corner but for the bar's two outer ends at 7. The
form precedence is `tile` > `bar` > `circle`, and a `steps` list wins over all three.
`fluid` makes the chip's edge the parent's width, held 1:1; `glow` lays the fill's own
light under the chip; `centered` centres the label column 10 px under the chip; `bare`
drops the resting edge from a fill that needs none; and `compact` is the mono lockup, the
name 500 12 px and the value 400 10 px in the code face, each on one line (ellipsized in a
narrow column), 6 px apart and 6 px under a 56 px `block`.

## Do & Don't

### Anatomy

**Do**: Let Swatch carry the name and the value, so every row of a sheet keeps one lockup and one accessible name.

```tsx
<Swatch color={tokens.primary} value="--primary">
  primary
</Swatch>
```

**Don't**: Set a bare block beside a hand-composed text column: the spacing and the type scale drift row to row, and the sample ships as an unnamed block.

```tsx
<Row snug alignCenter>
  <View style={{ height: 56, width: 56, borderRadius: 8, backgroundColor: "#4f46e5" }} />
  <Column tight>
    <Typography small medium>primary</Typography>
    <Typography tiny subtle>--primary</Typography>
  </Column>
</Row>
```

### Color source

**Do**: Pass the live token, so the sample repaints when the scheme flips.

```tsx
<Swatch color={tokens.card} value="--card">
  card
</Swatch>
```

**Don't**: Hard-code the value a token resolves to; the sample keeps showing the light color after the scheme flips to dark.

```tsx
<Swatch color="#ffffff" value="#ffffff">
  card
</Swatch>
```

# Switch

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/switch/switch.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/switch

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Switch } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

On / off switch, isolated or grouped in a settings list.

In glass mode a switch keeps its solid look on every platform: it is a small
mark inside content, not a surface, so its track and knob draw as in solid mode,
with no pane and no rim, a checked track in its solid brand fill. The track, the
label, the description and the hit target never move, and the checked state flips
at once. A disabled switch is inert.

`small` and `large` scale the track on the web.
Pass `chip` for a compact toolbar setting: a 32 px bordered capsule with a 26×16 track, a 10 px knob and the label after the switch. The web thumb follows the reference spring and Reduce Motion; native skins keep their own switch.
On iOS and Android the switch is the
platform's own control, which comes in one size (51x31 on iOS, 52x32 on Android), so
the size props leave it unchanged there.

Pass `ref` to access the interactive switch row, including its label. Use `useRef<ComponentRef<typeof Switch>>(null)` from React, or `useRef<View>(null)` with React Native's `View` type. Object and callback refs are supported and detach on unmount. Calling `ref.current?.focus()` or `.blur()` delegates to the host without activating the control. Browser focus is supported; native focus depends on the platform and React Native version, and is separate from accessibility focus.

On the web, Space activates the focused control on key release, and Enter also activates it. Holding Space does not repeat the change. Moving focus away, disabling the control, or composing text cancels a pending Space press.

## Usage

```tsx
<Switch defaultChecked>Available to chat</Switch>
```

## Variants

### Off

```tsx
<Switch>Available to chat</Switch>
```

### With description

```tsx
<Switch description="Show your availability to teammates.">Available to chat</Switch>
```

### Disabled

```tsx
<Switch disabled>Available to chat</Switch>
```

### Controlled

```tsx
<Stateful initial={true}>
  {(on, setOn) => <Switch checked={on} onChange={setOn}>Notifications</Switch>}
</Stateful>
```

### Settings list

`listed` gives each row a settings list's 10 px above and below, and `divided` rules a hairline above every row after the first, so the stack reads as one list.

```tsx
<Column tight>
  <Switch listed defaultChecked description="Frosted material on panels and sheets">Glass surfaces</Switch>
  <Switch listed divided description="Zero every duration, keep spinners">Reduced motion</Switch>
  <Switch listed divided defaultChecked>Haptics</Switch>
</Column>
```

## Do & Don't

### Off

**Do** — Keep the standard off track, the raised fill inside its `input` edge, so off stays clearly interactive and distinct from a disabled control.

```tsx
<Switch>Two-factor auth</Switch>
```

**Don't** — A washed-out off track reads as disabled, so users can't tell the switch is simply off versus locked.

```tsx
<Pressable style={{ maxWidth: 280, flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "space-between", gap: 16 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Two-factor auth</Text>
  <View style={{ position: "relative", flexShrink: 0, borderRadius: 9999, width: 36, height: 20, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.muted, 0.3) }}>
    <View style={{ position: "absolute", top: 2, left: 2, borderRadius: 9999, width: 16, height: 16, backgroundColor: tokens.muted }} />
  </View>
</Pressable>
```

### On

**Do** — Reserve the on switch for instantly reversible settings; route irreversible actions through a button plus confirmation.

```tsx
<Column cozy alignStart>
  <Switch defaultChecked>Auto-save drafts</Switch>
  <Button destructive small>Delete account…</Button>
</Column>
```

**Don't** — A switch applies instantly; wiring an on toggle to an irreversible action invites accidental, unconfirmed data loss.

```tsx
<Pressable style={{ maxWidth: 280, flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "space-between", gap: 16 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens["destructive-text"] ?? tokens.destructive }}>Permanently delete account</Text>
  <View style={{ position: "relative", flexShrink: 0, borderRadius: 9999, width: 36, height: 20, backgroundColor: tokens.primary }}>
    <View style={{ position: "absolute", top: 2, right: 2, borderRadius: 9999, width: 16, height: 16, backgroundColor: tokens.background, boxShadow: "0px 20px 44px -24px rgba(121, 100, 214, 0.22)" }} />
  </View>
</Pressable>
```

### Label the setting

**Do** — Label the setting, not the state; the switch communicates on or off.

```tsx
<Switch defaultChecked>Notifications</Switch>
```

**Don't** — An On/Off label duplicates what the switch position already shows.

```tsx
<View style={{ maxWidth: 280, flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "space-between" }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 13 }}>Notifications</Text>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 8 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Off</Text>
    <Switch />
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>On</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

## Supported props

### SwitchProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| checked | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Controlled on/off state; omit for uncontrolled use. |
| defaultChecked | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Initial state for uncontrolled use (a bare <Switch /> is interactive). |
| onChange | ((next: boolean) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired with the next checked value when the switch is toggled (both modes). Web keyboard activation supports Space on release and Enter. |
| onValueChange | ((next: boolean) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Alias of onChange, for parity with RN's value-style callbacks. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the pressable row. |
| small | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Size (pick one; default is the standard track). The web track scales; iOS and Android draw their platform switch, which comes in one size. |
| large | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Size (pick one; default is the standard track). The web track scales; iOS and Android draw their platform switch, which comes in one size. |
| chip | boolean \| undefined | no | false | A compact bordered capsule with its label after the switch, for a toolbar setting. |
| listed | boolean \| undefined | no | false | A row of a settings list: 10 px above and below the row, so a stack of switches reads as a list rather than a form (stack them in a `Column tight`). Pair with `divided` on every row after the first. |
| divided | boolean \| undefined | no | false | A hairline above the row in the `border` ink: a settings list's separator from the row before. |
| disabled | boolean \| undefined | no | false | State. |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | Optional label, rendered to the left of the track. |
| description | ReactNode | no |  | Optional muted description line, rendered under the label. |
| accessibilityLabel | string \| undefined | no |  | Accessible name for the switch when no visible `children` label is rendered (e.g. a switch embedded in an Action Panel whose label sits in sibling Text). Without it, a label-less switch announces only "switch, on/off". |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |
| ref | React.Ref<View> | no |  | Ref to the interactive switch row, including its label. Typed as a React Native View. On web, React Native Web exposes its DOM host; focus() and blur() move browser focus. Native host behavior depends on the platform and React Native version. Calling focus() does not activate the control or call accessibility focus APIs. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# TabBar

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/tab-bar/tab-bar.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/tab-bar

## Public imports

```tsx
import { TabBar } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Bottom app navigation: a row of equal-width destinations, each an icon over a short label, with exactly one active.
The mobile idiom (the iOS 26 floating tab bar / Material 3 navigation bar), rendered through the glass functional layer.

iOS and web share the iOS 26 anatomy: a 62 px capsule that floats above the
content (which scrolls beneath it), inset from the sides, with the safe-area
inset kept under the capsule, and the selected destination washed in the accent
as a capsule covering its whole cell. Android docks the Material 3 bar
full-bleed, 80 tall under a hairline, with its 64 by 32 icon pill. In glass mode
the selection is a control-layer pane on the active destination: the cell
capsule on iOS and web, the icon pill on Android. Solid mode retains the
ordinary platform surface.

## Usage

```tsx
<TabBar
  items={[
    { key: "home", label: "Home", icon: (active) => <Icon home size={19} primary={active} muted={!active} /> },
    { key: "search", label: "Search", icon: (active) => <Icon search size={19} primary={active} muted={!active} /> },
    { key: "profile", label: "Profile", icon: (active) => <Icon user size={19} primary={active} muted={!active} /> }
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Controlled

```tsx
<Stateful initial="home">
  {(active, setActive) => (
    <TabBar
      active={active}
      onSelect={setActive}
      items={[
        { key: "home", label: "Home", icon: (active) => <Icon home size={19} primary={active} muted={!active} /> },
        { key: "search", label: "Search", icon: (active) => <Icon search size={19} primary={active} muted={!active} /> },
        { key: "profile", label: "Profile", icon: (active) => <Icon user size={19} primary={active} muted={!active} /> }
      ]}
    />
  )}
</Stateful>
```

### Unread

An item with `unread` carries a small destructive dot over its glyph, and its accessible
name ends in ", unread". On the web the capsule floats 12 px off its container's sides
and bottom.

```tsx
<TabBar
  items={[
    { key: "home", label: "Home", icon: (active) => <Icon home size={19} primary={active} muted={!active} /> },
    { key: "inbox", label: "Inbox", unread: true, icon: (active) => <Icon inbox size={19} primary={active} muted={!active} /> },
    { key: "profile", label: "Profile", icon: (active) => <Icon user size={19} primary={active} muted={!active} /> }
  ]}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### Tab Bar

**Do** — Exactly one destination carries the primary tint on both its icon and label,
over the raised cell capsule on iOS and web or Material 3's active-indicator pill on Android;
the rest stay muted, so the current tab is always singular and unmistakable. On web the capsule is what lets a bar and a `Sidebar` in the same app shell mark the current destination the same way across the breakpoint that swaps them.

```tsx
<TabBar
  active="home"
  onSelect={() => {}}
  items={[
    { key: "home", label: "Home", icon: (active) => <Icon home size={19} primary={active} muted={!active} /> },
    { key: "search", label: "Search", icon: (active) => <Icon search size={19} primary={active} muted={!active} /> },
    { key: "profile", label: "Profile", icon: (active) => <Icon user size={19} primary={active} muted={!active} /> }
  ]}
/>
```

**Don't** — Tinting every destination primary erases the active indicator: nothing tells you which tab is current.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", borderTopWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.card, paddingTop: 6 }}>
  <View style={{ flex: 1, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", gap: 3, paddingVertical: 4 }}>
    <Icon home size={19} primary />
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 11, lineHeight: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens.primary }}>Home</Text>
  </View>
  <View style={{ flex: 1, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", gap: 3, paddingVertical: 4 }}>
    <Icon search size={19} primary />
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 11, lineHeight: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens.primary }}>Search</Text>
  </View>
  <View style={{ flex: 1, alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", gap: 3, paddingVertical: 4 }}>
    <Icon user size={19} primary />
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 11, lineHeight: 14, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens.primary }}>Profile</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

## Supported props

### TabBarProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | TabBarItem[] | yes |  |  |
| active | string \| undefined | no |  | The active item's key; omit for uncontrolled use. |
| defaultActive | string \| undefined | no |  | Initial active key for uncontrolled use (defaults to the first item's key). |
| onSelect | ((key: string) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Called with the pressed destination's key (both modes). |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the tablist row. |
| bottomInset | number \| undefined | no | 0 | Safe-area bottom inset, e.g. `insets.bottom`. It is added BELOW the bar's own symmetric vertical padding (not in place of it), so the bar clears the home indicator without making the bottom margin heavier than the top. Defaults to 0 (web desktop / no inset). |
| style | StyleProp<ViewStyle> | no |  | Outer layout composition only. Use bottomInset for the safe area. |

<!-- Source: https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/components/tabs.md -->
# Tabs

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/tabs/tabs.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/tabs

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Tabs } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Underline, pill, vertical, with badges.

On the web the underline look marks the active tab with a glowing accent bar on
the row's hairline, pills sit on a rounded track with a raised thumb, and the
vertical rail washes its active row in the accent.
iOS draws its segmented
control (UISegmentedControl): underline and pills are a capsule track with a
raised thumb, and vertical is a grouped rail. Android draws Material 3's tabs.
In glass mode a filled selection is a
control-layer pane behind the selected label, in the platform skin's selected
tint with readable foreground ink. Solid mode keeps the complete platform
treatment.

## Usage

```tsx
<Tabs tabs={["General", "Security", "Notifications"]} />
```

## Variants

### Pill

```tsx
<Tabs pills tabs={["All", "Active", "Archived"]} />
```

### Vertical

```tsx
<Tabs vertical tabs={["General", "Security", "Notifications"]} />
```

### Responsive vertical

`responsive` renders a vertical rail as the horizontal underline look when the
component's own container is at or below `sm` (640): container-measured, so a
settings rail inside a narrow column flattens to a top tab bar instead of
starving the panel beside it.

```tsx
<Tabs vertical responsive tabs={["General", "Security", "Notifications"]} />
```

### Badge counts

On the web a count's numerals take their tab's own ink.

```tsx
<Tabs tabs={[{ label: "All", badge: "142" }, { label: "Active", badge: "89" }, { label: "Archived", badge: "53" }]} />
```

### Disabled tab

```tsx
<Tabs tabs={["Overview", { label: "Billing", disabled: true }, "Settings"]} />
```

### Leading glyphs

A tab item takes an `icon`, a kit glyph before its label in the label's ink (15 px on
the web), as a settings rail names its sections.

```tsx
<Tabs vertical tabs={[{ label: "General", icon: "settings2" }, { label: "Members", icon: "users" }, { label: "Security", icon: "shieldCheck" }]} />
```

### Block

On the web a `block` underline row is equal columns with no gap between them, each
label centred in its own column under its share of the rule.

```tsx
<Tabs block tabs={["Overview", "Activity", "Settings"]} />
```

### Scrollable overflow

A row longer than its container pans horizontally instead of clipping, at any
container width and with no prop: the scroller is inert while the row
fits,
and on Android it then takes no sideways drag either, so a tap that drifts
sideways still selects its tab and a swipe that starts across the row scrolls
the page (while TalkBack explores by touch the scroller stays enabled, so the
exploring finger reaches every tab).
Selecting a tab (press or arrow key)
scrolls it fully into view with a sliver of its neighbor left showing. `block` shares the row equally and never
overflows; a vertical rail stacks instead.

```tsx
<Tabs tabs={["General", "Security", "Notifications", "Billing", "Integrations", "Advanced"]} />
```

### Wrapped overflow

`wrap` lays a row longer than its container out on further lines inside one
track instead of panning it, so every tab is on screen at once: the track fills
its container and grows taller, its corners staying concentric with the pills.
Reach for it where the strip is a page's own navigation on a phone (the docs
example rail); keep the scroller where the strip sits in a toolbar that must stay
one line tall. `block` never overflows and wins over `wrap`; a `responsive`
vertical rail honors `wrap` once it flattens.

```tsx
<Tabs wrap tabs={["General", "Security", "Notifications", "Billing", "Integrations", "Advanced", "Members", "Audit log"]} />
```

## Do & Don't

### Underline

**Do** — Underline and foreground-color only the active tab; leave the rest muted with no rule.

```tsx
<Tabs tabs={["Overview", "Activity", "Settings"]} defaultActive={0} />
```

**Don't** — Underlining every tab erases the active indicator: there is no way to tell which view is current.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", borderBottomWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, alignSelf: "flex-start" }}>
  <Pressable style={({ pressed }) => [{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingVertical: 10 }, pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null]}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Overview</Text>
    <View style={{ position: "absolute", bottom: 0, left: 0, right: 0, height: 2, borderRadius: 9999, backgroundColor: tokens.primary }} />
  </Pressable>
  <Pressable style={({ pressed }) => [{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingVertical: 10 }, pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null]}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Activity</Text>
    <View style={{ position: "absolute", bottom: 0, left: 0, right: 0, height: 2, borderRadius: 9999, backgroundColor: tokens.primary }} />
  </Pressable>
  <Pressable style={({ pressed }) => [{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", paddingHorizontal: 16, paddingVertical: 10 }, pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null]}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Settings</Text>
    <View style={{ position: "absolute", bottom: 0, left: 0, right: 0, height: 2, borderRadius: 9999, backgroundColor: tokens.primary }} />
  </Pressable>
</View>
```

### Pill

**Do** — Exactly one pill gets the elevated background; the rest sit flat on the muted track.

```tsx
<Tabs tabs={["All", "Active", "Archived"]} defaultActive={0} pills />
```

**Don't** — Giving every pill the raised background makes the group read as three buttons, not one selection.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 4, alignSelf: "flex-start", borderRadius: 8, backgroundColor: tokens.muted, padding: 4 }}>
  <Pressable style={({ pressed }) => [{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: tokens.background, boxShadow: "0px 16px 32px -22px rgba(121, 100, 214, 0.22)", paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 6 }, pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null]}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>All</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Pressable style={({ pressed }) => [{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: tokens.background, boxShadow: "0px 16px 32px -22px rgba(121, 100, 214, 0.22)", paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 6 }, pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null]}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Active</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Pressable style={({ pressed }) => [{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", justifyContent: "center", borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: tokens.background, boxShadow: "0px 16px 32px -22px rgba(121, 100, 214, 0.22)", paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 6 }, pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null]}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Archived</Text>
  </Pressable>
</View>
```

### Vertical

**Do** — Wash the active rail item in the accent so the selected pane is unmistakable.

```tsx
<Tabs tabs={["General", "Security", "Notifications"]} defaultActive={0} vertical />
```

**Don't** — With no filled active item the rail collapses into a plain link list and loses its current selection.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "column", alignItems: "stretch", gap: 4, width: 180 }}>
  <Pressable style={({ pressed }) => [{ width: "100%", flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: "transparent", paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 8 }, pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null]}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>General</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Pressable style={({ pressed }) => [{ width: "100%", flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: "transparent", paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 8 }, pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null]}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Security</Text>
  </Pressable>
  <Pressable style={({ pressed }) => [{ width: "100%", flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: "transparent", paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 8 }, pressed ? { opacity: 0.9 } : null]}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Notifications</Text>
  </Pressable>
</View>
```

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tabs | TabItem[] \| undefined | no |  | Triggers, left to right. Strings, or `{ label, badge }` for a count. |

# TextInput

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/text-input/text-input.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/text-input

## Public imports

```tsx
import { TextInput } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Single-line (or multiline) text entry. Control it with `value` + `onChangeText`, and style the box with the usual View style props. Common props: `placeholder`, `secureTextEntry` (passwords), `keyboardType`, and `multiline`.

## Usage

```tsx
<TextInput accessibilityLabel="Your name" defaultValue="Ada Lovelace" />
```

## Variants

### Placeholder

```tsx
<TextInput placeholder="Search components..." />
```

### Multiline

```tsx
<TextInput accessibilityLabel="Notes" multiline defaultValue={"Multi-line text\nwraps and grows as you type."} />
```

### Disabled

```tsx
<TextInput accessibilityLabel="Plan" defaultValue="Pro" editable={false} aria-disabled />
```

## Do & Don't

### Labelled fields

**Do**: Reach for `Input` for a form field: its `label` stays in view, names the field for assistive tech, and the field box is drawn for each platform.

```tsx
<Input label="Email" placeholder="ada@example.com" />
```

**Don't**: Let a bare TextInput's placeholder stand in for the label; it vanishes as soon as the user types, taking the field's only name with it.

```tsx
<TextInput placeholder="Email" />
```

### Disabled

**Do**: Pair `editable={false}` with `aria-disabled`. The browser then disables the field and takes it out of the tab order, and VoiceOver and TalkBack announce it as dimmed.

```tsx
<TextInput accessibilityLabel="Plan" defaultValue="Pro" editable={false} aria-disabled />
```

**Don't**: Stop at `editable={false}`. On the web that is only read-only: the field stays a Tab stop and is announced as read-only, not unavailable.

```tsx
<TextInput accessibilityLabel="Plan" defaultValue="Pro" editable={false} />
```

### Focus ring

**Do**: Leave the focus ring to the primitive. It takes the theme's `ring` colour 2 px off the field, like every kit control. The browser draws a text field's ring on every focus, a click included, since the field takes typing however it was focused.

```tsx
<TextInput accessibilityLabel="Your name" defaultValue="Ada Lovelace" />
```

**Don't**: Switch the outline off without painting a focus state of your own. A keyboard user then has no way to see which field takes their typing.

```tsx
<TextInput accessibilityLabel="Your name" defaultValue="Ada Lovelace" style={{ outlineWidth: 0, outlineStyle: "solid" }} />
```

| needsOffscreenAlphaCompositing | boolean \| undefined | no |  | Whether this view needs to rendered offscreen and composited with an alpha in order to preserve 100% correct colors and blending behavior. The default (false) falls back to drawing the component and its children with an alpha applied to the paint used to draw each element instead of rendering the full component offscreen and compositing it back with an alpha value. This default may be noticeable and undesired in the case where the View you are setting an opacity on has multiple overlapping elements (e.g. multiple overlapping Views, or text and a background). Rendering offscreen to preserve correct alpha behavior is extremely expensive and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is not turned on by default. If you do need to enable this property for an animation, consider combining it with renderToHardwareTextureAndroid if the view contents are static (i.e. it doesn't need to be redrawn each frame). If that property is enabled, this View will be rendered off-screen once, saved in a hardware texture, and then composited onto the screen with an alpha each frame without having to switch rendering targets on the GPU. |

| onStartShouldSetResponderCapture | ((event: GestureResponderEvent) => boolean) \| undefined | no |  | onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern, where the deepest node is called first. That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers. This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable. However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder. This can be handled by using the capture phase. Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component, it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture. So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start, it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true. |

# Text

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/text/text.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/text

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Text } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Renders text. In React Native every string must live inside a Text element, so you cannot put a bare string in a View. For type scale and tone in app code, reach for `<Typography>` (e.g. `<Typography h3>`, `<Typography body>`, `<Typography tiny muted>`), which owns the kit's roles and colors; use the raw Text primitive for the primitive-level cases it does not cover: `numberOfLines` truncation and nested inline runs.

## Usage

```tsx
<Text style={{ color: tokens.foreground }}>The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.</Text>
```

## Variants

### Truncation

```tsx
<Container xxs>
  <Text numberOfLines={1} style={{ color: tokens.foreground }}>
    This single line is clipped with an ellipsis when it overflows its container.
  </Text>
</Container>
```

### Nested runs

```tsx
<Text style={{ color: tokens.foreground }}>
  A run of text can carry an <Text style={{ fontWeight: "700" }}>inline emphasis</Text> that inherits everything else from its parent Text.
</Text>
```

## Do & Don't

### Styled type

**Do** — Reach for `Typography` for any styled type: it owns the kit's roles, sizes, and tones.

```tsx
<Column tight>
  <Typography h3>Heading</Typography>
  <Typography body>Body text</Typography>
  <Typography tiny muted>Muted caption</Typography>
</Column>
```

**Don't** — Hand-styling the raw Text primitive with literal font sizes and weights reinvents the type scale and drifts from the tokens.

```tsx
<View style={{ gap: 4 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 20, lineHeight: 28, fontWeight: "600", color: tokens.foreground }}>Heading</Text>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens.foreground }}>Body text</Text>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 16, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>Muted caption</Text>
</View>
```

# Textarea

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/textarea/textarea.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/textarea

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Textarea } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Multi-line input, with character count, with toolbar.

Pass `label` (and `required`) to name the field:
iOS and web render the label
above the control, while Android floats the Material 3 in-container label at the
top of the multiline box, making room for itself at the user's text size and
truncating on one line when it is longer than the box while the field's
accessible name stays the whole label.
The required star is decorative: a screen
reader hears the field as required,
from `aria-required` on the web and from its
name ("Bio, required") on iOS and Android.
The box fills the parent it is given; a step of its
own (`xs`, `lg`, …, with `start` to pin it to the leading edge) or a Container
step sets its measure.

The box is the single-line Input's on each platform. On the web it is the sunken
well with a 1 px hairline that steps to the subtle ink on hover, takes the `ring`
edge and a 4 px accent halo on focus and the `destructive` edge on error, with a
400 value on a 1.55 line; the count is an 11 px mono caption ("12 / 280").
iOS keeps
its 8 pt `card` box with the error wash and a tabular count ("12/280").
Android uses
the same opaque muted surface as the other filled fields, and its count sits at the
end of the supporting-text row.
Its label uses `primary-text` when focused and
`destructive-text` on error. The over-limit character count also uses
`destructive-text` on every platform. Without `rows` the field starts four rows tall.

Inside an overlay, Escape follows the overlay's cancellation policy. A supplied
`onKeyPress` runs first and can call `preventDefault()` to handle Escape locally.
Cancelling an IME candidate keeps the overlay open.

`dense` preserves application paragraph fields with 13/19.5 semibold values,
the dense field inset and explicit visible rows. `eyebrow` supplies the matching
web label. `accessibilityLabel` overrides the visible label’s accessible name;
`readOnly` prevents edits without dimming or removing the field from focus.
`systemFocus` keeps the platform system focus outline.

`embedded` renders a bare editor inside a parent-owned field surface and focus frame, as used by Chat. It implies `flush` and removes the independent backing and focus outline; the parent must provide a visible focus treatment.

## Usage

```tsx
<Textarea placeholder="A few words about this project" />
```

## Variants

### With label

```tsx
<Textarea label="Description" placeholder="A few words about this project…" />
```

### Pre-filled

```tsx
<Textarea defaultValue="Renders natively on iOS and Android and on the web." />
```

### Required

```tsx
<Textarea label="Bio" required />
```

### Character counter

```tsx
<Textarea showCount maxLength={280} />
```

### Formatting toolbar

```tsx
<Card flat flush style={{ overflow: "hidden" }}>
  <Row tight padTight>
    <Button ghost small>B</Button>
    <Button ghost small>I</Button>
  </Row>
  <Divider />
  <Textarea flush placeholder="Leave a comment…" />
</Card>
```

### Composer

`composer` sets a chat composer's metrics: 15 / 20 text 6 by 8 points in, one line by default (`rows` raises it), so one line sits
in a 44 point composer box beside 32 point controls. Pair it with `embedded`; Chat's
composer uses it.

```tsx
<Textarea embedded composer placeholder="What would you like to build?" accessibilityLabel="Message" />
```

### Disabled

```tsx
<Textarea disabled placeholder="A few words about this project" />
```

### Measure

```tsx
<Column>
  <Textarea xs start rows={2} placeholder="xs step, pinned to the start (320)" />
  <Textarea lg start rows={2} placeholder="lg step, pinned to the start (512)" />
  <Container lg start><Textarea rows={2} placeholder="Bare, in an lg Container: fills it (512)" /></Container>
</Column>
```

## Do & Don't

### With label

**Do** — Set `rows` for a sensible starting height so users can see their text; the field grows with the content from there.

```tsx
<Textarea label="Description" rows={3} value="This is a longer description that runs past one line and stays readable." />
```

**Don't** — A locked, single-line textarea hides long content with no way to expand.

```tsx
<View style={{ maxWidth: 400, flexDirection: "column", gap: 6 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Description</Text>
  <TextInput numberOfLines={1} value="This is a longer description that runs past one line and gets clipped." style={{ height: 32, width: "100%", borderRadius: 6, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.input, backgroundColor: tokens.background, paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 4, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens.foreground }} />
</View>
```

### Character counter

**Do** — Show the live count against the cap and turn it destructive past the limit so the overage is precise. `showCount` treats `maxLength` as a soft cap and flips the count (and the field) destructive automatically once you run over.

```tsx
<Textarea label="Bio" showCount maxLength={120} rows={3} value="I have been building things on the web for fifteen years and counting, across teams large and small, shipping product end to end." />
```

**Don't** — A vague "over limit" message gives no number, so users cannot tell how much to trim.

```tsx
<View style={{ maxWidth: 400, flexDirection: "column", gap: 6 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Bio</Text>
  <Textarea rows={3} value="I have been building things on the web for fifteen years and counting, across teams large and small, shipping product end to end." />
  <View style={{ marginTop: 4, flexDirection: "row", justifyContent: "flex-end" }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 11, color: tokens["muted-foreground"] }}>over limit</Text>
  </View>
</View>
```

### Formatting toolbar

**Do** — Make each control a real focusable button that toggles an active state when pressed.

```tsx
<Card flat flush style={{ overflow: "hidden" }}>
  <Row alignCenter tight padTight>
    <Button ghost small>B</Button>
    <Button ghost small>I</Button>
    <Button ghost small>{"</>"}</Button>
  </Row>
  <Divider />
  <Textarea rows={4} flush placeholder="Leave a comment" />
</Card>
```

**Don't** — Static, unclickable glyphs look like a toolbar but cannot be pressed or focused.

```tsx
<View style={{ width: 400, maxWidth: "100%", overflow: "hidden", borderRadius: 6, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border }}>
  <View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 4, borderBottomWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.muted, 0.3), paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 8 }}>
    <Text style={{ paddingHorizontal: 8, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "700" }}>B</Text>
    <Text style={{ paddingHorizontal: 8, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontStyle: "italic" }}>I</Text>
    <Text style={{ paddingHorizontal: 8, fontFamily: "monospace", fontSize: 11 }}>{"</>"}</Text>
  </View>
  <Textarea rows={4} placeholder="Leave a comment" style={{ borderRadius: 0, borderWidth: 0, boxShadow: "none" }} />
</View>
```

### Disabled

**Do**: Pass `disabled` so the field blocks editing and focus, matching its dimmed look: the browser takes it out of the tab order, and VoiceOver and TalkBack announce it as dimmed.

```tsx
<Textarea label="Description" rows={3} disabled value="Read-only content the user must not change." />
```

**Don't** — Dimming a textarea while leaving it editable looks disabled but still accepts input.

```tsx
<View style={{ maxWidth: 400, flexDirection: "column", gap: 6 }}>
  <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, fontWeight: "500", color: tokens.foreground }}>Description</Text>
  <TextInput multiline editable textAlignVertical="top" value="Read-only content the user must not change." style={{ minHeight: 80, width: "100%", borderRadius: 6, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.input, backgroundColor: tokens.background, paddingHorizontal: 12, paddingVertical: 8, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 20, color: tokens.foreground, opacity: 0.5 }} />
</View>
```

## Supported props

### TextareaProps

Includes `MeasureProps`; their supported fields are expanded below.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | string \| undefined | no |  | Controlled text value. Omit and use `defaultValue` for uncontrolled use. |
| onChangeText | ((next: string) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired with the next text value on each edit. |
| placeholder | string \| undefined | no |  | Placeholder shown while the field is empty. |
| label | string \| undefined | no |  | The field's persistent label. Its placement is platform-adaptive: iOS and web render it ABOVE the field; Android renders the Material 3 in-container FLOATING label — a MULTILINE float pinned to the first text line at rest, floating to the top once the field is focused or filled. The label names the field for a11y. |
| eyebrow | boolean \| undefined | no | false |  |
| systemFocus | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Preserve the platform system focus outline. |
| dense | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Dense paragraph-entry metrics matching the application field family. |
| terminal | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Bare monospace prompt metrics for a terminal transcript composer. Implies embedded. |
| composer | boolean \| undefined | no | false | A chat composer's entry: 15 / 20 text at 6 by 8 in, so one line sits in a 44 px composer box beside 32 px controls (the Claude desktop composer). Pair with `embedded`. |
| accessibilityLabel | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| readOnly | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Prevent edits while retaining focus and the resting appearance. |
| required | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Marks the field as required: appends a destructive "*" to the label (decorative, never in the accessible name) and announces the field as required, through aria-required on the web and with the word in its name ("Bio, required") on iOS and Android. The star and the spoken word take effect only alongside `label`. |
| rows | number \| undefined | no |  | Visible rows the field sizes to (4 when omitted). Sets the min height (rows times the skin's line plus the field's padding); the field still grows with content past this floor. |
| showCount | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Show a live character-count line inside the field's own anatomy: an end-aligned muted caption under the control reading "N / max" (just "N" when no `maxLength` is set), where N is the current text length. When on, `maxLength` becomes a SOFT cap rather than a hard one: it is NOT forwarded to the native TextInput (a hard cap silently drops the extra keystroke, so the overage could never be seen), the user can type past it, and once N exceeds `maxLength` the count turns destructive AND the field enters its error state automatically (red border/underline). Leave `showCount` off to keep `maxLength` as a hard input cap. |

# Toast

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/toast/toast.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/toast

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Toast, ToastProvider, useToast } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A transient notification card. Render a `<Toast>` directly, or drive them imperatively: mount a `<ToastProvider>` near your app root and call `toast(...)` from the `useToast()` hook to enqueue auto-dismissing toasts that stack over the app.

On the web and iOS the toast is a floating card:
the overlay panel at the card corner, up to 380px wide, with the intent glyph in its status color (the accent's sparkle on a neutral toast), a medium message over a muted description, and the action in the accent. A `brief` toast hugs its one line.
Android keeps the Material 3 snackbar on the inverse fill.

For a single brief notification, use `<ToastProvider single brief safeArea duration={2800}
bottomInset={28} horizontalInset={20}>`. New messages replace the current toast and
restart its lifetime. `safeArea` includes the device safe area. `brief` retains a
single line without the dismiss
control; Android retains its snackbar skin.

Tab reaches a toast's action and its dismiss, and Escape dismisses the toast that holds
focus, then returns focus to where it came from. A toast the user is not in never takes
Escape, so the key still reaches the page or the Dialog under it. A provider toast always
answers it (a `brief` one too), a directly rendered `<Toast>` when it has `onDismiss`.
On
iOS the same dismiss answers the accessibility escape (the VoiceOver two-finger scrub,
and Escape under Full Keyboard Access).
Android delivers no Escape key to a view, and
its back gesture is never taken for a toast.

## Usage

Toast is usually driven imperatively: mount a `<ToastProvider>` near your app root, then call the `toast(...)` handle from `useToast()` to enqueue an auto-dismissing card that floats over the app. Press the button to fire one. (`AppScreen` is just this demo's stand-in for your app root, so the toast has a screen to float over.)

```tsx
<AppScreen>
  <ToastProvider>
    <WithToast hook={useToast}>
      {({ toast }) => <Button onPress={() => toast({ message: "Profile updated" })}>Show toast</Button>}
    </WithToast>
  </ToastProvider>
</AppScreen>
```

## Variants

### Rendered directly

```tsx
<Toast message="Your changes were saved" description="They are live for everyone." />
```

### Success

```tsx
<Toast success message="Profile updated" />
```

### Destructive

```tsx
<Toast destructive message="Upload failed" />
```

### Warning

```tsx
<Toast warning message="Storage almost full" />
```

### With an action

```tsx
<Toast message="Message archived" action={{ label: "Undo", onPress: () => {} }} />
```

### Dismissible, informational

```tsx
<Toast info message="A new version is available" onDismiss={() => {}} />
```

## Do & Don't

### One short message

**Do** — Keep a toast to one short, plain message (with an optional one-line description), and pair a destructive or success intent with the matching message.

```tsx
<Toast success message="Copied to clipboard" />
```

**Don't** — Don't crowd a toast with long paragraphs or more than one action; a toast is a glance, not a dialog.

```tsx
<Toast
  message="We were unable to complete your request because the server returned an unexpected error and the operation was rolled back"
/>
```
