### ToastProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| brief | boolean \| undefined | no | false | A single-line notification pill without extra chrome. |
| message | string | yes |  | The headline line (required). |
| description | string \| undefined | no |  | A secondary line under the message. |
| action | ToastAction \| undefined | no |  | A trailing action button (e.g. Undo). |
| success | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Green success intent (icon + tint). |
| destructive | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Red danger intent (icon + tint). This is the name the intent axis uses across the kit (Button, AlertDialog, and every chart) and the one the design hand-off uses. |
| warning | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Amber warning intent (icon + tint). |
| info | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Brand-tinted informational intent (icon + tint). |
| icon | ReactNode | no |  | Override the auto intent icon; pass any node, or omit to use the intent glyph. |
| onDismiss | (() => void) \| undefined | no |  | When provided, render a trailing dismiss (x) that calls this. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | StyleProp<ViewStyle> | no |  | Outer layout composition only (width/flex within a parent), never a restyle hook. |

# Tooltip

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/tooltip/tooltip.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/tooltip

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Tooltip } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Small floating helper text on hover or focus.

The bubble floats over the page: it is drawn in the overlay layer of the nearest
`OverlayProvider`, placed against its trigger, and changes no layout, so a tip on a
table row's action never grows the cell. It centers on the trigger at the side you
pick, flips to the opposite side when the visible area has no room there, and slides
to stay inside it. Moving the pointer from the trigger onto the bubble keeps it up.
With no `OverlayProvider` mounted it still floats, on an absolute anchor beside the
trigger, but an ancestor that clips its content can then cut it off.

The bubble inverts against the page (dark in the light scheme, light in the dark one)
and sets its text in Dark Factory's label type;
iOS, which has no tooltip, shows the
same bubble, and Android keeps the Material 3 plain tooltip.

The trigger is a boolean axis of its own, resolved first match wins:

- `children`, an element you already have (an icon `Button`, a `Chip`, any
  control that owns its own press and accessible name). The child renders as-is
  and the tip hangs off it through a wrapper that only LISTENS: no accessibility
  role, no tab stop, and no press of its own, so the child stays the single
  interactive, labelled element, keeps its `onPress`, and the tip never toggles
  on tap. Hover and focus on the child both raise it.
- `iconTrigger`, a ghost icon button carrying a settings glyph.
- `textTrigger`, the `trigger` string as a pressable inline word.
- Otherwise the default: the `trigger` string as an outline Button.

Hover and focus are pointer-and-keyboard affordances. Touch pointers are
skipped,
and iOS and Android never fire hover at all.
On touch the built-in
triggers toggle the tip on tap (tap again to close it; a tip is never modal, so a
tap elsewhere goes to the page). A long press is not taken: it belongs to the
platform and to the control. An element trigger has no tap toggle either, because
that press belongs to the child, so on native and on touch the controlled `open`
prop is the way to show its tip: drive it from whatever the platform does offer (a
long press the child handles, a selected row, an inline help toggle). Keyboard
focus, including a hardware keyboard on a tablet, raises the tip on every platform.

Escape hides an open tip and leaves focus where it is (WCAG 1.4.13: hover and focus
content is dismissable without moving the pointer or focus). It goes through the kit's
one Escape owner, so a tip inside a Dialog or Popover closes first and the next Escape
reaches its host; a closed tip takes no Escape at all. A controlled tip reports the
close through `onOpenChange(false)`.
On iOS the same close answers the accessibility
escape (the VoiceOver two-finger scrub, and Escape on a hardware keyboard under Full
Keyboard Access).
Android delivers no Escape key to a view, and its back gesture is
never taken for a tip, so there the tip closes with focus or the controlled `open`.

## Usage

The examples pinned open leave room on the bubble's side, as a page would: the
bubble floats and takes no room of its own.

```tsx
<Column padLoose alignCenter>
  <Tooltip label="Open settings" trigger="Settings" open />
</Column>
```

## Variants

### Right

```tsx
<Tooltip label="Open settings" trigger="Settings" open right />
```

### Bottom

```tsx
<Column padLoose alignCenter>
  <Tooltip label="Open settings" trigger="Settings" open bottom />
</Column>
```

### Left

```tsx
<Tooltip label="Open settings" trigger="Settings" open left />
```

### Icon

```tsx
<Column padLoose alignCenter>
  <Tooltip label="Open settings" iconTrigger open />
</Column>
```

### Text

```tsx
<Column padLoose alignCenter>
  <Tooltip textTrigger label="Open settings" trigger="hover this text" open />
</Column>
```

### Element trigger

```tsx
<Column padLoose alignCenter>
  <Tooltip label="Open settings" open>
    <Button ghost icon accessibilityLabel="Open settings" iconLeft={<Icon settings size={16} />} />
  </Tooltip>
</Column>
```

### On hover

```tsx
<Tooltip label="Open settings" trigger="Hover me" />
```

## Do & Don't

### Short labels

**Do** — Keep tooltips short and supplementary; put essential steps in visible copy.

```tsx
<Column padLoose alignCenter>
  <Tooltip iconTrigger bottom open label="Rotate key" />
</Column>
```

**Don't** — Long, essential instructions hidden in a tooltip are missed on touch and by screen readers.

```tsx
<Column padLoose alignCenter>
  <Tooltip iconTrigger bottom open label="To rotate this key you must first revoke the old one in Settings, then confirm via email within 24 hours." />
</Column>
```

### Placement

**Do** — Pick the side with the most room; the tip flips and slides to stay on screen when it has none.

```tsx
<Column padLoose alignCenter>
  <Tooltip trigger="Save" top open label="Saves your changes" />
</Column>
```

**Don't** — Don't place a tip where it covers the control a user needs next; it floats over the page, so it masks whatever sits on that side.

```tsx
<View style={{ alignItems: "flex-start", gap: 4 }}>
  <Tooltip trigger="Filters" bottom open label="Refine results" />
  <Button outline small>Clear all</Button>
</View>
```

## Supported props

### TooltipProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | An arbitrary element for the tip to hang off: an existing Button, Chip, or any other control that already owns its own press and accessible name. The highest-precedence trigger: children win over `iconTrigger`, `textTrigger`, and the default Button. The child renders as-is and stays the single interactive, labelled element; the root view Tooltip wraps it in takes no accessibility role and no tab stop, listens only for hover and focus, and never claims the press, so a Button child keeps its `onPress` and the tip does not toggle on tap. |
| label | string \| undefined | no |  | The tip text shown in the bubble. |
| trigger | string \| undefined | no |  | The element the tip describes. By default rendered as a text `<Button outline small>`; set `iconTrigger` for a ghost icon button, `textTrigger` to hang the tip off an inline pressable word, or pass `children` to wrap an element you already have. Ignored when `children` is passed. |
| iconTrigger | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Render the trigger as a ghost icon button (a settings glyph) instead of the text Button. When set, `trigger` (the label string) is ignored. Ignored when `children` is passed, which takes precedence. |
| textTrigger | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Render the `trigger` string as a pressable inline word (an underlined hover-text affordance) rather than the default text Button, so the tip can hang off a run of body copy. | top | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Placement (pick one; default is top). |
| bottom | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Placement (pick one; default is top). |
| left | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Placement (pick one; default is top). |
| right | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Placement (pick one; default is top). |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

# Treemap

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/charts/treemap/treemap.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/treemap

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Treemap } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Squarified value tiles: each datum becomes a ramp-colored rectangle whose area is proportional to its value, packed largest-first with near-square aspect ratios, with the label and formatted value rendered inside only when the tile fits them.

Flat one-level data; nesting and drill-down are deferred scope. Press a tile to flag its value and share (the others dim); the accessible name carries every tile with its share regardless of which labels fit.

## Usage

```tsx
<Treemap
  title="Storage by service"
  data={[
    { label: "Media", value: 620 },
    { label: "Backups", value: 340 },
    { label: "Logs", value: 180 },
    { label: "Search index", value: 120 },
    { label: "Thumbnails", value: 90 },
    { label: "Exports", value: 45 },
    { label: "Other", value: 25 }
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Compact

```tsx
<Treemap
  compact
  data={[
    { label: "Chrome", value: 61 },
    { label: "Safari", value: 24 },
    { label: "Edge", value: 8 },
    { label: "Firefox", value: 5 },
    { label: "Other", value: 2 }
  ]}
/>
```

### Inspected

```tsx
<Treemap
  defaultSelected={0}
  data={[
    { label: "Platform", value: 4200 },
    { label: "Add-ons", value: 1400 },
    { label: "Services", value: 900 },
    { label: "Training", value: 300 }
  ]}
/>
```

### Outlined partitions

```tsx
<Treemap partitioned outlined formatValue={(v) => `${v}%`} data={[{label: "Web", value: 42}, {label: "Phone", value: 28}, {label: "Tablet", value: 18}, {label: "Desktop", value: 7}, {label: "CLI", value: 3}, {label: "Other", value: 2}]} />
```

## Do & Don't

### Treemap

**Do** - Reserve the treemap for part-of-whole data with real size contrast, where area comparison earns the space.

```tsx
<Treemap
title="Storage by service"
data={[
  { label: "Media", value: 620 },
  { label: "Backups", value: 340 },
  { label: "Logs", value: 180 },
]}
/>
```

**Don't** - A handful of near-equal shares reads better as a PieChart or a BarList; near-equal tiles defeat the area encoding.

```tsx
<Treemap
data={[
  { label: "A", value: 26 },
  { label: "B", value: 25 },
  { label: "C", value: 25 },
  { label: "D", value: 24 },
]}
/>
```

## Supported props

### TreemapProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data | TreemapDatum[] | yes |  | The tiles, laid out largest first by the squarified algorithm. |
| title | string \| undefined | no |  | Optional heading shown above the tiles. |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Density (omit for the default 240 plot height; compact is 160). |
| partitioned | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Slice successive values along alternating axes, keeping the data order. |
| outlined | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Show pale series washes with colored outlines and large readable values. |
| plain | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Strip the card surface for nesting inside an existing card (mirrors Stats). |
| formatValue | ((v: number) => string) \| undefined | no |  | Formats tile values and the flag (data formatting, not styling). |
| selected | number \| null \| undefined | no |  | Press-to-inspect: the selected tile index (controlled). Pass null for none. |
| defaultSelected | number \| undefined | no |  | Press-to-inspect: the initially selected tile (uncontrolled). |
| onSelect | ((index: number \| null) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired when a press selects a tile (or clears it with null). |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# Typography

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/typography/typography.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/typography

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Typography } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Type scale classes for headings, body text, and helper styles.

`terminal` selects the system terminal face while retaining the reading role, size, weight, and ink: pair it with `tiny`, `caption`, `small`, or a heading. The web uses the system monospace stack beginning with `ui-monospace`, SFMono-Regular, and Menlo; native platforms use Menlo or their monospace alias. Existing `mono` and code typography keep their current behavior.

Argus reading roles include `subheading`, `label`, `micro`, `tag`, `eyebrow`,
`eyebrowLg`, `stageLabel`, `statValue`, `metricValue`, and `formValue`. These extend
Typography itself. Semantic leading and tracking props preserve the reference's
fractional web metrics; for example `labelLeading` is the compact label line box
and `wideTracking` its uppercase eyebrow tracking. `extraBold` selects the 800 face.
The owner's exact-reference directive preserves the existing 9.5px eyebrows.

`foreground`, `inverse`, `action`, `actionForeground`, and `info` name the ink;
`hue` gives a stage its theme-aware identity text. `inverseHint`, `inverseSubtle`,
`inverseMuted`, `inverseSoft`, and `inverseFaint` express the reference's hierarchy
on branded surfaces. `numberOfLines` truncates a reading block, and accessible
labels and roles stay with the text. Existing roles and defaults keep working.

`section` lets a heading own its `count`, muted `description` and trailing `actions`.
They wrap along a shared baseline, preserving dense section anatomy. Pair it with
`h5 bold labelLeading` or `subheading bold labelLeading`; the latter uses the compact
metadata metrics. Actions move to the far edge and wrap below on narrow surfaces.

`level={1..6}` sets the heading level assistive tech hears without changing the
look. A heading role exposes its own level (`hero`, `pageTitle`, `display` and `h1` at 1, `sectionTitle` at 2, `cardTitle` at 3, `h2` to `h5` at
2 to 5, a `section` heading 6), so `<Typography h3 level={2}>` draws the h3 size
and is announced as a level-2 heading: a real `<h2>` on the web, the header trait
natively. On a non-heading role `level` makes the text a heading at that level.
`href` still wins: a link is never a heading. The level is a number because it is
the document outline, not a style (the same reason Row's `span` is one); the look
stays on the boolean role axis.

`hero` and `pageTitle` are the two fluid headlines, sized by the window rather than a
fixed step: `hero` is the landing headline (56 to 112 px at 7.2 percent of the window,
a .94 line, tracked -.045em) and `pageTitle` a page's own title (40 to 64 px at 5
percent, a 1.0 line, tracked -.04em). Both are medium-weight display face.

The page roles are the hand-off pages' own titles and leads, outside its type table:
`sectionTitle` (a page section's heading, display 500 28/1.1), `cardTitle` (a feature
card's title, display 500 22/1.15), `panelTitle` (a panel's title, display 500 20/1.2),
`tagline` (the line under a section's title, display 400 22/1.3), `pageLead` (a page's
summary, 18/1.55, held to the hand-off's 72ch measure), `sectionLead` (a section's introduction, 17/1.55), `cardBody` (a feature
card's description, 14/1.55), `sectionNote` (the note under a section's heading,
14/1.5), `pageBody` (a page's body paragraph, 15/1.6) and `pageNote` (a page's note paragraph,
14/1.6), the last six in the secondary ink and the last two held to an 80ch measure.
Four more are the component page's own: `pageLabel` (a panel's "Props", a rail's group
header, a table's header cell, a previous/next eyebrow: 500 11/1 tracked .08em in caps, in
the subtle ink; pass `mono` for the mono face, as the hand-off's page does), `knobLabel` (a
knob panel's label row, a knob's name and its type hint: 500 12/1 in the secondary ink, the
hint beside it in the `muted` tone, the third ink; pass `mono` for the mono face), `guideTitle` (a
guidance card's title, 600 16/1.3 in the interface face, a level-3 heading) and `guideBody`
(a guidance card's paragraph, 400 13.5/1.6 in the secondary ink). `pageLabel` is not the
`eyebrow`: that is the type table's accent-ink label tracked .1em. `pagerName` is the
previous or next card's name under its label: the display face, 500 18 on the face's own 22
line (the hand-off sets no ratio), in the foreground ink. Two are the reference sheet's cells
(the component page's props table): `specMeta` (a type or default cell, 400 12/1.55; pass
`mono` for the mono face and `subtle` or `muted` for the ink, as the sheet's cells take
them) and `specText` (a description cell or an inherited-props note, 400 13/1.55 in the
secondary ink).
line the same way: `pagerLabel` (the previous or next card's label over its name, the page
label's 500 11 tracked .08em in caps and subtle ink on a 14 line; pass `mono`), `legendLabel`
(a legend row's label beside its numbered disc, 500 14 on an 18 line in the foreground ink)
and `tileCaption` (a specimen tile's caption strip, 500 12 on a 16 line in the secondary ink;
pass `mono`). Three more are the component page's Variants and Tokens sections: `variantTitle`
(a variant card's title over its note and snippet, 500 14/1.3 in the foreground ink),
`linkName` (a link tile's name beside its arrow, 600 14 on the face's own 18 line in the
foreground ink) and `subsectionTitle` (a section's own sub-heading over a grid of tiles,
600 16 on the face's own 20 line in the interface face, a level-3 heading).

The section pages' card roles are the hand-off's section cards' own text, one role per
value set however many pages set it: `cardNote` (a card's foot caption or an in-card note,
400 12/1.6 in the subtle ink; pass `mono`), `codeLabel` (a code name on its own line, a
variant row's label or a token's name, 400 12 on a 16 line in the secondary ink; pass
`mono`), `inlineNote` (a note beside a specimen, 400 12 on a 15 line in the subtle ink),
`tileTitle` (a tile's title, display 500 15/1.3), `paneTitle` (a pane's title, display 500
16/1.2 tracked -.01em; pass `level` to announce it), `gridLabel` (a grid widget's label, 500
10 mono tracked .08em in caps on a 13 line, subtle ink), `tick` (a scale's tick label, 500 10
mono on a 13 line, secondary ink), `rowLabel` (a stat row's label, 500 11/1 mono tracked
.06em in caps, subtle ink), `rowValue` (the value beside it, display 500 22/1 tracked
-.02em), `headlineValue` (a card's headline figure, display 500 26/1 tracked -.02em),
`bigNumber` (a card's big number, display 500 40/1 tracked -.03em), `unit` (the unit after a
figure, 400 16 on a 20 line in the subtle ink, nested in the figure's Typography so it shares
its baseline), `sampleLabel` and `sampleMeta` (a sample's caption and meta line, 400 11 on 14
and 400 10 on 13 in the subtle ink; pass `mono`) and `base` (the 14 px body in the
foreground ink, 400 14 on an 18 line). The figures and titles rank with the titles, the
labels with the page label, and the notes, samples, unit and base with the reading roles.

`natural` sets the text on its face's own normal line at the role's size, the line the
hand-off's text takes where it sets a size with no ratio: JetBrains Mono 10, 11 and 12 px on
13, 14 and 16, Instrument Sans 12, 13 and 14 on 15, 16 and 18, Bricolage Grotesque 14 and
15 on 17 and 18 (measured in Chromium on the faces, 10 to 28 px). The face is the one the
text is set in: `mono`, a display role, or the interface face. It sits on the leading axis
after the fixed ratios and before `tightLeading`.

`cyan` and `mint` are two inks on the tone axis that name a fixed series hue whatever the
palette (the hand-off's `--cyan` and `--mint`, the `chart-2` and `chart-3` tokens), each
solved to 4.5:1 on the scheme's surfaces. Tone precedence: `destructive`, `warning`,
`success`, `cyan`, `mint`, `primary`, `subtle`, `muted`.

`code` is the standalone code pill (regular 13px mono on the muted fill, a 6 radius and 2
by 6 padding). `code inline` is the prose code chip, a word of code inside a sentence: the
hand-off's inline `<code>`, regular weight at .88 of the surrounding reading role's size
(pass that role beside it, `lead`, `small`, `pageBody`, `pageNote`, `pageLead` or
`sectionLead`; body when none), a 5 radius, 1 by 5 padding, the surface fill and a 1px
hairline rim. The chip keeps its regular weight inside a strong run, as the hand-off
applies bold and code independently. Under glass the fill is the same ink tint the pill
takes. Natively a Text nested in a Text has no border and no vertical box, so there the
chip draws its fill and horizontal padding only; `inline` without `code` does nothing.

## Do & Don't

### display

**Do** — Use display once per hero, then drop to a muted line for the supporting copy.

```tsx
<Column snug>
  <Typography display>Welcome</Typography>
  <Typography muted>Sign in to pick up where you left off.</Typography>
</Column>
```

**Don't** — Two display-size lines in one view fight for attention and leave no clear focal point.

```tsx
<View style={{ gap: 8 }}>
  <Typography display>Welcome</Typography>
  <Typography display>Get started</Typography>
</View>
```

### h1

**Do** — Give each page a single h1, then step down to h2 for the sections beneath it.

```tsx
<Column relaxed>
  <Typography h1>Billing</Typography>
  <Typography h2>Invoices</Typography>
</Column>
```

**Don't** — Two h1 titles on a page break the document outline and confuse assistive tech.

```tsx
<View style={{ gap: 4 }}>
  <Typography h1>Billing</Typography>
  <Typography h1>Invoices</Typography>
</View>
```

### h2

**Do** — Follow an h1 with h2 for its top-level sections; don't skip the scale.

```tsx
<Column relaxed>
  <Typography h1>Settings</Typography>
  <Typography h2>Profile</Typography>
</Column>
```

**Don't** — Jumping from h1 straight to h4 skips a level and flattens the visible hierarchy.

```tsx
<View>
  <Typography h1>Settings</Typography>
  <Typography h4 style={{ marginTop: 16 }}>Profile</Typography>
</View>
```

### h3

**Do** — Reserve heading styles for titles; set running text in a small body utility.

```tsx
<Column tight>
  <Typography h3>About Canvas</Typography>
  <Typography body>Canvas is a universal React Native UI kit for building consistent product interfaces.</Typography>
</Column>
```

**Don't** — Body copy set in a heading style is hard to read in bulk and flattens the hierarchy.

```tsx
<Typography h3>Canvas is a universal React Native UI kit for building consistent product interfaces.</Typography>
```

### h4

**Do** — Keep h4 to a short label and carry the explanation in a small supporting line.

```tsx
<Column tight>
  <Typography h4>Notifications</Typography>
  <Typography small>Choose how and when we reach you.</Typography>
</Column>
```

**Don't** — h4 is a minor heading, not a place for full sentences; long text at this weight reads as a wall.

```tsx
<View style={{ gap: 4, flexShrink: 1 }}>
  <Typography h4>Notifications</Typography>
  <Typography h4>A long descriptive sentence that explains everything in detail.</Typography>
</View>
```

### h5

**Do** — Use h5 only for the label; render the value in body so the pair stays scannable.

```tsx
<Column tight>
  <Typography h5>Members</Typography>
  <Typography body>Aisha, Bao, Cleo, and 9 others have access.</Typography>
</Column>
```

**Don't** — Setting the value in h5 too makes the label and its data indistinguishable.

```tsx
<View style={{ gap: 4 }}>
  <Typography h5>Members</Typography>
  <Typography h5>Aisha, Bao, Cleo, and 9 others have access.</Typography>
</View>
```

### body

**Do** — Keep body copy in sentence case and let inline code carry the technical emphasis.

```tsx
<Typography body>
  Run 
  <Typography code>npm install</Typography>
  , then restart the dev server before you continue.
</Typography>
```

**Don't** — All-caps emphasis inside body copy shouts and undercuts the relaxed reading rhythm.

```tsx
<Typography body>
  <Typography code>npm install</Typography>
   THEN restart the dev server BEFORE you continue.
</Typography>
```

### small

**Do** — Use small for secondary captions on a plain surface, not for the primary label.

```tsx
<Column tight>
  <Typography body>Save changes</Typography>
  <Typography small>Last saved 2 minutes ago.</Typography>
</Column>
```

**Don't** — small is muted-foreground; on a colored button it loses contrast and looks disabled.

```tsx
<Button secondary>
  <Typography small>Save changes</Typography>
</Button>
```

### tiny

**Do** — Reserve tiny for short metadata like timestamps and counts beside the main text.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter snug>
  <Typography body>Deploy succeeded</Typography>
  <Typography tiny>3m ago</Typography>
</Row>
```

**Don't** — tiny is for metadata, not legal prose; long copy at 11px strains the eye.

```tsx
<Typography tiny>These terms govern your use of the service and your data; please read them carefully before you continue past this screen.</Typography>
```

### muted

**Do** — Keep muted for de-emphasized context; give the actual action full foreground or primary color.

```tsx
<Typography body>
  Payment due May 31. 
  <Typography body primary underline>View invoices</Typography>
</Typography>
```

**Don't** — A primary, clickable action in muted-foreground reads as disabled and is easy to miss.

```tsx
<Typography muted style={{ alignSelf: "flex-start", textDecorationLine: "underline" }}>View your invoices</Typography>
```

### caption

**Do** — Use caption as a short eyebrow label above a section, then explain in body.

```tsx
<Column tight>
  <Typography caption>Billing</Typography>
  <Typography body>Your subscription renews automatically each month.</Typography>
</Column>
```

**Don't** — Uppercase, letter-spaced caption text is illegible for anything longer than a label.

```tsx
<Typography caption>Your subscription renews automatically each month unless you cancel from the billing page.</Typography>
```

### code

**Do** — Use code for inline tokens inside a sentence; reach for the code block component for multi-line snippets.

```tsx
<Typography body>
  Create a branch with 
  <Typography code>git checkout -b feature</Typography>
   before committing.
</Typography>
```

**Don't** — The inline code utility has tight padding and no scroll; multi-line blocks overflow and clip.

```tsx
<Typography code>git checkout -b feature
git add .
git commit -m "wip"</Typography>
```

### mono

**Do**: Use mono for identifiers and hashes, where every character must line up; set figures in a column or a changing value in `tabular` instead.

```tsx
<Row alignCenter between relaxed>
  <Typography small>Request ID</Typography>
  <Typography mono>req_8f2c10ab</Typography>
</Row>
```

**Don't** — Mono spacing makes prose sentences sparse and slow to read; it is meant for fixed-width data.

```tsx
<Typography mono>We could not process your request because the upstream service returned an unexpected response.</Typography>
```

### tabular

**Do**: Set figures read down a column or updated in place in `tabular`, so every digit takes the same width and the column lines up.

```tsx
<Column tight>
  <Row alignCenter between relaxed>
    <Typography small>Uptime</Typography>
    <Typography tabular>99.982%</Typography>
  </Row>
  <Row alignCenter between relaxed>
    <Typography small>Latency</Typography>
    <Typography tabular>118 ms</Typography>
  </Row>
</Column>
```

**Don't**: Tabular figures in running prose space the digits out of the sentence's rhythm; prose keeps the face's own figures.

```tsx
<Typography tabular>Your 14 invoices from 2024 total $1,180.</Typography>
```

## Inline links (href)

Inline text that NAVIGATES should be a real link, not pressable text that sets `location`: pass `href` and the web render becomes a genuine browser link (middle-click, new tab, crawlers, and assistive tech all treat it as one). Native platforms ignore `href`, so pair it with an `onPress` that runs the same navigation through your router; `underline` supplies the conventional link look, and `hrefAttrs` forwards `target` / `rel` / `download` on the web.

```tsx
<Typography small>
  Read the <Typography small underline href="https://canvas.nannier.com">Canvas docs</Typography> for the full component list.
</Typography>
```

# UptimeBar

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/charts/uptime-bar/uptime-bar.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/uptime-bar

## Public imports

```tsx
import { UptimeBar } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

The statuspage strip: per-period status pills (operational, degraded, down, unknown) with a summary caption and edge labels.

The pills run in a single row, oldest on the left, colored operational green, degraded amber, down red, or unknown muted (precedence down > degraded > unknown; an unmarked period is operational). An optional `caption` summarizes the strip above it, and `startLabel`/`endLabel` caption the physical edges below. The strip is a time axis, so it keeps left-to-right ordering in every locale, and its accessible name tallies every status.

`detailed` uses a display header, taller history marks and neutral unknown periods. Hovering a period expands it with an overshooting transition; Reduced Motion keeps it still.

## Usage

```tsx
<UptimeBar
  label="API uptime"
  caption="99.98% uptime"
  startLabel="90 days ago"
  endLabel="Today"
  periods={Array.from({ length: 90 }, (_, i) => (i === 61 ? { down: true } : i === 78 ? { degraded: true } : {}))}
/>
```

## Variants

### Compact

```tsx
<UptimeBar
label="CDN uptime"
compact
periods={Array.from({ length: 60 }, (_, i) => (i === 40 ? { degraded: true } : {}))}
/>
```

### With unknown periods

```tsx
<UptimeBar
  label="Worker uptime"
  periods={Array.from({ length: 30 }, (_, i) => (i < 6 ? { unknown: true } : {}))}
/>
```

### Middle caption

`midLabel` captions the middle of the strip, centred between the edge captions.

```tsx
<UptimeBar
  label="API uptime"
  startLabel="90 days ago"
  midLabel="45 days"
  endLabel="Today"
  periods={Array.from({ length: 90 }, (_, i) => (i === 61 ? { down: true } : {}))}
/>
```

### Detailed

A display header and taller marks for a status overview. A resting pointer expands its period; Reduced Motion keeps the marks still.

```tsx
<UptimeBar
  detailed
  label="API uptime"
  caption="99.94% uptime"
  startLabel="60 days ago"
  endLabel="Today"
  periods={Array.from({ length: 60 }, (_, i) => ({
    label: `Day ${i + 1}`,
    degraded: i === 17 || i === 41,
    down: i === 52,
    unknown: i === 3
  }))}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### UptimeBar

**Do** - Let the strip carry the whole anatomy: pills, summary caption, and edge labels, with the status tally in its accessible name.

```tsx
<UptimeBar
label="API uptime"
caption="99.98% uptime"
startLabel="90 days ago"
endLabel="Today"
periods={Array.from({ length: 90 }, (_, i) => (i === 61 ? { down: true } : {}))}
/>
```

**Don't** - A hand-rolled row of colored Views has no accessible tally and no edge-caption anatomy.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", gap: 2, maxWidth: 480 }}>
  {Array.from({ length: 90 }, (_, i) => (
    <View key={i} style={{ flex: 1, height: 24, borderRadius: 2, backgroundColor: i === 61 ? "red" : "green" }} />
  ))}
</View>
```

## Supported props

### UptimeBarProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| periods | UptimePeriod[] | yes |  | The periods to render, oldest first; each becomes one pill. |
| label | string \| undefined | no |  | What the strip measures (e.g. "API"); shown in the header and leading the accessible name. |
| caption | string \| undefined | no |  | A summary at the header's right (e.g. "99.98% uptime"). |
| startLabel | string \| undefined | no |  | Caption under the strip's left (oldest) edge (e.g. "90 days ago"). |
| endLabel | string \| undefined | no |  | Caption under the strip's right (latest) edge (e.g. "Today"). |
| midLabel | string \| undefined | no |  | Caption centred under the strip, between the edge captions (e.g. "1 incident · 2 degraded days"). |
| compact | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Density (omit for the default pill height). |
| detailed | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Display header and taller history marks for a status overview. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the root element. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.

# Video

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/video/video.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/video

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Video } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

Plays a clip with an optional poster: tap to play inline, or full transport controls
(the platform's own on iOS and Android, the kit's bar on the web),
with boolean fit, `autoplay`, `loop` and `muted` props.

Give it a `source` (a `{ uri }`, or a bundled asset from `require`), an optional `poster` shown until the clip's first frame is on screen, and the clip's `aspectRatio` (width over height, 16 / 9 by default): the frame fills its parent's width at that ratio and letterboxes the picture on black, inside the v4 hand-off's frame: a 14 px corner on a hairline (`radius` picks a step of the kit's scale instead). Without `controls` it is an inline player: the whole picture is one play and pause control, a play emblem sits over the paused picture, and a spinner shows while the clip loads. With `controls` each platform shows transport its own way:
iOS and Android hand the frame to their own player controls, and the web draws
the kit's control bar under the picture, with play and pause, the elapsed time, a seek slider, the length, mute, and full screen.

`autoplay` starts a clip once it is ready unless the system asks to reduce motion; browsers autoplay only `muted` clips, and this site's own policy blocks autoplay, so the examples here play on tap. Name every clip with `accessibilityLabel`: its controls are announced as "Play", "Pause", "Seek" and "Mute" followed by that name. Playback runs through the optional `expo-video` peer; without it the frame keeps its size and poster in a labeled frame.

## Usage

```tsx
<Video source={{ uri: "/video-sample.mp4" }} poster={{ uri: "/video-sample.jpg" }} accessibilityLabel="Sample clip" />
```

## Variants

### Controls

```tsx
<Video source={{ uri: "/video-sample.mp4" }} poster={{ uri: "/video-sample.jpg" }} controls accessibilityLabel="Sample clip with controls" />
```

### Cover

```tsx
<Video source={{ uri: "/video-sample.mp4" }} poster={{ uri: "/video-sample.jpg" }} cover aspectRatio={1} accessibilityLabel="Square crop of the sample clip" />
```

### Loop and muted

```tsx
<Video source={{ uri: "/video-sample.mp4" }} poster={{ uri: "/video-sample.jpg" }} loop muted accessibilityLabel="Looping muted sample clip" />
```

## Do & Don't

### Clips with sound

**Do**: Give a clip people watch with sound `controls`: they can seek, see how long it runs, and mute it.

```tsx
<Video source={{ uri: "/video-sample.mp4" }} poster={{ uri: "/video-sample.jpg" }} controls accessibilityLabel="Product walkthrough" />
```

**Don't**: Leave a clip with sound as an inline player; a tap can only play or pause it, so there is no way to seek, see its length, or mute it.

```tsx
<Video source={{ uri: "/video-sample.mp4" }} poster={{ uri: "/video-sample.jpg" }} accessibilityLabel="Product walkthrough" />
```

## Supported props

### VideoProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| source | VideoSource | yes |  | The clip: a remote `{ uri }`, or a bundled asset from `require(...)`. |
| poster | ImageSourcePropType \| undefined | no |  | A still shown until the clip's first frame is on screen: a remote `{ uri }` or a bundled asset. |
| contain | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Fit: show the whole picture, letterboxed on black. The default (pick one). |
| cover | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Fit: fill the frame, cropping the overflow (pick one). |
| stretch | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Fit: fill the frame by distorting the aspect ratio (pick one). |
| autoplay | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Start playing as soon as the clip is ready, unless the system asks to reduce motion. Browsers autoplay only muted clips, so pair it with `muted` on the web. |
| loop | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Play again from the start at the end. |
| muted | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Play without sound. |
| controls | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Transport controls: the platform's own player controls on iOS and Android, the kit's control bar on the web. |
| aspectRatio | number \| undefined | no |  | Width over height of the clip; the frame fills its parent's width at this ratio (default 16 / 9). |
| radius | ImageRadius \| undefined | no |  | Corner radius from the kit's radius scale (pick one): none, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl, 3xl, full. |
| accessibilityLabel | string \| undefined | no |  | The clip's accessible name, used in the names of its controls (default "video"). |
| onPlayingChange | ((playing: boolean) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Called when playback starts or stops. |
| onEnd | (() => void) \| undefined | no |  | Called when the clip plays to its end (each time round, when looping). |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | E2E hook forwarded to the frame. |
| style | LayoutStyle | no |  | Composition within a parent only, never a restyle hook and never a width: the parent layout container provides the bounds. |

# View

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/atoms/view/view.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/view

## Public imports

```tsx
import { View } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

The layout primitive: a flex container that
runs identically on iOS, Android, and the web.
A View is a column by default.

Reach for it directly only when no semantic primitive covers what you need: arrangement (direction, gap, alignment, padding) belongs to `Row` and `Column`, which are Views with that axis exposed as boolean props, and a bordered filled surface belongs to `Card`. Numbers are density-independent pixels.

## Usage

```tsx
<View style={{ width: 40, height: 40, borderRadius: 8, backgroundColor: tokens.primary }} />
```

## Variants

### Column

```tsx
<Container xs>
  <Column snug>
    <View style={{ height: 28, borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.15) }} />
    <View style={{ height: 28, borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.15) }} />
    <View style={{ height: 28, borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.15) }} />
  </Column>
</Container>
```

### Flex sizing

```tsx
<Container xs>
  <Row snug>
    <View style={{ flex: 1, height: 32, borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.15) }} />
    <View style={{ flex: 2, height: 32, borderRadius: 6, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.3) }} />
  </Row>
</Container>
```

### Padding

```tsx
<View style={{ padding: 16, borderRadius: 10, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.15) }}>
  <Typography>A padded View</Typography>
</View>
```

## Do & Don't

### Arrangement

**Do** — Row and Column carry direction, gap, alignment and padding as boolean props, so the arrangement reads as language and lands on the kit's spacing scale.

```tsx
<Row cozy alignCenter>
  <Emblem primary><Icon shield /></Emblem>
  <Typography semibold>Semantic arrangement</Typography>
</Row>
```

**Don't** — A hand-written flex style object restates what the primitives already name, drifts off the spacing scale, and has to be re-read to know what it does.

```tsx
<View style={{ flexDirection: "row", alignItems: "center", gap: 12 }}>
  <View style={{ width: 32, height: 32, borderRadius: 8, backgroundColor: alpha(tokens.primary, 0.12) }} />
  <Text style={{ color: tokens.foreground, fontWeight: "600" }}>Hand-rolled arrangement</Text>
</View>
```

### Surfaces

**Do** — A bordered, filled, padded surface is a Card; it carries the platform's own radius, hairline and elevation.

```tsx
<Card>
  <Typography>A real surface</Typography>
</Card>
```

**Don't** — Rebuilding the same box out of a View and four style properties drifts from the platform skins the moment one of them changes.

```tsx
<View style={{ width: 240, padding: 16, borderRadius: 10, borderWidth: 1, borderColor: tokens.border, backgroundColor: tokens.card }}>
  <Text style={{ color: tokens.foreground }}>A look-alike surface</Text>
</View>
```

Typical interface guidelines recommend touch targets that are at least 30 - 40 points/density-independent pixels. If a Touchable view has a height of 20 the touchable height can be extended to 40 with hitSlop={{top: 10, bottom: 10, left: 0, right: 0}} NOTE The touch area never extends past the parent view bounds and the Z-index of sibling views always takes precedence if a touch hits two overlapping views. |

| needsOffscreenAlphaCompositing | boolean \| undefined | no |  | Whether this view needs to rendered offscreen and composited with an alpha in order to preserve 100% correct colors and blending behavior. The default (false) falls back to drawing the component and its children with an alpha applied to the paint used to draw each element instead of rendering the full component offscreen and compositing it back with an alpha value. This default may be noticeable and undesired in the case where the View you are setting an opacity on has multiple overlapping elements (e.g. multiple overlapping Views, or text and a background). Rendering offscreen to preserve correct alpha behavior is extremely expensive and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is not turned on by default. If you do need to enable this property for an animation, consider combining it with renderToHardwareTextureAndroid if the view contents are static (i.e. it doesn't need to be redrawn each frame). If that property is enabled, this View will be rendered off-screen once, saved in a hardware texture, and then composited onto the screen with an alpha each frame without having to switch rendering targets on the GPU. |

# WaterfallChart

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/charts/waterfall-chart/waterfall-chart.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/waterfall-chart

## Public imports

```tsx
import { WaterfallChart } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

The running-total bridge: each step floats from the running total by its signed `value`, and a `total` step snapshots the running total as an absolute bar from zero.

The coloring is fixed semantics rather than a prop: rises green, falls red, totals the brand primary, so every bridge reads the same way. Scrubbing a step flags its change and running total.

## Usage

```tsx
<WaterfallChart
  title="Q3 revenue bridge"
  steps={[
    { label: "Q2", value: 4200, total: true },
    { label: "New", value: 980 },
    { label: "Expansion", value: 460 },
    { label: "Churn", value: -540 },
    { label: "FX", value: -120 },
    { label: "Q3", total: true },
  ]}
/>
```

## Variants

### Signed steps only

```tsx
<WaterfallChart
  steps={[
    { label: "Hired", value: 24 },
    { label: "Backfill", value: 8 },
    { label: "Attrition", value: -11 },
    { label: "Transfers", value: -3 },
    { label: "Net", total: true },
  ]}
/>
```

### Compact, inspected

```tsx
<WaterfallChart
  compact
  defaultSelected={2}
  steps={[
    { label: "Start", value: 100, total: true },
    { label: "Wins", value: 30 },
    { label: "Losses", value: -12 },
    { label: "End", total: true },
  ]}
/>
```

## Do & Don't

### WaterfallChart

**Do** - Bridge from one total to the next with signed steps; let the fixed coloring carry rise and fall.

```tsx
<WaterfallChart
title="Q3 revenue bridge"
steps={[
  { label: "Q2", value: 4200, total: true },
  { label: "New", value: 980 },
  { label: "Churn", value: -540 },
  { label: "Q3", total: true },
]}
/>
```

**Don't** - Plain bars of period totals hide the walk: what rose, what fell, and by how much.

```tsx
<Chart
data={[
  { label: "Q2", value: 4200 },
  { label: "Q3", value: 4640 },
]}
/>
```

# Wizard

Package: @nannier/canvas
Version: 4.3.1
Status: source-snapshot (not proof of an npm release)
Source SHA-256: 675fbe581e8b4ad6486d40d1b26a76d0ab3c2910cab444fa77edd63dd809f77b

Source: `src/organisms/wizard/wizard.md`
Human reference: https://canvas.nannier.com/components/wizard

## Public imports

```tsx
import { Wizard } from "@nannier/canvas";
```

The following examples are source excerpts. Supply application data and handlers; snippets using `tokens` read `const { tokens } = useTheme()` inside a component. Import React hooks from React. Intentional “Don't” examples illustrate unsupported patterns.

A modal workflow with a fixed step sidebar, a title and status header, and footer actions around a bounded, scrolling body. The application owns stage content, validation, saving and transitions; Wizard composes the existing Dialog, Steps and Button controls.

Add `embedded` to show an open wizard in a page as a specimen, the way a catalogue
or a showcase does: it keeps its look, its dialog role and its labelling, but it is
not modal. It does not take focus, trap Tab, set `aria-modal`, or close on Escape or
native back, and it renders in place in the page's flow instead of presenting into an
`OverlayProvider`.

## Usage

`ViewportOverlay` is docs-only scaffolding that presents the example above the docs page. In an application, mount Wizard beneath the app-root OverlayProvider.

```tsx
<Stateful initial={false}>
  {(open, setOpen) => <Stateful initial={0}>
    {(current, setCurrent) => <Column>
      <Button outline onPress={() => { setCurrent(0); setOpen(true); }}>Open project setup</Button>
      <ViewportOverlay><Wizard open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Set up a project"
        description="Choose the basics, then review your project."
        steps={[{ label: "Details" }, { label: "Review" }]} current={current}
        previous={current > 0 ? { label: "Details", onPress: () => setCurrent(0) } : undefined}
        status={`Step ${current + 1} of 2`}
        actions={<Button primary onPress={() => current === 0 ? setCurrent(1) : setOpen(false)}>{current === 0 ? "Review project" : "Create project"}</Button>}>
        <Column roomy>
          <Typography h3>{current === 0 ? "Project details" : "Ready to create"}</Typography>
          {current === 0 ? <Input label="Project name" defaultValue="Customer portal" /> : <Typography body>Customer portal is ready to create.</Typography>}
        </Column>
      </Wizard></ViewportOverlay>
    </Column>}
  </Stateful>}
</Stateful>
```

## Variants

### Team invitation

The status sits beside the title, with the previous action at the footer's start and the
application actions at its end. Compact steps occupy the fixed sidebar. When the panel is narrower than 520 points (a phone), the steps move under the title as segmented bars and the body takes the full width, so content such as a Chat is never squeezed beside the rail.

```tsx
<Wizard open embedded onOpenChange={() => {}} title="Create workspace"
  steps={[{ label: "Name" }, { label: "Members" }, { label: "Theme" }, { label: "Review" }]}
  current={1} status="Step 2 of 4" previous={{ label: "Back", onPress: () => {} }}
  actions={<Button>Continue</Button>}>
  <Typography body medium natural>Invite your team</Typography>
  <Input compact placeholder="noor@nannier.com" accessibilityLabel="First teammate email" />
  <Input compact placeholder="liang@nannier.com" accessibilityLabel="Second teammate email" />
</Wizard>
```

### Assistant workspace

`assistant` lays the wizard out like a desktop assistant window: the steps as a full-height
sidebar of rows, a 44 point top bar with the title and the status, and `previous` and
`actions` in a bar under the conversation. The body is unpadded so an `assistant flush` Chat fills it; a scrolled body
centers its content in the conversation's column. Below 720 points of panel the sidebar
gives way to segmented steps under the title.

```tsx
<Wizard open embedded assistant onOpenChange={() => {}} title="Plan a project" scrollBody={false}
  steps={[{ label: "Plan project" }, { label: "Review project plan" }, { label: "Plan workforce" }]}
  current={0} status="Autosaved" actions={<Button small ghost>Reset</Button>}>
  <Chat assistant flush meta="Claude CLI" messages={[{ id: "welcome", role: "assistant", content: "What should your project achieve?" }]} value="" onChangeText={() => {}} onSend={() => {}} />
</Wizard>
```

### Child owns scrolling

Set `scrollBody={false}` for a bounded child such as Chat that already manages its own thread scroll. The header and footer retain their positions.

```tsx
<Stateful initial={false}>
  {(open, setOpen) => <Column>
    <Button outline onPress={() => setOpen(true)}>Open planning conversation</Button>
    <ViewportOverlay><Wizard open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Plan a project"
      steps={[{ label: "Details" }, { label: "Conversation" }, { label: "Review" }]} current={1}
      scrollBody={false} status="Saved" actions={<Button primary onPress={() => setOpen(false)}>Done</Button>}>
      <Chat messages={[{ id: "welcome", role: "assistant", content: "What should your project achieve?" }]} value="" onChangeText={() => {}} onSend={() => {}} />
    </Wizard></ViewportOverlay>
  </Column>}
</Stateful>
```

## Do & Don't

### Named backward navigation

**Do** — Name the previous stage so its destination is clear.

```tsx
<Wizard open embedded onOpenChange={() => {}} title="Project setup" steps={[{ label: "Details" }, { label: "Review" }]} current={1} previous={{ label: "Details", onPress: () => {} }} />
```

**Don't** — Hide the destination behind a generic label.

```tsx
<Wizard open embedded onOpenChange={() => {}} title="Project setup" steps={[{ label: "Details" }, { label: "Review" }]} current={1} previous={{ label: "Back", onPress: () => {} }} />
```

## Accessibility

Dialog supplies the accessible modal name, focus management, live close action, Escape and native back behavior. Embedded specimens keep the bare panel without a close action or modal focus ownership. The current sidebar stage carries `aria-current="step"`. The previous action carries its stage name; application actions provide their own labels and disabled states. Footer buttons stay on one row; use Button `shrink` on application actions so long labels wrap within their button rather than moving the operation to another row. A controlled `onOpenChange` lets the application decide whether a dismissal request can proceed.

## Supported props

### WizardProps

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | boolean | yes |  | Controlled modal visibility. |
| title | string | yes |  | Names the modal and its fixed header. |
| description | string \| undefined | no |  | Supporting text below the title. |
| steps | Step[] | yes |  | Ordered stages; the application owns their content and transitions. |
| current | number | yes |  | Zero-based active stage; earlier stages read as complete. |
| onOpenChange | (open: boolean) => void | yes |  | Called when the close action, Escape or native back requests dismissal. |
| panelWidth | number \| undefined | no | 620 | Maximum panel width; defaults to the hand-off's 620px and shrinks to its parent. |
| previous | { label: string; onPress: () => void; disabled?: boolean; } \| undefined | no |  | Named previous stage action at the footer's start. |
| actions | ReactNode | no |  | Application actions at the footer's end. |
| status | string \| undefined | no |  | Save/progress status beside the title in the fixed header. |
| children | ReactNode | no |  |  |
| scrollBody | boolean \| undefined | no | true | Scroll the body (default true). Set false when a child, such as Chat, owns its scroll. |
| embedded | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Show the open wizard as a non-modal specimen, for a catalogue or a showcase: it keeps its look, its dialog role and its labelling, but does not take focus, trap Tab, claim `aria-modal`, or close on Escape or native back. It renders in place, in the flow of the page, as Dialog's contained form does, rather than presenting into an OverlayProvider. |
| assistant | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Lay the wizard out like a desktop assistant's window (the Claude desktop window, reference claude-desktop-chat): the steps as sidebar rows down the panel's full height, a 44 px top bar with the title and the status, and `previous` and `actions` in a bar under the conversation. The body is unpadded so an `assistant flush` Chat fills it; a scrolled body centers its content in the conversation's column. The description is not drawn. |
| testID | string \| undefined | no |  | Prefix for modal, steps, body-scroll and footer test hooks. |

See [installation](https://canvas.nannier.com/ai/4.3.1/installation.md) for required peers and feature fallbacks.
